title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
江西鄉試錄序
今
皇帝臨御之十年歲維甲午實天下大
比之秋江西廵按監察御史程宏
楊守隨暨方面重臣右布政使張
永按察使余複等僉謂登賢大事
弗恪遵
===
天子下福元元無窮時戶部左侍郎原
成憲或怠以徇曷以上答
傑奉
璽書握便宜重柄廵視茲土亦深致
嚴重之飭於是提調學校副使夏
寅徧歷郡邑預擇生儒之可備登
薦者得二千七百餘人以俟復慱
punctuated:
江西鄉試錄序
今皇帝臨御之十年，歲維甲午，實天下大比之秋。江西廵按監察御史程宏、楊守隨，暨方面重臣右布政使張永、按察使余複等，僉謂：「登賢大事，弗恪遵天子下福元元無窮時戶部左侍郎原成憲，或怠以徇，曷以上答？」傑奉璽書，握便宜重柄，廵視茲土，亦深致嚴重之飭。於是提調學校副使夏寅徧歷郡邑，預擇生儒之可備登薦者，得二千七百餘人以俟。復慱
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Jiangxi Provincial Examination

In the tenth year of the reign of the reigning Emperor, the cyclical year being jiawu (1474), it was truly the autumn of the triennial examination across the realm. The Regional Inspecting Censors of Jiangxi, Cheng Hong 程宏 and Yang Shousui 楊守隨, together with the senior provincial officials—Right Administration Commissioner Zhang Yong 張永, Surveillance Commissioner Yu Fu 余複, and others—all declared: "Promoting the worthy is a great affair; if we do not reverently observe the established statutes, or if we are negligent or partial, how can we answer to the Son of Heaven above and bring boundless blessings to the common people below?" [Note: two columns of text are transposed in the transcription here.] At that time, Left Vice Minister of Revenue Yuan Jie 原傑, bearing an imperial commission under the dynastic seal and wielding weighty authority to act at his discretion while touring and inspecting this territory, also issued stern and solemn admonitions. Thereupon, Surveillance Vice Commissioner for the Supervision of Schools Xia Yin 夏寅 traveled throughout the prefectures and districts to select in advance government students and Confucian scholars qualified to be presented as candidates, obtaining more than two thousand seven hundred men to await the examination. Furthermore, extensively…

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
採輿論走書幣四方延聘儒官以
司進退雖下至掌卷彌封謄録等
執事亦罔不柬諸有司中之端謹
有聲者充焉既八月正考官學正
汪雲自濮澤至同考官學正陳鑾
自蟆城至教諭沈環自安東至余
燠自東甌至鄭昭自汲郡至陳文
===
自三山至張琳自蒙莊至馮鉞自
芝城至謝文禮自于湖至而智則
灩輿正考至自姑蘇云及期闔院
帀之以熊羆之卒邏之以虎豹之
臣而集二千七百餘人者聲試之
九日辛卯試以四書五經經隨所
治越三日甲午試以論及詔誥表
punctuated: 採輿論，走書幣四方，延聘儒官以司進退；雖下至掌卷、彌封、謄録等執事，亦罔不柬諸有司中之端謹有聲者充焉。既八月，正考官學正汪雲自濮澤至，同考官學正陳鑾自蟆城至，教諭沈環自安東至，余燠自東甌至，鄭昭自汲郡至，陳文自三山至，張琳自蒙莊至，馮鉞自芝城至，謝文禮自于湖至，而智則灩輿正考至自姑蘇云。及期闔院，帀之以熊羆之卒，邏之以虎豹之臣，而集二千七百餘人者聲試之。九日辛卯，試以《四書》、《五經》，經隨所治；越三日甲午，試以論及詔、誥、表、
translation_en:
…gathered public opinion and sent letters and gifts in all directions to invite Confucian Education Officials (ruguan 儒官) to take charge of selecting and rejecting candidates. Even down to the functionaries in charge of the examination papers (zhangjuan 掌卷), sealing (mifeng 彌封), and transcribing (tenglu 謄錄), none were filled except by selecting upright, prudent, and reputable men from among the various local authorities.

When the eighth month arrived, the Chief Examiner, Subprefectural Director of Studies (xuezheng 學正) Wang Yun 汪雲, arrived from Puze 濮澤; the Associate Examiners—Subprefectural Director of Studies Chen Luan 陳鑾 from Macheng 蟆城 [?], District Director of Studies (jiaoyu 教諭) Shen Huan 沈環 from Andong 安東, Yu Yu 余燠 from Dong'ou 東甌, Zheng Zhao 鄭昭 from Jijun 汲郡, Chen Wen 陳文 from Sanshan 三山, Zhang Lin 張琳 from Mengzhuang 蒙莊, Feng Yue 馮鉞 from Zhicheng 芝城, and Xie Wenli 謝文禮 from Yuhu 于湖—all arrived, while I, Zhi 智, sharing the carriage as Chief Examiner [?], arrived from Gusu 姑蘇.

When the appointed time came, the examination compound was locked, surrounded by bear-like soldiers and patrolled by tiger-and-leopard-like officials, and the more than two thousand seven hundred assembled candidates were rigorously [?] examined. On the ninth day, xinmao, they were tested on the Four Books and Five Classics, each candidate taking the Classic in which he specialized. Three days later, on jiawu, they were tested with a discourse (lun 論), as well as an edict (zhao 詔), mandate (gao 誥), memorial (biao 表), or…

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
判詔誥表内科一道又三日丁酉
乃策之首之以
制書次之以經史及時務于時院内
外綱維振肅守隨實專之其提調
監試則以屬左叅政王克復左叅
議徐鑑僉事陳騏徐懷其贊理防
範則以屬永禝及右叅政魏元副
===
使陳煒趙銘左叅議葉顯右叅議
黄縉僉事張鑑陳琦胡靖申安凡
厥三試皆天日晶明祥飆披拂若
默有以相文運之隆音而又號令
清肅纖埃不驚於是乎就試之士
靡不得以專厥精思罄厥底藴而
發舒於霈然之辭以聽乎灼然之
punctuated: 判，詔、誥、表内科一道。又三日丁酉，乃策之：首之以制書，次之以經史及時務。于時院内外綱維振肅，守隨實專之。其提調、監試，則以屬左叅政王克復、左叅議徐鑑、僉事陳騏、徐懷；其贊理、防範，則以屬永禝及右叅政魏元，副使陳煒、趙銘，左叅議葉顯，右叅議黄縉，僉事張鑑、陳琦、胡靖、申安。凡厥三試，皆天日晶明，祥飆披拂，若默有以相文運之隆音。而又號令清肅，纖埃不驚。於是乎就試之士，靡不得以專厥精思，罄厥底藴，而發舒於霈然之辭，以聽乎灼然之……
translation_en: …and legal judgments (pan), with candidates specializing in one category among imperial decrees (zhao), imperial mandates (gao), and memorials (biao). Three days later, on the dingyou day [the fifteenth], they were tested with policy questions (ce): first on Imperial Edicts, and next on the Classics, Histories, and current affairs. At this time, inside and outside the examination compound, discipline and order were strictly maintained, for which [Bi] Shousui 畢守隨 was in fact solely responsible. As for the duties of Proctor (tidiao) and Censor-in-Attendance at Examinations (jianshi), these were entrusted to Left Administration Vice Commissioner Wang Kefu 王克復, Left Assistant Administration Commissioner Xu Jian 徐鑑, and Assistant Surveillance Commissioners Chen Qi 陳騏 and Xu Huai 徐懷. As for assisting in administration and maintaining security precautions, these duties were entrusted to [Li] Yongji 李永禝 as well as Right Administration Vice Commissioner Wei Yuan 魏元, Surveillance Vice Commissioners Chen Wei 陳煒 and Zhao Ming 趙銘, Left Assistant Administration Commissioner Ye Xian 葉顯, Right Assistant Administration Commissioner Huang Jin 黄縉, and Assistant Surveillance Commissioners Zhang Jian 張鑑, Chen Qi 陳琦, Hu Jing 胡靖, and Shen An 申安. Throughout all three sessions of the examination, the sky and sun were bright and clear, and auspicious breezes gently blew, as if unseen forces were quietly aiding the flourishing fortune of literary culture [reading 者 for 音?]. Moreover, commands and regulations were pure and solemn, so that not the slightest speck of dust was disturbed. Thus, among the scholars taking the examination, there was none who could not concentrate his finest thoughts, exhaust his deepest learning, and give full expression to them in torrential words, while awaiting the luminous…

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
既竣乃取而詳訂焉其較之之
法本之初試以觀其本領之淵源
參之次試以觀其辯論酬應與夫
裁決之微者又參之三試以觀其
===
傅而有用不徒區區循行數墨號
曰明經者之腐中苟有泛而不根
者鑿而立異者膚末而纖瑣者舉
不取取之必典則必瑩徹必端嚴
必豪壯不主臆見而發羣說不因
寸朽而弃良材據所取可登者亦
punctuated: 既竣，乃取而詳訂焉。其較之之法，本之初試，以觀其本領之淵源；參之次試，以觀其辯論、酬應與夫裁決之微者；又參之三試，以觀其傅而有用，不徒區區循行數墨、號曰明經者之腐。中苟有泛而不根者、鑿而立異者、膚末而纖瑣者，舉不取。取之必典則，必瑩徹，必端嚴，必豪壯。不主臆見而發羣說，不因寸朽而弃良材。據所取可登者亦
translation_en: … [The examination] having concluded, we took [the papers] and carefully evaluated them. As for the method of comparing them: we based it on the first session to observe the depth and source of their fundamental learning; we cross-referenced this with the second session to observe the subtleties of their argumentation, official correspondence, and judicial rulings; and we further cross-referenced it with the third session to observe whether their learning was broad [reading 傅 as 博] [?] and practical, and not merely the pedantry of those who mechanically follow the lines and count the ink-marks while styling themselves masters of the Classics. Among them, if there were any that were vague and unfounded, forced and striving for novelty, or superficial and petty, none were selected. Those selected had to be canonical and regular, lucid and penetrating, upright and rigorous, and vigorous and grand. We did not hold to personal prejudices, but rather brought forth a wide range of scholarly views; we did not discard fine timber on account of an inch of rot. Based on those we selected, the ones worthy of being placed on the list were also …

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
衆遵定額第抜其尤者九十又五
人葢治易者得十又八治書者得
二十又四治詩者得三十又七治
春秋者得九治禮記者得七其次
第一等之以三試之優劣其各經
所以取之之差一均之就試者之
多寡也棘撤榜揭既復錄文之可
式并所次氏名為書以
獻僉曰〔智〕宜序不得辭竊惟天之生
賢何為為天下也士君子之致用
何為亦所以為天下而奉承乎天
也然施設大者必其抱負涵養也
大主敬所以立為天下之大本窮
理所以達為天下之大用者於斯
punctuated: 衆，遵定額第抜其尤者九十又五人：葢治《易》者得十又八，治《書》者得二十又四，治《詩》者得三十又七，治《春秋》者得九，治《禮記》者得七。其次第一等之以三試之優劣，其各經所以取之之差，一均之就試者之多寡也。棘撤榜揭，既復錄文之可式，并所次氏名為書以獻。僉曰〔智〕宜序，不得辭。竊惟天之生賢何為？為天下也。士君子之致用何為？亦所以為天下而奉承乎天也。然施設大者，必其抱負涵養也大。主敬所以立為天下之大本，窮理所以達為天下之大用者，於斯
translation_en:
…numerous; conforming to the fixed quota, we selected only the most outstanding among them, ninety-five men in all: eighteen specializing in the Book of Changes (Yi), twenty-four specializing in the Book of Documents (Shu), thirty-seven specializing in the Book of Odes (Shi), nine specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu), and seven specializing in the Record of Rites (Liji). Their order of ranking was determined entirely by the relative merits of their performances across the three sessions, while the differences in the numbers selected from each Classic were proportioned strictly according to the greater or lesser number of candidates sitting for each. Once the thorny barriers of the compound were removed and the placard of successful candidates was posted, we further transcribed the compositions worthy of serving as models, together with the ranked list of names, into a book to present to the throne. All said that I, Zhi, ought to write the preface, and I could not decline.

I venture to reflect: For what purpose does Heaven give birth to worthy men? It is for the sake of the empire. For what purpose do scholar-gentlemen apply their talents in service? It is likewise for the sake of the empire, thereby fulfilling the will of Heaven. Yet for one's practical measures and accomplishments to be great, one's aspirations and self-cultivation must first be great. Holding fast to reverence in order to establish the great foundation for serving the empire, and exhaustively investigating principle in order to attain the great application for serving the empire—in this…

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
無盡而積累之則愈大愈妙而彌
綸參賛之具備矣時茍我用畢而
清之令〔智〕等所以取諸士子徒以
其言盖亦驗其餘窮理之一端誠以
理茍明則形諸辭也必正大而光
明辭而正大光明其涵養抱負與
夫異時之設施縣之可知兹寔亦
===
朝廷所以設科取士之意然有德者
固必有言而徒言者亦或未必有
德焉言出於德則縣兹以登者必
克奉乎天天民必克愛天事必
克恭治亂安危必克幹天之運禍
福榮辱必克唯天之安鼇極必藉
之以植
punctuated: 無盡，而積累之，則愈大愈妙，而彌綸參賛之具備矣，時茍我用，畢而清之。令〔智〕等所以取諸士子，徒以其言，盖亦驗其餘窮理之一端。誠以理茍明，則形諸辭也，必正大而光明；辭而正大光明，其涵養抱負與夫異時之設施，縣之可知，兹寔亦朝廷所以設科取士之意。然有德者固必有言，而徒言者亦或未必有德焉。言出於德，則縣兹以登者，必克奉乎天，天民必克愛，天事必克恭，治亂安危必克幹天之運，禍福榮辱必克唯天之安，鼇極必藉之以植，
translation_en: …inexhaustible; and when one accumulates them, they become ever greater and ever more profound, so that the wherewithal for ordering the world and assisting in the transforming powers of Heaven and Earth is complete. If the times should employ us, we can bring them forth in full and clarify [?] them [畢而清之; perhaps a misprint for 措之, "put them into practice"]. Now [令; for 今], the reason that [I,] Zhi, and my colleagues select candidates from among the scholars merely on the basis of their words is that this is also a way to test one aspect of their investigation of principle [? 驗其餘窮理之一端; 餘 is likely a misprint for 於]. Truly, if principle is clearly understood, then when it takes form in words, they will certainly be upright, great, and illustrious. When the words are upright, great, and illustrious, one's self-cultivation and aspirations, as well as the measures one will enact in the future, can be known from them [縣之, for 繇之]. This is indeed also the Court's intention in establishing the examination system to select scholars. Yet while those who possess virtue will certainly have fine words, those who merely have words do not necessarily possess virtue. If their words issue from virtue, then those who ascend by this path will certainly be able to serve Heaven: Heaven's people they will certainly be able to love; Heaven's affairs they will certainly be able to revere; in order and disorder, safety and peril, they will certainly be able to sustain the destiny of Heaven; in misfortune and fortune, honor and disgrace, they will certainly be able to rest solely in what Heaven ordains; the great pillars of the realm [鼇極] will certainly rely on them to stand firm, and…

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
瀌圖必籍之以壽兹寔維設科取士
之利哉言苟不德之出則動必違
天必土苴仁義必桎梏禮法必唯
欲之徇而身家之圖必漠然於民
之苦樂
國之休戚利必剝則蛇虺以敗類必柔
則脂韋以求媚必譎則鳳鳴鸑鷟
===
以盜名必奸則高城深府以衷毒
小用之必小以壞大用之必大以
壞遠之近之用之必遠之近之以
壞於戲科目得士而若兹其亦可
畏也哉其亦可愧也哉
直隷蘇州府儒學教授林智謹序
punctuated:
瀌圖必籍之以壽，兹寔維設科取士之利哉！言苟不德之出，則動必違天，必土苴仁義，必桎梏禮法，必唯欲之徇而身家之圖，必漠然於民之苦樂、國之休戚；利必剝，則蛇虺以敗類；必柔，則脂韋以求媚；必譎，則鳳鳴鸑鷟以盜名；必奸，則高城深府以衷毒。小用之必小以壞，大用之必大以壞，遠之近之用之必遠之近之以壞。於戲！科目得士而若兹，其亦可畏也哉！其亦可愧也哉！
直隷蘇州府儒學教授林智謹序。
translation_en:
… and the imperial plan [?] will surely rely on them to endure for ages. This is truly the benefit of establishing examination categories to select scholars! If, however, their words do not issue from virtue, then in their actions they will surely defy Heaven; they will surely treat benevolence and righteousness as mere dirt and straw; they will surely regard ritual and law as fetters and shackles; they will surely follow only their own desires and scheme for themselves and their families; and they will surely be indifferent to the sufferings and joys of the people and the weal and woe of the state. In pursuit of profit, they will surely be rapacious, acting like vipers and adders to ruin their own kind; they will surely be pliant, acting like greased leather to curry favor; they will surely be deceitful, crying like phoenixes to steal a reputation; and they will surely be treacherous, making their hearts like high walls and deep citadels to harbor venom within. If employed in a small capacity, they will surely cause small ruin; if employed in a great capacity, they will surely cause great ruin; whether employed far away or near at hand, they will surely cause ruin far and near. Alas! If the examination categories obtain scholars such as these, how terrifying it is indeed! How shameful it is indeed!
Respectfully prefaced by Lin Zhi 林智, Instructor in the Confucian School of Suzhou Prefecture in the Metropolitan Area (Zhili).

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
成化十年鄉試
監臨官
巡按江西監察御史楊守隨〔淮貞浙江鄞縣人丙戌進士〕
提調官
江西等處承宣布政使司左參政王克復〔師仁福建福清縣人丁丑進士〕
江西等處承宣布政使司左參議徐鑑〔克明浙江淳安縣人庚辰進士〕
監試官
江西等處提刑按察司僉事陳騏〔夢祥廣東南海縣人丁丑進士〕
江西等處提刑按察司僉事徐懷〔明德浙江建德縣人庚辰進士〕
===
考試官
直隸蘇州府儒學教授林智〔若濬福建莆田縣人甲子貢士〕
山西澤州儒學學正汪雲〔從龍直隸休寧縣人乙酉貢士〕
同考試官
直隸鳳陽府泗州儒學學正陳鑾〔叔和福建懷安縣人己卯貢士〕
直隸淮安府安東縣儒學教諭沈璟〔時健浙江蕭山縣人庚午貢士〕
福建建寧府甌寧縣儒學教諭余煥〔孔哲浙江開化縣人癸酉貢士〕
河南衛輝府汲縣儒學教諭鄭昭〔德懋福建福清縣人壬午貢士〕
福建福州府懷安縣儒學教諭陳文〔世道廣東歸善縣人丙子貢士〕
punctuated:
成化十年鄉試

監臨官
巡按江西監察御史楊守隨〔淮貞，浙江鄞縣人，丙戌進士〕。

提調官
江西等處承宣布政使司左參政王克復〔師仁，福建福清縣人，丁丑進士〕。
江西等處承宣布政使司左參議徐鑑〔克明，浙江淳安縣人，庚辰進士〕。

監試官
江西等處提刑按察司僉事陳騏〔夢祥，廣東南海縣人，丁丑進士〕。

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
然非與曰非也予一以貫之
小德川流大德敦化
五穀者種之美者也苟爲不熟不如荑稗夫仁
亦在乎熟之而已矣
易
坤道其順乎承天而時行
孚乃利用禴无咎
===
擬之而後言議之而後動擬議以成其變化鳴
鶴在陰其子和之我有好爵吾與爾靡之子
曰君子居其室出其言善則千里之外應之
況其邇者乎
窮理盡性以至於命
書
水火金木土穀惟修
厥貢惟金三品瑤琨篠簜齒革羽毛惟木島夷
卉服厥篚織貝
punctuated:
第壹場

四書
然？非與？」曰：「非也，予一以貫之。」
小德川流，大德敦化。
五穀者，種之美者也；苟爲不熟，不如荑稗。夫仁，亦在乎熟之而已矣。

易
坤道其順乎！承天而時行。
孚乃利用禴，无咎。
擬之而後言，議之而後動，擬議以成其變化。「鳴鶴在陰，其子和之。我有好爵，吾與爾靡之。」子曰：「君子居其室，出其言善，則千里之外應之，況其邇者乎？」
窮理盡性以至於命。

書
水、火、金、木、土、穀，惟修。
厥貢惟金三品，瑤、琨、篠、簜、齒、革、羽、毛、惟木。島夷卉服，厥篚織貝。
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books
"...Is it so, or not?" The Master said, "It is not. I have one thread that runs through it all." [Analects 15.3]
Smaller virtues flow like river currents; the great virtue makes transformations thick and abundant. [Doctrine of the Mean 30]
The five grains are the finest of seeds, yet if they do not ripen, they are worse than tares and barnyard grass. As for benevolence, it too lies simply in bringing it to ripeness. [Mencius 6A.19]

Classic of Changes (Yi)
How compliant is the Way of the Receptive (Kun)! It receives from Heaven and acts in accordance with the times. [Kun, Wenyan]
If one is sincere, it is beneficial even to offer a simple summer sacrifice; there is no blame. [Hexagram 45, Cui / Hexagram 46, Sheng]
One considers before speaking, and deliberates before acting; through consideration and deliberation one brings about transformations. "'A calling crane is in the shade; its young answers it. I have a fine goblet; I will share it with you.' The Master said: 'When the gentleman dwells in his chamber and sends forth words that are good, those a thousand li away respond to him—how much more so those who are near!'" [Xici shang 8]
Exhausting principle and fully realizing one's nature, so as to arrive at destiny. [Shuogua 1]

Classic of Documents (Shu)
Water, fire, metal, wood, earth, and grain—these are to be well regulated. [Counsels of the Great Yu]
Its tribute is metal of three grades, yao and kun jades, small and large bamboos, ivory, hides, feathers, hair, and timber. The island peoples wear garments of woven grass; their baskets contain woven shell-patterned silks. [Tribute of Yu]

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄

文王誥教小子有正有事無彝酒越庶國飲惟
祀德將無醉惟曰我民迪小子惟土物愛厥
心臧聰聽祖考之彝訓越小大德小子惟一
居寵思危罔不惟畏弗畏入畏推賢讓能庶官
乃和
詩
蠶月條桑取彼斧斨以伐遠揚猗彼女桑七月
鳴鵙八月載績載玄載黃我朱孔陽為公子
裳四月秀葽五月鳴蜩八月其穫十月隕蘀
一之日于貉取彼狐貍為公子裘
鐘鼓既設一朝右之
王命召虎式辟四方徹我疆土匪疚匪棘王國
來極
昔有成湯自彼氐羌莫敢不來享莫敢不來王
曰商是常天命多辟設都于禹之績歲事來
辟勿予禍適稼穡匪解天命降監下民有嚴
不僭不濫不敢怠遑命于下國封建厥福
===
春秋
punctuated:
文王誥教小子有正有事，無彝酒。越庶國，飲惟祀，德將無醉。惟曰：「我民迪小子，惟土物愛，厥心臧。聰聽祖考之彝訓，越小大德，小子惟一。」
居寵思危，罔不惟畏；弗畏入畏。推賢讓能，庶官乃和。
《詩》
蠶月條桑，取彼斧斨，以伐遠揚，猗彼女桑。七月鳴鵙，八月載績。載玄載黃，我朱孔陽，為公子裳。四月秀葽，五月鳴蜩。八月其穫，十月隕蘀。一之日于貉，取彼狐貍，為公子裘。
鐘鼓既設，一朝右之。
王命召虎：「式辟四方，徹我疆土。匪疚匪棘，王國來極。」
昔有成湯，自彼氐羌，莫敢不來享，莫敢不來王，曰商是常。天命多辟，設都于禹之績，歲事來辟，勿予禍適，稼穡匪解。天命降監，下民有嚴，不僭不濫，不敢怠遑，命于下國，封建厥福。
《春秋》
translation_en:
"King Wen admonished and instructed the young men, the principal officers, and the managers of affairs, not to indulge constantly in wine; and throughout the various states, that they should drink only on occasions of sacrifice, and then maintain their virtue so as not to become drunk. He said: 'Let my people guide the young men to cherish the products of the soil, and their hearts will be good. Let the young men hearken wisely to the constant instructions of their fathers and grandfathers, and in virtues small and great let them be single-minded.'" [Book of Documents, "Announcement about Drunkenness" (Jiu gao)]
"In a position of favor, think of peril, and never be without awe; he who is without awe falls into what is dreadful. Advance the worthy and yield to the able, and the various officials will be in harmony." [Book of Documents, "Officers of Zhou" (Zhou guan)]

Book of Odes (Shi)
"In the silkworm month they strip the mulberry branches, taking those axes and hatchets to lop the far-reaching and high-rising ones, and pulling down theleaves of the young mulberry trees. In the seventh month the shrike cries; in the eighth month they begin to spin. They dye it dark and yellow; our red is very bright, to make lower garments for the young noblemen. In the fourth month the milkwort is in spike; in the fifth month the cicada chirps. In the eighth month they harvest; in the tenth month the leaves fall. In the days of the first month they go after badgers, and take those foxes and wildcats, to make furs for the young noblemen." [Book of Odes, "Seventh Month" (Qi yue)]
"The bells and drums have been set up, and for a whole morning we honor him." [Book of Odes, "Red Bow" (Tong gong)]
"The king gave charge to Shao Hu: 'Open up the four quarters, and tithe my territories. Without distress, without urgency, bring them to the standard of the royal state.'" [Book of Odes, "Running Waters of the Jiang and Han" (Jiang Han)]
"Of old there was Tang the Successful; even from the Di and Qiang, none dared not come with offerings, none dared not come to acknowledge him as king, saying that Shang is everlasting. Heaven charged the many lords who established their capitals in the tracks of Yu's labors to come to the sovereign for the annual affairs: 'Do not visit us with calamity or reproof; we have not been remiss in husbandry.' Heaven sent down its inspection, and the people below were reverent; without error in reward, without excess in punishment, not daring to be indolent or at ease, he was charged over the states below, and grandly established his felicity." [Book of Odes, "Warriors of Yin" (Yin wu)]

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu)

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
王人子突救衛〔莊公六年〕　季子来歸〔閔公元年〕　楚屈
完来盟于師〔僖公四年〕　楚子使椒来聘〔文公九年〕
秦伯使術来聘〔文公十二年〕　吳子使札来聘〔襄公二十
九年〕
齊侯宋公江人黄人會于陽穀〔僖公三年〕　公會齊
侯宋公陳侯衛侯鄭伯許男曹伯侵蔡蔡潰遂伐
楚次于陘　盟于召陵　齊人執陳轅濤塗
及江人黄人伐陳〔僖公四年〕
宋人及楚人平〔宣公十五年〕　公會齊侯于夾谷　齊
===
人来歸鄆讙龜陰田〔定公十年〕
公如京師　公自京師遂會晉侯齊侯宋公衛
侯鄭伯曹伯邾人滕人伐秦〔成公十三年〕
禮記
御同於長者雖貳不辭偶坐不辭
禮樂交錯於中發形於外是故其成也懌恭敬
而温文立太傅少傅以養之欲其知父子君
臣之道也
五行以為質故事可復也
punctuated:
王人子突救衛〔莊公六年〕。季子来歸〔閔公元年〕。楚屈完来盟于師〔僖公四年〕。楚子使椒来聘〔文公九年〕。秦伯使術来聘〔文公十二年〕。吳子使札来聘〔襄公二十九年〕。
齊侯、宋公、江人、黄人會于陽穀〔僖公三年〕。公會齊侯、宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯侵蔡，蔡潰，遂伐楚，次于陘。盟于召陵。齊人執陳轅濤塗。及江人、黄人伐陳〔僖公四年〕。
宋人及楚人平〔宣公十五年〕。公會齊侯于夾谷。齊人来歸鄆、讙、龜陰田〔定公十年〕。
公如京師。公自京師遂會晉侯、齊侯、宋公、衛侯、鄭伯、曹伯、邾人、滕人伐秦〔成公十三年〕。
《禮記》：
御同於長者，雖貳不辭；偶坐不辭。
禮樂交錯於中，發形於外，是故其成也懌，恭敬而温文。立太傅、少傅以養之，欲其知父子君臣之道也。
五行以為質，故事可復也。
translation_en:
The King's man Zitu rescued Wei [6th year of Duke Zhuang]. Jizi came and returned to the state [1st year of Duke Min]. Qu Wan of Chu came and made a covenant with the army [4th year of Duke Xi]. The Viscount of Chu sent Jiao to come on a mission of friendly inquiries [9th year of Duke Wen]. The Earl of Qin sent Shu to come on a mission of friendly inquiries [12th year of Duke Wen]. The Viscount of Wu sent Zha to come on a mission of friendly inquiries [29th year of Duke Xiang].
The Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the men of Jiang, and the men of Huang met at Yanggu [3rd year of Duke Xi]. The Duke met the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Earl of Cao to make an incursion into Cai; the people of Cai scattered, whereupon the allies attacked Chu and halted at Xing. They made a covenant at Shaoling. The men of Qi seized Yuan Taotu of Chen. Together with the men of Jiang and the men of Huang, we attacked Chen [4th year of Duke Xi].
The men of Song made peace with the men of Chu [15th year of Duke Xuan]. The Duke met the Marquis of Qi at Jiagu. The men of Qi came and restored the lands of Yun, Huan, and Guiyin [10th year of Duke Ding].
The Duke went to the royal capital. From the royal capital the Duke thereupon met the Marquis of Jin, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Earl of Cao, the men of Zhu, and the men of Teng to attack Qin [13th year of Duke Cheng].
Record of Rites (Liji):
When attending an elder and receiving the same food, even if extra dishes are served, one does not decline them; when seated as a companion to keep a guest company, one does not decline them.
Rites and music interpenetrate within and manifest their forms without; therefore, when a man's education is complete, he is joyful, respectful, reverent, gentle, and refined. The Grand Mentor (Taifu) and Junior Mentor (Shaofu) are established to nurture him, desiring that he should know the way of father and son, ruler and minister.
The Five Phases serve as their substance, and therefore their affairs can be repeated.

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
使人觀感而自化以言教使人諷誦而自得
二者蓋相須焉稽之於古若堯舜之所以帝
天下禹湯文武之所以王天下其道不越于
此見之於經何者躬行心得而為身教之實
何者訓廸告戒而為言教之要民之從教有
可言歟洪惟
天朝
聖聖相承繼天立極倡以身教者至垂訓勵俗示以
言教者詳方今
===
聖皇在上躬行仁義以敦化原渙發
綸音以弘文教至治盛化並駕唐虞超越三代
可得鋪張其實以曉示天下後世歟諸士子
遠稽羣聖之嘉言善行近覩
昭代之懿範奎章蓋亦有年矣請著于篇
問周禮大司徒所以教萬民而賓興之者六藝
其一也夫禮所以教之中曰五禮者吉禮十
有二凶禮五賓禮八軍禮五嘉禮六其節目
之詳可指言歟樂所以教之和曰六樂者一
punctuated:
使人觀感而自化，以言教使人諷誦而自得，二者蓋相須焉。稽之於古，若堯、舜之所以帝天下，禹、湯、文、武之所以王天下，其道不越于此。見之於經，何者躬行心得而為身教之實？何者訓廸告戒而為言教之要？民之從教，有可言歟？洪惟天朝聖聖相承，繼天立極，倡以身教者至，垂訓勵俗，示以言教者詳。方今聖皇在上，躬行仁義以敦化原，渙發綸音以弘文教，至治盛化，並駕唐、虞，超越三代，可得鋪張其實，以曉示天下後世歟？諸士子遠稽羣聖之嘉言善行，近覩昭代之懿範奎章，蓋亦有年矣，請著于篇。

問：《周禮》大司徒所以教萬民而賓興之者，六藝其一也。夫禮所以教之中，曰「五禮」者，吉禮十有二、凶禮五、賓禮八、軍禮五、嘉禮六，其節目之詳，可指言歟？樂所以教之和，曰「六樂」者，一
translation_en:
…causing people to observe, be moved, and transform of themselves; and teaching by words, causing people to recite and grasp the meaning for themselves—these two indeed depend upon one another. Examining antiquity, the way by which Yao and Shun ruled the realm as Emperors, and by which Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu ruled the realm as Kings, did not go beyond this. As seen in the Classics, which matters represent personal practice and inner comprehension that constitute the substance of teaching by personal example? Which matters represent instruction, guidance, admonition, and warning that constitute the essentials of teaching by words? Can something be said of how the people followed these teachings? Greatly reflecting upon our Heavenly Dynasty, where sage succeeds sage, continuing the work of Heaven and establishing the supreme standard: in leading through teaching by personal example, it has been utmost; in handing down instructions to encourage customs and demonstrating through teaching by words, it has been thorough. Now, the Sage Emperor above personally practices benevolence and righteousness to enrich the source of transformation, and proclaims silken imperial decrees to broaden civil teaching. His ultimate governance and flourishing transformation ride abreast of Tang [Yao] and Yu [Shun] and surpass the Three Dynasties. Can the reality of this be set forth in detail so as to make it known to the realm and to future generations? You gentlemen have for years looked far back to examine the fine words and good deeds of the various sages, and closely witnessed the admirable models and imperial writings of our illustrious era; please set this forth in your essays.

Question: Among the means by which the Grand Minister of Education (da situ) in the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli) taught the myriad people and recommended them as guests to the court, the Six Arts were one. Now, ritual is the means to teach moderation. What are called the "Five Rites" comprise twelve auspicious rites, five mourning rites, eight guest rites, five military rites, and six felicitous rites—can their detailed particulars be pointed out and explained? Music is the means to teach harmony. What are called the "Six Musics" are: first…

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
曰雲門二曰咸池三曰大韶四曰大夏五曰
大濩六曰大武周人用之以祭祀何不同歟
射驗其中否以觀德行御調習驅馳使不失
正曰五射曰五御其節目何在書可以見心
畫數可以盡事變曰六書曰九數其名義何
詳然六藝之中禮樂為先禮莫重於祭祭必
有義若孔子廟庭顏曾思身任道統之傳配
享固宜然顏路曾晳孔鯉三子者父也子配
享於殿父從祀於廡禮因人情顏曾思之心
安乎周程張朱大明孔子之道於千百載之
下其功偉矣禮以義起周程張朱可配享乎
古樂之亡久矣秦漢之間去周未遠其器與
聲猶有存者逮于後世其論愈多而愈未定
然稽古禮文學者急務方今
===
聖人在位功成治定理宜有作爾多士應賓興而來
宜於廟庭禮議律呂本原斟酌推詳務求的
見試一言之以備
臨軒問焉
punctuated: 曰《雲門》，二曰《咸池》，三曰《大韶》，四曰《大夏》，五曰《大濩》，六曰《大武》，周人用之以祭祀，何不同歟？射驗其中否以觀德行，御調習驅馳使不失正，曰五射、曰五御，其節目何在？書可以見心畫，數可以盡事變，曰六書、曰九數，其名義何詳？然六藝之中，禮樂為先。禮莫重於祭，祭必有義。若孔子廟庭，顏、曾、思身任道統之傳，配享固宜；然顏路、曾晳、孔鯉，三子者父也，子配享於殿，父從祀於廡，禮因人情，顏、曾、思之心安乎？周、程、張、朱，大明孔子之道於千百載之下，其功偉矣，禮以義起，周、程、張、朱可配享乎？古樂之亡久矣，秦、漢之間去周未遠，其器與聲猶有存者，逮于後世，其論愈多而愈未定。然稽古禮文，學者急務。方今聖人在位，功成治定，理宜有作。爾多士應賓興而來，宜於廟庭禮議、律呂本原，斟酌推詳，務求的見，試一言之，以備臨軒問焉。
translation_en: … is called Yunmen (Cloud Gate), the second Xianchi (All-Embracing Reservoir), the third Dashao (Great Succession), the fourth Daxia (Great Xia), the fifth Dahuo (Great Protection), and the sixth Dawu (Great Martiality). Why did the people of Zhou use them differently in sacrifices? Archery tests whether one hits the mark in order to observe moral conduct, and charioteering trains in galloping and driving so as not to lose correctness; as for what are called the Five Archeries and the Five Charioteerings, wherein do their specific items lie? Calligraphy allows one to see the delineations of the mind, and mathematics allows one to exhaust the permutations of affairs; as for what are called the Six Scripts and the Nine Branches of Mathematics, what are the details of their names and meanings? Yet among the Six Arts, ritual and music come first. In ritual, nothing is more important than sacrifice, and sacrifice must have its principle of righteousness. Take, for instance, the temple court of Confucius (Kongzi 孔子): Yan Hui (顏回), Zeng Shen (曾參), and Zisi (子思) personally bore the transmission of the succession of the Way (daotong), so their being associated in the main offerings (peixiang) is certainly fitting. Yet Yan Lu (顏路), Zeng Xi (曾晳), and Kong Li (孔鯉) are the fathers of those three masters; when the sons are associated in the offerings in the main hall while the fathers receive ancillary sacrifices in the side galleries, since ritual is based on human feelings, could the minds of Yan, Zeng, and Zisi be at ease? Zhou Dunyi (周敦頤), the Cheng brothers (程顥, 程頤), Zhang Zai (張載), and Zhu Xi (朱熹) greatly illuminated the Way of Confucius hundreds and thousands of years later; their achievements are magnificent. Since ritual arises from righteousness, may Zhou, the Chengs, Zhang, and Zhu be associated in the main offerings? Ancient music has long been lost. During the Qin and Han dynasties, not yet far removed from the Zhou, some of its instruments and sounds still survived; coming down to later ages, discussions of it grew ever more numerous and ever less settled. Yet examining ancient ritual and cultural forms is an urgent duty for scholars. At present, a Sage sits upon the throne; merit is achieved and governance is stabilized, so in principle there ought to be new creations. You numerous scholars have come in response to the ceremonial invitation of local worthies; you should deliberate and investigate in detail the ritual discussions regarding the temple court and the fundamental origins of the musical pitch-pipes, striving to arrive at a definitive view. Try to set it forth in words, in preparation for the Emperor's personal inquiry at the palace.

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
問天下之事有是非一定而易見者有是非疑
似而難處者是則行之非則違之何難之有
惟夫事變之來也是非疑似欲伸法則虧恩
將全恩則廢法求其兩全難矣姑摭古人之
所遇者論之如石奢之於父石碏之於子全
私恩乎徇大義乎趙苞之守城徐庶之遇敵
全其母乎忠其君乎李璀之于父謀告之則
不孝不告則不忠棄疾之於君命告之則不
忠不告則不孝爲祭仲之女者將告父以害
===
其夫乎將從夫以逆其父乎爲杜伯之友者
將順君以誅友乎抑私友以違君乎王道之
于兄若何以爲恭唐太宗之于兄若何以全
友縮高之攻管爲子者若之何武后之計敵
業爲將者若之何唐武宗爲憲宗爲叔䧺
稷烏乎定周世宗爲君柴守禮爲臣朝宁烏
乎立薄昭何處而當濮園何稱而宜樂洲之
納合孰是靈州之棄守孰得漢之爵制功罪
何居唐之復讎雄誅何辨此皆事之至難當
punctuated: 問：天下之事，有是非一定而易見者，有是非疑似而難處者。是則行之，非則違之，何難之有？惟夫事變之來也，是非疑似，欲伸法則虧恩，將全恩則廢法，求其兩全難矣。姑摭古人之所遇者論之：如石奢之於父、石碏之於子，全私恩乎？徇大義乎？趙苞之守城、徐庶之遇敵，全其母乎？忠其君乎？李璀之于父謀，告之則不孝，不告則不忠；棄疾之於君命，告之則不忠，不告則不孝。爲祭仲之女者，將告父以害其夫乎？將從夫以逆其父乎？爲杜伯之友者，將順君以誅友乎？抑私友以違君乎？王道之于兄，若何以爲恭？唐太宗之于兄，若何以全友？縮高之攻管，爲子者若之何？武后之計敵，業爲將者若之何？唐武宗爲憲宗爲叔，䧺稷烏乎定？周世宗爲君，柴守禮爲臣，朝宁烏乎立？薄昭何處而當？濮園何稱而宜？樂洲之納合孰是？靈州之棄守孰得？漢之爵制，功罪何居？唐之復讎，雄誅何辨？此皆事之至難，當
translation_en: Question: Among the affairs of the world, there are those in which right and wrong are fixed and easily seen, and there are those in which right and wrong are ambiguous and difficult to handle. Where something is right, one carries it out; where it is wrong, one turns away from it—what difficulty is there in that? It is only when crises arise and right and wrong become ambiguous—when upholding the law impairs personal affection, or preserving personal affection ruins the law—that seeking to satisfy both becomes difficult. Let us provisionally gather and discuss situations encountered by the ancients: For instance, in the case of Shi She 石奢 toward his father and Shi Que 石碏 toward his son, should one preserve private affection or follow great righteousness? In Zhao Bao's 趙苞 defense of his city and Xu Shu's 徐庶 encounter with the enemy, should one save one's mother or be loyal to one's ruler? As for Li Cui 李璀 regarding his father's plot, to report it was unfilial, while not to report it was disloyal; as for Qiji 棄疾 regarding his ruler's command, to disclose it to his father was disloyal, while not to disclose it was unfilial. For someone in the position of Zhai Zhong's 祭仲 daughter, should she inform her father and thereby harm her husband, or follow her husband and thereby defy her father? For someone in the position of Du Bo's 杜伯 friend [Zuo Ru 左儒], should he obey his ruler and execute his friend, or favor his friend and defy his ruler? In the case of Wang Dao 王導 [transcribed 王道] toward his elder brother [Wang Dun 王敦], how could he act with brotherly respect? In the case of Emperor Taizong of Tang 唐太宗 toward his elder brother, how could he preserve fraternal devotion? When Su Gao 縮高 was called upon in the attack on Guan 管, what was his son to do? When Empress Wu 武后 schemed against her enemies, what was [Li Jingye 李敬業], already serving as a general [or: Jingye 敬業, with 敬 omitted and 業 surviving (?)], to do? When Emperor Wuzong of Tang 唐武宗 [error for Xuanzong 宣宗 (?)] stood as uncle to Emperor Xianzong's 憲宗 [descendant, i.e., Wuzong], how was the succession to the altars of state [or imperial ancestral order (?)] to be settled? When Emperor Shizong of Later Zhou 周世宗 was ruler and his biological father Chai Shouli 柴守禮 was a subject, how were their positions in the court audience to be established? How should Bo Zhao 薄昭 have been dealt with appropriately? By what title should the Prince of Pu (Puyuan 濮園) properly have been addressed? Regarding the acceptance or rejection of Weizhou [transcribed 樂洲 (?)], which course was right? Regarding the abandonment or defense of Lingzhou 靈州, which policy was sound? In the Han system of noble ranks [or: In Han's enfeoffment/punishment of Chen Tang 陳湯 and Feng Fengshi 馮奉世 (?)]—how should merit and guilt be adjudicated? In the Tang cases of blood vengeance, how should heroic righteousness and capital punishment [or amnesty and execution (?)] be distinguished? All of these are matters of the utmost difficulty, for which one ought…

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
求所以處之之術而未得焉者也試與諸士
子講之請陳高世之見以決萬古之疑
問格物致知學者先務盈天地間者惟萬物天
地亦物耳在天成象者則有風雷雨露日月
星辰天地之依附何在天體之旋轉何主風
雨霜露何自而成日月星辰何以運轉星麗
于天何隕而為石雷奮于地何化而為斧月
受日光諸星之明亦受日光歟月有弦望晦
朔之異月常圓歟月中黑處決為何物或為
===
顧兔在腹然歟否歟在地成形者則有人物
草木鳥獸河海人與鳥獸皆有知覺草木亦
有知覺歟萬物之生皆有種類麒麟亦有種
歟魚龍一也而鱗有陰陽之數何所見草木
一也而質有堅弱之分何所本百川衆流均
納諸海不見其溢何所泄歟孟子曰萬物皆
備於我諸士子格物之學固已講矣然欲誠
其身果何用其力歟願悉陳之毋隱
問異端之說多矣姑舉一二質之老氏虛無易
punctuated:
求所以處之之術而未得焉者也。試與諸士子講之，請陳高世之見，以決萬古之疑。
問：格物致知，學者先務。盈天地間者，惟萬物；天地亦物耳。在天成象者，則有風、雷、雨、露、日、月、星、辰。天地之依附何在？天體之旋轉何主？風、雨、霜、露何自而成？日、月、星、辰何以運轉？星麗于天，何隕而為石？雷奮于地，何化而為斧？月受日光，諸星之明亦受日光歟？月有弦、望、晦、朔之異，月常圓歟？月中黑處，決為何物？或為顧兔在腹，然歟否歟？在地成形者，則有人物、草木、鳥獸、河海。人與鳥獸皆有知覺，草木亦有知覺歟？萬物之生，皆有種類，麒麟亦有種歟？魚龍一也，而鱗有陰陽之數，何所見？草木一也，而質有堅弱之分，何所本？百川衆流，均納諸海，不見其溢，何所泄歟？孟子曰：「萬物皆備於我。」諸士子格物之學固已講矣，然欲誠其身，果何用其力歟？願悉陳之毋隱。
問：異端之說多矣，姑舉一二質之。老氏虛無，《易》
translation_en:
… have sought the proper method of handling them and yet failed to find it. Let us discuss them with you scholars: please set forth views that transcend the age so as to resolve the doubts of ten thousand generations.

Question: Investigating things and extending knowledge is the foremost task of the scholar. What fills the space between heaven and earth is nothing other than the myriad things; heaven and earth themselves are also things. Among the phenomena that take form as images in the heavens, there are wind, thunder, rain, dew, the sun, the moon, the stars, and the celestial markers. Upon what do heaven and earth depend and attach themselves? What governs the rotation of the celestial sphere? From what are wind, rain, frost, and dew formed? By what means do the sun, moon, stars, and celestial markers revolve? The stars are arrayed in the heavens—why do they fall and become stones? Thunder bursts forth from the earth—why does it transform into wedge-axes? The moon receives the light of the sun; does the brightness of the various stars also come from receiving the light of the sun? The moon has the variations of quarter, full, dark, and new phases, yet is the moon itself always round? What definitely is the dark spot inside the moon? Some say a gazing hare is in its belly—is this so or not? Among the things that take physical form on earth, there are human beings and creatures, grasses and trees, birds and beasts, rivers and seas. Humans as well as birds and beasts all possess perception and awareness; do grasses and trees also possess perception and awareness? The generation of the myriad things always follows distinct species and kinds; does the unicorn (qilin) also have a breeding species? Fish and dragons are alike, yet their scales conform to yin and yang numbers—on what basis is this observed? Grasses and trees are alike, yet their substance is divided into firm and supple—in what is this rooted? The hundred rivers and multitude of streams all empty into the sea, yet it is never seen to overflow—where does it drain away? Mencius said: "All the myriad things are complete within me." You scholars have certainly already studied the learning of investigating things; yet if one wishes to make one's person sincere, where indeed should one apply one's effort? Pray set it all forth in full and hold nothing back.

Question: The doctrines of heterodox teachings are numerous; let us tentatively raise one or two of them for examination. Laozi speaks of emptiness and non-being, while the Book of Changes (Yi) …

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
曰君子以虛受人佛氏寂滅易曰寂然不動
其義同歟老子之學虛靜無為沖退自守先
儒謂老子得易之體孟子得易之用其說然
歟釋氏之初經有二十四篇後世撰集愈繁
其說愈多厥後達磨不立文字獨有心靜見
理之說先儒謂老氏亦難為抗衡又謂攻之
者執說反出其下果何見歟再傳而有滅罪
資福生死輪迴之說其與虛無寂滅之教同
歟何宮殿相望金碧輝煥其壯麗反有過於
===
夫子廟庭者遂使天下之士徒誦孔氏書而
不務師法孔子顧乃徼福於文昌其惑甚矣
異端之說入於人心也深矣欲人不惑也難
矣孟子曰能言距楊墨者聖人之徒也諸士
子學聖人者也茲欲使天下之人不待家諭
戶曉而自不為異端之所惑必有其說願悉
陳之以觀所學之正
punctuated: 曰：「君子以虛受人」；佛氏寂滅，《易》曰：「寂然不動」，其義同歟？老子之學，虛靜無為，沖退自守，先儒謂老子得《易》之體，孟子得《易》之用，其說然歟？釋氏之初，經有二十四篇，後世撰集愈繁，其說愈多。厥後達磨不立文字，獨有心靜見理之說，先儒謂老氏亦難為抗衡，又謂攻之者執說反出其下，果何見歟？再傳而有滅罪資福、生死輪迴之說，其與虛無寂滅之教同歟？何宮殿相望，金碧輝煥，其壯麗反有過於夫子廟庭者，遂使天下之士，徒誦孔氏書，而不務師法孔子，顧乃徼福於文昌，其惑甚矣。異端之說，入於人心也深矣，欲人不惑也難矣。孟子曰：「能言距楊、墨者，聖人之徒也。」諸士子學聖人者也，茲欲使天下之人，不待家諭戶曉，而自不為異端之所惑，必有其說，願悉陳之，以觀所學之正。
translation_en: … says, "The superior man receives people with emptiness"; the Buddhists speak of quiescent extinction (jimie), and the Book of Changes (Yi) says, "Quiescent and unmoving"—are their meanings the same? The learning of Laozi emphasizes emptiness, stillness, and non-action, maintaining oneself through modesty and retreat. Former Confucians said that Laozi grasped the substance of the Changes while Mencius grasped the function of the Changes; is this view so? At the beginning of Buddhism, its scriptures had twenty-four sections [?]; in later generations, compilations became ever more voluminous and their doctrines ever more numerous. Thereafter, Bodhidharma (Damo) did not establish written words, holding solely the doctrine of seeing principle when the mind is still. Former Confucians said that even Laozi could hardly rival him, and also said that those who attack him hold views that actually fall below his; on what insight is this really based? Passed down further, there arose the doctrines of extinguishing sins to accumulate blessings and the transmigration of life and death; are these the same as the teachings of emptiness, non-being, and quiescent extinction? Why is it that their palaces and halls stand in sight of one another, resplendent in gold and jade-green, their magnificence even surpassing that of the temple courtyards of the Master (Confucius)? Consequently, scholars throughout the realm merely recite the books of Confucius without striving to take Confucius as their teacher and model, and instead seek blessings from Wenchang; their delusion is extreme! The doctrines of heterodoxy have entered deeply into people's minds, and it is difficult to wish that people not be deluded. Mencius said, "Whoever is able to speak out to resist Yang Zhu and Mo Di is a follower of the sages." You gentlemen are students of the sages. Now, if one wishes to cause the people of the realm, without waiting for every household and door to be instructed, to naturally avoid being deluded by heterodoxy, there must be a way to explain how. I hope you will set it forth in full, so that I may observe the orthodoxy of your learning.

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
四書
然非與曰非也予一以貫之
劉燿
同考試官教諭張　批〔聖人之言本明白簡易近時學者惟事穿鑿毋以非也無指然非歟爲說殊失本旨此篇不爲時論所〕
惑宛然聖賢問答氣象特錄之以爲學者式
同考試官教諭陳　批詞簡義明允宜高薦
同考試官教諭鄭　批題本主知而言場中作者體認不真至
以行立說惟此作得之
考試官學正汪　批正大典雅可取
考試官教授林　批必如此作方合本旨
===
賢者有悟道之幾聖人决其疑而示其要也夫聖人
之道其要在乎一以貫之而已賢者學將有得方信
而忽疑宜聖人舉以爲告也歟昔子貢之學多而能
識矣夫子欲其知所本也故有女以予爲多學而識
之問子貢於是對之以爲夫子學而不厭而古今事
變無不知好古敏求而禮樂名物無不達信乎多學
而能識也然而夫子之質生知也不思而得夫子之
punctuated:
四書

「然，非與？」曰：「非也，予一以貫之。」

劉燿
同考試官教諭張　批：〔聖人之言，本明白簡易，近時學者惟事穿鑿，毋以「非也」無指「然，非歟」爲說，殊失本旨。此篇不爲時論所〕惑，宛然聖賢問答氣象，特錄之以爲學者式。
同考試官教諭陳　批：詞簡義明，允宜高薦。
同考試官教諭鄭　批：題本主知而言，場中作者體認不真，至以行立說，惟此作得之。
考試官學正汪　批：正大典雅，可取。
考試官教授林　批：必如此作，方合本旨。

賢者有悟道之幾，聖人决其疑而示其要也。夫聖人之道，其要在乎一以貫之而已。賢者學將有得，方信而忽疑，宜聖人舉以爲告也歟！昔子貢之學，多而能識矣。夫子欲其知所本也，故有「女以予爲多學而識」之問。子貢於是對之，以爲夫子學而不厭，而古今事變無不知；好古敏求，而禮樂名物無不達，信乎多學而能識也。然而夫子之質，生知也，不思而得；夫子之
translation_en:
The Four Books

"[Zigong replied,] 'Yes—or is it not so?' The Master said, 'It is not so. I have one thread that runs through it all.'" [Analects 15.3]

By Liu Yao 劉燿

Comment by Associate Examiner County Director of Studies Zhang 張: 〔The words of the Sage are originally clear, plain, and simple. Recent scholars merely engage in forced interpretations, invariably arguing [reading 毋 for 每?] that "It is not so" does not refer back to "Yes—or is it not so?", which completely misses the original purport. This essay is not〕 misled 〔by contemporary theories〕; it vividly captures the spirit of question and answer between Sage and worthy, so we specially record it as a model for scholars.
Comment by Associate Examiner County Director of Studies Chen 陳: The diction is concise and the meaning clear; it truly deserves a high recommendation.
Comment by Associate Examiner County Director of Studies Zheng 鄭: The topic essentially speaks with a focus on knowledge. Writers in the examination hall failed to grasp its true meaning, going so far as to base their arguments on action; only this composition has got it right.
Comment by Examiner Subprefectural Director of Studies Wang 汪: Upright, grand, and classically elegant; worthy of selection.
Comment by Examiner Prefectural Director of Studies Lin 林: Only when written like this does it accord with the original purport.

When the worthy had an inkling of awakening to the Way, the Sage resolved his doubt and showed him its essential point. Now, as for the Way of the Sage, its essential point lies simply in having one thread that runs through it all. When the worthy's learning was about to bear fruit, no sooner had he affirmed a belief than he suddenly felt doubt—was it not fitting that the Sage should bring this up to instruct him? Formerly, in his learning, Zigong 子貢 had learned much and was able to retain it. The Master wished him to know the fundamental root, and therefore asked the question, "Do you take me to be one who learns much and retains it in memory?" Zigong thereupon replied to him, thinking to himself that the Master learned without flagging, so that there was nothing in the changing affairs of antiquity and the present that he did not know; and that he loved antiquity and was earnest in seeking it, so that there was nothing in the names and objects of rites and music that he did not master—truly, he learned much and was able to retain it! And yet, the Master's natural endowment was that of one born with knowledge, grasping things without having to think; the Master's…

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
聖人縱也自識而明殆非多學而識之者歟子貢方
信而忽疑如此蓋其積學功至而亦將有得也夫子
因是告之以為我非徒多學而識之者也特一以貫
之焉耳且天下之物萬不齊也固未嘗不多學然多
學之中不過一理貫通之而已豈誇多云乎哉天下
之事萬不同也亦未嘗不博學然博學之中不過一
理融會之而已豈務博云乎哉博也而同歸于一
也而該攝乎博賾也其可不知所務耶聖人以是而
告之所以決其疑而使之領其要也歟抑考之魯論
===
孔子之於曾子不待其問而直告之曰吾道一以貫
之曾子復深諭之曰唯若子貢則先發其疑而後告
之而子貢終亦不能知曾子之唯者蓋曾子真積力
久行而將有所得子貢積學功至知而將有所得二
子之所學於此可見
小德川流大德敦化
劉麟
同考試官教諭馮 批題本正大塲中作者往往牽綴或失
德字宇宙為體川流為用不旨此篇認理明白措詞老健是宜錄出
punctuated:
聖，人縱也，自識而明，殆非多學而識之者歟？子貢方信而忽疑如此，蓋其積學功至，而亦將有得也。夫子因是告之，以為：「我非徒多學而識之者也，特一以貫之焉耳。」且天下之物萬不齊也，固未嘗不多學，然多學之中，不過一理貫通之而已，豈誇多云乎哉？天下之事萬不同也，亦未嘗不博學，然博學之中，不過一理融會之而已，豈務博云乎哉？博也而同歸于一，一也而該攝乎博，賜也其可不知所務耶？聖人以是而告之，所以決其疑而使之領其要也歟！抑考之《魯論》，孔子之於曾子，不待其問而直告之曰：「吾道一以貫之。」曾子復深諭之曰：「唯。」若子貢，則先發其疑而後告之，而子貢終亦不能知曾子之「唯」者，蓋曾子真積力久，行而將有所得；子貢積學功至，知而將有所得。二子之所學，於此可見。

小德川流，大德敦化。
劉麟
同考試官教諭馮　批：題本正大，塲中作者往往牽綴，或失「德」字，宇宙為體、川流為用本旨。此篇認理明白，措詞老健，是宜錄出。
translation_en:
…sagehood was granted to him by Heaven; he understands naturally and is clear-minded. Could it be that he is not one who learns much and retains it?” That Zigong 子貢 just believed it and then suddenly doubted it like this was because his accumulated learning had reached a high level of effort and he too was about to attain understanding. The Master therefore told him, thinking: “I am not merely one who learns much and retains it; I simply thread it all together with a single principle.” Moreover, the myriad things in the world are uneven. To be sure, one never fails to learn much, yet within that extensive learning there is nothing more than a single principle threading through it all—how could it be a matter of boasting of quantity? The myriad affairs in the world are different. Likewise, one never fails to learn broadly, yet within that broad learning there is nothing more than a single principle fusing it all together—how could it be a matter of striving for breadth? Breadth returns alike to unity, and unity [missing char in print: 一] encompasses breadth—how could Si 賜 [Zigong, here transcribed 賾] not know what he ought to devote himself to? That the sage told him this was in order to resolve his doubt and cause him to grasp the essential point! Furthermore, if we examine it in the Analects (Lu Lun 魯論), in Confucius’s 孔子 dealings with Zengzi 曾子, without waiting for a question he directly told him, “My Way is threaded together by a single principle,” and Zengzi in turn deeply understood it and said, “Yes.” As for Zigong, Confucius first prompted his doubt and only afterward told him, and in the end Zigong was still unable to match [知, likely for 如] Zengzi’s “Yes.” This is because Zengzi had accumulated genuine effort over a long time and was about to attain understanding through practice, whereas Zigong had reached a high level of effort in accumulated learning and was about to attain understanding through knowledge. What the two disciples learned can be seen from this.

“The lesser virtues flow like river currents; the greater virtues make transformation敦厚 [thick and rich].”
Liu Lin 劉麟
Associate Examiner Instructor Feng 馮 comments: The topic is inherently upright and grand, yet writers in the examination hall often patch things together contrivedly, or lose sight of the word “virtue” (de 德) and the original purport of taking the cosmos as substance and the flowing currents as function [? 宇宙為體川流為用不旨]. This essay recognizes the principles clearly and its phrasing is mature and vigorous; it is fitting to select it for publication.

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭余　批〔一破包括無遺況文整理到真佳作也〕
考試官學正汪　批〔中庸此節言天地之道作者多以聖人對講此作得旨可嘉〕
考試官教授林　批〔辭順理明非他卷所及〕
萬物各具一理萬理同出一原蓋天地之道合萬為
一一實萬分者也中庸以是而言天道㕔旨微矣昔
子思子論聖人之德而取譬於天地至此復明取譬
之意謂夫天地間萬物並育而不相害道並行而不
相悖人見其不害不悖而已而其所以不害不悖者
===
一小德之川流小德者全體之分彼其萬物散殊各
正性命而充塞乎天地生者生育者育何相害焉四
時錯行日月代明而循環乎宇宙往者過來者續何
相悖焉不曰小德而曰小德川流則如川之流脉絡
分明而往不息所謂萬物各具一太極者是也人見
其並育並行而已而其所以並育並行者一大德之
敦化大德者萬殊之本彼其維天之命於穆不已渾
然莫窺其眹兆萬物於此而並育也上天之載無聲
無臭窈然莫測其機緘道於此而並行也不曰大德
punctuated:
同考試官教諭余　批：〔一破包括無遺，況文整理到，真佳作也。〕
考試官學正汪　批：〔《中庸》此節言天地之道，作者多以聖人對講，此作得旨，可嘉。〕
考試官教授林　批：〔辭順理明，非他卷所及。〕

萬物各具一理，萬理同出一原。蓋天地之道，合萬為一，一實萬分者也。《中庸》以是而言天道，㕔旨微矣。昔子思子論聖人之德而取譬於天地，至此復明取譬之意。謂夫天地間萬物並育而不相害，道並行而不相悖。人見其不害不悖而已，而其所以不害不悖者，一小德之川流。小德者，全體之分。彼其萬物散殊，各正性命，而充塞乎天地，生者生、育者育，何相害焉？四時錯行，日月代明，而循環乎宇宙，往者過、來者續，何相悖焉？不曰「小德」而曰「小德川流」，則如川之流，脉絡分明而往不息，所謂「萬物各具一太極」者是也。人見其並育並行而已，而其所以並育並行者，一大德之敦化。大德者，萬殊之本。彼其「維天之命，於穆不已」，渾然莫窺其眹兆，萬物於此而並育也；「上天之載，無聲無臭」，窈然莫測其機緘，道於此而並行也。不曰「大德」
translation_en:
Associate Examiner and Instructor Yu comments: [The opening statement encompasses everything without omission; moreover, the essay is well-organized and reaches the heart of the principle—truly an excellent piece.]
Examiner and Director of Studies Wang comments: [This section of the Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong) speaks of the Way of Heaven and Earth. Most candidates treat it in parallel with the sage, but this piece grasps the true purport and is commendable.]
Examiner and Instructor Lin comments: [The phrasing is smooth and the reasoning clear; it is beyond the reach of other papers.]

The myriad things each possess a single principle, and the myriad principles all issue from a single source. For the Way of Heaven and Earth unites the myriad into one, and the one reality is divided into the myriad. That the Doctrine of the Mean speaks in these terms of the Way of Heaven—its [?] purport is subtle indeed! Formerly, Master Zisi discussed the virtue of the sage by drawing an analogy to Heaven and Earth, and reaching this point he again clarifies the meaning of that analogy. He says that between Heaven and Earth, the myriad things are nourished together without harming one another, and courses run together without contradicting one another. People merely see that they do not harm or contradict one another, yet that whereby they do not harm or contradict one another is entirely the river-like flow of lesser virtues. The lesser virtues are the divisions of the whole substance. As the myriad things scatter in their diversity, each rectifying its nature and destiny and filling Heaven and Earth, those that are born are born and those that are nourished are nourished—how could they harm one another? As the four seasons alternate in their courses and the sun and moon succeed one another in brightness, circulating through the cosmos, what goes passes by and what comes continues on—how could they contradict one another? It does not merely say "lesser virtues," but says "lesser virtues flow like river currents," meaning that like the flow of a river, their veins and channels are distinct and they go on without cease; this is what is meant by the saying, "Each of the myriad things possesses a Supreme Ultimate (Taiji)." People merely see that they are nourished together and run together, yet that whereby they are nourished together and run together is entirely the rich transformation of the great virtue. The great virtue is the root of the myriad differentiations. In that "the decree of Heaven, how profound and unceasing it is!"—boundless and undifferentiated, none can spy out its incipient signs, yet herein the myriad things are nourished together. In that "the doings of High Heaven have neither sound nor smell"—obscure and unfathomable, none can measure its subtle mechanism, yet herein the courses run together. It does not merely say "great virtue" …

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
而曰大德敦化其敦厚其化根本盛大而出無窮所
謂萬物統體一太極者是也吁一本散於萬殊萬殊
原於一本此天地之所以為大而聖人之德之大從
可知矣抑又論之小德川流即率性之道時中之中
在聖人則物各付物也大德敦化即天命之性未發
之中在聖人則純亦不已也子思子於下章言至聖
之德所以明小德之川流至誠之道所以明大德之
敦化其脉絡貫通如此非深於道其孰能之
五穀者種之美者也苟為不熟不如荑稗夫仁
亦在乎熟之而已矣
===
同考試官教諭謝　批〔孟子本以五穀喻仁學者未達其旨〕
〔五穀不止仁言殊失本旨此作得之錄出以祛群惑〕
王任
考試官學正汪　批〔此篇認理明白措詞不腐宜錄之〕
考試官教授林　批〔說理詳盡無踰此篇〕
大賢既喻仁道至大而不可不熟必申言人之為仁
而惟在乎熟蓋道莫大乎仁也為仁不熟則反不如
為他道之有成仁其可以不熟乎哉孟子即物喻之
punctuated:
而曰「大德敦化」，其敦厚其化，根本盛大而出無窮，所謂萬物統體一太極者是也。吁！一本散於萬殊，萬殊原於一本，此天地之所以為大，而聖人之德之大從可知矣。抑又論之，「小德川流」，即率性之道、時中之中，在聖人則物各付物也；「大德敦化」，即天命之性、未發之中，在聖人則純亦不已也。子思子於下章言「至聖」之德，所以明「小德之川流」；「至誠」之道，所以明「大德之敦化」。其脉絡貫通如此，非深於道，其孰能之？
五穀者，種之美者也；苟為不熟，不如荑稗。夫仁，亦在乎熟之而已矣。
王任
同考試官教諭謝批：〔孟子本以五穀喻仁，學者未達其旨，五穀不止仁言，殊失本旨。此作得之，錄出以祛群惑。〕
考試官學正汪批：〔此篇認理明白，措詞不腐，宜錄之。〕
考試官教授林批：〔說理詳盡，無踰此篇。〕
大賢既喻仁道至大而不可不熟，必申言人之為仁而惟在乎熟。蓋道莫大乎仁也，為仁不熟，則反不如為他道之有成，仁其可以不熟乎哉？孟子即物喻之，
translation_en:
… rather it says, "Great virtue makes transformations thick and deep," meaning that as it deepens its transformations, its root is grand and its outflow inexhaustible; this is what is meant by the myriad things collectively embodying a single Supreme Ultimate (Taiji). Alas! One root disperses into myriad differentiations, and the myriad differentiations originate from one root. This is why Heaven and Earth are great, and from this the greatness of the sage's virtue can be known! Moreover, if we discuss it further, "Lesser virtues flow like river currents" refers to the Way of following one's nature and the Equilibrium that is timely in the world—in the sage, it is responding to each thing according to what it is. "Great virtue makes transformations thick and deep" refers to the nature conferred by the Mandate of Heaven and the Equilibrium before feelings are aroused—in the sage, it is purity that never ceases. Master Zisi, in the subsequent chapters, speaks of the virtue of the "most sage" in order to clarify how "lesser virtues flow like river currents," and the Way of the "most sincere" in order to clarify how "great virtue makes transformations thick and deep." With its connecting threads running through like this, who could be capable of it unless he was profound in the Way?

"The five grains are the finest of seeds; yet if they do not ripen, they are worse than tares and barnyard grass. As for benevolence, it too consists simply in bringing it to ripeness."

By Wang Ren 王任.
Associate Examiner Instructor Xie 謝 comments: [Mencius originally used the five grains as a metaphor for benevolence. Scholars have failed to grasp his purport, taking the five grains to refer to more than just benevolence, which quite misses the original meaning. This essay gets it right; we transcribe and publish it to dispel the doubts of the multitude.]
Examiner Subprefectural Instructor Wang 汪 comments: [This essay understands the principles clearly and its phrasing is not hackneyed; it ought to be recorded.]
Examiner Prefectural Professor Lin 林 comments: [In explaining the principles thoroughly and exhaustively, none surpasses this essay.]

Having used a metaphor to show that the Way of benevolence is supremely great and must not fail to be brought to ripeness, the Great Worthy necessarily reiterates that a person's practice of benevolence lies solely in bringing it to ripeness. For no Way is greater than benevolence; if one practices benevolence without bringing it to ripeness, it is on the contrary inferior to practicing some other way with success. How, then, could benevolence fail to be brought to ripeness? When Mencius draws a metaphor from physical things, …

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
切矣且物之可食莫五穀若也五穀非種之美者乎
使或雨暘之不時耘耔之弗力秀而不實曾荑稗之
不若矣蓋荑稗雖不能如五穀之美然既成熟亦有
可食者焉心之全德惟仁是也仁非道之大者乎使
或涵養之未至持守之弗堅功虧一簣曾他道之不
若矣蓋他道雖不能如仁道之大然既有成亦有可
觀者焉夫仁不可不熟如此熟之之道又豈鹵莽滅
裂之可致哉必也知而好好而樂瑩然俾無物欲之
蔽而無蔽之外奚加功勉而利利而安渾然俾無私
意之間而無間之外奚容力是知為仁必貴乎熟而
不可徒恃其種之美又豈可以仁之難熟而甘為他
道之有成也歟大抵仁者天之尊爵也人之安宅也
知其為尊守之而不慕乎人爵之榮知其為安居之
而不徇乎外物之誘得志與民由之不得志獨行其
道焉往而不善哉孟子假粗喻精而即五穀以為訓
其勉人為仁之意亦深矣學者不可不知
易
===
坤道其順乎承天而時行
punctuated:
切矣。且物之可食，莫五穀若也，五穀非種之美者乎？使或雨暘之不時，耘耔之弗力，秀而不實，曾荑稗之不若矣。蓋荑稗雖不能如五穀之美，然既成熟，亦有可食者焉。心之全德，惟仁是也，仁非道之大者乎？使或涵養之未至，持守之弗堅，功虧一簣，曾他道之不若矣。蓋他道雖不能如仁道之大，然既有成，亦有可觀者焉。夫仁不可不熟如此，熟之之道，又豈鹵莽滅裂之可致哉？必也知而好，好而樂，瑩然俾無物欲之蔽，而無蔽之外，奚加功？勉而利，利而安，渾然俾無私意之間，而無間之外，奚容力？是知為仁必貴乎熟，而不可徒恃其種之美；又豈可以仁之難熟，而甘為他道之有成也歟！大抵仁者，天之尊爵也，人之安宅也。知其為尊，守之而不慕乎人爵之榮；知其為安，居之而不徇乎外物之誘。得志，與民由之；不得志，獨行其道，焉往而不善哉！孟子假粗喻精，而即五穀以為訓，其勉人為仁之意亦深矣，學者不可不知。

《易》
坤道其順乎，承天而時行。
translation_en:
…is apt indeed. Moreover, among edible things, none compares to the five grains. Are the five grains not the finest of seeds? Yet if rain and sunshine are untimely, or weeding and hilling are not done with effort, so that they flower without bearing fruit, they are not even as good as tares and wild millet. For although tares and wild millet cannot match the excellence of the five grains, once they have ripened, there is still something edible about them. As for the complete virtue of the mind, it is benevolence alone. Is benevolence not the greatest of ways? Yet if one's cultivation of it is not thorough, or one's preservation of it is not firm, so that the effort falls short by a single basket of earth, it is not even as good as other ways. For although other ways cannot match the greatness of the way of benevolence, once they are brought to completion, there is still something worthy of observation in them. Since it is thus imperative that benevolence be brought to maturity, how could the way to mature it be achieved through carelessness and crudity? One must know it and therefore love it, love it and therefore delight in it, making it pure and clear so that there is no obscuration by material desires; and beyond this freedom from obscuration, what further effort need be added? One must practice it with effort and therefore find it advantageous, find it advantageous and therefore be at peace in it, making it whole and seamless so that there is no interruption by selfish intentions; and beyond this freedom from interruption, what further exertion can be admitted? From this we know that in practicing benevolence one must value bringing it to maturity, and must not merely rely on the excellence of its seed; nor how could one, because benevolence is difficult to mature, be content with achieving success in some other way? In general, benevolence is the high nobility bestowed by Heaven and the peaceful abode of man. Knowing its nobility, one guards it and does not covet the glory of human nobility; knowing its peace, one dwells in it and does not yield to the enticements of external things. When one achieves one's ambition, one follows it together with the people; when one does not achieve one's ambition, one practices one's way alone—where could one go and not do well? Mencius borrowed the coarse to illustrate the subtle, taking the five grains as his lesson; his intention in encouraging people to practice benevolence was profound indeed, and scholars must not fail to know it.

Classic of Changes (Yi)
How compliant is the way of Kun! It receives from Heaven and acts at the proper time.

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
律
同考試官教諭馮　批〔彖多順承天釋坤之元文言此節復明承天之義場中作者多以亨利貞混說失本旨惟此作得之而且文〕
〔采燦然亦當首選孰得與之抗衡哉〕
同考試官教諭余　批〔文言一題人多泛講不能發明坤順之義此作理明而辭不窘求人意表可嘉〕
考試官學正汪　批〔承天時行即坤道之順也作者語多有□是篇簡當可取〕
考試官教授林　批〔發明坤順承天之義殆無餘藴〕
===
文言賛坤道之順必言其所以順也蓋承天之施行
不違時此坤道之所以順也文言聖人以此發明坤
元之義何其至與甞觀坤之彖傳既以乃順承天賛
坤德之元矣文言至此復申彖傳之意我謂天乾為純
陽坤則純乎陰而無間故其德至順而無以加非若
巽離兊之陰間乎陽而為入為明為説者焉乾為至
剛坤則一於柔而不雜故其德極順而無以尚非若
震坎艮之陽雜乎陰而為動為險為止者焉坤道其
順如此果何以驗之乎觀其發於用者可見矣彼乾
punctuated:
律。

同考試官教諭馮　批：〔彖多順承天釋坤之元，文言此節復明承天之義。場中作者多以亨、利、貞混說，失本旨，惟此作得之，而且文采燦然，亦當首選，孰得與之抗衡哉？〕
同考試官教諭余　批：〔文言一題，人多泛講，不能發明坤順之義。此作理明而辭不窘，求人意表，可嘉。〕
考試官學正汪　批：〔承天時行，即坤道之順也。作者語多有□，是篇簡當可取。〕
考試官教授林　批：〔發明坤順承天之義，殆無餘藴。〕

文言賛坤道之順，必言其所以順也。蓋承天之施，行不違時，此坤道之所以順也。文言聖人以此發明坤元之義，何其至與！甞觀坤之彖傳，既以「乃順承天」賛坤德之元矣；文言至此，復申彖傳之意。我謂天乾為純陽，坤則純乎陰而無間，故其德至順而無以加，非若巽、離、兊之陰間乎陽，而為入、為明、為説者焉。乾為至剛，坤則一於柔而不雜，故其德極順而無以尚，非若震、坎、艮之陽雜乎陰，而為動、為險、為止者焉。坤道其順如此，果何以驗之乎？觀其發於用者可見矣。彼乾
translation_en:
Lü [given name of candidate; or possibly a garbled surname].

Associate Examiner Feng, Instructor (jiaoyu), comments: [Where the Commentary on the Decision (Tuan) says "thus docilely receiving from Heaven" [where 多 is a woodblock error for 乃] to explain the "originating" (yuan) quality of the Kun hexagram, this section of the Commentary on the Words of the Text (Wenyan) further clarifies the meaning of receiving from Heaven. Most writers in the examination compound conflated it with "penetrating" (heng), "advantageous" (li), and "correct and firm" (zhen), losing the original purport. Only this composition grasps it, and moreover its literary brilliance shines forth; it too deserves to be selected first—who could rival it?]
Associate Examiner Yu, Instructor, comments: [On this topic from the Commentary on the Words of the Text, most candidates spoke in vague generalities and were unable to elucidate the meaning of the docility of Kun. In this composition the principles are clear and the phrasing is unconstrained, seeking insights beyond ordinary expectations; it is commendable.]
Examiner Wang, Director of Studies (xuezheng), comments: [Receiving from Heaven and acting in accordance with the times is precisely the docility of the Way of Kun. The wording of other candidates mostly had [?], whereas this essay is concise, fitting, and worthy of selection.]
Examiner Lin, Professor (jiaoshou), comments: [It elucidates the meaning of Kun docilely receiving from Heaven, leaving almost no subtle implication unexplored.]

When the Commentary on the Words of the Text (Wenyan) praises the docility of the Way of Kun (the Receptive), it necessarily states the reason why it is docile. For it receives the bestowal of Heaven and acts without violating the seasons—this is why the Way of Kun is docile. How supreme it is that in the Commentary on the Words of the Text the Sage used this to elucidate the meaning of the originating quality (yuan) of Kun! If we examine the Commentary on the Decision (Tuanzhuan) for Kun, it already praised the originating virtue of Kun with the words "thus docilely receiving from Heaven"; coming to this point, the Commentary on the Words of the Text reiterates the meaning of the Commentary on the Decision, as if to say [reading 我謂天 as a garbled transcription of 殆謂夫]: Qian (the Creative) is pure yang, whereas Kun is purely yin without admixture; therefore its virtue is supremely docile and nothing can be added to it—unlike Xun, Li, and Dui, in which yin is interspersed with yang to represent penetration, brightness, and joyousness. Qian is supremely firm, whereas Kun is wholly yielding without impurity; therefore its virtue is utterly docile and nothing can surpass it—unlike Zhen, Kan, and Gen, in which yang is mixed with yin to represent movement, danger, and keeping still. Since the Way of Kun is so docile, by what indeed can we verify it? One can see it by observing how it manifests in function. That Qian…

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
知大始坤則以簡而成之發育萬物與天道同一運
用未嘗先時而自為也陽一以施陰則以兩而承之
資生萬彙與天道同一流行未嘗後時而不為也坤
道之順為何如哉抑又論之乾為父坤為母六十四
卦所由出也故彖皆以元亨利貞為言文言於乾則
始元而終貞於坤則始貞而終元何歟蓋乾以君之
所主在元坤以藏之所主在貞故也聖人翼易之旨
各有攸當學者詳之
窮理盡性以至於命
劉麟
===
同考試官教諭馮　批〔發揮理性命處先後照應一氣呵成無斧鑿痕視彼襞隙腐而補綴者有遲疑矣〕
同考試官教諭余　批〔天下之理人物之性不外陰陽健順而已作者脉此支離可厭惟此融會歸一其深於學者□深於□〕
考試官學正汪　批〔以道立說得旨〕
考試官教授林　批〔寓出聚人作易極功可觀〕
造斯道之極致契斯道之本原惟其能然也蓋易
者載道之器也然則造道之極而契其原者非聖人
punctuated:
知大始，坤則以簡而成之，發育萬物，與天道同一運用，未嘗先時而自為也；陽一以施，陰則以兩而承之，資生萬彙，與天道同一流行，未嘗後時而不為也。坤道之順為何如哉！抑又論之，乾為父，坤為母，六十四卦所由出也，故彖皆以元亨利貞為言。文言於乾則始元而終貞，於坤則始貞而終元，何歟？蓋乾以君之，所主在元；坤以藏之，所主在貞故也。聖人翼《易》之旨，各有攸當，學者詳之。

窮理盡性以至於命
劉麟
同考試官教諭馮　批〔發揮理、性、命處，先後照應，一氣呵成，無斧鑿痕，視彼襞隙腐而補綴者有遲疑矣。〕
同考試官教諭余　批〔天下之理、人物之性，不外陰陽健順而已。作者脉此，支離可厭，惟此融會歸一，其深於學者□深於□。〕
考試官學正汪　批〔以道立說，得旨。〕
考試官教授林　批〔寓出聚人作《易》極功，可觀。〕

造斯道之極致，契斯道之本原，惟其能然也。蓋《易》者，載道之器也。然則造道之極而契其原者，非聖人
translation_en:
…knows the great beginnings, whereas Kun (Earth) brings things to completion through simplicity. In nurturing and developing the myriad things, it operates in unison with the Way of Heaven, never acting on its own ahead of the proper time. Yang bestows as one, whereas Yin receives as two. In giving birth to the myriad categories of beings, it flows in unison with the Way of Heaven, never failing to act behind the proper time. How great indeed is the docility of the Way of Kun!

Furthermore, let us consider this: Qian is the father and Kun is the mother, from which all sixty-four hexagrams originate; therefore, the Judgment (Tuan) for both speaks of "originating, penetrating, advantageous, and correct and firm" (yuan heng li zhen). Why is it that the Commentary on the Words of the Text (Wenyan) for Qian begins with "originating" (yuan) and ends with "correct and firm" (zhen), whereas for Kun it begins with "correct and firm" and ends with "originating"? It is because Qian rules over them, so its governing principle lies in origination; Kun stores them, so its governing principle lies in correctness and firmness. The meanings with which the Sage gave wings to the Changes (Yi) are each fitting in their own way; students should examine them in detail.

"Exhausting principle and fully realizing nature, thereby arriving at destiny."
By Liu Lin 劉麟

Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies Feng 馮 comments: [In expounding upon principle, nature, and destiny, the earlier and later parts correspond to each other, written in a single breath without a trace of artificial chisel-marks. Compared to those who patch together stale and fragmented clichés [?], there is a vast difference [?].]
Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies Yu 余 comments: [The principles of the world and the natures of human beings and things are nothing more than Yin and Yang, vigor and docility. When other writers trace this [?], they fall into tiresome fragmentation; only this essay fuses them into a unified whole. He is profound in learning [?] profound in [?]...]
Examiner and Subprefectural Director of Studies Wang 汪 comments: [By establishing his argument upon the Way, he grasps the essential meaning.]
Examiner and Prefectural Director of Studies Lin 林 comments: [It brings out the ultimate achievement of the Sage [?] in making the Changes; it is well worth reading.]

To reach the ultimate limit of this Way and to tally with the fundamental source of this Way—only because it is able to do so! For the Changes is the vessel that carries the Way. This being so, as for reaching the ultimate of the Way and tallying with its source, if not for the Sage…

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
作易其孰能與於此哉且夫易書未作道在天地易
書既作道具卦爻所謂道者理性命是也彼天下物
理雖有萬殊不越乎陰陽兩端而已易則陰陽闔闢
變化無窮于以冒天下之道極天下之賾如彰往察
來微顯闡幽則天下之理無一而不窮矣彼人物之
性固有不一亦不外乎健順二者而已易則雜物撰
德該括無遺于以通天下之志類萬物之情如體仁
和義服牛乘馬則人物之性無一而不盡矣夫理乃
天命之本然而性乃天命之所賦今既有以窮夫天
===
下之理而又有以盡夫人物之性其於天命之沖漠
無眹者與之胞合而無間天道之於穆不已者與之
渾融而為一矣是則天道具於易易道契於天聖人
作易之極功如此說卦發揮其蘊不既深乎抑觀他
章有曰知幽明之故死生之說亦窮理之事知周萬
物而道濟天下亦盡性之事範圍天地曲成萬物而
至於無方無體亦至命之事也似此亦聖人作易之
極功彼言聖人用易之能事此易所以為性命之源
也歟
punctuated: 作《易》，其孰能與於此哉？且夫《易》書未作，道在天地；《易》書既作，道具卦爻。所謂道者，理、性、命是也。彼天下物理，雖有萬殊，不越乎陰陽兩端而已。《易》則陰陽闔闢，變化無窮，于以冒天下之道，極天下之賾，如彰往察來、微顯闡幽，則天下之理無一而不窮矣。彼人物之性，固有不一，亦不外乎健順二者而已。《易》則雜物撰德，該括無遺，于以通天下之志，類萬物之情，如體仁和義、服牛乘馬，則人物之性無一而不盡矣。夫理乃天命之本然，而性乃天命之所賦。今既有以窮夫天下之理，而又有以盡夫人物之性，其於天命之沖漠無眹者，與之胞合而無間；天道之於穆不已者，與之渾融而為一矣。是則天道具於《易》，《易》道契於天，聖人作《易》之極功如此，《說卦》發揮其蘊，不既深乎？抑觀他章有曰「知幽明之故，死生之說」，亦窮理之事；「知周萬物，而道濟天下」，亦盡性之事；「範圍天地，曲成萬物」，而至於「無方無體」，亦至命之事也。似此亦聖人作《易》之極功，彼言聖人用《易》之能事，此《易》所以為性命之源也歟！
translation_en: … creating the Classic of Changes (Yi), who could participate in this? Moreover, before the book of Changes was created, the Way resided in Heaven and Earth; once the book of Changes was created, the Way was embodied in the hexagrams and lines. What is called the Way is none other than principle (li), nature (xing), and destiny (ming). Although the principles of things in the world have ten thousand differences, they do not go beyond the two extremes of yin and yang. In the Changes, yin and yang close and open in endless transformation, thereby encompassing the Way of the world and probing the subtlest complexities of the world—such as illuminating the past and discerning the future, making the manifest subtle and elucidating the obscure—so that there is not a single principle in the world that is not exhaustively investigated. Although the natures of humans and things are certainly not uniform, they too do not lie outside the two qualities of vigor and顺 (compliance/docility). The Changes brings together diverse things and sets forth their virtues, encompassing everything without omission, thereby communicating the intentions of the world and classifying the conditions of the myriad things—such as embodying benevolence and harmonizing with righteousness, or breaking oxen to the yoke and riding horses—so that there is not a single nature of humans or things that is not fully realized. Now, principle is the inherent reality of the Mandate of Heaven, while nature is what is endowed by the Mandate of Heaven. Since one is now able both to exhaustively investigate the principles of the world and to fully realize the natures of humans and things, one merges seamlessly without gap with the Mandate of Heaven in its tranquil, signless vacuity, and blends into a single whole with the Way of Heaven in its profound and ceaseless operation. Thus, the Way of Heaven is embodied in the Changes, and the Way of the Changes tallies with Heaven. Such is the ultimate achievement of the sages in creating the Changes; in expounding its depths, has not the "Discussion of the Trigrams" (Shuogua) gone deep indeed? Furthermore, if we look at another chapter, where it says "knowing the causes of the obscure and the manifest, and the explanation of death and life," this too is the business of exhaustively investigating principle; "knowledge encompassing the myriad things, and the Way bringing aid to the whole world," this too is the business of fully realizing nature; "delineating Heaven and Earth, and intricately completing the myriad things," all the way to "having no spatial restriction and no fixed form," this too is the business of arriving at destiny. While the present passage speaks of the ultimate achievement of the sages in creating the Changes, that other passage speaks of the accomplished capacity of the sages in using the Changes. Is this not why the Changes is the source of nature and destiny!

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
書
水火金木土穀惟修
羅奎
同考試官教諭沈　批〔此題似易而難作者昧於相制相助之理紛紛錯　令人眩惑此卷發明簡當而一發尤佳必有學之士也〕
考試官學正汪　批〔理明辭暢非苟筆所到〕
考試官教授林　批〔以財成輔相立意超出衆作〕
高　為何承
因天地自然之利盡財成輔相之功盖水火金木土
===
穀此天地自然之利也然非財成以制其過輔相以
補其不及又何以成其利而養乎民哉昔大禹陳養
民之政於帝舜之前以為為政莫要於養民養民莫
先於六府彼天一生水地二生火皆民所急而不可一
日無者矣天三生木地四生金亦民所資而不可一日
缺者矣以至土與穀也何莫非天地所生而切於民
生日用者乎然六者雖出於天地而修之則繫乎人
為是故水克火火克金金克木木克土而生五穀然
不能無過與不及焉其或過而盛也則相制以洩之
punctuated:
《書》

「水火金木土穀惟修」

羅奎
同考試官教諭沈　批：〔此題似易而難，作者昧於相制相助之理，紛紛錯　，令人眩惑。此卷發明簡當，而一發尤佳，必有學之士也。〕
考試官學正汪　批：〔理明辭暢，非苟筆所到。〕
考試官教授林　批：〔以財成輔相立意，超出衆作。〕
高　為何承

因天地自然之利，盡財成輔相之功。盖水、火、金、木、土、穀，此天地自然之利也。然非財成以制其過，輔相以補其不及，又何以成其利而養乎民哉？昔大禹陳養民之政於帝舜之前，以為為政莫要於養民，養民莫先於六府。彼天一生水，地二生火，皆民所急而不可一日無者矣；天三生木，地四生金，亦民所資而不可一日缺者矣；以至土與穀也，何莫非天地所生，而切於民生日用者乎？然六者雖出於天地，而修之則繫乎人為。是故水克火，火克金，金克木，木克土，而生五穀，然不能無過與不及焉。其或過而盛也，則相制以洩之，

Book of Documents (Shu)

"Water, fire, metal, wood, earth, and grain must be regulated."

Luo Kui 羅奎
Associate Examiner and Instructor Shen 沈 comments: [This topic seems easy yet is difficult. Those who write on it are often blind to the principles of mutual restraint and mutual assistance, producing a confused muddle [?] that leaves the reader dazzled and perplexed. This paper's exposition is concise and apt, and its opening development is especially fine; he must be a scholar of genuine learning.]
Examiner and Director of Studies Wang 汪 comments: [The reasoning is clear and the diction fluent; this is not something achieved by a careless brush.]
Examiner and Instructor Lin 林 comments: [Framing the central idea around "regulating and completing" and "assisting and furthering," it surpasses all the other compositions.]
Gao 高 [?] He Cheng 何承 [?]

By building upon the natural benefits of Heaven and Earth, one fulfills the work of regulating and completing, assisting and furthering. Now water, fire, metal, wood, earth, and grain—these are the natural benefits of Heaven and Earth. Yet without regulating and completing them to restrain their excesses, and assisting and furthering them to supplement their deficiencies, how could one bring their benefits to completion and nourish the people? In antiquity, the Great Yu set forth the governance of nourishing the people before Emperor Shun, holding that in governance nothing is more essential than nourishing the people, and in nourishing the people nothing takes precedence over the Six Treasuries. That Heaven as One generates water, and Earth as Two generates fire—both are things the people urgently need and cannot be without for a single day. That Heaven as Three generates wood, and Earth as Four generates metal—these too are things the people rely upon and cannot lack for a single day. And as for earth and grain, which of them is not generated by Heaven and Earth and vital to the daily necessities of the people's livelihood? Yet although these six issue from Heaven and Earth, their regulation depends upon human effort. Therefore, water overcomes fire, fire overcomes metal, metal overcomes wood, and wood overcomes earth, while earth generates the five grains; yet among them there cannot but be excesses and deficiencies. When one of them is excessive and overly flourishing, they mutually restrain one another to drain it, …

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
使之不至於大過所謂財成天地之道是已其或不
及而衰也則相助以補之使之不至於不及所謂輔
相天地之宜是已如此則五行各順其理五穀各遂
其生而六府孔修矣養民之政莫有要於此者抑大
禹此言所以推明伯益儆戒無虞之旨也故此既言
水火金木土穀惟修下文繼言正德利用厚生惟和
九功惟敘九敘惟歌是則無虞之時矣而又戒之董
之勸之而俾勿壞是即儆戒之意也虞廷大臣同心
相與告君者如此其所以致無爲之治也宜哉
===
前王教臣之小子欲其知謹酒之節教民之小子欲
考試官教授林　批〔能道先酒者義旨也熟於是經者〕
考試官學正汪　批〔得疏通知遠之旨〕
〔故録之以範後學〕
同考試官教諭沈　批〔長題不難於歸敘而難於收束此作得之〕

文王誥教小子有正有事無彝酒越庶國飲惟
祀德將無醉惟曰我民迪小子惟土物愛厥
心臧聰聽祖考之彝訓越小大德小子惟一
punctuated:
使之不至於大過，所謂「財成天地之道」是已；其或不及而衰也，則相助以補之，使之不至於不及，所謂「輔相天地之宜」是已。如此，則五行各順其理，五穀各遂其生，而六府孔修矣，養民之政莫有要於此者。抑大禹此言，所以推明伯益「儆戒無虞」之旨也。故此既言「水、火、金、木、土、穀，惟修」，下文繼言「正德、利用、厚生，惟和。九功惟敘，九敘惟歌」，是則無虞之時矣，而又「戒之，董之，勸之，而俾勿壞」，是即儆戒之意也。虞廷大臣同心相與告君者如此，其所以致無爲之治也，宜哉！

何喬壽
前王教臣之小子，欲其知謹酒之節；教民之小子，欲…
translation_en:
…so as not to let them reach great excess—this is what is meant by "regulating and completing the Way of Heaven and Earth." And when they are perhaps deficient and weak, they assist one another to supplement them, so as not to let them fall into deficiency—this is what is meant by "aiding and assisting the suitability of Heaven and Earth." In this manner, the Five Phases each follow their principles, the Five Grains each fulfill their growth, and the Six Treasuries are greatly ordered. In the governance of nourishing the people, nothing is more essential than this. Moreover, these words of Great Yu serve to elucidate the meaning of Boyi's admonition to "be cautious and vigilant when there is no cause for anxiety." Therefore, having here said "Water, Fire, Metal, Wood, Earth, and Grain are well ordered," the text below continues by saying "Rectifying virtue,benefiting tools, and enriching life are harmonized; the nine services are ordered, and the nine orderings are sung." That is indeed a time free of anxiety! Yet he further says to "caution them with beauty, supervise them with majesty, encourage them with the nine songs, so that they be not spoiled"—this is precisely the meaning of caution and vigilance. That the great ministers of the court of Yu were of one mind in advising their sovereign like this—is it any wonder that it brought about governance through non-action!

Examiner, Subprefectural Director of Studies Wang, comments: [It grasps the principle of being penetrative,comprehending, and far-reaching (the teaching of the Book of Documents); therefore we record it to serve as a model for later students.]
Associate Examiner, District Director of Studies Shen, comments: [In a long topic, the difficulty lies not in organizing the narrative, but in drawing it to a close; this composition has achieved it.]
