title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
北遵謹酒之訓蓋縱酒喪德人不可以不謹也前王
於臣民之小子得不有以教之而使知所謹哉昔武
王封康叔於衛而告之若曰我穆考文王肇國西土
以庶邦庶士之小子血氣未定尤易縱酒故尊誥教
之爾小子將有官守者也當豫養其良心豈可彝於酒
而至喪德乎將有職業者也當先存其德性豈可常
於酒而至亂性乎然及於庶國之飲也惟於克羞饋
祀之時亦必以德將之無至於醉也惟於以往蒸嘗
之日亦必以禮制之弗及於亂也然在官小子既教
===
以謹酒之節矣在民小子又可不以謹酒之訓而戒
之乎謂夫我民之祖考亦常訓道其子孫勤務穡惟
土物之是愛服田畝無外物之是慕則心之所守者
正而善日生志之所向者專而慾日窒夫爾之祖考
垂訓者如此爾為子孫者要當聰聽乃祖之彝訓無
以嗜酒為小德小德大德視之惟一可也明聽乃考
之常教勿以戒酒為小節小節大節視之無二可也
吁文王誥毖之意如此武王舉以告康叔豈非欲其
明大命於妹邦也歟抑考酒誥一篇武王毖酒作也
punctuated: 北遵謹酒之訓。蓋縱酒喪德，人不可以不謹也。前王於臣民之小子，得不有以教之而使知所謹哉？昔武王封康叔於衛，而告之若曰：我穆考文王，肇國西土，以庶邦庶士之小子血氣未定，尤易縱酒，故尊誥教之：爾小子將有官守者也，當豫養其良心，豈可彝於酒而至喪德乎？將有職業者也，當先存其德性，豈可常於酒而至亂性乎？然及於庶國之飲也，惟於克羞饋祀之時，亦必以德將之，無至於醉也；惟於以往蒸嘗之日，亦必以禮制之，弗及於亂也。然在官小子，既教以謹酒之節矣；在民小子，又可不以謹酒之訓而戒之乎？謂夫我民之祖考，亦常訓道其子孫，勤務穡，惟土物之是愛；服田畝，無外物之是慕。則心之所守者正，而善日生；志之所向者專，而慾日窒。夫爾之祖考垂訓者如此，爾為子孫者，要當聰聽乃祖之彝訓，無以嗜酒為小德，小德大德視之惟一可也；明聽乃考之常教，勿以戒酒為小節，小節大節視之無二可也。吁！文王誥毖之意如此，武王舉以告康叔，豈非欲其明大命於妹邦也歟？抑考《酒誥》一篇，武王毖酒作也。
translation_en:
[皆?] follow the instruction of being cautious with wine. Indeed, indulging in wine destroys virtue, so people cannot fail to be cautious. How could the former king not have something with which to instruct the young among his officials and common people so as to make them know where to exercise caution?

In the past, when King Wu enfeoffed Kangshu in Wei, he spoke to him to this effect: "My reverent late father, King Wen, founded the state in the western lands. Because the young among the many officials of the various states had not yet settled in their blood and vital energy and were especially prone to indulge in wine, he specially admonished and instructed them: 'You young ones who will hold official posts ought to cultivate your innate goodness beforehand—how could you habitually indulge in wine and come to destroy your virtue? You who will have official duties ought first to preserve your moral nature—how could you constantly take to wine and come to disorder your nature?' Yet when it came to drinking in the various states, only at the time of presenting food offerings and sacrifices was it permitted, and even then one had to conduct oneself with virtue so as not to reach drunkenness; only on the days of going to perform the winter and autumn sacrifices was it permitted, and even then one had to regulate oneself with ritual propriety so as not to reach disorder.

"However, having already taught the young who are in office the restraint of being cautious with wine, how could he not also warn the young among the common people with the instruction of being cautious with wine? He said that the ancestors and late fathers of our people also constantly instructed and guided their descendants to work diligently at harvesting and cherish only the products of the soil, and to labor in the fields without coveting external things. Then what the mind holds fast to is upright, and goodness grows daily; what the will directs itself toward is focused, and desires are daily blocked. Now since the instructions handed down by your ancestors and late fathers are like this, you who are their descendants must listen attentively to the constant instructions of your ancestors: do not regard a fondness for wine as a minor matter of virtue, for minor virtues and great virtues should be viewed as one; listen clearly to the regular teachings of your late fathers: do not regard abstaining from wine as a minor matter of conduct, for minor conduct and great conduct should be viewed without duality."

Alas! Such was the intent of King Wen's admonitions and cautions, and when King Wu cited them to tell Kangshu, was it not because he wished him to make bright the great mandate in the land of Mei? Moreover, if we examine the "Announcement About Drunkenness" (Jiu gao) as a whole, King Wu composed it as a caution against wine…

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
然此述文王之教曰飲惟祀下文申已誥是曰父母
慶則可飲酒充羞耇則可飲酒羞饋祀則可飲酒本
欲其絕其飲今乃反開其端者不禁之禁也聖人之
教不迫而民從者此也旨哉
詩
蠶月條桑取彼斧斨以伐遠揚猗彼女桑七月
鳴鵙八月載績載玄載黃我朱孔陽為公子
裳四月秀葽五月鳴蜩八月其穫十月隕蘀
一之日于貉取彼狐狸為公子裘
胡泰
===
同考試官教諭張　批此詩本言男服事乎外女服事乎內以
〔終首章無衣無褐之意場中作者多昧乎此間有知者文〕
同考試官教諭陳　批場中詩卷千餘作此題者多不得旨求
〔不足以發之詞理俱到僅見此篇是用錄出〕
同考試官教諭鄭　批不泛不畧而民忠愛之意宛然可見
〔其文理純正者無踰此篇〕
考試官學正汪　批辭理俱優佳作也
考試官教授林　批詞氣和平如此作方得詩人意
punctuated:
然此述文王之教曰「飲惟祀」，下文申已誥，是曰父母慶則可飲酒，充羞耇則可飲酒，羞饋祀則可飲酒。本欲其絕其飲，今乃反開其端者，不禁之禁也。聖人之教不迫而民從者，此也。旨哉！

詩
「蠶月條桑，取彼斧斨，以伐遠揚，猗彼女桑。七月鳴鵙，八月載績。載玄載黃，我朱孔陽，為公子裳。四月秀葽，五月鳴蜩。八月其穫，十月隕蘀。一之日于貉，取彼狐狸，為公子裘。」
胡泰
同考試官教諭張　批：此詩本言男服事乎外，女服事乎內，以〔終首章「無衣無褐」之意。場中作者多昧乎此，間有知者，文〕
同考試官教諭陳　批：場中《詩》卷千餘，作此題者多不得旨，求〔不足以發之。詞理俱到，僅見此篇，是用錄出。〕
同考試官教諭鄭　批：不泛不畧，而民忠愛之意宛然可見。〔其文理純正者，無踰此篇。〕
考試官學正汪　批：辭理俱優，佳作也。
考試官教授林　批：詞氣和平，如此作方得詩人意。
translation_en:
Yet here, in recounting the teaching of King Wen, it says, "Drink only at sacrifices," whereas below, in setting forth his own pronouncement, he says that when celebrating the joy of one's parents one may drink wine, when presenting delicacies to the aged one may drink wine, and when offering food in sacrifice one may drink wine. Fundamentally he wished them to cease their drinking, yet now he instead opens up occasions for it—this is a prohibition that operates without strictly prohibiting. That the teaching of the sages is not coercive and yet the people follow it lies precisely in this. Profound indeed!

Classic of Poetry (Shijing)
"In the silkworm month they strip the mulberry branches, taking those axes and hatchets to lop the far-reaching and high-rising boughs, pulling down the tender mulberry leaves. In the seventh month the shrike cries; in the eighth month they begin to twist hemp. They dye it dark and yellow; our vermilion is very bright, to make lower garments for the young lords. In the fourth month the milkwort goes to seed; in the fifth month the cicada cries. In the eighth month is the harvest; in the tenth month falls the foliage. In the days of the first month they go after raccoon-dogs, taking those foxes and wildcats to make furs for the young lords."
By Hu Tai 胡泰
Associate Examiner, County Director of Studies (jiaoyu) Zhang comments: This ode fundamentally speaks of men performing their duties without and women performing their duties within, so as to [carry through the meaning of "without robes, without coarse cloth" in the first stanza. Most writers in the examination hall were blind to this; among the few who understood it, their writing was inadequate to bring it out. Only in this essay are both expression and reasoning fully achieved, and therefore we have selected it for recording.] [Note: In the woodblock print, the second line of small double-line commentary for Zhang's and Chen's comments was accidentally transposed between the two columns.]
Associate Examiner, County Director of Studies Chen comments: Among over a thousand Classic of Poetry papers in the examination hall, most of those writing on this topic missed the main import; seeking [one whose literary style and reasoning are pure and upright, none surpasses this essay.]
Associate Examiner, County Director of Studies Zheng comments: Neither diffuse nor sketchy, and the people's spirit of loyalty and affection is vividly manifest.
Examiner, Department Director of Studies (xuezheng) Wang comments: Superior in both diction and reasoning; an excellent piece.
Examiner, Prefectural Director of Studies (jiaoshou) Lin comments: Its tone and expression are harmonious and balanced; only by writing like this does one grasp the intent of the poet.

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
醫時而服事乎內既奉上以禦寒感時而服事乎外
亦奉上以禦寒蓋蠶績狩獵皆所以為禦寒計也邠
民預為之而皆奉乎上其忠愛無已之意何如哉昔
周公陳后稷公劉風化之所由使瞽矇朝夕諷誦以
教成王謂夫邠人以卒歲不可以無衣不可以無
褐故當治蠶之月采桑以供蠶食桑之大者可以條
取也則取彼斧斨以伐遠揚焉桑之小者不可條取
也則取其葉而猗彼女桑焉蠶事於此乎備矣至於七
月鳴鵙之後八月麻熟可績之時則績其麻以為布
===
績事於此乎成矣凡此蠶績之所成皆染之或玄其
色或黃其色而其朱者尤為鮮明其服事乎內也如
此豈私以自奉哉皆以供上而為公子之裳庶足以
為禦寒之資又何無衣之足慮耶邠民愛上之心猶
未已也時乎四月葽感陰氣而秀時乎五月蜩感陰
氣而鳴則陽極陰生之時矣八月而禾早可穫十月
而草木隕落則大寒將至之候矣雖蠶桑無所不備
而禦寒猶恐不足故於一陽之月悉率左右而為于
貉之舉從其羣醜以取狐狸之皮其服事乎外也如
punctuated:
醫時而服事乎內，既奉上以禦寒；感時而服事乎外，亦奉上以禦寒。蓋蠶績狩獵，皆所以為禦寒計也。邠民預為之，而皆奉乎上，其忠愛無已之意何如哉！

昔周公陳后稷、公劉風化之所由，使瞽矇朝夕諷誦以教成王，謂夫邠人以卒歲不可以無衣，不可以無褐。故當治蠶之月，采桑以供蠶食。桑之大者可以條取也，則取彼斧斨，以伐遠揚焉；桑之小者不可條取也，則取其葉，而猗彼女桑焉，蠶事於此乎備矣。至於七月鳴鵙之後，八月麻熟可績之時，則績其麻以為布，績事於此乎成矣。凡此蠶績之所成，皆染之，或玄其色，或黃其色，而其朱者尤為鮮明。其服事乎內也如此，豈私以自奉哉？皆以供上而為公子之裳，庶足以為禦寒之資，又何無衣之足慮耶？

邠民愛上之心猶未已也。時乎四月，葽感陰氣而秀；時乎五月，蜩感陰氣而鳴，則陽極陰生之時矣。八月而禾早可穫，十月而草木隕落，則大寒將至之候矣。雖蠶桑無所不備，而禦寒猶恐不足，故於一陽之月，悉率左右而為于貉之舉，從其羣醜以取狐狸之皮。其服事乎外也如
translation_en:
Responding to [醫, typo for 感?] the season, they attend to their duties indoors, already presenting offerings to their superiors to ward off the cold; moved by the season, they attend to their duties outdoors, likewise presenting offerings to their superiors to ward off the cold. Indeed, sericulture, spinning, and hunting are all means of preparing against the cold. The people of Bin make these preparations in advance and present them all to their superiors—how boundless is their loyalty and affection!

In antiquity, the Duke of Zhou set forth the origins of the moral transformation wrought by Houji and Duke Liu, having the blind musicians recite them morning and evening to instruct King Cheng. He said that to finish out the year, the people of Bin could not be without fine clothes and could not be without coarse cloth. Therefore, in the month for tending silkworms, they gather mulberry leaves to feed them. Where the mulberry trees are large enough that branches may be lopped off, they take axes and hatchets to chop the far-reaching and high-rising boughs; where the mulberry trees are too small for their branches to be lopped, they pluck the leaves and pull down the tender mulberry trees. With this, the work of sericulture is complete. Then, after the shrike cries in the seventh month, when the hemp is ripe for spinning in the eighth month, they spin the hemp to make cloth. With this, the work of spinning is accomplished. All these products of sericulture and spinning are dyed—some dark in color, some yellow in color, while the vermilion is especially bright. Such is their attention to duties indoors; how could it be for their own private use? All of it is offered to their superiors to make lower garments for the young lords, which may suffice as provisions against the cold—what need is there to worry about having no clothes?

Yet the affection of the people of Bin for their superiors does not stop even here. When it is the fourth month, the milkwort responds to the yin vital force and goes to seed; when it is the fifth month, the cicada responds to the yin vital force and chirps—for this is the time when yang reaches its peak and yin is born. In the eighth month, the early grain is ready for harvest, and in the tenth month, grasses and trees shed their leaves—for these are the signs that the great cold is about to arrive. Although nothing is lacking in their sericulture and mulberry tending, they still fear that protection against the cold may be insufficient. Therefore, in the month of the first return of yang, they lead out all their attendants to go hunting for raccoon-dogs, following the great crowds to take the pelts of foxes and wildcats. Such is their attention to duties outdoors…

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
此豈私以自用哉亦以奉上而為公子之裘庶足以
周禦寒之具又何無褐之足慮耶吁蠶績之所成狩
獵之所獲皆不自愛以奉其上邠民何如其知義哉
雖然自食其力而急乎上者人情之常邠人則汲汲
於愛上何耶蓋自后稷教稼穡公劉篤民事其至誠
惻怛之意施於民者非一日矣是以國人感之至愛
之深而報之惟恐其或後也所謂上下之情交相忠
愛者以此故吾每誦七月之詩未嘗不歎先公風化
之遠云
===
昔有成湯自彼氐羌莫敢不來享莫敢不來王
曰商是常天命多辟設都于禹之績歲事來
辟勿予禍適稼穡匪解天命降監下民有嚴
不僭不濫不敢怠遑命于下國封建厥福
鄔旦
同考試官教諭張　批〔高宗平荊楚服諸侯本於不僭不濫不敢怠遑所致場中作者殊戾本旨是篇立意高而辭不泛〕
宜冠本經
同考試官教諭陳　批〔得詩人美盛德告成功之旨〕
punctuated:
此，豈私以自用哉？亦以奉上而為公子之裘，庶足以周禦寒之具，又何無褐之足慮耶？吁！蠶績之所成、狩獵之所獲，皆不自愛以奉其上，邠民何如其知義哉！雖然，自食其力而急乎上者，人情之常；邠人則汲汲於愛上，何耶？蓋自后稷教稼穡，公劉篤民事，其至誠惻怛之意施於民者，非一日矣。是以國人感之至、愛之深，而報之惟恐其或後也。所謂上下之情交相忠愛者以此。故吾每誦《七月》之詩，未嘗不歎先公風化之遠云。
「昔有成湯，自彼氐羌，莫敢不來享，莫敢不來王，曰商是常。天命多辟，設都于禹之績。歲事來辟，勿予禍適，稼穡匪解。天命降監，下民有嚴，不僭不濫，不敢怠遑，命于下國，封建厥福。」
鄔旦
同考試官教諭張　批：〔高宗平荊楚、服諸侯，本於不僭不濫、不敢怠遑所致。場中作者殊戾本旨，是篇立意高而辭不泛，〕宜冠本經。
同考試官教諭陳　批：〔得詩人美盛德、告成功之旨。〕
translation_en:
…such as this; how could they keep them privately for their own use? Rather, they presented them to their superiors to make fur garments for the young lords, hoping thereby to make complete the means of keeping out the cold—what need was there to worry about having no coarse cloth? Ah! In both what they produced from sericulture and spinning and what they took in the hunt, they did not begrudge their own goods in serving their superiors—how well the people of Bin understood righteousness! Even so, while living off one's own labor and attending urgently to one's superiors is normal human feeling, why were the people of Bin so eagerly devoted to loving their superiors? It is because ever since Hou Ji taught sowing and reaping and Duke Liu devoted himself earnestly to the people's affairs, their utmost sincerity and compassionate care had been bestowed upon the people for more than a single day. Therefore, the people of the state were moved to the utmost and loved them deeply, fearing only that they might be tardy in repaying them. What is meant by the feelings of superior and inferior mutually uniting in loyalty and affection is precisely this. Thus, whenever I recite the ode "Seventh Month" (Qiyue), I never fail to sigh in admiration at how far-reaching was the transformative influence of the former dukes.

"Of old there was Tang the Accomplished; from those Di and Qiang, none dared not come to present offerings, none dared not come to acknowledge him as king, saying: 'Shang is our constant rule.' Heaven charged the many lords to establish their capitals amidst the achievements of Yu. For the annual affairs they came before the sovereign: 'Do not visit us with misfortune or rebuke; in sowing and reaping we have not been remiss.' Heaven's charge descends to inspect, and the people below are reverent; neither erring in reward nor excessive in punishment, not daring to be indolent or at ease—thus was he charged over the states below, grandly establishing his blessings."

Wu Dan

Associate Examiner Instructor Zhang comments: 〔That Gaozong pacified Jing-Chu and brought the feudal lords to submission was rooted in his neither erring in reward nor being excessive in punishment, and not daring to be indolent or at ease. Other writers in the examination hall went quite contrary to this fundamental purport; this essay sets its conception high and its phrasing is not diffuse.〕 It deserves to top the candidates in this Classic.

Associate Examiner Instructor Chen comments: 〔It grasps the poet's purport in praising illustrious virtue and announcing successful accomplishment.〕

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭鄭　批〔此說出高宗中興氣象宛然可見本房得〕〔此誠宜爲是者者歟〕
考試官學正汪　批〔鋪叙嚴整可取〕
考試官教授林　批〔頌義宜簡古此作得之〕
詩人叙賢王中興之功必原其所以致中興之道夫
功莫大乎平荆楚而服諸侯也然非賢王敬天人而
謹刑賞亦何以致此哉此祀高宗之樂謂夫盤庚沒
而殷道衰楚人叛之久矣我高宗旣克之則告之曰
昔我祖成湯之世自彼氐羌之遠莫敢不來享而盡
===
獻納之誠莫敢不來王而盡世見之禮而曰此商之
常禮也况女荆楚曷敢不至哉荆楚旣平則諸侯畏
服由是友邦冢君天命建都于禹所治之地者皆以
歲事而來辟盖以祈王之不譴而曰我之稼穡不敢
怠也烈文辟公天命建國於禹所奠之區者皆以歲
事而來朝盖以冀王之不責而曰我之稼穡不敢解
也庶可以免咎矣我高宗中興之功如此夫豈無所
自耶盖以天命降監不在乎他皆在民之視聽則下
民亦有嚴矣惟高宗賞所當賞不僭也而此心之
punctuated:
同考試官教諭鄭　批〔此說出高宗中興氣象，宛然可見。本房得〕〔此，誠宜爲是者者歟？〕
考試官學正汪　批〔鋪叙嚴整，可取。〕
考試官教授林　批〔頌義宜簡古，此作得之。〕

詩人叙賢王中興之功，必原其所以致中興之道。夫功莫大乎平荆楚而服諸侯也；然非賢王敬天人而謹刑賞，亦何以致此哉？此祀高宗之樂，謂夫盤庚沒而殷道衰，楚人叛之久矣，我高宗旣克之，則告之曰：「昔我祖成湯之世，自彼氐羌之遠，莫敢不來享而盡獻納之誠，莫敢不來王而盡世見之禮，而曰：『此商之常禮也。』况女荆楚，曷敢不至哉？」荆楚旣平，則諸侯畏服。由是友邦冢君，天命建都于禹所治之地者，皆以歲事而來辟，盖以祈王之不譴，而曰：「我之稼穡不敢怠也；」烈文辟公，天命建國於禹所奠之區者，皆以歲事而來朝，盖以冀王之不責，而曰：「我之稼穡不敢解也，」庶可以免咎矣。我高宗中興之功如此，夫豈無所自耶？盖以天命降監，不在乎他，皆在民之視聽，則下民亦有嚴矣。惟高宗賞所當賞，不僭也，而此心之
translation_en:
Associate Examiner County Instructor Zheng comments: "This brings out the spirit of Gaozong's dynastic revival so that it is vividly visible. Having obtained this in my examination ward, is it not truly fitting that it be selected as the foremost [?]?"
Examiner Subprefectural Instructor Wang comments: "The exposition is rigorous and well-ordered; it is worthy of selection."
Examiner Prefectural Instructor Lin comments: "An essay on the Sacrificial Odes should be concise and archaic in style; this composition achieves that."

When the poet recounts the meritorious achievement of the worthy king's dynastic revival, he necessarily traces the Way by which that revival was brought about. Now, no achievement is greater than pacifying Jing-Chu and bringing the feudal lords to submission; yet had the worthy king not revered Heaven and man and been prudent with punishments and rewards, how could he have brought this about? This musical ode for the sacrifice to Gaozong states that after Pan Geng died and the Way of Yin declined, the people of Chu had long rebelled against it. Once our Gaozong conquered them, he admonished them, saying: "In the past, in the age of our ancestor Cheng Tang, even from as far away as the Di and Qiang tribes, none dared not come to present offerings and exhaust their sincerity in paying tribute, and none dared not come to acknowledge him as king and fulfill the ritual of generational audience, saying: 'This is the constant rule of Shang.' How much less, then, could you of Jing-Chu dare not come?" Once Jing-Chu was pacified, the feudal lords submitted in awe. Thereupon, the rulers of allied states, whom Heaven had mandated to establish their capitals in the lands brought to order by Yu, all came before the sovereign for the annual accounting of affairs, praying that the king would not reprimand them, saying: "We have not dared to be negligent in our husbandry." The illustrious feudal lords, whom Heaven had mandated to establish their states in the regions settled by Yu, all came to court for the annual accounting of affairs, hoping that the king would not reprove them, saying: "We have not dared to be remiss in our husbandry," so that they might thereby escape blame. Such was the achievement of our Gaozong's dynastic revival—yet how could it have been without a source? For when the Mandate of Heaven looks down from on high, it rests nowhere else than in the seeing and hearing of the people; thus the common people below are also to be held in awe. Only because Gaozong rewarded those who ought to be rewarded, without excess, while in the [exercise of] this mind…

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
行不敢怠刑所當刑刑不濫也而此心之存不敢慢
則所以敬天而畏民者至矣是以皇天眷命奄有四
海福於此乎大建保佑命之奄有九有福於此乎永
錫此高宗所以受命而中興也然則荊楚平而諸侯
服豈偶然哉嗟夫莫爲於前雖美弗彰莫爲於後雖
盛弗傳有商之興非成湯莫能成創造之功非高宗
莫能致中興之盛此高宗所以無愧爲湯之孫而百
世不遷之廟所由立殷武之樂所由作也登歌之際
美盛德而告成功夫豈不宜
===
春秋
王人子突救衛〔莊公六年〕　季子來歸〔閔公元年〕　楚
屈完來盟于師〔僖公四年〕　楚子使椒來聘〔文公九年〕
秦伯使術來聘〔文公十二年〕　吳子使札來聘〔襄公二〕
十九年
同考試官教諭謝　批〔春秋之法内人之賢否事之得失而筆削〕
有〔自然之権度此作揣摩作者之意稱之以爵品藻人物之〕
王任
準的
punctuated:
行不敢怠；刑所當刑，刑不濫也，而此心之存不敢慢，則所以敬天而畏民者至矣。是以皇天眷命，奄有四海，福於此乎大建；保佑命之，奄有九有，福於此乎永錫。此高宗所以受命而中興也。然則荊楚平而諸侯服，豈偶然哉？嗟夫！莫爲於前，雖美弗彰；莫爲於後，雖盛弗傳。有商之興，非成湯莫能成創造之功，非高宗莫能致中興之盛。此高宗所以無愧爲湯之孫，而百世不遷之廟所由立，《殷武》之樂所由作也。登歌之際，美盛德而告成功，夫豈不宜？

《春秋》
「王人子突救衛」〔莊公六年〕、「季子來歸」〔閔公元年〕、「楚屈完來盟于師」〔僖公四年〕、「楚子使椒來聘」〔文公九年〕、「秦伯使術來聘」〔文公十二年〕、「吳子使札來聘」〔襄公二〕十九年。
王任
同考試官教諭謝批：〔《春秋》之法，内人之賢否、事之得失，而筆削〕有〔自然之権度。此作揣摩作者之意，稱之以爵，品藻人物之〕準的。
translation_en:
…in action he did not dare to be remiss; in punishing those who ought to be punished, punishments were not excessive, and in preserving this mind he did not dare to be negligent. Thus, the way in which he revered Heaven and stood in awe of the people was utmost. Therefore, August Heaven favored him with its mandate to encompass the Four Seas, and blessings were thereby grandly established; it protected, helped, and charged him to encompass the Nine Regions, and blessings were thereby eternally bestowed. This was how Gaozong received the Mandate and achieved a dynastic revival. This being so, when Jing-Chu was pacified and the feudal lords submitted, how could it have been by chance? Alas! If nothing is done beforehand, though admirable it will not be manifest; if nothing is done afterward, though flourishing it will not be transmitted. In the rise of the Shang, none but Cheng Tang could have accomplished the merit of founding the dynasty, and none but Gaozong could have brought about the flourishing of its revival. This is why Gaozong was not ashamed to be the descendant of Tang, why his temple that is not removed for a hundred generations came to be established, and why the music of the "Yinwu" ("Martial Yin") came to be composed. On the occasion of ascending to sing, to praise his abundant virtue and announce his accomplished work—how could this not be fitting?

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu)
"The King's man Zitu went to the relief of Wei" [6th year of Duke Zhuang]; "Jizi came and returned" [1st year of Duke Min]; "Qu Wan of Chu came to make a covenant with the army" [4th year of Duke Xi]; "The Viscount of Chu sent Jiao to come on a mission of friendly inquiries" [9th year of Duke Wen]; "The Earl of Qin sent Shu to come on a mission of friendly inquiries" [12th year of Duke Wen]; "The Viscount of Wu sent Zha to come on a mission of friendly inquiries" [29th year of Duke Xiang].
Wang Ren
Comment by Associate Examiner County Director of Studies Xie: [In the method of the Spring and Autumn Annals, according to [?] the worthiness or unworthiness of men and the success or failure of affairs, its writing and deleting] possess [a natural standard of weighing and measuring. This composition fathoms the intent of the author, weighing them by rank [?] as a] standard [for appraising historical figures].

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
考試官學正汪　批以中字立論高出人一頭地佳作也
考試官教授林　批此作得書法可取
春秋待人之例不一而責賢之意甚備夫責乎賢者
制行得其中也季札賢而過乎中春秋不進之以特
筆而待之以常例責備之意何如哉何則中者帝王
相傳之心法也夫子假魯史以寓王法舍中何以那
是故王朝下士以人通諸侯公子以名著例也而子
突能申王命以赴黔牟之急季友復歸宗國以爲公
室之輔賢可知矣進而書字書子非特筆乎桓莊之
===
春秋荊楚無大夫亦例也而屈完如師能服齊桓之
義繼好以徼先君之福賢可想矣進而書族又非特
筆乎馴致魯文之世楚穆遣椒而來聘秦康命術以
脩禮意非不誠而椒僅以名書事非不善而術但以
名錄豈以楚僭于周秦介乎狄故略之歟若季札讓
國天下賢之曰突曰完未克升其堂與若椒若術詎
得窺其藩籬今焉銜命而來至于曲阜見禮而知政
聞樂而知德中國之賢者未能或之先也聖人不以
字不以氏不以公子特書之而略以名紀則是例之
punctuated:
考試官學正汪批：以「中」字立論，高出人一頭地，佳作也。
考試官教授林批：此作得書法，可取。
《春秋》待人之例不一，而責賢之意甚備。夫責乎賢者，制行得其中也。季札賢而過乎中，《春秋》不進之以特筆，而待之以常例，責備之意何如哉！何則？中者，帝王相傳之心法也。夫子假魯史以寓王法，舍中何以那？是故王朝下士以「人」通，諸侯公子以「名」著，例也。而子突能申王命以赴黔牟之急，季友復歸宗國以爲公室之輔，賢可知矣，進而書字、書子，非特筆乎？桓、莊之《春秋》，荊楚無大夫，亦例也。而屈完如師，能服齊桓之義，繼好以徼先君之福，賢可想矣，進而書族，又非特筆乎？馴致魯文之世，楚穆遣椒而來聘，秦康命術以脩禮，意非不誠而椒僅以名書，事非不善而術但以名錄，豈以楚僭于周、秦介乎狄，故略之歟？若季札讓國，天下賢之，曰突、曰完，未克升其堂與；若椒、若術，詎得窺其藩籬？今焉銜命而來，至于曲阜，見禮而知政，聞樂而知德，中國之賢者未能或之先也。聖人不以字、不以氏、不以公子特書之，而略以名紀，則是例之
translation_en:
Examiner and Subprefectural Instructor (xuezheng) Wang comments: By grounding its argument in the word "equilibrium" (zhong 中), this essay stands a head above others; it is a fine work.
Examiner and Prefectural Instructor (jiaoshou) Lin comments: This essay grasps the principles of historiographical recording (shufa) and is worthy of selection.
The precedents by which the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) treats individuals are not uniform, yet its intent in demanding perfection of the worthy is most thorough. What is demanded of the worthy is that in regulating their conduct they attain the mean (zhong). Ji Zha 季札 was worthy, yet he went beyond the mean; that the Spring and Autumn Annals does not promote him with a special entry, but treats him according to ordinary precedent—how profound is its intent in demanding perfection of him! Why is this so? The mean is the method of the mind transmitted from one sovereign to another. When the Master borrowed the history of Lu 魯 to lodge the kingly law, if he set aside the mean, wherewith could he proceed? Therefore, that lower servicemen of the royal court are referred to generically as "man" (ren 人) and sons of feudal lords are recorded by their personal names (ming 名) is the standard precedent. Yet Zi Tu 子突 was able to uphold the royal command to hasten to the rescue of Qianmou 黔牟 in his distress, and Ji You 季友 returned to his ancestral state to serve as a support to the ducal house; their worthiness can thus be known. Promoting them by recording their style name (zi 字) or the honorific "Master" (zi 子)—is this not a special entry? In the Spring and Autumn Annals of the reigns of Dukes Huan 桓 and Zhuang 莊, that Jing-Chu 荊楚 had no grand masters recorded is also the standard precedent. Yet when Qu Wan 屈完 went to the army, he was able to submit to the righteousness of Duke Huan of Qi 齊桓, renewing friendly relations to seek the blessings of the former rulers; his worthiness can thus be imagined. Promoting him by recording his clan name (zu 族)—is this not also a special entry? Coming down gradually to the age of Duke Wen of Lu 魯文, King Mu of Chu 楚穆 sent Jiao 椒 to come on a mission of friendly inquiry, and Duke Kang of Qin 秦康 commanded Shu 術 to cultivate ritual courtesy. Their intentions were not insincere, yet Jiao was written down merely by his personal name; their acts were not unvirtuous, yet Shu was recorded only by his personal name. Was this not because Chu usurped royal titles against Zhou 周 and Qin was hemmed in among the Di 狄 peoples, and therefore the text treated them summarily? As for Ji Zha yielding the state, the whole world deemed him worthy. The likes of Tu and Wan could not even ascend to his hall [?]; how could the likes of Jiao and Shu catch so much as a glimpse inside his hedge? Now he came bearing a command and arrived at Qufu 曲阜; upon observing the rites he understood the governance, and upon hearing the music he understood the virtue—none of the worthies of the Central States could surpass him. Yet the Sage did not specially record him by his style name, his lineage name, or as a ducal son, but summarily registered him by his personal name; thus he classed him by precedent…

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
擬術而曾一突完之不若況季友乎殊不知帝王之
道賢可禪則以天下為公而不拘於世及子可繼則
以天下為家而不必於禪授故壽夢之欲傳國乎季
子者以大王之心為心也諸樊餘祭之拳拳者以仲
雍之心為心也彼王僚無季歷之賢而季子為太伯
之讓豈至德乎使爭弒禍興覆師喪國誰階之也謂
非賢且智過而不得其中者哉貶而書名所以望之
深而責之備也大抵聖人之待人猶化工之於物大
以成大小以成小物各付物而已奚容心焉公子喜
時春秋猶賢其後世豈有季子之高風而春秋不以
賢者責之哉噫惟與天地同德而達乎時中然後能
與於此非聖人莫能脩之信夫
===
齊侯宋公江人黃人會于陽穀〔僖公三年〕　公會齊
侯宋公陳侯衛侯鄭伯許男曹伯侵蔡　蔡潰遂
伐楚次于陘　盟于召陵　齊人執陳轅濤
塗　及江人黃人伐陳〔僖公四年〕
舒洪
同考試官教諭謝　批此題主胡傳本平易場中諸作或泥公
punctuated:
擬術，而曾一突、完之不若，況季友乎？殊不知帝王之道，賢可禪，則以天下為公，而不拘於世及；子可繼，則以天下為家，而不必於禪授。故壽夢之欲傳國乎季子者，以大王之心為心也；諸樊、餘祭之拳拳者，以仲雍之心為心也。彼王僚無季歷之賢，而季子為太伯之讓，豈至德乎？使爭弒禍興，覆師喪國，誰階之也？謂非賢且智過而不得其中者哉！貶而書名，所以望之深而責之備也。大抵聖人之待人，猶化工之於物，大以成大，小以成小，物各付物而已，奚容心焉？公子喜時，《春秋》猶賢其後世，豈有季子之高風，而《春秋》不以賢者責之哉？噫！惟與天地同德，而達乎時中，然後能與於此。非聖人莫能脩之，信夫！

齊侯、宋公、江人、黃人會于陽穀〔僖公三年〕。公會齊侯、宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯侵蔡。蔡潰，遂伐楚，次于陘。盟于召陵。齊人執陳轅濤塗。及江人、黃人伐陳〔僖公四年〕。
舒洪
同考試官教諭謝批：此題主《胡傳》，本平易。場中諸作，或泥公
translation_en:
…compared to Jiao[?] and Shu, and not even equal to a single Tu or Wan, much less Ji You! Little do they know that in the Way of emperors and kings, when a worthy can be yielded to, they take the realm as public and are not bound by hereditary succession; when a son can succeed, they take the realm as a family possession and do not insist on abdication. Thus, Shoumeng’s desire to transmit the state to Jizi (Ji Zha) was taking the heart of King Tai as his own heart; the earnest devotion of Zhufan and Y祭 (Yuji) was taking the heart of Zhongyong as their own heart. That King Liao lacked the worthiness of Jili, yet Jizi practiced the yielding of Taibo—how could this be supreme virtue? Causing the disasters of contention and regicide to arise, armies to be overthrown and the state to be ruined—who laid the steps for this? Can it not be called a case of the worthy and wise going too far and failing to attain the Mean? Demoting him and recording him only by personal name is the way of placing deep hopes in him and holding him to the standard of perfection. In general, the sage’s treatment of men is like Creative Nature’s relation to things: the great are brought to completion as great, the small are brought to completion as small; each thing is simply dealt with according to what it is—how could any personal bias be admitted therein? Even for Gongzi Xishi, the Spring and Autumn Annals praised his descendants as worthy; how could there be the lofty character of Jizi, and yet the Spring and Autumn Annals not hold him to the standard of a worthy? Alas! Only one who shares the virtue of Heaven and Earth and attains the timely Mean can participate in this. "None but a sage could have compiled and revised it"—truly so!

"The Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, a man of Jiang, and a man of Huang met at Yanggu" [3rd year of Duke Xi]. "The Duke met the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Earl of Cao to make an incursion into Cai. Cai collapsed in rout, and thereupon they attacked Chu, halting at Xing. They covenanted at Shaoling. A man of Qi seized Yuan Taotu of Chen. Together with a man of Jiang and a man of Huang, we attacked Chen" [4th year of Duke Xi].
Shu Hong.

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
可用策以伐楚不當用之以伐陳者執以服楚之後執陳伐鄭
伯必驕者間得奇正之說又分截不明者殊失本旨惟此作得其
意有關鍵有斷制非麟經中之作者乎故表而出之
考試官學正汪　批〔此題胡氏專辨陽穀一會之謀作者往往〕〔昧旨惟此篇體傳之意而文足以發之故錄出以範學者〕
考試官教授林　批〔批得屬詞比事之旨〕
即伯好而知其攘夷之謀究伯事以驗其用人之實
于以見齊桓陽穀之會結江黄以謀伐楚而其行師
之奇正處事之方略春秋詳書始末以善之也嘅念
===
周道既微楚氛寖惡陵我中華已非一日幸而齊桓
者出畫安攘之遠謀啓陽穀之大會彼諸侯之爵莫
尊乎宋宋公既至中華之友邦協矣要荒之君莫遠
乎江黄江黄既來外夷之右臂失矣吾想其會聚之
時意豈不曰荆尸甚堅乘廣甚銳今欲制之計將安
在必也孰當其前俾之進焉不能敵孰擬其後俾之
退焉無所憑謀既定于十全師遂合于八國侵蔡而
南及陘而次諸侯大衆厚集其陣聲罪致討則楚人
理屈而吾之內勢既震所謂聚而為正也江人黄人
punctuated:
可用策以伐楚，不當用之以伐陳者；執以服楚之後，執陳伐鄭，伯必驕者；間得奇正之說，又分截不明者，殊失本旨。惟此作得其意，有關鍵，有斷制，非麟經中之作者乎？故表而出之。
考試官學正汪　批：〔此題胡氏專辨陽穀一會之謀，作者往往〕〔昧旨。惟此篇體傳之意，而文足以發之，故錄出以範學者。〕
考試官教授林　批：〔批得屬詞比事之旨。〕
即伯好而知其攘夷之謀，究伯事以驗其用人之實。于以見齊桓陽穀之會，結江、黄以謀伐楚，而其行師之奇正、處事之方略，《春秋》詳書始末以善之也。嘅念周道既微，楚氛寖惡，陵我中華，已非一日。幸而齊桓者出，畫安攘之遠謀，啓陽穀之大會。彼諸侯之爵，莫尊乎宋；宋公既至，中華之友邦協矣。要荒之君，莫遠乎江、黄；江、黄既來，外夷之右臂失矣。吾想其會聚之時，意豈不曰：荆尸甚堅，乘廣甚銳，今欲制之，計將安在？必也孰當其前，俾之進焉不能敵；孰擬其後，俾之退焉無所憑。謀既定于十全，師遂合于八國。侵蔡而南，及陘而次。諸侯大衆，厚集其陣，聲罪致討，則楚人理屈，而吾之內勢既震，所謂聚而為正也。江人、黄人
translation_en:
…that the Duke could use a stratagem to attack Chu, yet ought not to have used it to attack Chen; others hold fast to the notion that after submitting Chu, by seizing [Yuan Taotu of] Chen and attacking Zheng [?], the Hegemon must have grown arrogant; and while some occasionally grasp the theory of the unorthodox and orthodox forces, their structural divisions are unclear—all of which utterly miss the fundamental purport. Only this essay grasps the meaning: it has pivotal points and decisive judgments. Is its author not a master of the Unicorn Classic [Spring and Autumn Annals]? Therefore, I have singled it out for publication.

Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: 〔On this topic, Master Hu specifically analyzes the strategy behind the single meeting at Yanggu, yet writers frequently〕〔miss the point. Only this essay embodies the meaning of the Commentary, and its prose is sufficient to bring it forth; therefore it is recorded here to serve as a model for scholars.〕

Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: 〔He has grasped the purport of connecting words and comparing events.〕

By examining the Hegemon's friendly meeting, one knows his plan for repelling the barbarians; by investigating the Hegemon's deeds, one verifies the reality of how he employed men. From this we see how Duke Huan of Qi, at the meeting of Yanggu, allied with Jiang and Huang in order to plan the campaign against Chu; and as for the unorthodox and orthodox deployments in his conduct of the army and his strategic plans in handling affairs, the Spring and Autumn Annals records the beginning and end in detail in order to commend them.

Alas! Once the Way of Zhou had declined, the miasma of Chu grew increasingly noxious, encroaching upon our Central States for more than a single day. Fortunately, Duke Huan of Qi emerged, devising far-reaching plans to pacify [the interior] and repel [the barbarians], and inaugurating the great assembly at Yanggu. Among the ranks of the feudal lords, none is more exalted than Song; once the Duke of Song arrived, the friendly states of the Central Realm were brought into harmony. Among the rulers of the remote and wild domains, none are more distant than Jiang and Huang; once Jiang and Huang came, the right arm of the outer barbarians was lost. I imagine that at the time of their assembly, did their thoughts not run thus: "The 'Jing-corpse' battle array of Chu is exceedingly solid, and their 'cheng-guang' chariot squadrons are exceedingly sharp. If we now wish to subdue them, where shall our strategy lie? Surely we must decide who will confront their front, so that if they advance they cannot withstand us, and who will menace their rear, so that if they retreat they have nothing to rely upon."

Once the plan was settled with complete certainty, the armies of the eight states were consequently joined. They invaded Cai and moved south, reaching Xing where they halted. The great multitude of the feudal lords massed their formations thickly, proclaiming Chu's crimes and conducting a punitive expedition; thus the men of Chu were put in the wrong, and our internal might already reverberated—this is what is called gathering together to form the orthodox force. Meanwhile, the men of Jiang and the men of Huang…

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
〈且守其境按兵不動則楚人勢孤而吾之外援已成
所謂分而為奇也偉哉克敵制勝之謀允矣戰勝攻
取之策及夫屈完如師桓則退于召陵而盟禮定陳
人悞軍桓則循海以歸而濤塗執文告昭宣于一時
武略震驚于四裔功既成矣志既遂矣然後扱及江
黃之師以為伐陳之舉則知侵蔡次陘而二國不與
自為掎角之勢明矣故春秋於陽穀之役六會而末
言者善是謀也非所謂即伯好而知其攘夷之謀究
伯事以驗其用人之實者乎吁齊桓一匡天下免民
===
左衽其功正在于此春秋備書之也宜哉大抵膺勝
而動好謀而成自入春秋以來未有及於此獨治楚
之事者也獨惜乎葵丘既盟楚人滅黃而〔師出無所救山〕
卒使小國賢君坐困於蠻夷之手可見江〔黃之來而不〕
桓而桓有負於江黃矣孟子曰五伯桓公為〔盛者此盛矣〕
五伯假之也觀此益信
禮記
禮樂交錯於中發形於外是故其成也懌恭敬
而温文立太傅少傅以養之欲其知父子君
punctuated:
〈且守其境，按兵不動，則楚人勢孤，而吾之外援已成，所謂「分而為奇」也。偉哉克敵制勝之謀，允矣戰勝攻取之策！及夫屈完如師，桓則退于召陵而盟禮定；陳人悞軍，桓則循海以歸而濤塗執。文告昭宣于一時，武略震驚于四裔。功既成矣，志既遂矣，然後扱及江、黃之師以為伐陳之舉，則知侵蔡、次陘而二國不與，自為掎角之勢明矣。故《春秋》於陽穀之役，六會而末言者，善是謀也。非所謂即伯好而知其攘夷之謀，究伯事以驗其用人之實者乎？吁！齊桓一匡天下，免民左衽，其功正在于此，《春秋》備書之也，宜哉！大抵膺勝而動，好謀而成，自入《春秋》以來，未有及於此獨治楚之事者也。獨惜乎葵丘既盟，楚人滅黃，而〔師出無所救山〕，卒使小國賢君坐困於蠻夷之手，可見江〔黃之來而不〕桓，而桓有負於江、黃矣。孟子曰：「五伯，桓公為〔盛者此盛矣〕，五伯假之也。」觀此益信。
《禮記》
「禮樂交錯於中，發形於外，是故其成也懌，恭敬而温文。立太傅、少傅以養之，欲其知父子、君
translation_en:
…meanwhile guarded their own borders and held their troops in place without moving; thus the men of Chu were isolated in strength while our external support was already formed—this is what is called "dividing to create the unorthodox (surprise) force." Grand indeed was the plan for overcoming the enemy and securing victory; sound indeed was the strategy for winning battles and taking by attack! When Qu Wan came to the army, Duke Huan retreated to Shaoling and the covenant rites were settled; when the men of Chen misled the army, Duke Huan returned along the sea coast and Yuan Taotu was seized. Civil proclamations were brilliantly promulgated in that age, and martial strategy shook the four borderlands. Once the merit was achieved and the ambition fulfilled, only then did he draw upon the troops of Jiang and Huang to undertake the campaign against Chen; from this we know that when invading Cai and halting at Xing those two states did not take part, and that they naturally formed a pincer posture (jijiao zhi shi) is clear. Therefore, in the campaign of Yanggu, the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) records the meeting of the six [actually four] and mentions them at the end because it approved of this plan. Is this not what is meant by examining the hegemon's amity to know his plan for repelling the barbarians, and investigating the hegemon's deeds to verify the reality of how he employed men? Alas! Duke Huan of Qi united and rectified all under Heaven, saving the people from folding their robes to the left [like barbarians]; his merit lay precisely in this, and that the Spring and Autumn Annals recorded it in full is fitting indeed! Broadly speaking, moving only after securing victory and succeeding through a fondness for planning—since the beginning of the Spring and Autumn period, nothing had matched this singular affair ofbringing Chu to order. It is only to be regretted that after the covenant at Kuiqiu, the men of Chu destroyed Huang, and [no troops went forth to rescue them (?)], ultimately leaving the worthy ruler of a small state to sit trapped at the hands of the southern barbarians. From this it can be seen that Jiang [and Huang did not fail (?)] Duke Huan, whereas Duke Huan failed Jiang and Huang! Mencius said: "Of the Five Hegemons, Duke Huan was the most [flourishing...]; the Five Hegemons borrowed [benevolence and righteousness]." Viewing this, one believes it all the more.

Record of Rites (Liji)
"Ritual and music interpenetrate within and manifest their form without; therefore, when his character is completed, he is joyful, reverent, respectful, gentle, and accomplished. The Grand Mentor (Taifu) and Junior Mentor (Shaofu) are established to nurture him, desiring that he know the way of father and son, ruler and…

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
臣之道也
葉元
同考試官學正陳　批〔題本正大作者多分截不明晚得此卷理明詞達讀之令人躍然〕
考試官學正汪　批〔先王所以教養者欲其明人倫也此作良是〕
考試官教授林　批〔批得三王教養世子之道〕
觀先王於世子教有成功養有常職者無非欲其審夫人倫之理焉蓋父子君臣人之大倫也然所以教
而養之者豈非欲世子知乎此哉且夫三王之教世
===
子有禮以脩外而禮之脩則達於中有樂以脩內而
樂之脩則達於外然既有諸中必發形於外是以其
成也懌忻之情油然而生悅懌之意藹然而出有以
見其內之和恭見乎外敬主乎中溫而不暴文而不
野有以見其外之和如此則教之之道可謂大矣苟
非其人道不虛行於是設太傅之官以身為教于以
長而成之使禮樂之道無不行立少傅之職以言為
教于以造而就之俾禮樂之教無敢廢如此則養之
之道可謂至矣夫所以教養之者豈有他哉誠以內
punctuated:
臣之道也。
葉元
同考試官學正陳　批〔題本正大，作者多分截不明，晚得此卷，理明詞達，讀之令人躍然。〕
考試官學正汪　批〔先王所以教養者，欲其明人倫也，此作良是。〕
考試官教授林　批〔批得三王教養世子之道。〕
觀先王於世子，教有成功，養有常職者，無非欲其審夫人倫之理焉。蓋父子、君臣，人之大倫也，然所以教而養之者，豈非欲世子知乎此哉？且夫三王之教世子，有禮以脩外，而禮之脩則達於中；有樂以脩內，而樂之脩則達於外。然既有諸中，必發形於外，是以其成也，懌忻之情油然而生，悅懌之意藹然而出，有以見其內之和；恭見乎外，敬主乎中，溫而不暴，文而不野，有以見其外之和。如此，則教之之道可謂大矣。苟非其人，道不虛行。於是設太傅之官，以身為教，于以長而成之，使禮樂之道無不行；立少傅之職，以言為教，于以造而就之，俾禮樂之教無敢廢。如此，則養之之道可謂至矣。夫所以教養之者，豈有他哉？誠以內
translation_en:
… and the way of ruler and minister."

Ye Yuan 葉元

Associate Examiner Department Director Chen 陳 comments: 〔The topic itself is upright and grand, yet most writers failed to divide its sections clearly. Late in the reading I came upon this paper: its reasoning is clear and its expression fluent; reading it makes one leap with delight.〕
Examiner Department Director Wang 汪 comments: 〔The reason the former kings instructed and nurtured him was that they wished him to understand human moral relationships; this composition gets it right indeed.〕
Examiner Prefectural Director of Studies Lin 林 comments: 〔He has penetrated [?] the way in which the Three Kings instructed and nurtured the heir apparent.〕

When we observe that in dealing with the heir apparent the former kings achieved success in his instruction and maintained regular offices for his nurturing, it was for no other reason than that they wished him to discern the principles of human moral relationships. For father and son, ruler and minister, are the great moral relationships of mankind; yet in instructing and nurturing him, was it not precisely that they wished the heir apparent to understand these?

Moreover, in the Three Kings' instruction of the heir apparent, there were rites to cultivate the exterior, and the cultivation of rites reached into the interior; there was music to cultivate the interior, and the cultivation of music reached out to the exterior. Now once something is possessed within, it necessarily manifests itself in outward form. Therefore, upon his completion, feelings of gladness arise spontaneously and an air of joyful harmony shines forth richly, whereby one may see the harmony of his interior; respectfulness is displayed on the outside while reverence presides within, gentle and not violent, refined and not rustic, whereby one may see the harmony of his exterior. Being thus, the way of instructing him may truly be called great.

Yet if there are not the right men, the Way does not operate in a vacuum. Accordingly, they established the office of Grand Mentor (taifu) to teach by personal example, thereby fostering and bringing him to completion, so that the way of rites and music would never fail to be practiced; and they instituted the post of Junior Mentor (shaofu) to teach by words, thereby molding and bringing him to accomplishment, so that the teaching of rites and music would never dare be neglected. Being thus, the way of nurturing him may truly be called utmost.

Now as for the reason they instructed and nurtured him, was there anything else to it? Truly it was because within…

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
則父子人之大倫也今所以教養世子者正欲其知
乎父子之親焉外則君臣亦人之大倫也今所以教
養世子者正欲其知乎君臣之義焉吁教養之道既
無不盡世子之德又豈有不成者哉大抵世子者天
下之大本也處夫儲貳之位將有承天踐阼之任君
國子民之責爲君父者苟教之無方養之無法何以
成君人之德而勝負荷之重哉故曰有父之親有君
之尊然後兼天下而有之然則先王之教養世子豈
事虛文也哉
===
五行以爲質故事可復也
趙王
同考試官學正陳　批〔此場中作者多執五行爲質處支援不切惟此能覆說前章之事深合本旨宜錄以冠本房〕
考試官學正汪　批〔發明五行爲質處可觀〕
考試官教授林　批〔允如初考〕
惟歲事取正於五行故歲事既周而可舉蓋五行之
氣周而復始也國家歲事之常苟能取正於五行之
時令則其事又豈不可周而復始哉記禮者謂古聖
punctuated:
則父子，人之大倫也；今所以教養世子者，正欲其知乎父子之親焉。外則君臣，亦人之大倫也；今所以教養世子者，正欲其知乎君臣之義焉。吁！教養之道既無不盡，世子之德又豈有不成者哉？大抵世子者，天下之大本也。處夫儲貳之位，將有承天踐阼之任，君國子民之責。爲君父者，苟教之無方，養之無法，何以成君人之德，而勝負荷之重哉？故曰：「有父之親，有君之尊，然後兼天下而有之。」然則先王之教養世子，豈事虛文也哉？

「五行以爲質，故事可復也。」
趙王
同考試官學正陳　批〔此場中作者多執「五行爲質」處，支援不切。惟此能覆說前章之事，深合本旨，宜錄以冠本房。〕
考試官學正汪　批〔發明「五行爲質」處，可觀。〕
考試官教授林　批〔允如初考。〕

惟歲事取正於五行，故歲事既周而可舉。蓋五行之氣，周而復始也。國家歲事之常，苟能取正於五行之時令，則其事又豈不可周而復始哉？記禮者謂古聖
translation_en:
…within the family, father and son constitute one of the great human relationships; the reason for educating and nurturing the Heir Apparent now is precisely to make him understand the affection between father and son. Outside the family, ruler and minister likewise constitute one of the great human relationships; the reason for educating and nurturing the Heir Apparent now is precisely to make him understand the righteousness between ruler and minister. Ah! Once the way of education and nurture is carried out in full, how could the virtue of the Heir Apparent fail to be brought to completion? In general, the Heir Apparent is the great foundation of the realm. Occupying the position of heir and second to the throne, he will in time bear the charge of receiving the Mandate of Heaven and ascending the throne, and the responsibility of ruling the state and treating the people as his children. If the ruler and father educates him without proper method and nurtures him without proper model, how could he perfect the virtue required to rule over men and bear so heavy a burden? Therefore it is said: "Only when one understands the affection due a father and the reverence due a ruler can one encompass the whole world and possess it." This being so, in educating and nurturing the Heir Apparent, were the Former Kings merely engaging in empty formality?

"The Five Phases are taken as the substance, and therefore human affairs can be repeated."
Zhao Wang 趙王
Associate Examiner and Subprefectural Director of Studies Chen 陳 comments: [In this session, most candidates clung rigidly to the phrase "taking the Five Phases as the substance," and their supporting arguments missed the mark. Only this essay is able to refer back to the affairs discussed in the preceding passage, deeply matching the fundamental purport of the text. It should be selected to head my examination ward.]
Examiner and Subprefectural Director of Studies Wang 汪 comments: [Its elucidation of "taking the Five Phases as the substance" is well worth reading.]
Examiner and Prefectural Director of Studies Lin 林 comments: [Truly as the initial examiner judged.]

Because the affairs of the year take their standard from the Five Phases, once the affairs of the year have completed their cycle, they can be carried out again. For the vital forces of the Five Phases complete their cycle and begin anew. If the regular annual affairs of the state can take their standard from the seasonal ordinances of the Five Phases, how then could those affairs not likewise complete their cycle and begin anew? The compiler of the Record of Rites states that when the ancient sages…

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
人作則必本造化彼彼春木夏火秋金冬水而土旺四
季位居中央此五行之運於四時而有十二月也聖
人作為五聲六律十二管而取正於五行之時令則
春角夏徵秋商冬羽宮配乎中央而更迭為主每月
各有其律焉造為五味六和十二食而取正於五行
之時令則春酸夏苦秋辛冬鹹滑甘寓乎四時而更
相為質每月各有其食焉以至施為五色六章十二
衣而又取正於五行之時令則春青夏朱秋白冬黑
黃合乎中央而更相為主每月豈不各有其衣乎惟
===
其取正於五行之時令如此則其事有可復者焉如
聲律用於今歲既一周矣來歲由春徂冬皆可依昔
而舉用非若他事之宜於已然而不宜於將然也色
味用於今歲既一終矣來歲自春至冬悉可循序而
興行非如他事之宜於已往而不宜於將來也愚故
曰惟歲事取正於五行故歲事既周而可舉者以此
抑考是章之旨自天地以為本至人情以為田皆是
覆說前章諸事無非聖人仰觀於天俯察於地近取
諸人作為典則以示教於天下也然為法甚備為治
punctuated: 人作則，必本造化。彼彼春木、夏火、秋金、冬水，而土旺四季、位居中央，此五行之運於四時，而有十二月也。聖人作為五聲、六律、十二管，而取正於五行之時令，則春角、夏徵、秋商、冬羽，宮配乎中央，而更迭為主，每月各有其律焉；造為五味、六和、十二食，而取正於五行之時令，則春酸、夏苦、秋辛、冬鹹，滑甘寓乎四時，而更相為質，每月各有其食焉；以至施為五色、六章、十二衣，而又取正於五行之時令，則春青、夏朱、秋白、冬黑，黃合乎中央，而更相為主，每月豈不各有其衣乎？惟其取正於五行之時令如此，則其事有可復者焉。如聲律用於今歲既一周矣，來歲由春徂冬，皆可依昔而舉用，非若他事之宜於已然而不宜於將然也；色味用於今歲既一終矣，來歲自春至冬，悉可循序而興行，非如他事之宜於已往而不宜於將來也。愚故曰：「惟歲事取正於五行，故歲事既周而可舉」者，以此。抑考是章之旨，自「天地以為本」至「人情以為田」，皆是覆說前章諸事，無非聖人仰觀於天、俯察於地、近取諸人，作為典則，以示教於天下也。然為法甚備，為治
translation_en: … the ancient sages established regulations, they necessarily grounded them in the workings of nature. Now [?], wood in spring, fire in summer, metal in autumn, and water in winter, while earth flourishes across all four seasons and occupies the central position—this is how the Five Phases revolve through the four seasons to form the twelve months. The sages created the five notes, six pitch-standards, and twelve pitch-pipes, taking their standard from the seasonal ordinances of the Five Phases; thus, with the jiao note in spring, zhi in summer, shang in autumn, and yu in winter, and the gong note corresponding to the center, they alternate as the dominant tone, so that each month has its own pitch-pipe. They instituted the five flavors, six harmonizations, and twelve seasonal foods, taking their standard from the seasonal ordinances of the Five Phases; thus, with sour in spring, bitter in summer, acrid in autumn, and salty in winter, while slippery and sweet reside throughout the four seasons, they alternate as the fundamental substance, so that each month has its own food. And extending to the application of the five colors, six emblems, and twelve seasonal garments, they again took their standard from the seasonal ordinances of the Five Phases; thus, with green in spring, vermilion in summer, white in autumn, and black in winter, while yellow corresponds to the center, they alternate as the dominant color—does not each month then have its own garment? Precisely because they take their standard from the seasonal ordinances of the Five Phases in this way, these affairs can be repeated. For example, once the notes and pitch-standards have completed a full cycle of use in the current year, in the coming year from spring to winter they can all be instituted and used just as before, unlike other affairs that suit what has already been done but do not suit what is yet to come. Once the colors and flavors have reached the end of their use in the current year, in the coming year from spring to winter they can all be put into practice in their proper sequence, unlike other affairs that suit the past but do not suit the future. This is why I say: "It is only because the yearly affairs take their standard from the Five Phases that, once the yearly affairs have completed their cycle, they can be instituted again." Furthermore, if we examine the meaning of this chapter, from "taking Heaven and Earth as the root" down to "taking human feelings as the field," it all recapitulates the various matters of the preceding chapter: none of it is anything other than the sages looking up to contemplate Heaven, looking down to examine Earth, and drawing near at hand from humanity to create canons and rules by which to instruct the world. Yet when the laws are most complete and governance…

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
其祥定有休徵以應之矣故下文又以四靈以為畜
言之於此可見聖人體信達順之道也歟
論
王者以仁義為麗
同考試官教諭沈　批〔議論曲折且善斷制非有筆底皮裹陽秋者不能也多士之冠舍子其誰〕
考試官學正汪　批〔議論層疊愈出愈奇讀之令人起敬置之魁選與論翕然〕
羅奎
===
考試官教授林　批〔筆力老蒼氣勢雄偉真百鳥中之孤鳳也〕
天子所以光天下者不以人麗為麗而以天麗
為麗焉天麗之麗乃麗天下之麗也豈以宮室
為哉麗天下莫切於仁義莫大於仁義仁義乃
天麗之麗耳不必雕飾而自煇煌於天下不必
聳瞻而自壯觀於天下宮室云乎哉宮室乃人
麗之麗耳人麗之麗不過麗人之目不能麗人
之心不過麗人之欲不能麗人之天仁義乃麗
人之心麗人之天王者以仁義為麗是乃為真
punctuated:
其祥，定有休徵以應之矣。故下文又以「四靈以為畜」言之，於此可見聖人體信達順之道也歟！

論
王者以仁義為麗
羅奎
同考試官教諭沈　批〔議論曲折，且善斷制，非有筆底皮裹陽秋者不能也。多士之冠，舍子其誰？〕
考試官學正汪　批〔議論層疊，愈出愈奇，讀之令人起敬。置之魁選，與論翕然。〕
考試官教授林　批〔筆力老蒼，氣勢雄偉，真百鳥中之孤鳳也。〕

天子所以光天下者，不以人麗為麗，而以天麗為麗焉。天麗之麗，乃麗天下之麗也，豈以宮室為哉？麗天下莫切於仁義，莫大於仁義。仁義乃天麗之麗耳，不必雕飾而自煇煌於天下，不必聳瞻而自壯觀於天下，宮室云乎哉？宮室乃人麗之麗耳。人麗之麗，不過麗人之目，不能麗人之心；不過麗人之欲，不能麗人之天。仁義乃麗人之心，麗人之天。王者以仁義為麗，是乃為真
translation_en:
…is auspicious [reading 甚祥 for 其祥], there will certainly be felicitous signs to respond to it. Therefore, the text below goes on to speak of "having the Four Numinous Creatures as one's domestic animals." From this, can one not see the sage's Way of embodying trustworthiness and achieving harmony?

Discourse
"The True King Takes Benevolence and Righteousness as His Magnificence"
Luo Kui 羅奎
Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Shen: [The argumentation is intricate and well-judged; none could have written this without harboring the critical discernment of the *Spring and Autumn Annals* ("leather-wrapped *Annals*") beneath his brush. To crown the multitude of scholars, if not you, then who?]
Comment by Examiner Director of Studies Wang: [The arguments build in layers, growing ever more marvelous as they unfold; reading it inspires awe. Placing it among the top selections accords harmoniously with public opinion [reading 輿論 for 與論].]
Comment by Examiner Instructor Lin: [The brush-force is seasoned and vigorous, its momentum grand and majestic—truly a lone phoenix among a hundred birds.]

That by which the Son of Heaven illuminates All under Heaven is not by taking human magnificence as magnificence, but by taking heavenly magnificence as magnificence. The magnificence of heavenly magnificence is the magnificence that adorns All under Heaven; how could it consist in palaces and halls? For adorning All under Heaven, nothing is more essential than benevolence and righteousness, and nothing is greater than benevolence and righteousness. Benevolence and righteousness are the magnificence of heavenly magnificence: without needing carved ornaments, they naturally shine resplendently throughout All under Heaven; without needing to tower on high for men's gaze, they naturally present a grand spectacle to All under Heaven. Need one speak of palaces and halls? Palaces and halls are merely the magnificence of human magnificence. The magnificence of human magnificence merely dazzles people's eyes, and cannot adorn people's minds; it merely gratifies people's desires, and cannot adorn people's heavenly nature. Benevolence and righteousness, however, adorn people's minds and adorn people's heavenly nature. When the True King takes benevolence and righteousness as his magnificence, this is what constitutes true…

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
麗矣蕭何以宮室爲壯麗能麗天下哉究何之
心正以天下而定人心初服非極壯觀無以聳
天下之觀瞻一天下之心志貽範後世使無以
加故於未央之作極大其規模殊不知王者之
麗天下不在於宮室而在於仁義仁即天下之
廣居也義即天下之大道也能大脩其仁大脩
其義則仁也義也即嚴人心之殿陛即凜人心
之門墻即固人心之郛郭豈在於壯宮室始足
以誇麗於天下哉天下之心同此仁也同此義
===
也以仁義爲麗豈不麗其所麗哉大脩於一身
麗於一家矣大脩於一家麗於一國矣大脩於
一國麗于天下矣大脩於天下麗于四夷矣贊
化育者在是參天地者在是宮室之麗寧有此
哉若宮室有以麗天下堯何土階其級也禹何
宮室其卑也惟其所以麗者不在乎此此古先
聖王皆不以此爲麗而以仁義爲麗焉堯之都
平陽光被四表堯以仁義爲麗也舜之都蒲坂
光宅天下舜以仁義爲麗也禹之都安邑文命
punctuated: 麗矣。蕭何以宮室爲壯麗，能麗天下哉？究何之心，正以天下而定，人心初服，非極壯觀，無以聳天下之觀瞻，一天下之心志，貽範後世，使無以加；故於未央之作，極大其規模。殊不知王者之麗天下，不在於宮室，而在於仁義。仁即天下之廣居也，義即天下之大道也。能大脩其仁、大脩其義，則仁也、義也，即嚴人心之殿陛，即凜人心之門墻，即固人心之郛郭。豈在於壯宮室，始足以誇麗於天下哉？天下之心，同此仁也，同此義也。以仁義爲麗，豈不麗其所麗哉？大脩於一身，麗於一家矣；大脩於一家，麗於一國矣；大脩於一國，麗于天下矣；大脩於天下，麗于四夷矣。贊化育者在是，參天地者在是。宮室之麗，寧有此哉？若宮室有以麗天下，堯何土階其級也？禹何宮室其卑也？惟其所以麗者不在乎此，此古先聖王皆不以此爲麗，而以仁義爲麗焉。堯之都平陽，光被四表，堯以仁義爲麗也；舜之都蒲坂，光宅天下，舜以仁義爲麗也；禹之都安邑，文命
translation_en: …splendor. Xiao He 蕭何 took palaces and halls as magnificent splendor, but could that make all under Heaven splendid? If we examine He's mind, it was precisely because all under Heaven had just been settled [reading 而 as 初] and people's hearts had newly submitted; without the utmost magnificence, there would be nothing with which to awe the gaze of all under Heaven, unify the minds and wills of all under Heaven, and leave a model for later generations so that nothing more could be added to it. Therefore, in the construction of the Weiyang Palace 未央宮, he made its scale as grand as possible. Yet he failed to realize that a true king's making all under Heaven splendid lies not in palaces and halls, but in benevolence and righteousness. Benevolence is the wide abode of all under Heaven; righteousness is the great thoroughfare of all under Heaven. If one can grandly cultivate one's benevolence and grandly cultivate one's righteousness, then benevolence and righteousness themselves make majestic the palace steps in people's hearts, make awe-inspiring the gates and walls in people's hearts, and make secure the outer ramparts in people's hearts. How could it depend on making palaces and halls magnificent before being sufficient to boast of splendor to all under Heaven? The hearts of all under Heaven share this same benevolence and share this same righteousness. Taking benevolence and righteousness as splendor—does this not make splendid that which truly constitutes splendor? When grandly cultivated in one's own person, it is splendid throughout the family; when grandly cultivated in the family, it is splendid throughout the state; when grandly cultivated in the state, it is splendid throughout all under Heaven; when grandly cultivated throughout all under Heaven, it is splendid among the four barbarian tribes. Assisting the transforming and nourishing powers of nature lies in this; forming a triad with Heaven and Earth lies in this. How could the splendor of palaces and halls ever possess such power? If palaces and halls were the means to make all under Heaven splendid, why did Yao 堯 have steps of earthen turf? Why did Yu 禹 keep his palaces and halls so humble? Only because that by which they achieved splendor did not lie therein—for this reason, the ancient sage-kings all did not take such things as splendor, but took benevolence and righteousness as splendor. When Yao made his capital at Pingyang 平陽, his radiance reached the four extremities—that was Yao taking benevolence and righteousness as splendor. When Shun 舜 made his capital at Puban 蒲坂, he gloriously inhabited all under Heaven—that was Shun taking benevolence and righteousness as splendor. When Yu made his capital at Anyi 安邑, his civilizing mandates…

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
□于四海禹以仁義為麗也懋昭大德兆民允
殖非湯之都于亳以仁義為麗乎光于四方顯
于西土非文王之都于岐以仁義為麗乎丕單
稱德海隅率俾抑非武王都于鎬以仁義為麗
乎王者既皆以仁義為麗矣何也何獨以宮室
為麗哉以宮室為麗必不能麗天下矣彼其飛
宮傾室非不麗也適足以來胥讒麗何在焉瑤
臺瓊室非不麗也適足以致怨讟麗何有焉作
阿房走咸陽跨渭川非不欲麗天下也然未免
===
於焦土又何麗之有哉是則麗天下誠不在宮
室而在於仁義也脩之以仁義不必麗宮室而
自麗於天下矣蕭何以宮室為麗非矣雖曰天
子當以四海為家惟極壯麗方能鎮服其心然
亦末上論事耳豈知所本也歟雖然何固不知
所本然漢高亦豈知所本者耶未央之成初見
其壯麗之極固未嘗不怒及聆四海為家之語
又未嘗不悅此其心非以宮室為麗乎噫漢之
君相舉不知所麗矣然自漢而下能知仁義哉為
punctuated: □于四海，禹以仁義為麗也。懋昭大德，兆民允殖，非湯之都于亳，以仁義為麗乎？光于四方，顯于西土，非文王之都于岐，以仁義為麗乎？丕單稱德，海隅率俾，抑非武王都于鎬，以仁義為麗乎？王者既皆以仁義為麗矣，何也何獨以宮室為麗哉？以宮室為麗，必不能麗天下矣。彼其飛宮傾室，非不麗也，適足以來胥讒，麗何在焉？瑤臺瓊室，非不麗也，適足以致怨讟，麗何有焉？作阿房，走咸陽，跨渭川，非不欲麗天下也，然未免於焦土，又何麗之有哉？是則麗天下誠不在宮室而在於仁義也。脩之以仁義，不必麗宮室而自麗於天下矣。蕭何以宮室為麗，非矣。雖曰天子當以四海為家，惟極壯麗方能鎮服其心，然亦末上論事耳，豈知所本也歟？雖然，何固不知所本，然漢高亦豈知所本者耶？未央之成，初見其壯麗之極，固未嘗不怒；及聆「四海為家」之語，又未嘗不悅，此其心非以宮室為麗乎？噫！漢之君相，舉不知所麗矣。然自漢而下，能知仁義哉為
translation_en:
… [spread] throughout the Four Seas: thus Yu took benevolence and righteousness as his magnificence. "Energetically displaying his great virtue, so that the millions of people truly multiplied"—was this not Tang, with his capital at Bo, taking benevolence and righteousness as his magnificence? "Shining throughout the four quarters, manifest in the western regions"—was this not King Wen, with his capital at Qi, taking benevolence and righteousness as his magnificence? "Greatly exhausting the praise of his virtue, so that even the corners of the sea were led to submit"—was this not furthermore King Wu, with his capital at Hao, taking benevolence and righteousness as his magnificence?

Since the true kings all took benevolence and righteousness as their magnificence, why then did [Xiao] He alone take palaces and chambers as magnificence? If one takes palaces and chambers as magnificence, one certainly cannot make the empire magnificent. Look at those soaring palaces and perilous chambers [of Jie]: it is not that they lacked magnificence, yet they served only to invite mutual slander—where, then, was the magnificence? The jade terraces and gemmed chambers [of Zhou]: it is not that they lacked magnificence, yet they served only to bring about resentment and seditious murmuring—what magnificence was there in that? Constructing the Epang Palace, running to Xianyang, and spanning the Wei River [under Qin]: it is not that he did not wish to display magnificence to the empire, yet in the end it could not escape becoming scorched earth—what magnificence was there in that?

Thus, making the empire magnificent truly lies not in palaces and chambers, but in benevolence and righteousness. If one cultivates it with benevolence and righteousness, there is no need to make palaces and chambers magnificent, and yet one will naturally be magnificent throughout the empire. For Xiao He to take palaces and chambers as magnificence was wrong. Although he said that the Son of Heaven ought to take the Four Seas as his home and that only the utmost grandeur and magnificence could overawe and subdue men's hearts, this was merely discussing affairs from the standpoint of superficialities—how could he know what is fundamental? Even so, while He indeed did not know what is fundamental, how could Emperor Gao of Han be considered one who knew what is fundamental either? When the Weiyang Palace was completed, upon first seeing the extreme of its grandeur and magnificence, he indeed did not fail to be angry; yet once he heard the words about "taking the Four Seas as his home," he in turn did not fail to be pleased. In his heart, was this not taking palaces and chambers as magnificence? Alas! Ruler and minister of the Han alike failed to know wherein true magnificence lies. Yet from the Han onward, those able to know [taking?] [?] benevolence and righteousness as…

text:
□□有唐之太宗近似矣而失之雜於夷宋之太祖
庶幾矣而未能醇於王是以終不如唐虞三代之
以仁義麗天下麗萬世也求其以仁義麗天下
者幸惟我
聖天子在

伏以
自愧巖棲之士獲叨
廷對之榮儒道生榮士林增重茲蓋伏遇
