title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
擢崇文則載封聖賢之僞嚴覆試之法匪樹私
恩復拔萃之科大明公道特
賜臨軒之問用資訪道之勤臣等章句腐儒縉紳
末品正誼明道愧董仲舒之賢良博學宏詞慚
張九齡之蹇諤濫膺鶚薦幸覩
龍飛新進十一人舉登名於
天府諸科十七士咸通籍於金閨此誠千載之奇
逢一朝之新制也臣等效用有階報恩無地敢
不益精舊學求無忝於甲科永竭愚衷冀有裨
===
於
盛治伏願人文宣朗如雲漢之昭回
聖學緝熙同日星之炳煥固臣民於有極綿
宗社於無疆臣等無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
表稱
謝以
聞
punctuated: 擢，崇文則載封聖賢之僞。嚴覆試之法，匪樹私恩；復拔萃之科，大明公道。特賜臨軒之問，用資訪道之勤。臣等章句腐儒，縉紳末品。正誼明道，愧董仲舒之賢良；博學宏詞，慚張九齡之蹇諤。濫膺鶚薦，幸覩龍飛。新進十一人，舉登名於天府；諸科十七士，咸通籍於金閨。此誠千載之奇逢，一朝之新制也。臣等效用有階，報恩無地，敢不益精舊學，求無忝於甲科；永竭愚衷，冀有裨於盛治。伏願人文宣朗，如雲漢之昭回；聖學緝熙，同日星之炳煥。固臣民於有極，綿宗社於無疆。臣等無任瞻天仰聖，激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。
translation_en:
… military governors' power [reading 擢 as 權], and in exalting civil culture You again enfeoffed the descendants [reading 僞 as 後] of the sages and worthies. Making strict the regulations for re-examination, You did not establish private favor; restoring the specialty examination for Persons of Outstanding Talent (Bocui), You greatly illuminated the public way. You specially bestowed questions delivered from the palace veranda, thereby aiding Your diligence in inquiring into the Way.

We, Your servants, are pedantic Confucians of chapter and phrase, the lowest rank among the gentry. In rectifying righteousness and clarifying the Way, we fall short in shame before the Worthy and Upright (Xianliang) Dong Zhongshu; in Erudite Literature and Magnificent Phrases (Boxue hongci), we blush before the outspoken integrity of Zhang Jiuling. Having undeservedly received the osprey recommendation, we have the good fortune to behold the dragon in flight. The eleven newly presented metropolitan graduates have all had their names entered in the Heavenly Prefecture; the seventeen scholars of the various specialty examinations have all been registered on the rolls of the Golden Gate. This is truly a rare encounter of a thousand years, and a new institution of our dynasty.

Now that we, Your servants, have a stepping-stone to render service, yet lack any ground sufficient to repay Your grace, how dare we not further refine our former learning, seeking not to disgrace the top-tier examination category, and forever exhaust our humble loyalty, hoping to be of some aid to Your flourishing governance? We humbly wish that human culture may shine forth brightly, like the radiant revolving of the Milky Way, and that Your Sacred Learning may continue in bright illumination, dazzling like the sun and stars—securing subjects and people in the standard of perfection, and perpetuating the ancestral temples and altars of state without bound. We, Your servants, are overcome to the utmost with emotion and trepidation as we gaze up at Heaven and look up to Your Sacredness, and we reverently present this memorial of gratitude for Your Majesty's hearing.

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
第一問
同考試官學正陳　批〔問李正太學中多不知言今身教言教之實惟此能以古之嘉言善行及我〕　趙王
朝懿範奎章條答無遺信策手也
考試官學正汪　批〔條答詳明可取〕
考試官教授林　批〔叙古頌〕
今最為切當非深於治道者不能欽羨欽羨
===
行而世為天下法言而世為天下則此聖人所
以為天地立心為生民立命為萬世開太平者
也前乎二帝三王所以繼天立極者此也後乎我
朝
列聖所以繼往開來者靡非此乎且聖人者出中天
地而立身綱常之寄其道豈有他哉亦惟身教
言教二者相須而並行焉稽之於古如明峻德
而慎徽五典允迪厥德而克諧以孝克舜之身
教也祗台德先而懋貽大德緝熙敬止而細行
punctuated:
第一問
同考試官學正陳　批：〔問李正太學中多不知言，今身教、言教之實，惟此能以古之嘉言善行，及我朝懿範奎章，條答無遺，信策手也。〕　趙王
考試官學正汪　批：〔條答詳明，可取。〕
考試官教授林　批：〔叙古頌今，最為切當，非深於治道者不能，欽羨，欽羨。〕

行而世為天下法，言而世為天下則。此聖人所以為天地立心，為生民立命，為萬世開太平者也。前乎二帝三王，所以繼天立極者此也；後乎我朝列聖，所以繼往開來者靡非此乎！且聖人者出，中天地而立，身綱常之寄，其道豈有他哉？亦惟身教、言教二者，相須而並行焉。稽之於古，如明峻德而慎徽五典，允迪厥德而克諧以孝，克舜之身教也；祗台德先而懋貽大德，緝熙敬止而細行
translation_en:
First Policy Question

Associate Examiner and Subprefectural Instructor (Xuezheng) Chen comments: [Regarding the question on the substance of teaching by personal example and teaching by words—which many in the National University [?] do not know how to discuss [? 問李正太學中多不知言今身教言教之實]—this essay alone is able to answer item by item without omission, drawing upon the fine words and good deeds of antiquity as well as the admirable models and imperial writings of our dynasty. Truly the hand of a master of policy essays!] Candidate: Zhao Wang 趙王 [?].

Examiner and Subprefectural Instructor (Xuezheng) Wang comments: [The item-by-item answers are detailed and clear; worthy of selection.]

Examiner and Prefectural Instructor (Jiaoshou) Lin comments: [Its narration of antiquity and eulogy of the present are most fitting and appropriate. None who is not deeply versed in the Way of governance could achieve this. Admirable, truly admirable!]

When he acts, for generations it serves as a model for All under Heaven; when he speaks, for generations it serves as a standard for All under Heaven. This is whereby the sage establishes the mind for Heaven and Earth, establishes destiny for the living people, and opens up supreme peace for ten thousand generations. In earlier times, this was whereby the Two Emperors and Three Kings succeeded Heaven and established the supreme standard; in later times, is not this also whereby the successive sacred emperors of our dynasty have carried on the past and opened up the future? Moreover, when a sage emerges, he stands in the center between Heaven and Earth, embodying in his person the charge of the Three Bonds and Five Constant Virtues—how could his Way be anything other than this? It is simply that teaching by personal example and teaching by words are mutually necessary and practiced together. Examining this in antiquity: illuminating lofty virtue and cautiously beautifying the Five Canons, sincerely pursuing his virtue and being able to harmonize through filial piety—this was the teaching by personal example of Yao [克, OCR for 堯] and Shun; revering his own virtue first and earnestly bequeathing [貽, OCR for 昭] great virtue, continuing luminous and reverent comportment and even in minor conduct…

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
亦於禹湯文武之身教也咨舜以允執厥中命
契以勞來匡直與夫危微精一之訓欽四□工
之語非堯舜之言教乎甄訓言以貽孫子而色
荒禽荒之戒具制官刑以儆有位而三風十愆
之訓明與夫毖酒之教皇極之訓非禹湯文武
之言教乎是以萬邦協和四方風動文命四敷
而兆民允懷西土怙冒而丕單稱德民之從教
治之隆盛無以加矣洪惟我
朝
===
太祖高皇帝備至聖之資創一統之業褒崇
先帝隆武王尊親之孝分封諸王敦帝克睦族之仁
祖訓一篇允矣家國之元龜
大誥三編貽乎臣民之至寶身教言教揆之二帝
三王符節相合也
太宗文皇帝懋德建中端一身以出治慮人心善孝
有未協也輯
為善陰隲
孝順事實二書以勸俗勵乎
punctuated: 亦於——禹、湯、文、武之身教也。咨舜以「允執厥中」，命契以「勞來匡直」，與夫「危微精一」之訓、「欽四□工」之語，非堯、舜之言教乎？甄訓言以貽孫子，而「色荒禽荒」之戒具；制官刑以儆有位，而「三風十愆」之訓明；與夫毖酒之教、皇極之訓，非禹、湯、文、武之言教乎？是以萬邦協和，四方風動，文命四敷而兆民允懷，西土怙冒而丕單稱德，民之從教、治之隆盛，無以加矣。洪惟我朝太祖高皇帝，備至聖之資，創一統之業，褒崇先帝，隆武王尊親之孝；分封諸王，敦帝克睦族之仁。《祖訓》一篇，允矣家國之元龜；《大誥》三編，貽乎臣民之至寶。身教、言教，揆之二帝、三王，符節相合也。太宗文皇帝，懋德建中，端一身以出治；慮人心善孝有未協也，輯《為善陰隲》、《孝順事實》二書以勸俗，勵乎
translation_en:
…also mindful [of even small matters]—this was the teaching by personal example of Yu, Tang, King Wen, and King Wu. Consulting Shun with the charge to "sincerely hold fast the Mean," commanding Xie to "encourage them to come, restore them to straightness," along with the admonition on the "precariousness [of the human mind] and subtlety [of the mind of the Way], refined and single-minded," and the words "reverently [attend to the] four [neighbors?], [brighten] the works"—were these not the teaching by words of Yao and Shun? Fashioning instructive words to bequeath to grandsons and sons, wherein the warnings against "excess in women and excess in hunting" were set forth in full; instituting official punishments to warn those in office, whereby the admonition regarding the "three evil customs and ten offenses" was made clear; together with the teaching on caution against wine and the instruction on the Supreme Ultimate—were these not the teaching by words of Yu, Tang, King Wen, and King Wu? Therefore, the myriad states were brought into harmony and the four quarters were moved as by the wind; cultural mandates were spread in all four directions and the millions of people sincerely cherished [virtue]; the western lands looked up to [them] as a sheltering canopy and great and small alike praised [their] virtue. The people's compliance with teaching and the flourishing abundance of governance could not be surpassed!

Reflecting deeply upon our Dynasty: Emperor Gao, the Grand Progenitor (Taizu), endowed with the qualities of the utmost sage, founded the enterprise of grand unification. In honoring and exalting his imperial ancestors, he heightened the filial piety of King Wu in revering his kin; in enfeoffing the various princes, he strengthened the benevolence of Emperor Yao [reading 克 as 堯] in harmonizing his clan. The single work Ancestral Injunctions (Zuxun) is truly the great divination tortoise for family and state; the three parts of the Grand Pronouncements (Dagao) are a supreme treasure bequeathed to officials and people. His teaching by personal example and teaching by words, when measured against the Two Emperors and Three Kings, match like two halves of a tally. Emperor Wen, the Grand Ancestor (Taizong), cultivated virtue and established the Mean, rectifying his own person to issue forth governance. Concerned that in people's minds goodness and filial piety might not yet be in full accord, he compiled the two books Secret Blessings for Doing Good (Weishan yinzhi) and True Exemplars of Filial Piety (Xiaoshun shishi) to encourage popular customs, inspiringly…

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
綸音之渙發
宣宗章皇帝法
祖敬
天備一德以守文憲天下綱常有未正也製
五倫一書以導民郁乎
睿藻之輝煌身教言教質之二帝三王軌轍相同
也方今
聖皇在上克篤前烈益弘文教崇大孝於
慈闈溥至恩於同姓緝熙
===
聖學臨幸辟雍頒
明詔懇懇乎求賢養老之言發
德音切切乎制治保邦之訓是以綱舉目張而政
治為之脩明禮備樂和而教化為之洋溢人稷
契戶程朱大回淳古之風家詩書俗仁讓丕變
雍熙之治駕唐虞而越三代矣夫豈漢唐宋之
可擬哉愚何幸躬逢其盛
第二問
punctuated:
綸音之渙發。宣宗章皇帝法祖敬天，備一德以守文，憲天下綱常有未正也，製《五倫》一書以導民，郁乎睿藻之輝煌。身教、言教，質之二帝三王，軌轍相同也。

方今聖皇在上，克篤前烈，益弘文教，崇大孝於慈闈，溥至恩於同姓，緝熙聖學，臨幸辟雍，頒明詔，懇懇乎求賢養老之言，發德音，切切乎制治保邦之訓。是以綱舉目張而政治為之脩明，禮備樂和而教化為之洋溢。人稷、契，戶程、朱，大回淳古之風；家《詩》、《書》，俗仁讓，丕變雍熙之治，駕唐、虞而越三代矣，夫豈漢、唐、宋之可擬哉？愚何幸躬逢其盛！

第二問
translation_en:
… the dissemination of His Imperial Words! Emperor Xuanzong Zhang (the Xuande Emperor) modeled himself on his ancestors and revered Heaven, perfecting pure virtue to maintain civil rule. Concerned [reading 憲 as 慮] that the cardinal principles and constant virtues throughout the realm were not yet rectified, he composed the book Book of the Five Relationships (Wulun shu) to guide the people—how resplendent was the brilliance of his imperial literary composition! In teaching by personal example and teaching by words, when measured against the Two Emperors and Three Kings, their tracks are identical.

At present, the Sacred Emperor is on the throne. Capable of consolidating the achievements of his predecessors and further expanding civil education, he exalts great filial piety toward the Empress Dowager's palace, extends the utmost grace to the imperial clan, and continuously illuminates his sacred learning. He has personally visited the Imperial University (Biyong), promulgated bright edicts with earnest words on seeking the worthy and nourishing the aged, and issued benevolent decrees with urgent instructions on securing order and preserving the state. Therefore, the main ropes are lifted and the mesh opens, so governance becomes well-ordered and clear; rites are complete and music is harmonious, so moral transformation overflows. Every person is a Ji or Xie, and every household a Cheng or Zhu, greatly restoring the customs of pure antiquity; every family studies the Odes and Documents, and the customs are humane and yielding, grandly transforming into a reign of harmonious peace. It surpasses Tang and Yu and transcends the Three Dynasties—how could Han, Tang, or Song possibly be compared to it? How fortunate am I to personally witness its flourishing!

Second Question

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭張 批〔策場正欲觀士子學識此卷斟酌廟廷　議禮尤爲允當他日〕
臨帖有聞必不遺予矣
同考試官教諭陳 批〔此策善答所問較之前二場允稱其士　林之翹楚者〕
同考試官教諭鄭 批〔場中能條答六藝者衆然於議祀禮處　多無的見此策斟酌得宜必有識之士也〕
考試官學正汪 批〔六藝一策隨問隨答足見博古通今之學〕
考試官教授林 批〔條答詳明綽有的見〕
===
對六藝之用於古者當考其詳祀禮之行於今
者當揆以義六藝之所先者禮而禮之所重者
祭此皆吾儒之所當講所以不能不屢執事之
問也粤稽諸古周禮大司徒所以教萬民而賓
興之者六藝其一也禮所以教之中有五禮焉
吉禮十有二所謂禋祀實柴槱燎血祭之類是
也凶禮五所謂喪荒弔禬恤之屬是也賓禮八
非朝宗覲遇會同問視之謂乎軍禮五非師均
田役封之謂乎飲食冠昏賓射饗燕脤膰賀慶
punctuated:
同考試官教諭張批：〔策場正欲觀士子學識，此卷斟酌廟廷議禮，尤爲允當。他日〕臨帖有聞，必不遺予矣。
同考試官教諭陳批：〔此策善答所問，較之前二場，允稱其士林之翹楚者。〕
同考試官教諭鄭批：〔場中能條答六藝者衆，然於議祀禮處多無的見。此策斟酌得宜，必有識之士也。〕
考試官學正汪批：〔六藝一策，隨問隨答，足見博古通今之學。〕
考試官教授林批：〔條答詳明，綽有的見。〕

對：六藝之用於古者，當考其詳；祀禮之行於今者，當揆以義。六藝之所先者禮，而禮之所重者祭，此皆吾儒之所當講，所以不能不屢執事之問也。粤稽諸古，《周禮》大司徒所以教萬民而賓興之者，六藝其一也。禮所以教之中，有五禮焉：吉禮十有二，所謂禋祀、實柴、槱燎、血祭之類是也；凶禮五，所謂喪、荒、弔、禬、恤之屬是也；賓禮八，非朝、宗、覲、遇、會、同、問、視之謂乎？軍禮五，非師、均、田、役、封之謂乎？飲食、冠、昏、賓射、饗燕、脤膰、賀慶，
translation_en:
Associate Examiner and Instructor Zhang comments: [The policy session is precisely where we wish to observe a candidate's learning and insight. This paper's deliberation on court discussions of ritual is especially fitting and proper. Some day, when] he is summoned before the throne [?] and gains renown, he will surely not let me down.
Associate Examiner and Instructor Chen comments: [This policy essay answers the question well. Compared with his work in the first two sessions, he truly deserves to be called an outstanding talent among the literati.]
Associate Examiner and Instructor Zheng comments: [In the examination hall there are many who can answer item by item concerning the Six Arts, yet when it comes to discussing sacrificial rituals, most lack definite insight. This policy essay deliberates appropriately; he must be a scholar of discernment.]
Examiner and Director of Studies Wang comments: [In this policy essay on the Six Arts, he answers each point as it is asked, which is enough to show learning that is well-versed in antiquity and conversant with the present.]
Examiner and Instructor Lin comments: [His itemized answers are detailed and clear, showing ample and definite insight.]

Response: As for the application of the Six Arts in antiquity, we ought to examine their details; as for the practice of sacrificial rituals in the present day, we ought to measure them by righteous principle. What comes first among the Six Arts is ritual, and what is most important in ritual is sacrifice. All of these are matters that we Confucians ought to discuss, and that is why they could not but trouble Your Excellency to ask about them. Examining antiquity, in the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli), among the means by which the Grand Minister of Education (dasitu) taught the myriad people and presented them as guests to the court, the Six Arts were one. Ritual is the means of teaching centrality, and within it there are the Five Rituals: the Auspicious Rituals number twelve, which are what are called the pure sacrifice (yinsi), the burnt offering on a pile of wood (shichai), the piled-wood beacon offering (youliao), the blood sacrifice (xueji), and the like; the Inauspicious Rituals number five, which are what are called rites for mourning (sang), famine (huang), condolence (diao), relief after disaster (gui), and commiseration after invasion (xu), and the like; as for the eight Guest Rituals, do they not refer to spring court visits (chao), summer court visits (zong), autumn audiences (jin), winter encounters (yu), occasional assemblies (hui), general audiences (tong), inquiries (wen), and ceremonial inspections (shi)? As for the five Military Rituals, do they not refer to mobilization of armies (shi), equalization of imposts (jun), hunting expeditions (tian), labor services (yi), and the demarcation of boundaries (feng)? Rites of food and drink, capping, wedding, guest archery, feasts and banquets, sharing sacrificial meat (fanfan), and felicitations and celebrations…

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
又嘉禮之有六也此五禮節目之詳可知矣樂
所以教之和有六樂焉黄帝之樂曰雲門周人
冬至舞之以祀天神帝堯之樂曰咸池周人夏
至舞之以祀地祇大磬舜樂也周人祭四望則
舞之大夏禹樂也周人祭大川則舞之湯有大
濩之樂周人舞之以祭姜嫄武王作大武之樂
周人舞之以祭宗廟此周人用樂之不同可知
矣射所以觀德行御所以正驅馳射有五曰白
矢參連剡注襄尺井儀焉御有五曰鳴和鸞逐
===
水曲過君表舞交衢逐禽左焉此射御之節目
也書以見心畫數以盡事變書有六曰象形會
意轉注處事假借諧聲而已數有九曰方田粟
布衰分少廣商功均輸盈朒方程勾股而已此
書數之名義也六藝之中禮樂為先禮莫重於
祭而祭必有義若顔曾思身任道統之傳其配
享於孔子也固宜然顔路曾晳孔鯉父也顔曰
曾參孔伋子也以道統之傳論之則父固不及
於子然而古者立廟尊以明人倫烏有子而可
punctuated:
又嘉禮之有六也。此五禮節目之詳可知矣。樂所以教之和，有六樂焉：黄帝之樂曰《雲門》，周人冬至舞之以祀天神；帝堯之樂曰《咸池》，周人夏至舞之以祀地祇；《大磬》，舜樂也，周人祭四望則舞之；《大夏》，禹樂也，周人祭大川則舞之；湯有《大濩》之樂，周人舞之以祭姜嫄；武王作《大武》之樂，周人舞之以祭宗廟。此周人用樂之不同可知矣。射所以觀德行，御所以正驅馳。射有五：曰白矢、參連、剡注、襄尺、井儀焉；御有五：曰鳴和鸞、逐水曲、過君表、舞交衢、逐禽左焉。此射、御之節目也。書以見心畫，數以盡事變。書有六：曰象形、會意、轉注、處事、假借、諧聲而已；數有九：曰方田、粟布、衰分、少廣、商功、均輸、盈朒、方程、勾股而已。此書、數之名義也。

六藝之中，禮、樂為先；禮莫重於祭，而祭必有義。若顔、曾、思身任道統之傳，其配享於孔子也固宜。然顔路、曾晳、孔鯉，父也；顔曰、曾參、孔伋，子也。以道統之傳論之，則父固不及於子；然而古者立廟，尊以明人倫，烏有子而可
translation_en:
…are in turn the six types of felicitous rites. From this, the detailed items of the Five Rites can be known. Music is that by which harmony is taught, and there are Six Musics: the music of the Yellow Emperor is called Yunmen (Cloud Gate), which the people of Zhou danced at the winter solstice to sacrifice to the heavenly spirits; the music of Emperor Yao is called Xianchi (All-Embracing Pond), which the people of Zhou danced at the summer solstice to sacrifice to the earthly deities; Daqing [for Dashao 大韶, Great Succession] is the music of Shun, which the people of Zhou danced when sacrificing to the Four Vistas; Daxia (Great Xia) is the music of Yu, which the people of Zhou danced when sacrificing to the great rivers; Tang had the music of Dahuo (Great Protection), which the people of Zhou danced to sacrifice to Jiang Yuan; and King Wu created the music of Dawu (Great Martial), which the people of Zhou danced to sacrifice in the ancestral temple. From this, the differences in how the people of Zhou employed music can be known. Archery is that by which virtuous conduct is observed, and charioteering is that by which driving and galloping are rectified. There are five techniques of archery: namely, "white arrowhead" (baishi, shooting clean through the target), "thrice-linked" (sanlian, firing three arrows in succession), "pointed-downward shot" (yanzhu), "yielding a foot" (xiangchi, stepping back a foot from the lord), and "well-formation deportment" (jingyi, four arrows piercing the target in a square). There are five techniques of charioteering: namely, "harmonizing the bells" (ming heluan), "following the bends of the river" (zhu shuiqu), "passing the ruler's markers" (guo junbiao), "circling at the crossroads" (wu jiaoqu), and "driving game to the left" (zhu qinzuo). These are the specific items of archery and charioteering. Calligraphy is to manifest the delineations of the mind, and mathematics is to exhaust the permutations of affairs. There are six principles of script: namely, pictographs (xiangxing), compound ideographs (huiyi), derivative cognates (zhuanzhu), indicative symbols (chushi), phonetic loans (jiajie), and形-and-sound compounds (xiesheng), and that is all. There are nine categories of mathematics: namely, field measurement (fangtian), millet and cloth exchange (subu), proportional distribution (cufen), diminishing breadths (shaoguang), consultations on engineering works (shanggong), equitable taxation and transport (junshu), excess and deficit (yingnu), rectangular arrays (fangcheng), and base and altitude of right triangles (gougu), and that is all. These are the names and meanings of calligraphy and mathematics.

Among the Six Arts, rites and music come first; among rites, none is more important than sacrifice, and sacrifice must have its right principle. Figures such as Yan [Hui], Zeng [Shen], and Zisi personally bore the transmission of the Successive Orthodoxy of the Way (daotong), so that they should be associated in the sacrifices (peixiang) to Confucius is certainly fitting. Yet Yan Lu, Zeng Xi, and Kong Li were the fathers; Yan Hui [transcribed as 曰], Zeng Shen, and Kong Ji (Zisi) were the sons. Judged in terms of the transmission of the Orthodoxy of the Way, the fathers certainly did not equal the sons; yet when the ancients established temples, they revered them in order to clarify human moral relations—how could there be a son who may…

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
以先父乎子雖齊聖不先父食故禹不先鯀湯
不先契文武不先不窋其理章章乎明矣子配
享堂上父從祀廡間雖道統攸繫顏曾思之心
其安乎哉然禮因人情莫若別立後寢主之以
孔叔梁紇配之以顏路曾晳孔鯉則彝倫以明
道統益尊而父子之間兩無礙矣若夫周子以
自得之學而著太極易通之旨兩程以誠敬之
學而接孔孟道學之傳張子訂頑砭愚而西銘
有作朱子開來繼往而孔道大明此五子所以
===
有功於前聖有功於後學而朱子則集諸儒之
大成其功尤多也以五子從祀兩廡而不獲乎
配享亦以世之先後而為之耳以德行論則五
子固不下於子貢以下之諸賢而功則倍之以
著述論則五子又多於鄭康成以下之諸儒而
理則過之然禮以義起以周程張朱配享廟廷
而儕於顏曾思孟之列則道學益顯祀典大明
而天下之公議未必不以為當也至於古樂之
亡久矣秦漢去周未遠其器與聲猶有存者逮
punctuated: 以先父乎？「子雖齊聖，不先父食。」故禹不先鯀，湯不先契，文、武不先不窋，其理章章乎明矣。子配享堂上，父從祀廡間，雖道統攸繫，顏、曾、思之心其安乎哉？然禮因人情，莫若別立後寢，主之以孔叔梁紇，配之以顏路、曾晳、孔鯉，則彝倫以明，道統益尊，而父子之間兩無礙矣。若夫周子以自得之學而著《太極》、《易通》之旨，兩程以誠敬之學而接孔、孟道學之傳，張子訂頑砭愚而《西銘》有作，朱子開來繼往而孔道大明，此五子所以有功於前聖，有功於後學，而朱子則集諸儒之大成，其功尤多也。以五子從祀兩廡而不獲乎配享，亦以世之先後而為之耳。以德行論，則五子固不下於子貢以下之諸賢，而功則倍之；以著述論，則五子又多於鄭康成以下之諸儒，而理則過之。然禮以義起，以周、程、張、朱配享廟廷，而儕於顏、曾、思、孟之列，則道學益顯，祀典大明，而天下之公議未必不以為當也。至於古樂之亡久矣，秦、漢去周未遠，其器與聲猶有存者，逮
translation_en:
… precede a father? "Even though a son be a sage of equal perfection, he does not partake of the sacrificial offerings before his father." Thus Yu 禹 did not precede Gun 鯀, Tang 湯 did not precede Xie 契, and Kings Wen 文 and Wu 武 did not precede Buzhu 不窋; the principle behind this is abundantly clear. When the sons share in the main sacrifices up in the hall while their fathers are accorded merely secondary sacrifices down in the side-corridors, even though this is tied to the transmission of the Way, how could the hearts of Yan Hui 顏回, Zeng Shen 曾參, and Zisi 子思 be at ease? Yet ritual is rooted in human feelings. Nothing would be better than to establish a separate rear shrine with Kong Shuliang He 孔叔梁紇 as the principal spirit, joined as associates by Yan Lu 顏路, Zeng Xi 曾晳, and Kong Li 孔鯉. Then the constant human relationships would be made clear, the transmission of the Way would be even more revered, and between fathers and sons there would be no hindrance on either side.

As for Master Zhou (Zhou Dunyi 周敦頤), through the learning he attained for himself he set forth the purport of the Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate (Taijitu 太極圖) and Penetrating the Book of Changes (Yitong 易通); the two Cheng brothers (Cheng Hao 程顥 and Cheng Yi 程頤), through their learning of sincerity and reverence, continued the transmission of the Learning of the Way from Confucius and Mencius; Master Zhang (Zhang Zai 張載) corrected the obstinate and remedied the foolish by composing the Western Inscription (Ximing 西銘); and Master Zhu (Zhu Xi 朱熹) opened the way for future generations while carrying on the past, thereby making the Way of Confucius shine brightly. This is how these Five Masters rendered meritorious service both to the former sages and to later scholars—while Master Zhu synthesized the great achievements of all the Confucian scholars, so his merit is greatest of all. That these Five Masters receive only secondary sacrifices in the two side-corridors without being granted the honor of sharing in the main sacrifices is simply due to the chronological order of the eras in which they lived. Judged by moral conduct, the Five Masters are certainly not inferior to the worthies from Zigong 子貢 downward, while their merit is double theirs; judged by their writings, the Five Masters have produced even more than the scholars from Zheng Kangcheng (Zheng Xuan 鄭玄) downward, while the principles they expounded surpass theirs. Now, ritual arises from righteousness: if Zhou, the Cheng brothers, Zhang, and Zhu were elevated to share in the sacrifices in the main temple hall, ranked alongside Yan Hui, Zeng Shen, Zisi, and Mencius, then the Learning of the Way would become ever more illustrious, the sacrificial canon would be made brilliantly clear, and public opinion throughout the realm would surely not fail to deem it fitting.

As for ancient music, it has long been lost. Since the Qin and Han dynasties were not yet far removed from the Zhou, some of its instruments and melodies still survived. Coming down…

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
乎後世有私孝孫之所參和峴之所制王朴之
論徒徇其末而不知其本是以愈多而愈不遠
也迨蔡季通之作律呂新書此朱子之所以深
取焉雖然稽古禮文固學者急務然而朝廷禮
議愚已略陳於前矣若夫律呂本原蔡氏新書
詳悉無遺至於先求聲氣之元則存乎其人焉
愚生學識膚淺斟酌未得其宜也推詳未獲其
要也姑撮其大畧為執事言倘以為可與而進
之則挾此而往以俟
聖天子臨軒之問
第三問
同考試官教諭沈　批〔士生百世下而欲辨□□人於百世之上使是非□□□□□□□□□□□□□□〕
羅□
考試官學正汪　批〔當今人心非博學洽聞胸中有□□□□□□□□□□〕
考試官教授林　批〔有考據有□□□□□□□□□□□〕
punctuated:
乎後世，有私孝孫之所參、和峴之所制、王朴之論，徒徇其末而不知其本，是以愈多而愈不遠也。迨蔡季通之作《律呂新書》，此朱子之所以深取焉。雖然，稽古禮文固學者急務，然而朝廷禮議，愚已略陳於前矣。若夫律呂本原，《蔡氏新書》詳悉無遺；至於先求聲氣之元，則存乎其人焉。愚生學識膚淺，斟酌未得其宜也，推詳未獲其要也。姑撮其大畧為執事言，倘以為可與而進之，則挾此而往，以俟聖天子臨軒之問。
第三問
同考試官教諭沈　批〔士生百世下，而欲辨□□人於百世之上，使是非□□□□□□□□□□□□□□〕
羅□
考試官學正汪　批〔當今人心，非博學洽聞、胸中有□□□□□□□□□□〕
考試官教授林　批〔有考據，有□□□□□□□□□□□〕
translation_en:
…to later ages, there were the revisions of Zu Xiaosun [transcribed as 私孝孫][?], the regulations established by He Xian, and the discourses of Wang Pu. They merely pursued the superficial branches without understanding the fundamental root; therefore, the more numerous their efforts became, the less far-reaching they were [?]. Only when Cai Jitong (Cai Yuanding) composed the New Treatise on Pitch-Pipes (Lülü xinshu) did Master Zhu (Zhu Xi) find something to deeply approve of. Even so, investigating ancient ritual texts is certainly an urgent task for scholars, yet regarding the ritual deliberations of the court, I, in my foolishness, have already briefly set them forth above. As for the fundamental origins of the pitch-pipes, Mr. Cai's New Treatise is thorough and leaves nothing out; when it comes to first seeking the primal source of sound and vital breath (qi), however, that depends upon the right person. I, a foolish student, am of shallow learning and understanding: in weighing matters I have not attained what is appropriate, and in investigating details I have not grasped the essential points. For now, I have gathered the general outline to speak of it before Your Reverences. Should you deem me worthy of endorsement and advancement, I shall carry this forth to await the Sacred Son of Heaven's personal questioning at the Palace Examination.

Third Question
Associate Examiner and Instructor Shen comments: [For a scholar born a hundred generations later to wish to distinguish […] people a hundred generations before, causing right and wrong […] (14 illegible characters).]
Luo […]
Examiner and Director of Studies Wang comments: [Matches people's minds today [?]; without broad learning, wide knowledge, and having within one's breast […] (10 illegible characters).]
Examiner and Instructor Lin comments: [It possesses evidential grounding, and possesses […] (11 illegible characters).]

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
權然後知輕重度然後知長短故君子於事□
之來度以本然之權度則天下無難處之事矣
夫事莫不有是非亦莫不有利害是非利害混
於一途則當酌其輕重以制事焉法重於恩割
恩以伸法可也恩重於法屈法以續恩可也法
恩具重則又當委曲而兩全之焉古之人有處
之者矣事重于身於是乎舍生取義寧□重于親
於是乎不告而娶事重于天下於是乎竊負而
逃訢然樂而忘天下如此則天下無難處之事
===
矣愚嘗讀史而觀古人之遇事變如孰事所舉
者未嘗不歎其不幸而際此兩難也然豈無道
以處之乎夫父既犯法曲護而保全之必不得
已復命于朝行而竊負以逃□□□為過石奢之
死陋矣如父何吾□肯□□□□□親君子是之
蓋國為重家為輕也毋有賊李寒告而求生之
以不得已委城于將佐而輕身赴母亦奚為失
趙苞之事忠矣如毋何故徐庶請辭先主程子
是之蓋母為重功為輕也懷光之逆李瓘逃以
punctuated: 權然後知輕重，度然後知長短。故君子於事□之來，度以本然之權度，則天下無難處之事矣。夫事莫不有是非，亦莫不有利害。是非利害混於一途，則當酌其輕重以制事焉。法重於恩，割恩以伸法可也；恩重於法，屈法以續恩可也；法恩具重，則又當委曲而兩全之焉，古之人有處之者矣。事重于身，於是乎舍生取義；寧□重于親，於是乎不告而娶；事重于天下，於是乎竊負而逃，訢然樂而忘天下。如此，則天下無難處之事矣。愚嘗讀史，而觀古人之遇事變如孰事所舉者，未嘗不歎其不幸而際此兩難也，然豈無道以處之乎？夫父既犯法，曲護而保全之；必不得已，復命于朝，行而竊負以逃，□□□為過？石奢之死陋矣，如父何？吾□肯□□□□□親，君子是之，蓋國為重、家為輕也。毋有賊，李寒告而求生之；以不得已，委城于將佐，而輕身赴母，亦奚為失？趙苞之事忠矣，如毋何？故徐庶請辭先主，程子是之，蓋母為重、功為輕也。懷光之逆，李瓘逃以
translation_en:
By weighing, one knows what is light and what is heavy; by measuring, one knows what is long and what is short. Therefore, when a gentleman is confronted with the arrival of affairs and contingencies [?], if he measures them by the inherent standard of weighing and measuring, there will be no affair in the world that is difficult to handle. Now, every affair has its right and wrong, and also its benefit and harm. When right and wrong, benefit and harm are mingled together in a single situation, one must deliberate over their relative weight in order to regulate the affair. When the law outweighs grace, it is permissible to sever grace in order to uphold the law; when grace outweighs the law, it is permissible to bend the law in order to preserve grace; when both law and grace are heavy, then one should find an accommodating way to preserve both—men of antiquity had ways of handling this. When a matter outweighs one's own life, one gives up life and chooses righteousness; when continuing posterity [?] outweighs disobeying one's parents, one marries without first informing them; when a matter outweighs the Empire, one secretly carries one's father on one's back and flees, joyfully forgetting the Empire. In this way, there is no affair in the world that is difficult to handle.

I have read history and observed how men of antiquity encountered emergencies such as those cited by Your Excellency [the Examiner], and I have never failed to sigh over their misfortune in meeting with such dilemmas; yet how could there be no way to handle them? When one's father has violated the law, one should go to every length to shield and preserve him; if there is truly no alternative, one may report back to the court and then secretly carry him on one's back and flee—how could [this] be a fault? The death of Shi She 石奢 was narrow-minded indeed; what good did it do his father? That Wu [Shang 伍尚?] was willing [?] to [...] his parent, the gentleman approves of it, for the state was weightier and the family lighter. When one's mother is held by bandits, one should report it in tears [?] and seek to save her life; if there is no alternative, to entrust the city to one's subordinate officers and go alone to one's mother—how would that be a mistake? Zhao Bao's 趙苞 conduct was loyal indeed, yet what of his mother? Thus when Xu Shu 徐庶 asked to take leave of the Former Lord (Liu Bei 劉備), Master Cheng (Cheng Yi 程頤) approved of it, for his mother was weightier and meritorious achievement lighter. In the rebellion of Li Huaiguang 李懷光, had Li Guan 李瓘 fled in order to…

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
諫其父進以告〔君死可哀矣子南之誅棄〕
既不諫其君又不告其父死何益邪父與夫孰
重而可逆其父然順父以害夫亦非也雍姬於
是乎失君與友孰重而敢逆其君然順君以誅
友亦非也左儒於是乎得王導雖弟〔王〕臣也王
敦雖兄國賊也當是之時知有天下不知有其
兄自附周公殆非過矣建成無功太子也秦王
有功藩王也當是之際但知有兄不知有天下
自附子臧豈至此乎無忌之命縮高是以父攻
===
子也在子不可拒在父不可往高之辭適宜矣
武后之討敬業是以逆攻順也僞周不可附敬
業不可討孝逸之功爲罪矣武宗君也宣宗嘗
北面而事之可以叔而加其君乎是未知春秋
之議逆祀也守禮父也世世宗不由空桑而生可
以天子而臣其父乎是未知孟子之論北山也
薄昭之罪赦之固不可誅之亦未當先正謂當
上慰母心斯可也濮園之議稱親固不可稱伯
亦未安先儒謂當增一父字庶幾也維州之取
punctuated: 諫其父，進以告〔君，死可哀矣；子南之誅，棄〕既不諫其君，又不告其父，死何益邪？父與夫孰重，而可逆其父？然順父以害夫，亦非也，雍姬於是乎失。君與友孰重，而敢逆其君？然順君以誅友，亦非也，左儒於是乎得。王導雖弟，〔王〕臣也；王敦雖兄，國賊也。當是之時，知有天下，不知有其兄，自附周公，殆非過矣。建成無功，太子也；秦王有功，藩王也。當是之際，但知有兄，不知有天下，自附子臧，豈至此乎？無忌之命縮高，是以父攻子也。在子不可拒，在父不可往，高之辭適宜矣。武后之討敬業，是以逆攻順也。僞周不可附，敬業不可討，孝逸之功爲罪矣。武宗，君也，宣宗嘗北面而事之，可以叔而加其君乎？是未知《春秋》之議逆祀也。守禮，父也，世世宗不由空桑而生，可以天子而臣其父乎？是未知《孟子》之論《北山》也。薄昭之罪，赦之固不可，誅之亦未當，先正謂當上慰母心，斯可也。濮園之議，稱親固不可，稱伯亦未安，先儒謂當增一「父」字，庶幾也。維州之取…
translation_en: …remonstrated with his father, and coming forward reported it [to his ruler; his death was lamentable indeed. In the execution of Zinan, Qiji (?)] neither remonstrated with his ruler nor informed his father—what good did his death do? Between father and husband, which is weightier, such that one could defy one's father? Yet to obey one's father so as to harm one's husband is also wrong; in this, Yong Ji erred. Between ruler and friend, which is weightier, such that one would dare defy one's ruler? Yet to obey one's ruler so as to execute a friend is also wrong; in this, Zuo Ru got it right. Although Wang Dao was the younger brother, he was a [royal] minister; although Wang Dun was the elder brother, he was a traitor to the state. At that time, to know only that there was the empire and not that he had an elder brother, comparing himself to the Duke of Zhou, was hardly an excess. Although Jiancheng lacked merit, he was the Heir Apparent; although the Prince of Qin had merit, he was a feudatory prince. At that juncture, had he known only that he had an elder brother and not that there was the empire, comparing himself to Zizang, how would it have come to that? When Wuji commanded Suo Gao, it was to use a father to attack his son. On the son's part he could not resist, and on the father's part he could not go; Suo Gao's refusal was quite proper. When Empress Wu suppressed Jingye, it was to use rebellion to attack legitimacy. The usurping Zhou should not have been adhered to, and Jingye should not have been suppressed; thus Xiaoyi's merit became a crime. Emperor Wuzong was the ruler, and Emperor Xuanzong had once faced north to serve him as a subject; could he then place himself above his ruler because he was an uncle? This is not to understand the Spring and Autumn Annals' (Chunqiu) critique of reversing the sacrificial order. Shouli was the father, and Emperor Shizong [Xuanzong (?)] was not born out of a hollow mulberry tree; could he then treat his father as a subject because he was the Son of Heaven? This is not to understand the Mencius's (Mengzi) discussion of the ode "Northern Mountain" (Beishan). As for Bo Zhao's crime, to pardon him was certainly impossible, yet to execute him was also inappropriate; former worthies said one ought to comfort the mother's heart above, and that would suffice. In the debate over the Prince of Pu's ritual status, to call him "parent" (qin) was certainly impossible, yet to call him "uncle" (bo) was also unsettling; former Confucians said one ought to add the character "father" (fu), which would come close to what is right. Regarding the taking of Weizhou…

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
令當以李德裕之言為是益維州本唐故地所
當得也豈可以小信而妨大計靈州之棄守當
以輔臣之言為是蓋靈州乃必爭之地不可棄
也豈可以險要移于夷狄傳曰大夫無遂事又
曰大夫出境有利於社稷者專之可也以是而
酌陳湯之矯制興師不罪可矣又何功乎是難
免乎匡衡之議傳曰殺人而義令勿讎讎又曰父
不受誅子復讎可也以是而論徐元慶之手刃
父讎赦之可矣又何誅乎宜有取乎柳宗元之
駁嗟夫天下之事幸而處其常則易不幸而遇
其變則難使不度於本然之權度其不至背倫
逆理傷恩害義者幾希愚生僭議及此惟執事
有以折衷之
第四問
同考試官教諭謝　批〔格物一窮正欲觀士子學識此作有考據〕
吳秀
考試官學正汪　批〔歸宿非體認親切者不能宜置前列〕
批〔條答天地萬物之理皆鑿鑿有據以為物之〕
punctuated:
令，當以李德裕之言為是。益維州本唐故地，所當得也，豈可以小信而妨大計？靈州之棄守，當以輔臣之言為是。蓋靈州乃必爭之地，不可棄也，豈可以險要移于夷狄？《傳》曰：「大夫無遂事。」又曰：「大夫出境，有利於社稷者，專之可也。」以是而酌陳湯之矯制興師，不罪可矣，又何功乎？是難免乎匡衡之議。《傳》曰：「殺人而義，令勿讎讎。」又曰：「父不受誅，子復讎可也。」以是而論徐元慶之手刃父讎，赦之可矣，又何誅乎？宜有取乎柳宗元之駁。嗟夫！天下之事，幸而處其常則易，不幸而遇其變則難。使不度於本然之權度，其不至背倫逆理、傷恩害義者幾希。愚生僭議及此，惟執事有以折衷之。

第四問
同考試官教諭謝　批〔格物一窮，正欲觀士子學識。此作有考據。〕
吳秀
考試官學正汪　批〔歸宿非體認親切者不能，宜置前列。〕
批〔條答天地萬物之理，皆鑿鑿有據，以為物之〕
translation_en:
…or surrender [of Weizhou 維州], one should take the words of Li Deyu 李德裕 to be right. For Weizhou [reading 益 as 蓋] was originally old Tang territory that ought to be recovered; how could one allow minor trustworthiness to obstruct a grand design? As for abandoning or defending Lingzhou 靈州, one should take the words of the輔臣 (chief minister [Li Hang 李沆]) to be right. For Lingzhou was a strategic point that had to be contested and could not be abandoned; how could one hand a strategic stronghold over to the barbarians?

The Commentary says: "A Grand Master does not act on his own authority." Yet it also says: "Once a Grand Master crosses the border, in matters advantageous to the Altars of Soil and Grain, it is permissible for him to act on his own initiative." Weighing against this Chen Tang's 陳湯 forging an imperial decree to mobilize troops, it would have sufficed not to punish him—what merit could he claim? Thus he could hardly escape the criticism of Kuang Heng 匡衡. The Commentary [Rites of Zhou] says: "Where a killing is righteous, order that no vengeance be taken [reading 讎讎 with redundant character]." And another Commentary [Gongyang] says: "When a father suffers an unjust execution, it is permissible for the son to avenge him." Judging by this Xu Yuanqing's 徐元慶 slaying of his father's enemy with his own hand, it would have sufficed to pardon him—why then execute him? Rightly should one adopt the refutation by Liu Zongyuan 柳宗元.

Alas! In the affairs of the world, when one is fortunate enough to deal with normal circumstances, it is easy; when one is unfortunate enough to encounter extraordinary contingencies, it is difficult. If one does not measure them against the inherent standard of weighing circumstances, rare indeed are those who do not end up violating human relationships, defying principle, harming affection, and injuring righteousness! As a foolish student I have presumptuously discussed matters to this extent; I only pray that Your Excellency will weigh and judge them.

Question Four

Wu Xiu 吳秀

Associate Examiner Xie, Instructor (jiaoyu 教諭), comments: 〔In exhaustively investigating things [? 格物一窮], the very aim is to observe the candidate's learning and insight. This essay is well-grounded in evidence.〕

Examiner Wang, Director of Studies (xuezheng 學正), comments: 〔Its ultimate conclusion is something none could achieve without intimate personal realization; it should be placed in the front ranks.〕 [And] comments: 〔Its itemized responses on the principles of Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things are all solidly substantiated, taking the [principles] of things…〕…

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
理會于一心尤見學識
考試官教授林　批窮理誠身之學此作見之
窮天下之理於萬物會萬物之理於一心天地
萬物本吾一體苟於天下之物無一而不格萬
物之理無一而不窮則天地雖大萬物雖多皆
吾度内豈有性外之物哉請因明問以復其萬
一夫盈天地間者惟萬物天地亦物耳天地非
陰陽不能成天地萬物非陰陽不能成萬物天
地萬物一陰陽也陰陽一太極也天之體圓以
===
氣而依乎地地之體方以形而附乎天天地之
所以自相依附者一太極也天之行徤其旋轉
也當晝則自左旋而向右向夕則自前降而歸
後當夜則右轉而復左將旦則自後升而趨前
然其所以旋轉無窮者亦一太極也以在天成
象者言之風則火氣之化雨則水氣之化金氣
之肅而為霜土氣之升而為露其所以成者陰
陽之氣聚而有跡耳日曰太陽月曰太陰星則
少陽而辰則少陰也其所以運者陰陽之氣升
punctuated:
理會于一心，尤見學識。
考試官教授林　批：窮理誠身之學，此作見之。
窮天下之理於萬物，會萬物之理於一心。天地萬物，本吾一體。苟於天下之物無一而不格，萬物之理無一而不窮，則天地雖大，萬物雖多，皆吾度内，豈有性外之物哉？請因明問以復其萬一。夫盈天地間者惟萬物，天地亦物耳。天地非陰陽不能成天地，萬物非陰陽不能成萬物。天地萬物，一陰陽也；陰陽，一太極也。天之體圓，以氣而依乎地；地之體方，以形而附乎天。天地之所以自相依附者，一太極也。天之行徤，其旋轉也，當晝則自左旋而向右，向夕則自前降而歸後，當夜則右轉而復左，將旦則自後升而趨前，然其所以旋轉無窮者，亦一太極也。以在天成象者言之：風則火氣之化，雨則水氣之化，金氣之肅而為霜，土氣之升而為露，其所以成者，陰陽之氣聚而有跡耳；日曰太陽，月曰太陰，星則少陽，而辰則少陰也，其所以運者，陰陽之氣升
translation_en:
…principles of things converge in the single mind particularly reveals his scholarly insight.

Examiner, Prefectural Director of Studies Lin, comments: The learning of exhausting principles and making the person sincere is seen in this composition.

To exhaust the principles of all under Heaven in the myriad things, and to gather the principles of the myriad things into the single mind: Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things are originally one body with us. If there is not a single thing under Heaven that is not investigated, and not a single principle of the myriad things that is not exhausted, then even though Heaven and Earth are vast and the myriad things are numerous, all are within our measure—how could there be any thing outside our nature? Allow me to follow your perceptive question in order to reply with one ten-thousandth part of it.

Now, what fills the space between Heaven and Earth is only the myriad things, and Heaven and Earth themselves are also things. Without yin and yang, Heaven and Earth cannot form Heaven and Earth; without yin and yang, the myriad things cannot form the myriad things. Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things are one yin and yang; yin and yang are one Supreme Ultimate (taiji). The body of Heaven is round, relying upon Earth through vital force (qi); the body of Earth is square, cleaving to Heaven through physical form. That by which Heaven and Earth mutually rely upon and cleave to each other is the one Supreme Ultimate. The movement of Heaven is vigorous. In its rotation, during the day it revolves from the left and turns toward the right; toward evening it descends from the front and returns to the back; during the night it turns from the right and returns to the left; and near dawn it ascends from the back and hastens to the front. Yet that by which it rotates endlessly is also the one Supreme Ultimate.

Speaking of those things that form phenomena in the heavens: wind is the transformation of the qi of Fire, rain is the transformation of the qi of Water, the austerity of the qi of Metal becomes frost, and the rising of the qi of Earth becomes dew; that by which they are formed is simply the qi of yin and yang gathering and leaving traces. The sun is called Greater Yang (taiyang), the moon is called Greater Yin (taiyin), the stars are Lesser Yang (shaoyang), and the zodiacal spaces (chen) are Lesser Yin (shaoyin); that by which they revolve is simply the qi of yin and yang ascending…

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
而復降耳至於星隕而為石隕化而為斧非怪
誕也在天本氣隕地則成形矣月星無光受日
之光其明一也但月光生於日所照魄生於日
所蔽當日則光消就日則明盡此弦望晦朔所
由分也月質常圓受日之光猶粉塗其半月中
黑處山河之影猶鏡照物顧兔在腹世俗惑也
何莫而非太極為之根柢乎以吾裡成形者言
之人得氣之正氣正而理亦通鳥獸得氣之偏
氣偏而理亦塞然皆有知覺也若夫草木流灌
===
之則敷榮摧折之則枯落謂其無知覺則不可
鳥獸胎而生卵而化五穀草木種而生根而長
謂其無種亦不可至於麒麟之生鍾天地之和
應文明之瑞世不常有豈有種耶魚龍皆鱗族
然魚得陰數故其鱗三十有六積老陰之數也
龍得陽數故其鱗八十有一積老陽之數也草
木皆植物草得陰氣故其質弱木得陽氣故其
質堅草木之分本乎陰陽也海則水流東極氣
盡而散如沃焦釜無有遺餘是以江漢朝宗而
punctuated:
而復降耳。至於星隕而為石，隕化而為斧，非怪誕也，在天本氣，隕地則成形矣。月星無光，受日之光，其明一也。但月光生於日所照，魄生於日所蔽，當日則光消，就日則明盡，此弦、望、晦、朔所由分也。月質常圓，受日之光，猶粉塗其半；月中黑處，山河之影，猶鏡照物；顧兔在腹，世俗惑也。何莫而非太極為之根柢乎？
以吾裡成形者言之：人得氣之正，氣正而理亦通；鳥獸得氣之偏，氣偏而理亦塞，然皆有知覺也。若夫草木，流灌之則敷榮，摧折之則枯落，謂其無知覺則不可。鳥獸胎而生、卵而化，五穀草木種而生、根而長，謂其無種亦不可。至於麒麟之生，鍾天地之和，應文明之瑞，世不常有，豈有種耶？魚龍皆鱗族，然魚得陰數，故其鱗三十有六，積老陰之數也；龍得陽數，故其鱗八十有一，積老陽之數也。草木皆植物，草得陰氣，故其質弱；木得陽氣，故其質堅，草木之分本乎陰陽也。海則水流東極，氣盡而散，如沃焦釜，無有遺餘，是以江漢朝宗而
translation_en:
… and then descends again. As for stars falling and becoming stones, or falling and transforming into axes, this is nothing bizarre or preposterous: in the heavens they are originally vital force (qi), and when they fall to earth they take on physical form. The moon and stars have no light of their own, but receive the light of the sun; their brightness is one and the same. However, the moon's light is produced where the sun shines upon it, and its dark disk (po) is produced where it is shielded from the sun. Facing the sun, the darkness vanishes [at full moon]; approaching the sun, its brightness is exhausted [at new moon]. This is how the quarter moons (xian), the full moon (wang), the last day of the lunar month (hui), and the new moon (shuo) are differentiated. The substance of the moon is always round, and its receiving the light of the sun is like having half of it coated with white powder. The dark places within the moon are the reflections of mountains and rivers, just as a mirror reflects things; the notion of a "gazing hare" in its belly is a vulgar delusion. What among these does not have the Supreme Ultimate (Taiji) as its foundation?

To speak of the things that take physical form on earth [? 吾裡, likely a transcription error for 在地]: humans obtain the uprightness of vital force, and because their vital force is upright, their principle (li) is also penetrative; birds and beasts obtain the partiality of vital force, and because their vital force is partial, their principle is also obstructed—yet all of them possess consciousness and perception. As for grasses and trees, if one waters them they blossom and flourish, and if one breaks them they wither and fall; to say they have no perception will not do. Birds and beasts are born from wombs or hatch from eggs, while the five grains, grasses, and trees sprout from seeds and grow from roots; to say they have no seeds will also not do. Yet as for the birth of the unicorn (qilin), it concentrates the harmony of Heaven and Earth and responds as an auspicious omen to an age of civilized fluorescence; it does not constantly exist in the world, so how could it have a seed? Fish and dragons are both scaly creatures, yet fish obtain the yin number, and therefore their scales are thirty-six, the product of the number of Old Yin (six times six); dragons obtain the yang number, and therefore their scales are eighty-one, the product of the number of Old Yang (nine times nine). Grasses and trees are both plants, yet grasses obtain yin vital force, so their substance is weak; trees obtain yang vital force, so their substance is firm—the distinction between grasses and trees is rooted in yin and yang. As for the sea, water flows to the easternmost extreme, where its vital force is exhausted and dissipates, like pouring water into a scorched cauldron with nothing left over. Therefore, the Yangzi and Han rivers pay court to the sea …

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
日夜而不見其泄百川歸海亘古今而不見其
溢矣何莫而非太極爲之樞紐乎然天地之間
何往而非物何物而非理無一不具於吾之心
學者苟能格物以窮其理窮理以至於誠身則
無適而非仁矣殆見天高地下心之廣也日照
月臨心之明也雲行雨施心之游也山川流峙
心之動靜也飛潛動植心之形見也何者而非
吾性分内乎故曰仁者以天地萬物爲一體管
見如斯惟執事進退
===
第五問
同考試官教諭馮　批〔以仁義爲闢異端之本足見所學其〕
黄表
亦聖人之徒歟
同考試官教諭余　批〔闢異端吾儒分内事也然非所學所養之〕
正不能此策立議嚴整條答詳明他日爲政必有補風教宜
置前列
考試官學正汪　批〔異端一策凛凛正氣使異端之徒聞之〕
亦將逃而歸吾儒矣
punctuated:
日夜而不見其泄，百川歸海，亘古今而不見其溢矣。何莫而非太極爲之樞紐乎？然天地之間，何往而非物？何物而非理？無一不具於吾之心。學者苟能格物以窮其理，窮理以至於誠身，則無適而非仁矣。殆見天高地下，心之廣也；日照月臨，心之明也；雲行雨施，心之游也；山川流峙，心之動靜也；飛潛動植，心之形見也。何者而非吾性分内乎？故曰：「仁者以天地萬物爲一體。」管見如斯，惟執事進退。
第五問
同考試官教諭馮　批〔以仁義爲闢異端之本，足見所學。其〕亦聖人之徒歟！
黄表
同考試官教諭余　批〔闢異端，吾儒分内事也。然非所學所養之〕正不能。此策立議嚴整，條答詳明，他日爲政，必有補風教，宜置前列。
考試官學正汪　批〔異端一策，凛凛正氣，使異端之徒聞之，〕亦將逃而歸吾儒矣。
translation_en:
… day and night without being seen to drain away, and the hundred rivers return to the sea throughout antiquity and the present without being seen to overflow. Which of these does not have the Supreme Ultimate as its pivot? Yet between heaven and earth, where does one go that there are not things, and what thing is there that is not principle? Not a single one fails to be complete within my own mind. If the student can investigate things so as to exhaust their principles, and exhaust principles so as to arrive at making the person sincere, then nowhere he goes will not be humaneness. One will nearly see that the height of heaven and the lowness of earth are the breadth of the mind; the shining of the sun and the approach of the moon are the brightness of the mind; the movement of clouds and the bestowal of rain are the roaming of the mind; the flowing of rivers and the standing of mountains are the activity and stillness of the mind; the flying, submerging, moving, and rooted beings are the manifestations of the mind. Which of these is not within the allotment of my own nature? Therefore it is said: "The humane person takes heaven, earth, and the myriad things as one body." Such is my narrow view; it is solely for Your Excellency to advance or reject it.

Fifth Question
Huang Biao 黄表
Associate Examiner and Instructor (jiaoyu) Feng comments: Taking humaneness and righteousness as the foundation for refuting heterodoxies is sufficient to show what he has learned. Is he not also a disciple of the sages!
Associate Examiner and Instructor (jiaoyu) Yu comments: Refuting heterodoxies is the proper duty of us Confucians. Yet unless what one has learned and cultivated is orthodox, one cannot do so. This policy essay establishes its arguments with rigor and order, and answers point by point with detail and clarity. When he engages in governance in the future, he will surely be of help to moral customs and education; he ought to be placed in the front ranks.
Examiner and Director of Studies (xuezheng) Wang comments: This policy essay on heterodoxies has an awe-inspiring orthodox spirit; if the followers of heterodoxy were to hear it, they too would flee from them and return to us Confucians.

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教授林　批〔批邪正之辯與夫闢之之術詞嚴義正足見學識之高〕
甚矣異端之蠹人心也不啻洚水之墊溺猛獸
之通人夷狄之為我中華病也治之不可不急
驅之不可不力攘斥之不可不嚴且遠也夫然
後人心之蠹銷而仁義之大道廓如也治之驅
之攘斥之其術安在不過脩其本以勝之而已
夫豈可以口舌諍勢力加哉彼老子為周柱下
史退而隱去嘗著道德五千言而漢明帝時又
有西方所謂佛者入焉老氏以虛無為宗而易
大象曰君子以虛受人似也殊不知易之謂虛
無而有有焉無所不具也佛氏以寂滅為教而
易大傳曰寂然不動似也殊不知易之謂寂寂
而感感焉無所不通也且老子之學虛靜無為
沖退自守其自言曰將欲取之必固與之將欲
闔闢其體其用視之孟子存心養性擴充其四
端者氷炭相反邵子以為老子得易之體孟子
得易之用不其謬歟佛書之初僅有二十四篇
punctuated:
考試官教授林　批〔批邪正之辯與夫闢之之術，詞嚴義正，足見學識之高。〕

甚矣，異端之蠹人心也！不啻洚水之墊溺、猛獸之通人、夷狄之為我中華病也。治之不可不急，驅之不可不力，攘斥之不可不嚴且遠也。夫然後人心之蠹銷，而仁義之大道廓如也。治之、驅之、攘斥之，其術安在？不過脩其本以勝之而已，夫豈可以口舌諍、勢力加哉！彼老子為周柱下史，退而隱去，嘗著道德五千言；而漢明帝時，又有西方所謂佛者入焉。老氏以虛無為宗，而《易·大象》曰：「君子以虛受人。」似也，殊不知《易》之謂虛，無而有有焉，無所不具也。佛氏以寂滅為教，而《易·大傳》曰：「寂然不動。」似也，殊不知《易》之謂寂，寂而感感焉，無所不通也。且老子之學，虛靜無為，沖退自守，其自言曰：「將欲取之，必固與之。」將欲闔闢，其體其用，視之孟子存心養性、擴充其四端者，氷炭相反。邵子以為「老子得《易》之體，孟子得《易》之用」，不其謬歟？佛書之初，僅有二十四篇，
translation_en:
Examiner and Confucian Instructor Lin comments: [The distinction between heterodoxy and orthodoxy and the method for refuting them are set forth in stern words and righteous principles, amply demonstrating the height of his learning and insight.]

Grave indeed is the way heterodoxies corrode the human mind! It is no less than floodwaters drowning the people, fierce beasts pressing upon men [?], or barbarian tribes afflicting our Central Lands. Controlling them cannot but be urgent, driving them away cannot but be forceful, and repelling and rejecting them cannot but be strict and far-reaching. Only then will that which corrodes the human mind be dissolved, and the great Way of benevolence and righteousness be opened wide. Wherein lies the method for controlling them, driving them away, and repelling and rejecting them? It is nothing more than cultivating the root in order to overcome them—how could one do so merely by arguing with tongue and lips or by applying force and power! That Laozi served as Archivist Beneath the Pillar under the Zhou, withdrew into seclusion, and once composed the five thousand words on the Way and Its Virtue (Daode); and in the time of Emperor Ming of the Han, there also entered from the West the one called Buddha. Master Lao took emptiness and non-being as his cardinal principle, while the Great Image Commentary (Daxiang) of the Changes (Yi) says, "The superior man receives others with emptiness." This seems similar, yet one fails to realize that what the Changes calls emptiness is non-being that yet possesses being, lacking nothing whatsoever. The Buddha took quiescent extinction as his teaching, while the Great Treatise (Dazhuan) of the Changes says, "Quiescent and unmoving." This seems similar, yet one fails to realize that what the Changes calls quiescence is quiescence that yet responds when stimulated, penetrating everywhere without obstruction. Moreover, the learning of Laozi is empty, tranquil, and non-acting, modestly retiring and guarding itself; yet as he himself said, "If you would take from a thing, you must first assuredly give to it," and "If you would [contract it, you must first] shuts and opens [?]." In its substance and its function, when compared with Mencius's preserving the mind, nourishing one's nature, and expanding the Four Beginnings, they are as opposite as ice and glowing charcoal. Master Shao held that "Laozi attained the substance of the Changes, while Mencius attained the function of the Changes"—is that not erroneous? In the beginning, the Buddhist scriptures consisted of only twenty-four chapters [sic, for forty-two chapters], …

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
言甚鄙俚其後竊引莊列之語恣爲妄誕之書
及梁而有達麼者出一切掃蕩遂有心靜見理
之論當時既無真儒而老莊亦皆淺近朱子謂
老氏亦難抗衡程子謂攻之者執說反出其下
不其然歟自是而下浸失本真竟爲滅罪資福
生死輪廻之說以營居室衣食之計雖使老佛
復生亦必厭惡而況不爲老佛者乎柰何智者
溺于茫昧愚者誘于禍福或割田園以擴其居
或竭粟帛以給其用而名山勝境宮殿巍峩有
===
所惑也有所利也創建不爲之制也繪飾不爲
之度也僭擬不問糜費不惜也反有過於吾夫
子廟庭之閎于禮制者不亦宜乎他如誦法孔
子而徼福文昌斯蓋其之下者嗚呼異端之說
盤據轇轕信之者深奉之者至人其人火其書
廬其居恐未易及但當脩吾仁義之道使天下
之人曉然皆知仁義吾心之固有如水火如穀
粟如布帛雖欲一日離之而不可得則仁之於
父子也義之於君臣也推之夫婦長幼朋友無
punctuated: 言甚鄙俚。其後竊引莊、列之語，恣爲妄誕之書。及梁而有達麼者出，一切掃蕩，遂有心靜見理之論。當時既無真儒，而老、莊亦皆淺近。朱子謂老氏亦難抗衡，程子謂攻之者執說反出其下，不其然歟？自是而下，浸失本真，竟爲滅罪資福、生死輪廻之說，以營居室衣食之計。雖使老、佛復生，亦必厭惡，而況不爲老、佛者乎？柰何智者溺于茫昧，愚者誘于禍福，或割田園以擴其居，或竭粟帛以給其用，而名山勝境，宮殿巍峩，有所惑也，有所利也。創建不爲之制也，繪飾不爲之度也，僭擬不問，糜費不惜也，反有過於吾夫子廟庭之閎于禮制者，不亦宜乎？他如誦法孔子而徼福文昌，斯蓋其之下者。嗚呼！異端之說，盤據轇轕，信之者深，奉之者至。「人其人，火其書，廬其居」，恐未易及。但當脩吾仁義之道，使天下之人曉然皆知仁義吾心之固有，如水火，如穀粟，如布帛，雖欲一日離之而不可得。則仁之於父子也，義之於君臣也，推之夫婦、長幼、朋友，無
translation_en: …its words were extremely crude and vulgar. Later on, they stealthily borrowed the sayings of Zhuangzi and Liezi, wantonly fabricating absurd and preposterous books. By the Liang dynasty, when Bodhidharma (Damo 達麼) appeared, he swept everything away, and thereupon arose the doctrine of seeing principle through a tranquil mind. At that time there were no true Confucians, and the followers of Laozi and Zhuangzi were also all shallow. Master Zhu (Zhu Xi 朱熹) said that even the followers of Laozi found it hard to contend with them, and Master Cheng (Cheng Hao 程顥 / Cheng Yi 程頤) said that those who attacked them held to arguments that actually fell below them—is this not so? From that point onward, they gradually lost their original truth, and ultimately produced doctrines of eradicating sins, accumulating blessings, and the cycle of birth, death, and reincarnation, as a scheme to secure dwellings, food, and clothing. Even if Laozi and the Buddha were to come back to life, they would surely detest and despise this, let alone those who are not followers of Laozi and the Buddha! Why is it, then, that the wise drown in their obscure subtleties, while the foolish are enticed by their talk of fortune and misfortune—some carving up fields and gardens to expand their dwellings, others exhausting grain and silk to supply their needs, so that in famous mountains and scenic spots their palaces and halls tower aloft? It is because people are deluded by something, and seek profit in something. Their construction is not subjected to regulations, their painted decorations are not restricted by measure, their僭擬 (usurpations of imperial style) go unquestioned, and their lavish waste is unspared. That these should actually surpass the grandeur of our Master's temple courtyards as prescribed by ritual regulation—is it not only to be expected? As for others who recite and model themselves on Confucius yet pray for blessings from Wenchang 文昌, these are surely the lowest of all. Alas! Heterodox doctrines are entrenched and entangled; those who believe in them do so deeply, and those who revere them do so to the utmost. "To return their people to laity, burn their books, and turn their monasteries into ordinary dwellings" is, I fear, not easily achieved. We should simply cultivate our Way of benevolence and righteousness, so that all people under Heaven clearly understand that benevolence and righteousness are inherent in our own minds—like water and fire, like grain and millet, like cloth and silk, which one cannot part from even for a single day, even if one wished to. Then, from benevolence between father and son, and righteousness between ruler and minister, extended to husband and wife, elder and younger, and friend and friend, there will be nowhere…

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
適而不盡其道也彼佛老之棄親戚去人倫毀
身滅性而淪于夷狄之歸者自將日銷月鑠而
不得為吾道蠹也孟子曰君子反經而已矣經
正則庶民興庶民興斯無邪慝矣愚敢以是復
明問未知執事以為何如
punctuated: 適而不盡其道也。彼佛、老之棄親戚、去人倫、毀身滅性而淪于夷狄之歸者，自將日銷月鑠，而不得為吾道蠹也。孟子曰：「君子反經而已矣。經正則庶民興，庶民興，斯無邪慝矣。」愚敢以是復明問，未知執事以為何如？
translation_en: …wherever one goes, one will fulfill the Way in its entirety. As for those followers of the Buddha and Laozi who abandon their kin, cast off human relationships, injure their bodies, and extinguish their innate nature, thereby sinking into the ways of the barbarians—they will naturally waste away by the day and melt away by the month, and will no longer be able to act as wood-borers eating away at our Way. Mencius said: "The superior man simply returns to the constant standard. When the constant standard is rectified, the common people are roused to virtue; when the common people are roused to virtue, there will be no perverse wickedness." I, in my simplicity, venture to offer this in reply to your enlightened inquiry, not knowing what Your Honor may think of it.

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
江西鄉試錄後序
迺成化十年甲午大比之秋戶部
左侍郎原傑適將
上命巡視江西以科舉登賢重典有司
者不可以非人處其經費必周而
當監察御史程宏楊守隨復議以
貢院湫隘不足以容衆兼夏潦之
後堂屋皆倚側欝蒸之氣拂人不
可以居乃與藩臬二司執事者謀
所以更新加廣焉於堂後別建屋
十二棟令高大敗弊者悉易之拓
地於右方從衡若干尺於是場屋
儼然以改觀有容矣既定書幣四
方延聘□等至則禮遇加隆而防
punctuated:
江西鄉試錄後序

迺成化十年甲午大比之秋，戶部左侍郎原傑適將上命巡視江西，以科舉登賢重典，有司者不可以非人處，其經費必周而當。監察御史程宏、楊守隨復議以貢院湫隘，不足以容衆，兼夏潦之後，堂屋皆倚側，欝蒸之氣拂人，不可以居，乃與藩、臬二司執事者謀所以更新加廣焉。於堂後別建屋十二棟，令高大，敗弊者悉易之，拓地於右方，從衡若干尺，於是場屋儼然以改觀有容矣。既定，書幣四方延聘□等，至則禮遇加隆，而防
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Jiangxi Provincial Examination

In the autumn of the triennial examination in the jiawu year, the tenth year of the Chenghua era [1474], Left Vice Minister of Revenue Yuan Jie 原傑 happened to be inspecting Jiangxi on the Emperor's command. Considering that the civil service examination for promoting the worthy is a ceremony of great importance, he held that those in charge must not be unsuitable men, and that its expenditures had to be thorough and appropriate. Investigating Censors Cheng Hong 程宏 and Yang Shousui 楊守隨 further deliberated that because the examination compound was low-lying and cramped, insufficient to accommodate the multitude, and moreover because after the summer floods the halls and rooms were all leaning and tilted, with sultry, steaming vapors assailing people so that it was uninhabitable, they consulted with the administrators of the Provincial Administration Commission and Surveillance Commission on how to renovate and expand it. Behind the main hall they separately built twelve buildings, making them tall and spacious, and completely replaced all that was dilapidated and ruined; they also expanded the grounds on the right side by a certain number of feet in length and breadth. Thereupon, the examination compound took on an impressive new appearance and had ample room. Once this was settled, letters and gifts were sent in all directions to invite [us] [?], and when we arrived, we were treated with heightened courtesy, while the precautions…

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
慎益嚴凡入院諸執事皆精一時
之選而諸士子就試者二千七百
餘人仲秋八日庚寅張宴於南昌
道宴畢以樂導送入院辛卯四鼓
入諸生其命題則揭五經四書而
刺之付之至公而任之無情若化
工之誕物吾何得輕重之偏私之
===
倒置之豈惟禁之即使肆之勢能
為乎至公無情之主之也是日也
輕雲開霽北風微涼甲午再試丁
酉三試風日益清朗無煩暑流汗
之苦諸士子人人自奮有李白揚
眉吐氣激昂青雲之志且終塲以
疾故不入者不百人雲等夜以繼
punctuated: 慎益嚴，凡入院諸執事皆精一時之選。而諸士子就試者二千七百餘人。仲秋八日庚寅，張宴於南昌道，宴畢，以樂導送入院。辛卯四鼓，入諸生。其命題則揭《五經》、《四書》而刺之，付之至公而任之無情，若化工之誕物，吾何得輕重之、偏私之、倒置之？豈惟禁之，即使肆之，勢能為乎？至公無情之主之也。是日也，輕雲開霽，北風微涼。甲午再試，丁酉三試，風日益清朗，無煩暑流汗之苦。諸士子人人自奮，有李白揚眉吐氣、激昂青雲之志。且終塲以疾故不入者不百人。雲等夜以繼
translation_en: … precautions and vigilance grew even stricter, and all the functionaries who entered the examination compound were the finest selections of the moment. The scholars who came to sit for the examination numbered more than two thousand seven hundred. On the eighth day of the eighth lunar month, gengyin, a banquet was laid out at the Nanchang Circuit; when the banquet ended, they were escorted into the examination compound to the accompaniment of music. On the xinmao day, at the fourth watch of the night, the candidates were admitted. As for the setting of examination topics, passages from the Five Classics and Four Books were held up and chosen by lot, entrusting the matter to utmost impartiality and leaving it to unfeeling objectivity—like the Creator bringing forth myriad things, how could we weigh them unevenly, show partiality, or invert their proper order? Not only is this forbidden, even if one wished to act willfully, would circumstances allow it? Utmost impartiality and unfeeling objectivity govern it. On that day, light clouds cleared after the rain and a northern breeze brought a gentle coolness. On the jiawu day the second session was held, and on the dingyou day the third session; the breeze and sunshine grew ever clearer and brighter, without the misery of oppressive heat and running sweat. Every one of the scholars roused himself to effort, possessing the lofty, cloud-vaulting ambition of Li Bai 李白 "raising his brows and pouring forth his spirit." Moreover, through to the end of the sessions, fewer than a hundred men failed to enter on account of illness. Yun and my colleagues worked through the night into…

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
日收其文之粹者九十五人自錄
限以定額啁焉惜之而已既小錄
成謂秉宜序後惟人以眇眇之軀
而虛靈應物之地不滿方寸然理
而正之安而和之推而廣之則與
天□可以同大可以相終始者蓋
吾之心天地之心吾之氣天地之
===
氣正則俱正順則俱順正順之感
休祥以集人心與天地相流通豈
容毫毛間哉先是靈芝產於豐城
甘露降於吉水道路籍籍傳以為
異識者知其為人文兆矣而未察
其端以予觀於諸執事之秉心甚
謀一付之至公無情則人心和矣
punctuated: 日，收其文之粹者九十五人。自錄限以定額，啁焉惜之而已。既小錄成，謂秉宜序後。惟人以眇眇之軀，而虛靈應物之地不滿方寸，然理而正之，安而和之，推而廣之，則與天□可以同大，可以相終始者，蓋吾之心，天地之心；吾之氣，天地之氣。正則俱正，順則俱順，正順之感，休祥以集。人心與天地相流通，豈容毫毛間哉？先是，靈芝產於豐城，甘露降於吉水，道路籍籍，傳以為異。識者知其為人文兆矣，而未察其端。以予觀於諸執事之秉心甚謀，一付之至公無情，則人心和矣。
translation_en:
…day, selecting the finest of their essays from ninety-five men. As the roster was limited by the fixed quota, they could only lament and regret [those left out]. Once the examination record was completed, they said that I, Bing, ought to write the postface.

Now, although a person has but a puny body, and the seat of spiritual intelligence that responds to myriad things is less than a square inch, yet if one orders and rectifies it, calms and harmonizes it, and extends and broadens it, then it can be as great as Heaven and [Earth] [?], and can endure alongside them from beginning to end. This is because our mind is the mind of Heaven and Earth, and our vital energy (qi) is the vital energy of Heaven and Earth. When it is upright, all is upright; when it is harmonious, all is harmonious. Through the resonance of uprightness and harmony, auspicious portents gather. Since the human mind and Heaven and Earth flow into one another, how could there be even a hair's breadth of separation between them?

Prior to this, numinous mushrooms (lingzhi) grew in Fengcheng 豐城 and sweet dew fell in Jishui 吉水. Along the roads people talked excitedly, passing the word around and regarding these as marvels. Those with insight knew them to be omens of cultural and literary flourishing, yet they had not discerned their ultimate source. As I observe how all the officiating personnel maintained their minds and deliberated carefully [?], entrusting everything entirely to supreme impartiality without personal bias, human minds have thereby been brought into harmony. …

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
心和則氣和氣和則天地之和應
宜其徵兆爲之先見而人才于是
挺出吾閩知九十五人中必多名
德忠孝之士起而增
國華安
社稷福无疆開太平承道統以收
國家百年養士之功豈不偉然大丈
===
夫哉於乎西江一省也科舉一事
也有諸數事之謀爲感召且爾使
居寧物之地而一付之至公無情
其和順感通又當何如謂世不底
平俗不還厚禮樂刑政教化之具
不備舉雨暘不時若四夷不賓服
草木鳥獸不咸遂休徵嘉兆不至
punctuated: 心和則氣和，氣和則天地之和應。宜其徵兆爲之先見，而人才于是挺出。吾閩知九十五人中，必多名德忠孝之士，起而增國華，安社稷，福无疆，開太平，承道統，以收國家百年養士之功，豈不偉然大丈夫哉！於乎！西江一省也，科舉一事也，有諸數事之謀爲，感召且爾；使居寧物之地，而一付之至公無情，其和順感通又當何如！謂世不底平，俗不還厚，禮樂刑政教化之具不備舉，雨暘不時若，四夷不賓服，草木鳥獸不咸遂，休徵嘉兆不至，
translation_en: When hearts are harmonious, vital breath (qi) is harmonious; when vital breath is harmonious, the harmony of Heaven and Earth responds. It is fitting that its portents appeared in advance, and men of talent have thereupon stood forth. I therefore [閩, likely a transcription error for 固/因] [?] know that among the ninety-five men [selected as provincial graduates], there must be many gentlemen of renowned virtue, loyalty, and filial piety who will rise to enhance the glory of the dynasty, bring peace to the altars of soil and grain, bestow boundless blessings, inaugurate great peace, and carry on the transmission of the Way (daotong), thereby reaping the fruits of the state's century-long cultivation of scholars—will they not be truly magnificent men! Alas! Jiangxi (Xijiang) is but a single province, and the civil service examination is but a single affair; yet with the planning and conduct of the various officials in charge [數事, likely a transcription error for 執事] [?], the sympathetic resonance summoned forth is already like this. Suppose one were to occupy a position of pacifying all creatures [or governing the realm, 宰物?] [?] and likewise commit everything to the utmost impartiality without personal bias—what then would the harmonious resonance and sympathetic response be like! To say that the world would not achieve peace, that customs would not return to generosity, that the instruments of rites, music, punishments, governance, and moral transformation would not all be instituted, that rain and sunshine would not be seasonably compliant, that the four surrounding peoples would not submit in allegiance, that plants, trees, birds, and beasts would not all flourish, and that auspicious signs and propitious omens would not arrive…

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
吾不信也今而後蓋望之諸士子
矣
山西澤州儒學學正汪□□謹序
punctuated:
吾不信也。今而後，蓋望之諸士子矣。

山西澤州儒學學正汪□□謹序。
translation_en:
… I would not believe it. From now on, our hopes indeed rest upon these gentlemen.

Respectfully prefaced by Wang [□□], Instructor of the Confucian School of Zezhou in Shanxi.

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
江西鄉試錄
成化十年
punctuated:
江西鄉試錄
成化十年
translation_en:
Record of the Jiangxi Provincial Examination
Tenth Year of the Chenghua Era (1474)

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
江西鄉試錄序
今
皇帝臨御之十年歲維甲午實天下大
比之秋江西巡按監察御史程宏
楊守隨暨方面重臣右布政使張
永按察使余複等僉謂登賢大事
弗恪導
===
天子下福元元無窮時戸部左侍郎原
成憲或怠以徇曷以上答
傑奉
璽書握便宜重柄巡視玆土亦深致
嚴重之飭於是提調學校副使夏
寅徧歷郡邑預擇生儒之可備登
薦者得二千七百餘人以俟複博
punctuated:
江西鄉試錄序

今皇帝臨御之十年，歲維甲午，實天下大比之秋。江西巡按監察御史程宏、楊守隨，暨方面重臣右布政使張永、按察使余複等，僉謂：「登賢大事，弗恪導天子，下福元元無窮，時戸部左侍郎原成憲，或怠以徇，曷以上答？」傑奉璽書，握便宜重柄，巡視玆土，亦深致嚴重之飭。於是提調學校副使夏寅徧歷郡邑，預擇生儒之可備登薦者，得二千七百餘人以俟。複博
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Jiangxi Provincial Examination

In the tenth year of the reign of the reigning Emperor, the cyclical year being jiawu (1474), it was truly the autumn of the great triennial examination throughout the Empire. The Regional Inspectors and Investigating Censors of Jiangxi, Cheng Hong 程宏 and Yang Shousui 楊守隨, together with the senior provincial officials—Right Administration Commissioner Zhang Yong 張永, Surveillance Commissioner Yu Fu 余複, and others—all declared: "Promoting the worthy is a great affair of state. If we do not reverently adhere to the established statutes, or if we grow lax and give way to favoritism, how can we answer the Son of Heaven above and bring boundless blessings to the common people below?" [Note: columns on the second half-leaf are transposed in the transcription.] At this time, Left Vice Minister of Revenue Yuan Jie 原傑, bearing an imperial credential and wielding heavy authority to act at his discretion while touring and inspecting this region, also issued solemn and strict admonitions. Thereupon, Surveillance Vice Commissioner for the Supervision of Schools Xia Yin 夏寅 traveled throughout the prefectures and districts to select in advance government students and Confucian scholars qualified to be presented for the examination, obtaining more than two thousand seven hundred men to await the event. Furthermore, having broadly…

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
採輿論走書幣四方延聘儒官以
司進退雖下至掌卷彌封謄錄等
執事亦罔不柬諸有司中之端謹
有聲者充焉既八月正考官學正
汪雲自濮澤至同考官學正陳鑾
自蟆城至教諭沈環自安東至余
燠自東甌至鄭昭自汲郡至陳文
===
自三山至張琳自蒙莊至馮鉞自
芝城至謝文禮自于湖至而智則
濫與正考至自姑蘇云及期闔院
布之以熊羆之卒邏之以虎豹之
臣而集二千七百餘人者聿試之
九日辛卯試以四書五經經隨所
治越三日甲午試以論及詔誥表
punctuated: 採輿論，走書幣四方，延聘儒官以司進退。雖下至掌卷、彌封、謄錄等執事，亦罔不柬諸有司中之端謹有聲者充焉。既八月，正考官學正汪雲自濮澤至；同考官學正陳鑾自蟆城至，教諭沈環自安東至，余燠自東甌至，鄭昭自汲郡至，陳文自三山至，張琳自蒙莊至，馮鉞自芝城至，謝文禮自于湖至；而智則濫與正考，至自姑蘇云。及期，闔院布之以熊羆之卒，邏之以虎豹之臣，而集二千七百餘人者聿試之。九日辛卯，試以《四書》、《五經》，經隨所治；越三日甲午，試以論及詔、誥、表、
translation_en: …gathered public opinion, and dispatched letters and gifts in all directions to invite Confucian educational officials to preside over the selection and rejection of candidates. Even down to the functionaries in charge of receiving examination papers, sealing names, and transcribing copies, every one of them was chosen from among upright, cautious, and reputable local officials to fill the posts. When the eighth month arrived, the Examiner, Subprefectural Director of Studies Wang Yun 汪雲, arrived from Puze 濮澤 [Huozhou 霍州]; the Associate Examiners—Subprefectural Director of Studies Chen Luan 陳鑾 from Macheng 蟆城 [?], District Director of Studies Shen Huan 沈環 from Andong 安東, Yu Yu 余燠 from Dong'ou 東甌 [Wenzhou 溫州], Zheng Zhao 鄭昭 from Jijun 汲郡 [Weihui 衛輝], Chen Wen 陳文 from Sanshan 三山 [Fuzhou 福州], Zhang Lin 張琳 from Mengzhuang 蒙莊, Feng Yue 馮鉞 from Zhicheng 芝城 [Jianning 建寧], and Xie Wenli 謝文禮 from Yuhu 于湖 [Dangtu 當塗]—all arrived; while I, Zhi 智, unworthily shared the post of Examiner, arriving from Gusu 姑蘇 [Suzhou 蘇州]. When the appointed time came, the examination compound was locked, stationed with bear-like soldiers, and patrolled by tiger-and-leopard-like officers, and the more than two thousand seven hundred assembled candidates were examined therein. On the ninth day, xinmao, they were examined on the Four Books and the Five Classics, each candidate taking the Classic in which he specialized; three days later, on jiawu, they were examined with a discourse, as well as an imperial edict, imperial mandate, memorial, or…

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
判詔誥表內科一道又三日丁酉
乃篆之首之以
制書次之以經史及時務于時院內
外綱維振肅守隨實專之其提調
監試則以屬左叅政王克復左叅
議徐鑑僉事陳騏徐懷其贊理防
範則以屬永復及右叅政魏元副
===
使陳煒趙銘左叅議葉顒右叅議
黃縉僉事張鑑陳琦胡靖申安凡
厥三試皆天日晶明祥飆披拂若
默有以相文運之隆者而又號令
清肅纖埃不驚於是乎就試之士
靡不得以專厥精思罄厥底蘊而
發舒於霈沛然之辭以聽乎灼然之
punctuated: 判，詔、誥、表、內科一道。又三日丁酉，乃篆之，首之以制書，次之以經史及時務。于時院內外綱維振肅，守隨實專之；其提調、監試，則以屬左叅政王克復、左叅議徐鑑、僉事陳騏、徐懷；其贊理、防範，則以屬永復及右叅政魏元、副使陳煒、趙銘，左叅議葉顒、右叅議黃縉、僉事張鑑、陳琦、胡靖、申安。凡厥三試，皆天日晶明，祥飆披拂，若默有以相文運之隆者。而又號令清肅，纖埃不驚，於是乎就試之士，靡不得以專厥精思，罄厥底蘊，而發舒於霈沛然之辭，以聽乎灼然之
translation_en: … and legal judgments, with one question selected from among edicts, patents, memorials, and inner-court documents. Three days later, on the dingyou day [the fifteenth], they were tested on policy questions [篆之, typo for 策之?], beginning with imperial decrees and books, followed by the Classics, histories, and current affairs. At this time, inside and outside the examination compound, discipline and order were strictly maintained, for which Shousui [李守隨?] held sole overarching responsibility. The duties of proctoring and monitoring the examination were assigned to Left Administration Vice Commissioner Wang Kefu 王克復, Left Assistant Administration Commissioner Xu Jian 徐鑑, and Assistant Surveillance Commissioners Chen Qi 陳騏 and Xu Huai 徐懷. The duties of assisting in administration and maintaining security were assigned to Yongfu [永復] as well as Right Administration Vice Commissioner Wei Yuan 魏元, Surveillance Vice Commissioners Chen Wei 陳煒 and Zhao Ming 趙銘, Left Assistant Administration Commissioner Ye Yong 葉顒, Right Assistant Administration Commissioner Huang Jin 黃縉, and Assistant Surveillance Commissioners Zhang Jian 張鑑, Chen Qi 陳琦, Hu Jing 胡靖, and Shen An 申安. Throughout all three sessions, the sky and sun were bright and clear, and auspicious breezes wafted gently, as though unseen forces were quietly aiding the flourishing of literary fortune. Moreover, commands and regulations were pure and solemn, with not a speck of dust disturbed. Thus, among the scholars sitting for the examination, there were none who could not concentrate their finest thoughts, exhaust their deepest store of learning, and give full expression to them in abundant, flowing words, awaiting the clear and discerning…

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
擇焉試畢同考官乃分經而較之
煥鉞較治易者卷環較治書者卷
昭文璘較治詩者卷文禮較治春
秋者卷鑾較治禮記者卷較各定
智與雲乃取而詳訂焉其較之之
法本之初試以觀其本領之淵源
叅之次試以觀其辯論酬應與夫
裁決之徹者又叅之三試以觀其
===
博而有用不徒區區循行數墨號
曰明經者之腐中苟有泛而不根
者鑿而立異者膚末而纖瑣者舉
不取取之必典則必瑩徹必端嚴
必豪壯不主臆見而發聲說不因
寸朽而弃良材據所取可登者亦
punctuated: 擇焉。試畢，同考官乃分經而較之：煥、鉞較治《易》者卷，環較治《書》者卷，昭、文、璘較治《詩》者卷，文禮較治《春秋》者卷，鑾較治《禮記》者卷。較各定，智與雲乃取而詳訂焉。其較之之法，本之初試以觀其本領之淵源，叅之次試以觀其辯論、酬應與夫裁決之徹者，又叅之三試以觀其博而有用，不徒區區循行數墨、號曰明經者之腐。中苟有泛而不根者、鑿而立異者、膚末而纖瑣者，舉不取。取之必典則，必瑩徹，必端嚴，必豪壯。不主臆見而發聲說，不因寸朽而弃良材。據所取可登者亦
translation_en: …selection. Once the examination was completed, the Associate Examiners divided the papers by Classic and evaluated them: Huan 煥 and Yue 鉞 evaluated the papers of those specializing in the Book of Changes (Yi 易); Huan 環 evaluated the papers of those specializing in the Book of Documents (Shu 書); Zhao 昭, Wen 文, and Lin 璘 evaluated the papers of those specializing in the Book of Odes (Shi 詩); Wenli 文禮 evaluated the papers of those specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu 春秋); and Luan 鑾 evaluated the papers of those specializing in the Record of Rites (Liji 禮記). When each had determined their evaluations, Zhi 智 and Yun 雲 took the papers and carefully reviewed and finalized them. As for the method of evaluation, it was grounded in the first session to observe the depth and source of the candidates' fundamental learning; cross-referenced with the second session to observe the thoroughness of their argumentation, official correspondence, and legal judgments; and further cross-referenced with the third session to observe whether their knowledge was broad and practical, rather than the mere pedantry of those who simply follow the lines and count the ink-marks while claiming to have mastered the Classics. Among the papers, if there were any that were vague and unfounded, forced and contrarian, or superficial and trivial, none were selected. Those selected had to be canonical and regular, lucid and penetrating, upright and rigorous, and vigorous and grand. We did not favor subjective opinions in making our pronouncements [?], nor did we discard fine timber on account of a tiny flaw. Based on what we selected, those worthy of being placed on the list were also…

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
衆遴定額第拔其尤者九十又五
人蓋治易者得十又八治書者得
二十又四治詩者得三十又七治
春秋者得九治禮記者得七其次
第一等之以三試之優劣其各經
所以取之之差一均之就試者之
多寡也棘撤榜揭既復錄文之可
式并所次氏名為書以
獻僉屬智宜序不得辭竊惟天之生
賢何為為天下也士君子之致用
何為亦所以為天下而奉承乎天
也然施設大者必其抱負涵養也
大主敬所以立為天下之大本窮
理所以達為天下之大用者於斯
punctuated: 衆。遴定額，第拔其尤者九十又五人：蓋治《易》者得十又八，治《書》者得二十又四，治《詩》者得三十又七，治《春秋》者得九，治《禮記》者得七。其次第，一等之以三試之優劣；其各經所以取之之差，一均之就試者之多寡也。棘撤榜揭，既復錄文之可式并所次氏名為書以獻，僉屬智宜序，不得辭。竊惟天之生賢何為？為天下也。士君子之致用何為？亦所以為天下而奉承乎天也。然施設大者，必其抱負涵養也大。主敬所以立為天下之大本，窮理所以達為天下之大用者，於斯
translation_en: …numerous. In selecting according to the fixed quota, we ranked and chose the ninety-five most outstanding candidates among them: eighteen who specialized in the Book of Changes (Yi), twenty-four who specialized in the Book of Documents (Shu), thirty-seven who specialized in the Book of Odes (Shi), nine who specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu), and seven who specialized in the Record of Rites (Liji). Their order of ranking was determined entirely by the relative merit of their performance across the three sessions; the differences in the number of candidates selected from each Classic were balanced entirely according to the number of candidates who sat for the examination in each. Once the thorny enclosure was unsealed and the roster of successful candidates posted, we further compiled the essays worthy of serving as models together with the ranked list of names into a book to present to the throne. Everyone enjoined that I, Zhi, should write a preface, and I could not decline. I venture to reflect: why does Heaven bring forth worthy men? It is for the sake of all under Heaven. Why do scholars and gentlemen devote themselves to practical service? It is likewise for the sake of all under Heaven, and to uphold and carry out the will of Heaven. Yet for one's measures and achievements to be great, one's aspirations and self-cultivation must also be great. Holding fast to reverence in order to establish the great foundation for serving all under Heaven, and exhaustively investigating principle in order to attain the great application for serving all under Heaven—herein…

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
蕪盡而積累之則愈大愈妙而彌
綸參贊之具備矣時苟我用舉而
措之今智等所以取諸士子徒以
其言盖亦驗其能窮理之一端誠以
理苟明則形諸辭也必正大而光
明辭而正大光明其涵養抱負與
夫異時之設施繇之可知茲寔亦
===
朝廷所以設科取士之意然有德者
固必有言而徒言者亦或未必有
德焉言出於德則繇茲以登者必
克奉承乎天天民必克愛天事必
克恭治亂安危必克斡天之運禍
福榮辱必克唯天之安釐極必藉
之以植
punctuated: 蕪盡而積累之，則愈大愈妙，而彌綸參贊之具備矣，時苟我用，舉而措之。今智等所以取諸士子，徒以其言，盖亦驗其能窮理之一端。誠以理苟明，則形諸辭也，必正大而光明；辭而正大光明，其涵養抱負與夫異時之設施，繇之可知。茲寔亦朝廷所以設科取士之意。然有德者固必有言，而徒言者亦或未必有德焉。言出於德，則繇茲以登者，必克奉承乎天：天民必克愛，天事必克恭，治亂安危必克斡天之運，禍福榮辱必克唯天之安；釐極必藉之以植，
translation_en: … are exhausted [? 蕪盡 -> 無盡], and when accumulated, they become ever greater and ever more subtle, so that the wherewithal to encompass and assist in the cosmic processes is complete; if the times should employ us, we simply take it up and put it into practice. Now, the reason I, Zhi, and my colleagues select candidates from among the scholars merely by means of their words is that this too serves to test one aspect of their ability to fathom principle. Truly, if principle is understood, then when it takes form in words, they will surely be upright, great, and illustrious; and when one's words are upright, great, and illustrious, his self-cultivation and aspirations, as well as the measures he will implement in the future, can be known thereby. This is indeed the very intention for which the court established the examinations to select scholars. Yet while those who possess virtue will certainly have fine words, those who merely have words may not necessarily possess virtue. When words issue from virtue, those who ascend to office through this path will surely be able to uphold and serve Heaven: they will surely be able to love Heaven's people, they will surely be able to be reverent in Heaven's affairs, in order and disorder, security and peril, they will surely be able to turn the destiny of Heaven, and in misfortune and fortune, honor and disgrace, they will surely be able to rest content in Heaven alone; the royal standard of rule will surely rely on them to be established, and…

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
鴻圖必籍之以壽茲寔維設科取士
之利哉言苟不德之出則動必違
天必土苴仁義必桎梏禮法必唯
欲之徇而身家之圖必漠然於民
之苦樂
國之蕃利必剟則蛇蝕以敗類必柔
則脂韋以求媚必譎則鳳鳴鷙翰
===
以盜名必奸則高城深府以衷毒
小用之必小以壞大用之必大以
壞遠之近之用之必遠之近之以
壞於戲科目得士而若茲其亦可
畏也哉其亦可愧也哉
直隸蘇州府儒學教授林智謹序
punctuated:
鴻圖必籍之以壽，茲寔維設科取士之利哉！言苟不德之出，則動必違天，必土苴仁義，必桎梏禮法，必唯欲之徇而身家之圖，必漠然於民之苦樂、國之蕃利；必剟，則蛇蝕以敗類；必柔，則脂韋以求媚；必譎，則鳳鳴鷙翰以盜名；必奸，則高城深府以衷毒。小用之必小以壞，大用之必大以壞，遠之近之用之，必遠之近之以壞。於戲！科目得士而若茲，其亦可畏也哉！其亦可愧也哉！
直隸蘇州府儒學教授林智謹序。
translation_en:
… the grand imperial plan will surely rely on them to endure. This is truly the benefit of establishing the examination categories to select scholars! Yet if their words do not issue from virtue, then in action they will surely defy Heaven; they will surely treat benevolence and righteousness as mere dregs and straw; they will surely regard rites and laws as fetters and shackles; they will surely indulge only their own desires and scheme for themselves and their families; they will surely remain indifferent to the sufferings and joys of the people and to the flourishing benefits of the state. They will surely be rapacious [?], preying like snakes to ruin their own kind; they will surely be pliant, acting as greased leather to curry favor; they will surely be deceitful, singing like phoenixes while bearing the wings of birds of prey in order to steal a reputation; they will surely be treacherous, building high walls and deep fastnesses in their hearts to harbor malice. If employed in a small capacity, they will surely bring about small ruin; if employed in a great capacity, they will surely bring about great ruin; whether employed in distant or near posts, they will surely bring ruin far and near. Alas! If the examination system obtains scholars who are like this, how terrifying it is indeed! How shameful it is indeed!

Respectfully prefaced by Lin Zhi 林智, Instructor of the Confucian School of Suzhou Prefecture in the Southern Metropolitan Area (Zhili).

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
成化十年鄉試
監臨官
巡按江西監察御史楊守隨〔惟貞浙江鄞縣人丙戌進士〕
提調官
江西等處承宣布政使司左叅政王克復〔師仁福建福清縣人丁丑進士〕
江西等處承宣布政使司左叅議徐鑑〔克明浙江淳安縣人庚辰進士〕
監試官
江西等處提刑按察司僉事陳驥〔夢祥廣東南海縣人丁丑進士〕
江西等處提刑按察司僉事徐懷〔明德浙江建德縣人庚辰進士〕
===
考試官
直隷蘇州府儒學教授林智〔若濬福建莆田縣人甲子貢士〕
山西澤州儒學學正汪雲〔從龍直隷休寧縣人乙酉貢士〕
同考試官
直隷鳳陽府泗州儒學學正陳鑾〔叔和福建懷安縣人己卯貢士〕
直隷淮安府安東縣儒學教諭沈璟〔時健浙江蕭山縣人庚午貢士〕
福建建寧府甌寧縣儒學教諭余煥〔孔哲浙江開化縣人癸酉貢士〕
河南衛輝府汲縣儒學教諭鄭昭〔德懋福建福清縣人壬午貢士〕
福建福州府懷安縣儒學教諭陳文〔世道廣東歸善縣人丙子貢士〕
punctuated:
成化十年鄉試

監臨官
巡按江西監察御史楊守隨〔惟貞，浙江鄞縣人，丙戌進士〕。

提調官
江西等處承宣布政使司左叅政王克復〔師仁，福建福清縣人，丁丑進士〕。
江西等處承宣布政使司左叅議徐鑑〔克明，浙江淳安縣人，庚辰進士〕。

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
然非與曰非也予一以貫之
小德川流大德敦化
五穀者種之美者也苟為不熟不如荑稗夫仁
亦在乎熟之而已矣
易
坤道其順乎承天而時行
乎乃利用禴无咎
===
擬之而後言議之而後動擬議以成其變化鳴
鶴在陰其子和之我有好爵吾與爾靡之子
曰君子居其室出其言善則千里之外應之
況其邇者乎
窮理盡性以至於命
書
水火金木土穀惟修
厥貢惟金三品瑤琨篠簜齒革羽毛惟木島夷
卉服厥篚織貝
punctuated:
第壹場
四書：
「然。」「非與？」曰：「非也。予一以貫之。」
小德川流，大德敦化。
五穀者，種之美者也；苟為不熟，不如荑稗。夫仁，亦在乎熟之而已矣。

易：
坤道其順乎！承天而時行。
孚乃利用禴，无咎。
擬之而後言，議之而後動，擬議以成其變化。「鳴鶴在陰，其子和之。我有好爵，吾與爾靡之。」子曰：「君子居其室，出其言善，則千里之外應之，況其邇者乎？」
窮理盡性以至於命。

書：
水、火、金、木、土、穀，惟修。
厥貢惟金三品，瑤、琨、篠、簜，齒、革、羽、毛，惟木。島夷卉服，厥篚織貝。

First Session

"Yes." "Is it not so?" He said, "No! I have one thread that runs right through it." [Analects 15.3]
Smaller virtues flow like river currents; the great virtue brings about massive transformations. [Doctrine of the Mean 30]
The five grains are the finest of plants; yet if they do not ripen, they are worse than tares and wild grass. With benevolence, too, the whole point consists simply in bringing it to maturity. [Mencius 6A.19]

How compliant is the way of Kun [Earth]! It receives from Heaven and acts in accordance with the seasons. [Wenyan on Hexagram 2, Kun]
If one has sincerity [Note: original prints 乎 for 孚], then it is favorable to offer even a simple summer sacrifice; there will be no blame. [Hexagram 45, Cui, or Hexagram 46, Sheng]
One considers before speaking, and deliberates before acting; through consideration and deliberation one completes the transformations. "'A crane cries in the shade, and its young answers it. I have a fine goblet; I will share it with you.'" The Master said, "When the superior man abides in his chamber and sends forth words that are good, those a thousand li away respond to him—how much more those who are near?" [Xici I.8]
Exhaustively investigating principle and fully realizing one's nature, until one arrives at destiny. [Shuogua 1]
