title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
其遵謹酒之訓盖縱酒喪德人不可以不謹也前王
於臣民之小子得不有以教之而使知所謹哉昔武
王封康叔於衛而告之若曰我穆考文王肇國西土
以庶邦庶士之小子血氣未定尤易縱酒故專誥教
之爾小子將有官守者也當有職業者也當豫養其良心豈可彝於酒
而至喪德乎將有職業者也當先存其德性豈可常
於酒而至亂性乎然及於庶國之飲也惟於克羞饋
祀之時亦必以德將之無至於醉也惟於以往蒸嘗
之日亦必以禮制之弗及於亂也然在官小子既教
===
以謹酒之節矣在民小子又可不以謹酒之訓而戒
之乎謂夫我民之祖考亦常訓導其子孫勤稼穡惟
土物之是愛服田畝無外物之是慕則心之所守者
正而善日生志之所向者專而慾日窒夫爾之祖考
垂訓者如此爾為子孫者要當聰聽乃祖之彝訓無
以謹酒為小德小德大德視之惟一可也明聽乃考
之常教勿以戒酒為小節小節大節視之無二可也
吁文王誥毖之意如此武王舉以告康叔豈非欲其
明大命於妹邦也歟抑考酒誥一篇武王毖酒作也
punctuated: 其遵謹酒之訓。盖縱酒喪德，人不可以不謹也。前王於臣民之小子，得不有以教之而使知所謹哉？昔武王封康叔於衛而告之若曰：我穆考文王肇國西土，以庶邦庶士之小子血氣未定，尤易縱酒，故專誥教之：「爾小子將有官守者也，當有職業者也，當豫養其良心，豈可彝於酒而至喪德乎？將有職業者也，當先存其德性，豈可常於酒而至亂性乎？然及於庶國之飲也，惟於克羞饋祀之時，亦必以德將之，無至於醉也；惟於以往蒸嘗之日，亦必以禮制之，弗及於亂也。」然在官小子既教以謹酒之節矣，在民小子又可不以謹酒之訓而戒之乎？謂夫：「我民之祖考亦常訓導其子孫，勤稼穡惟土物之是愛，服田畝無外物之是慕，則心之所守者正而善日生，志之所向者專而慾日窒。夫爾之祖考垂訓者如此，爾為子孫者，要當聰聽乃祖之彝訓，無以謹酒為小德，小德大德視之惟一可也；明聽乃考之常教，勿以戒酒為小節，小節大節視之無二可也。」吁！文王誥毖之意如此，武王舉以告康叔，豈非欲其明大命於妹邦也歟？抑考《酒誥》一篇，武王毖酒作也。
translation_en:
… them to follow the precept of exercising caution with wine. Indeed, indulging in wine destroys virtue, so people cannot fail to be cautious. How could the former king not have a way to instruct the young among his officials and commoners so as to make them know wherein to be cautious?

In the past, when King Wu enfeoffed Kangshu in Wei, he instructed him to this effect: Our reverent late father King Wen, when founding our state in the western lands, recognized that the youths among the many states and many officers, whose vital energies were not yet settled, were especially prone to indulge in wine; therefore he specifically admonished and instructed them: "You youths are those who will hold official posts [and will have duties]; you ought to nurture your innate good mind beforehand—how could you habitually indulge in wine to the point of destroying your virtue? You are those who will have duties; you ought first to preserve your moral nature—how could you constantly give yourselves to wine to the point of disordering your nature? Even when it comes to drinking across the many states, only at the time when one is able to present food offerings and sacrifices is it permitted, and even then one must sustain oneself with virtue so as not to reach drunkenness; only on the days when one goes to perform the winter and autumn sacrifices is it permitted, and even then one must regulate oneself with ritual propriety so as not to reach disorder."

Yet once the youths in office had been instructed in the restraint of exercising caution with wine, how could the youths among the common people not also be admonished with the precept of exercising caution with wine? He said: "The ancestors and forefathers of our people also constantly guided and instructed their descendants to be diligent in sowing and reaping, cherishing only the products of the soil, and to labor in the fields without coveting external things. Then what the mind holds fast to is upright and goodness grows daily; what the will is directed toward is focused and desires are daily restrained. Now since the instructions handed down by your ancestors and forefathers are like this, you who are their descendants must listen attentively to the constant instructions of your ancestors: do not regard caution with wine as a minor virtue, for minor virtues and great virtues should be viewed as one; listen clearly to the regular teachings of your forefathers: do not regard abstaining from wine as a minor matter of conduct, for minor matters and great matters of conduct should be viewed without distinction."

Ah! Such was the intent of King Wen's admonitory caution; when King Wu cited it to instruct Kangshu, was it not because he wished him to make bright the great mandate in the land of Mei? Moreover, if we examine the "Announcement About Drunkenness" (Jiu gao) as a whole, King Wu composed it to warn against wine. …

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
然此述文王之教曰飲惟祀下文申已誥慈曰父母
慶則可飲酒羌羞耇則可飲酒羞饋祀則可飲酒本
欲禁絕其飲今乃反開其端者不禁之禁也聖人之
教不迫而民從者此也旨哉
詩
蠶月條桑取彼斧斨以伐遠揚猗彼女桑七月
鳴鵙八月載績載玄載黃我朱孔陽為公子
裳四月秀葽五月鳴蜩八月其穫十月隕蘀
一之日于貉取彼狐狸為公子裘
胡泰
===
同考試官教諭張　批〔此詩本言男服事乎外女服事乎內以終首章無衣無褐之意場中作者多昧乎此間有知者文不足以發之詞理俱到僅見此篇是用錄出〕
同考試官教諭陳　批〔場中詩卷千餘作此題者多未得旨求其文理純正者無踰此篇〕
同考試官教諭鄭　批〔不泛不畧豳民忠愛之意宛然可見〕
考試官學正汪　批〔辭理俱優佳作也〕
考試官教授林　批〔必如此作方得詩人意〕
punctuated:
然此述文王之教曰「飲惟祀」，下文申已誥慈曰父母慶則可飲酒，羌羞耇則可飲酒，羞饋祀則可飲酒。本欲禁絕其飲，今乃反開其端者，不禁之禁也。聖人之教不迫而民從者，此也。旨哉！

詩
「蠶月條桑，取彼斧斨，以伐遠揚，猗彼女桑。七月鳴鵙，八月載績，載玄載黃，我朱孔陽，為公子裳。四月秀葽，五月鳴蜩，八月其穫，十月隕蘀。一之日于貉，取彼狐狸，為公子裘。」
胡泰
同考試官教諭張批：〔此詩本言男服事乎外，女服事乎內，以終首章「無衣無褐」之意。場中作者多昧乎此，間有知者，文不足以發之。詞理俱到，僅見此篇，是用錄出。〕
同考試官教諭陳批：〔場中詩卷千餘，作此題者多未得旨，求其文理純正者，無踰此篇。〕
同考試官教諭鄭批：〔不泛不畧，豳民忠愛之意宛然可見。〕
考試官學正汪批：〔辭理俱優，佳作也。〕
考試官教授林批：〔必如此作，方得詩人意。〕
translation_en:
… Yet here, in recounting the teachings of King Wen, it says, "Drink only at sacrifices," whereas below, in reiterating his own admonitions [?], it says that when parents rejoice one may drink wine, when presenting food to the aged [?] one may drink wine, and when offering food in sacrifice one may drink wine. Initially intending to prohibit and put an end to their drinking, he instead opens up occasions for it—this is a prohibition by means of non-prohibition. That the teaching of the sages does not coerce and yet the people follow it is because of this. How profound!

Classic of Poetry (Shijing)
"In the silkworm month they strip the mulberry branches, taking those axes and hatchets to lop the far-reaching and high-rising ones, and pulling down the leaves of the young mulberries. In the seventh month the shrike cries; in the eighth month they begin to spin—making black, making yellow; our vermilion is very bright, to make lower garments for the young noblemen. In the fourth month the milkwort is in spike; in the fifth month the cicada cries; in the eighth month is the harvest; in the tenth month fall the leaves. In the days of the first month they go after raccoon-dogs, taking those foxes and wildcats to make furs for the young noblemen."
Hu Tai 

Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies Zhang comments: [This ode originally speaks of men laboring outside and women laboring inside, so as to complete the meaning of "without clothes, without coarse cloth" in the first stanza. Most writers in the examination hall were blind to this; among the few who understood it, their writing was insufficient to bring it out. Only in this essay do we see both diction and principle fully achieved, and therefore it has been selected for inclusion.]
Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies Chen comments: [Among the more than one thousand Classic of Poetry papers in the examination hall, most who wrote on this topic failed to grasp its main point. Seeking one whose literary expression and reasoning are pure and upright, none surpasses this essay.]
Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies Zheng comments: [Neither vague nor cursory; the loyal and affectionate sentiments of the people of Bin are vividly discernible.]
Examiner and Subprefectural Director of Studies Wang comments: [Superior in both diction and reasoning; an excellent piece.]
Examiner and Prefectural Director of Studies Lin comments: [It must be written like this to capture the poet's intent.]

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
因時而服事乎外既奉上以禦寒感時而服事乎
亦奉上以禦寒蓋蠶績狩獵皆所以爲禦寒計也邠
民預爲之而皆奉乎上其忠愛無已之意何如哉昔
周公陳后稷公劉風化之所由使瞽矇朝夕諷誦以
教成王謂夫邠人以卒歲不可以無衣又不可以無
褐故當治蠶之月采桑以供蠶食桑之大者可以條
取也則取彼斧□□伐遠揚焉桑之小者不可條取
也則取其葉而□□□焉蠶事於此乎備矣至於七
月鳴鵙之後八月麻熟可績之時則績其麻以爲布
===
績事於此乎成矣凡此蠶績之所成皆染之或玄其
色或黃其色而其朱者尤爲鮮明其服事乎內也如
此豈私以自奉哉皆以供上而爲公子之裳庶足以
爲禦寒之資又何無衣之足慮耶邠民愛上之心猶
未已也時乎四月葽感陰氣而秀時乎五月蜩感陰
氣而鳴則陽極陰生之時矣八月而禾早可穫十月
而草木隕落則大寒將至之候矣雖蠶績無所不備
而禦寒猶恐不足故於一陽之月悉率左右而爲于
貉之舉從其羣醜以取狐狸之皮其服事乎外也如
punctuated:
因時而服事乎外，既奉上以禦寒；感時而服事乎，亦奉上以禦寒。蓋蠶績、狩獵，皆所以爲禦寒計也。邠民預爲之，而皆奉乎上，其忠愛無已之意何如哉！

昔周公陳后稷、公劉風化之所由，使瞽矇朝夕諷誦以教成王。謂夫邠人以卒歲不可以無衣，又不可以無褐。故當治蠶之月，采桑以供蠶食。桑之大者，可以條取也，則取彼斧□□伐遠揚焉；桑之小者，不可條取也，則取其葉而□□□焉。蠶事於此乎備矣。至於七月鳴鵙之後，八月麻熟可績之時，則績其麻以爲布，績事於此乎成矣。凡此蠶績之所成，皆染之，或玄其色，或黃其色，而其朱者尤爲鮮明。其服事乎內也如此，豈私以自奉哉？皆以供上而爲公子之裳，庶足以爲禦寒之資，又何無衣之足慮耶？

邠民愛上之心猶未已也。時乎四月，葽感陰氣而秀；時乎五月，蜩感陰氣而鳴，則陽極陰生之時矣。八月而禾早可穫，十月而草木隕落，則大寒將至之候矣。雖蠶績無所不備，而禦寒猶恐不足。故於一陽之月，悉率左右而爲于貉之舉，從其羣醜以取狐狸之皮。其服事乎外也如
translation_en:
Adapting to the season to labor outside [Wait—in the original print, the characters 內 and 外 may be transposed or missing a character: "Adapting to the season to labor outside [in the home?], they already present offerings to their superiors to ward off the cold; moved by the season to labor [within/outside?], they likewise present offerings to their superiors to ward off the cold."] Indeed, sericulture and weaving, as well as hunting, are all measures taken to ward off the cold. The people of Bin (邠) prepare for these in advance and dedicate them all to their superiors—how boundless is their loyalty and affection!

In antiquity, the Duke of Zhou (周公) set forth the origins of the moral transformation wrought by Houji (后稷) and Duke Liu (公劉), having the blind musicians recite them morning and evening to instruct King Cheng (成王). He said that to get through the end of the year, the people of Bin could not be without fine clothes, nor could they be without coarse garments. Therefore, in the month for tending silkworms, they gather mulberry leaves to feed the silkworms. As for the large mulberry trees whose branches can be lopped off, they take those axes [and hatchets to] lop off the far-reaching and high-rising branches; as for the small mulberry trees whose branches cannot be lopped off, they pluck their leaves and [leave the branches intact] [?]. With this, the work of sericulture is complete. Come the time after the shrike cries in the seventh month, when the hemp is ripe for spinning in the eighth month, they spin the hemp into cloth; with this, the work of spinning is accomplished. All that is produced from this sericulture and spinning is dyed—some black in color, some yellow in color, while the vermilion is especially bright. Such is their labor within the home; how could it be for their own private enjoyment? All of it is offered to their superiors to make lower garments for the young lords, hoping it will suffice as the means to ward off the cold—what need is there to worry about having no fine clothes?

Yet the love of the people of Bin for their superiors does not stop even here. When it is the fourth month, the milkwort responds to the yin qi and goes to seed; when it is the fifth month, the cicada responds to the yin qi and chirps—this is the time when yang reaches its extreme and yin is born. In the eighth month, the grain is early enough to be harvested, and in the tenth month, the grasses and trees shed their leaves—these are the signs that the great cold is about to arrive. Although nothing in their sericulture and spinning has been left unprepared, they still fear it may not suffice to ward off the cold. Therefore, in the month of the first return of yang [the eleventh month], they lead out all their attendants to go hunting for raccoon-dogs, following the crowds to take the pelts of foxes and wildcats. Such is their labor outside the home…

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
此豈私以自用哉亦以奉上而爲公子之裘庶足以
周衛禦寒之具又何無褐之足慮耶吁蠶績之所成狩
獵之所獲皆不自愛以奉其上邠民何如其知義哉
雖然自食其力而忘乎上者人情之常邠人則汲汲
於愛上何耶盖自后稷教稼穡公劉篤民事其至誠
惻怛之意施於民者非一日矣是以國人感之至愛
之深而報之惟恐其或後也所謂上下之情交相忠
愛者以此故吾每誦七月之詩未嘗不歎先公風化
之遠云
===
昔有成湯自彼氐羌莫敢不来享莫敢不来王
曰商是常天命多辟設都于禹之績歲事来
辟勿予禍適稼穡匪解天命降監下民有嚴
不僭不濫不敢怠遑命于下國封建厥福
鄒旦
同考試官教諭張　批〔高宗平荆楚服諸侯本於不僭不濫不敢怠遑所致塲中作者殊戾本旨是篇立意高而辭不泛〕
宜冠本經
同考試官教諭陳　批得詩人美盛德告成功之旨
punctuated:
此，豈私以自用哉？亦以奉上而爲公子之裘，庶足以周衛禦寒之具，又何無褐之足慮耶？吁！蠶績之所成，狩獵之所獲，皆不自愛以奉其上，邠民何如其知義哉！雖然，自食其力而忘乎上者，人情之常；邠人則汲汲於愛上，何耶？盖自后稷教稼穡，公劉篤民事，其至誠惻怛之意，施於民者非一日矣。是以國人感之至、愛之深，而報之惟恐其或後也。所謂上下之情交相忠愛者以此。故吾每誦《七月》之詩，未嘗不歎先公風化之遠云。
「昔有成湯，自彼氐羌，莫敢不来享，莫敢不来王，曰商是常。天命多辟，設都于禹之績。歲事来辟，勿予禍適，稼穡匪解。天命降監，下民有嚴。不僭不濫，不敢怠遑。命于下國，封建厥福。」
鄒旦
同考試官教諭張批：〔高宗平荆楚、服諸侯，本於不僭不濫、不敢怠遑所致。塲中作者殊戾本旨，是篇立意高而辭不泛，〕宜冠本經。
同考試官教諭陳批：得詩人美盛德、告成功之旨。
translation_en:
…like this, how could they keep them selfishly for their own use? These too were presented to their superiors to make fur coats for the young lords, which might suffice to provide full protection against the cold—so what need was there to worry about having no coarse cloth? Ah! Neither what was produced by sericulture and spinning nor what was taken in the hunt did they begrudge for themselves, offering it all up to their superiors—how deeply the people of Bin understood righteousness! Even so, to live by one's own labor and forget one's superiors is the ordinary way of human feeling; why then were the people of Bin so eager in their love for their superiors? It is because ever since Hou Ji taught sowing and reaping and Duke Liu devoted himself earnestly to the people's affairs, their utmost sincerity and compassionate care had been bestowed upon the people for far more than a single day. Therefore, the people of the state were moved to the utmost and loved them deeply, fearing only that they might be slow in repaying them. This is what is meant by the feelings of superiors and inferiors being bound in mutual loyalty and affection. Thus, whenever I recite the ode "Seventh Month" (Qiyue), I never fail to sigh in admiration at how far-reaching was the transformative influence of the former dukes.

"Of old there was Tang the Successful; from those Di and Qiang, none dared not come to present offerings, none dared not come to acknowledge him as king, saying: 'Shang is our constant rule.' Heaven commanded the many lords to establish their capitals amidst the achievements of Yu. For the annual affairs they came before their sovereign: 'Do not visit us with misfortune or rebuke; in sowing and reaping we have not been remiss.' Heaven's mandate looked down from above, and the people below were reverent and awe-inspiring. He neither erred in reward nor exceeded in punishment; he dared not be indolent or take his ease. Thus Heaven gave its mandate over the states below, and grandly established his felicity."

By Zou Dan 鄒旦.

Associate Examiner, Instructor (jiaoyu) Zhang comments: 〔That Gaozong pacified Jing-Chu and brought the feudal lords to submission stemmed fundamentally from his neither erring in reward nor exceeding in punishment, and his not daring to be indolent or take his ease. Other writers in the examination hall went quite contrary to the original meaning of the text, whereas this essay is lofty in its conception and not diffuse in its phrasing;〕 it deserves to be placed first in this Classic.

Associate Examiner, Instructor Chen comments: It grasps the poet's intent in praising splendid virtue and announcing successful achievement.

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭鄭〔批說出高宗中興氣象宛然可見本房得〕
〔此誠堂不足者歟〕
考試官學正汪〔批鋪叙嚴整可取〕
考試官教授林〔批頌義宜簡古此作得之〕
詩人敘賢王中興之功必原其所以致中興之道夫
功莫大乎平荆楚而服諸侯也然非賢王敬天人而
謹刑賞亦何以致此哉此祀高宗之樂謂夫盤庚沒
而殷道衰楚人叛之久矣我高宗既克之則告之曰
昔我祖成湯之世自彼氐羌之遠莫敢不來享而盡
===
獻納之誠莫敢不來王而盡世見之禮而曰此商之
常禮也况女荆楚曷敢不至哉荆楚既平則諸侯畏
服由是友邦冢君天命建都于禹所治之地者皆以
歲事而來辟蓋以祈王之不譴而曰我之稼穡不敢
怠也烈文辟公天命建國於禹所奠之區者皆以歲
事而來朝蓋以冀王之不責而曰我之稼穡不敢解
也庶可以免咎矣我高宗中興之功如此夫豈無所
自耶蓋以天命降監不在乎他皆在民之視聽則下
民亦有嚴矣惟高宗賞所當賞賞不僭也刑此心之
punctuated:
同考試官教諭鄭〔批：說出高宗中興氣象，宛然可見。本房得此，誠堂不足者歟！〕
考試官學正汪〔批：鋪叙嚴整，可取。〕
考試官教授林〔批：頌義宜簡古，此作得之。〕

詩人敘賢王中興之功，必原其所以致中興之道。夫功莫大乎平荆楚而服諸侯也，然非賢王敬天人而謹刑賞，亦何以致此哉？此祀高宗之樂，謂夫盤庚沒而殷道衰，楚人叛之久矣。我高宗既克之，則告之曰：「昔我祖成湯之世，自彼氐羌之遠，莫敢不來享而盡獻納之誠，莫敢不來王而盡世見之禮，而曰：『此商之常禮也。』况女荆楚，曷敢不至哉？」荆楚既平，則諸侯畏服。由是友邦冢君，天命建都于禹所治之地者，皆以歲事而來辟，蓋以祈王之不譴，而曰：「我之稼穡不敢怠也。」烈文辟公，天命建國於禹所奠之區者，皆以歲事而來朝，蓋以冀王之不責，而曰：「我之稼穡不敢解也，庶可以免咎矣。」我高宗中興之功如此，夫豈無所自耶？蓋以天命降監，不在乎他，皆在民之視聽，則下民亦有嚴矣。惟高宗賞所當賞，賞不僭也；刑此心之
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Zheng, Instructor, 〔comment: It brings out the spirit of Gaozong's dynastic restoration so vividly that it can be seen before one's eyes. For our examination ward to obtain this—is it not truly more than enough [? 誠堂不足者歟, likely a transcription error for 誠何不足者歟 or 誠無不足者歟]?〕
Examiner Wang, Subprefectural Instructor, 〔comment: The exposition is rigorous and well-ordered; it is worthy of selection.〕
Examiner Lin, Prefectural Instructor, 〔comment: An essay on the Sacrificial Odes ought to be concise and archaic in style; this composition achieves that.〕

When the poet recounts the achievement of a worthy king's dynastic restoration, he necessarily traces the way by which that restoration was brought about. Now, no achievement is greater than pacifying Jing-Chu and bringing the feudal lords to submission. Yet had the worthy king not revered Heaven and man and been謹慎 (cautious) with punishments and rewards, how could he have brought this about? This music for sacrificing to Gaozong speaks of how, after Pan Geng died and the Way of Yin declined, the people of Chu had long rebelled against it. Once our Gaozong conquered them, he proclaimed to them: "In the age of our ancestor Cheng Tang of old, even from as far away as the Di and Qiang tribes, none dared not come to present offerings and exhaust their sincerity in tribute, and none dared not come to pay homage to the king and fulfill the ritual of generational audience, saying: 'This is the constant norm of Shang.' How much more so for you, Jing-Chu—how dare you not come?" Once Jing-Chu was pacified, the feudal lords were awed into submission. Thereupon, the rulers of friendly states, whom Heaven had mandated to establish their capitals in the lands brought to order by Yu, all came before the sovereign on the occasion of their annual affairs, praying that the king would not reprove them, and saying: "We have not dared to be remiss in our husbandry." The illustrious feudal princes, whom Heaven had mandated to establish their states in the regions settled by Yu, all came to court on the occasion of their annual affairs, hoping that the king would not censure them, and saying: "We have not dared to be slack in our husbandry, so that we may perhaps escape blame." Such was the achievement of our Gaozong's restoration—how could it have been without a source? For when Heaven's mandate looks down to inspect, it rests in nothing else than the seeing and hearing of the people; thus the common people below are also to be held in awe. Only because Gaozong rewarded those who ought to be rewarded, his rewards were not excessive; [?] [刑, likely a block-cutting error for 而] the… of this mind…

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
有不敢怠刑所當刑刑不濫也而此心之存不敢慢
則所以敬天而畏民者至矣是以皇天眷命奄有四
海福於此乎大建保佑命之奄有九有福於此乎永
錫此高宗所以受命而中興也然則荆楚平而諸侯
服豈偶然哉嗟夫莫爲於前雖美弗彰莫爲於後雖
盛弗傳有商之興非成湯莫能成創造之功非高宗
莫能致中興之盛此高宗所以無愧爲湯之孫而百
世不遷之廟所由立殷武之樂所由作也登歌之際
美盛德而告成功夫豈不宜
===
春秋
王人子突救衛〔莊公六年〕　季子來歸〔閔公元年〕　楚
屈完來盟于師〔僖公四年〕　楚子使椒來聘〔文公九年〕
秦伯使術來聘〔文公十二年〕　吳子使札來聘〔襄公二
十九年〕
同考試官教諭謝　批〔春秋之法因人之賢否事之得失而筆削有自然之權度此作描寫傳例故錄之以爲品藻人物之〕
王任
準的
punctuated:
有不敢怠；刑所當刑，刑不濫也，而此心之存不敢慢，則所以敬天而畏民者至矣。是以皇天眷命，奄有四海，福於此乎大建；保佑命之，奄有九有，福於此乎永錫。此高宗所以受命而中興也。然則荆楚平而諸侯服，豈偶然哉？嗟夫！莫爲於前，雖美弗彰；莫爲於後，雖盛弗傳。有商之興，非成湯莫能成創造之功，非高宗莫能致中興之盛。此高宗所以無愧爲湯之孫，而百世不遷之廟所由立，《殷武》之樂所由作也。登歌之際，美盛德而告成功，夫豈不宜？

《春秋》
「王人子突救衛」〔莊公六年〕、「季子來歸」〔閔公元年〕、「楚屈完來盟于師」〔僖公四年〕、「楚子使椒來聘」〔文公九年〕、「秦伯使術來聘」〔文公十二年〕、「吳子使札來聘」〔襄公二十九年〕。
王任
同考試官教諭謝批：〔《春秋》之法，因人之賢否、事之得失，而筆削有自然之權度。此作描寫傳例，故錄之以爲品藻人物之準的。〕
translation_en:
… [having this mind,] he dared not be indolent; he punished those who ought to be punished, so punishments were not excessive, and in preserving this mind he dared not be negligent. Thus, the way in which he revered Heaven and stood in awe of the people reached the utmost. Therefore, August Heaven looked upon him with favor and gave him the mandate to hold all within the four seas, and blessings were thereby grandly established; it protected, aided, and mandated him to hold all the nine regions, and blessings were thereby perpetually bestowed. This was how Gaozong received the mandate and achieved a dynastic revival. This being so, when Jing-Chu was pacified and the feudal lords submitted, how could it have been by chance? Alas! If nothing is done before, though worthy, it will not be manifest; if nothing is done after, though flourishing, it will not be transmitted. In the rise of the Shang, none but Cheng Tang could have accomplished the merit of founding the dynasty, and none but Gaozong could have brought about the flourishing of its revival. This is why Gaozong was not ashamed to be the descendant of Tang, why the ancestral temple that is not moved for a hundred generations was established, and why the music of the "Yinwu" was composed. When ascending to sing this ode, to praise his abundant virtue and announce his accomplished work to the spirits—how could this not be fitting?

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu)
"The King's man Zitu went to the rescue of Wei" [6th year of Duke Zhuang]; "Jizi came and returned" [1st year of Duke Min]; "Qu Wan of Chu came to make a covenant with the army" [4th year of Duke Xi]; "The Viscount of Chu sent Jiao to come on a mission of friendly inquiry" [9th year of Duke Wen]; "The Earl of Qin sent Shu to come on a mission of friendly inquiry" [12th year of Duke Wen]; "The Viscount of Wu sent Zha to come on a mission of friendly inquiry" [29th year of Duke Xiang].

By Wang Ren 王任.
Associate Examiner, Instructor Xie, comments: [In the method of the Spring and Autumn Annals, depending on the worthiness or unworthiness of men and the success or failure of affairs, its recording and deleting possess a natural standard of weighing and measuring. This piece delineates the precedents of the commentary, so we record it to serve as a standard for evaluating historical figures.]

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
考試官學正□　批〔以中字立論高出人一頭地佳作也〕
考試官教授林　批〔此作得書法可取〕
春秋待人之例不一而責賢之意甚備夫貴乎賢者
制行得其中也季札賢而過乎中春秋不進之以特
筆而待之以常例責備之意何如哉何則中者帝王
相傳之心法也夫子假魯史以寓王法舍中何以耶
是故王朝下士以人通諸侯公子以名著例也而子
突能申王命以赴黔牟之急季友復歸宗國以爲公
室之輔賢可知矣進而書字書子非特筆乎桓莊之
===
春秋荊楚無大夫亦例也而屈完如師能服齊桓之
義繼好以徼先君之福賢可想矣進而書族又非特
筆乎馴致魯文之世楚稍遣椒而來聘秦康命術以
脩禮意非不誠而椒僅以名書事非不善而術但以
名錄豈以楚僭于周秦介乎狄故略之歟若季札讓
國天下賢之曰突曰完未克升其堂奧若椒若術詎
得窺其藩籬今焉銜命而來至于曲阜見禮而知政
聞樂而知德中國之賢者未能或之先也聖人不以
字不以氏不以公子特書之而略以名紀則是例之
punctuated:
考試官學正□　批：〔以「中」字立論，高出人一頭地，佳作也。〕
考試官教授林　批：〔此作得書法，可取。〕

《春秋》待人之例不一，而責賢之意甚備。夫貴乎賢者，制行得其中也。季札賢而過乎中，《春秋》不進之以特筆，而待之以常例，責備之意何如哉！何則？中者，帝王相傳之心法也。夫子假魯史以寓王法，舍中何以耶？是故王朝下士以「人」通，諸侯公子以名著，例也；而子突能申王命以赴黔牟之急，季友復歸宗國以爲公室之輔，賢可知矣，進而書字、書「子」，非特筆乎？桓、莊之《春秋》，荊楚無大夫，亦例也；而屈完如師，能服齊桓之義，繼好以徼先君之福，賢可想矣，進而書族，又非特筆乎？馴致魯文之世，楚稍遣椒而來聘，秦康命術以脩禮，意非不誠而椒僅以名書，事非不善而術但以名錄，豈以楚僭于周、秦介乎狄，故略之歟？若季札讓國，天下賢之，曰突、曰完，未克升其堂奧；若椒、若術，詎得窺其藩籬？今焉銜命而來，至于曲阜，見禮而知政，聞樂而知德，中國之賢者未能或之先也。聖人不以字、不以氏、不以「公子」特書之，而略以名紀，則是例之
translation_en:
Examiner and Confucian School Director □ comments: 〔By grounding its argument in the concept of "the Mean" (zhong), this stands head and shoulders above the rest; it is a fine piece of work.〕
Examiner and Prefectural Director of Studies Lin comments: 〔This composition grasps the principles of calligraphic recording and is worthy of selection.〕

The precedents by which the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) treats individuals are not uniform, yet its intention in demanding perfection of the worthy is thoroughly complete. What is valued in a worthy man is that in regulating his conduct he attains the Mean. Ji Zha 季札 was worthy, yet he exceeded the Mean; when the Spring and Autumn Annals does not promote him with a special entry, but instead treats him according to the ordinary precedent, how profound is its intention of demanding perfection of him! Why is this so? The Mean is the mental discipline handed down from one sovereign king to another. When the Master borrowed the history of Lu 魯 to lodge within it the Kingly Law, if he set aside the Mean, wherewith could he do so?

Therefore, that a lower serviceman of the royal court is referred to generically as "man" (ren), and that a prince of a feudal lord is recorded by his personal name, are standard precedents; yet Zitu 子突 was able to set forth the royal command to rush to the aid of Qianmou 黔牟 in his crisis, and Jiyou 季友 returned to his ancestral state to serve as a support to the ducal house—their worthiness can thus be known. Promoting them by recording a courtesy name or the title "Master" (zi)—is this not a special entry? In the Spring and Autumn Annals of the reigns of Dukes Huan 桓 and Zhuang 莊, that Jing-Chu 荊楚 had no great officers recorded is also a standard precedent; yet when Qu Wan 屈完 went to the army, he was able to submit to the righteousness of Duke Huan of Qi 齊桓 and renew friendly relations so as to seek the blessings of the former rulers—his worthiness can thus be imagined. Promoting him by recording his clan name—is this not also a special entry?

Coming gradually to the era of Duke Wen of Lu 魯文, Chu 楚 began to send Jiao 椒 to come on a mission of friendly inquiry, and Duke Kang of Qin 秦康 commanded Shu 術 to cultivate ritual relations. The intention was not insincere, yet Jiao was written down solely by his personal name; the affair was not ignoble, yet Shu was recorded merely by his personal name. Was it not because Chu usurped royal prerogatives against Zhou 周, and Qin lay hemmed in among the Di 狄 barbarians, that the text treated them summarily?

As for Ji Zha yielding the state, the whole world deemed him worthy. Men like Zitu and Qu Wan were not even able to ascend to his hall and inner chambers; how could men like Jiao and Shu manage even to peer through his hedge? Now he came bearing a mission and arrived at Qufu 曲阜; upon observing the rites he understood the governance, and upon hearing the music he understood the virtue—even the worthies of the Central States could not surpass him. Yet the Sage did not specially record him by his courtesy name, nor by his lineage name, nor as "Prince" (gongzi), but summarily registered him by his personal name. Thus, in terms of precedent…

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
擬術而曾一窔究之不若況季友乎殊不知帝王之
道賢可禪則以天下為公而不拘於世及子可繼則
以天下為家而不必於禪授故壽夢之欲傳國乎季
子者以大王之心為心也諸樊餘祭之拳拳者以仲
雍之心為心也彼王僚無季歷之賢而季子為太伯
之讓豈至德乎使爭弑禍興覆師喪國誰階之也謂
非賢且智過而不得其中者哉貶而書名所以望之
深而責之備也大抵聖人之待人猶化工之於物大
以成大小以成小物各付物而已奚容心焉公乎喜
時春秋猶賢其後世豈有季子之高風而春秋不以
賢者責之哉噫惟與天地同德而達乎時中然後能
與於此非聖人莫能脩之信夫
齊侯宋公江人黃人會于陽穀〔僖公二年〕 公會齊
侯宋公陳侯衛侯鄭伯許男曹伯侵蔡 遂
伐楚次于陘 盟于召陵 齊人執陳轅濤
塗 及江人黃人伐陳〔僖公四年〕
舒洪
同考試官教諭謝 批此題主胡傳本平易場中諸作或□□□
punctuated:
擬術，而曾一窔究之不若，況季友乎？殊不知帝王之道，賢可禪則以天下為公，而不拘於世及；子可繼則以天下為家，而不必於禪授。故壽夢之欲傳國乎季子者，以大王之心為心也；諸樊、餘祭之拳拳者，以仲雍之心為心也。彼王僚無季歷之賢，而季子為太伯之讓，豈至德乎？使爭弑禍興，覆師喪國，誰階之也？謂非賢且智過而不得其中者哉！貶而書名，所以望之深而責之備也。大抵聖人之待人，猶化工之於物，大以成大，小以成小，物各付物而已，奚容心焉？公乎喜時，《春秋》猶賢其後，世豈有季子之高風，而《春秋》不以賢者責之哉？噫！惟與天地同德，而達乎時中，然後能與於此。非聖人莫能脩之，信夫！
齊侯、宋公、江人、黃人會于陽穀〔僖公二年〕；公會齊侯、宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯侵蔡，遂伐楚，次于陘，盟于召陵；齊人執陳轅濤塗；及江人、黃人伐陳〔僖公四年〕。
舒洪
同考試官教諭謝批：「此題主《胡傳》，本平易。場中諸作，或□□□
translation_en:
…[Jiao 椒 (?)] and Shu 術, and not even on a par with [Tu 突 and Wan 完 (?)], much less Ji You 季友! They fail to understand that in the Way of emperors and kings, when a worthy man can be yielded the throne, the realm is treated as shared by all without being bound to hereditary succession; when a son is fit to succeed, the realm is treated as a family inheritance without needing to resort to abdication. Thus, when Shoumeng 壽夢 wished to transmit the state to Jizi 季子 (Jizha 季札), he took the mind of King Tai 大王 as his own mind; when Zhufan 諸樊 and Yuzhai 餘祭 held fast to this intention, they took the mind of Zhongyong 仲雍 as their own mind. That King Liao 王僚 lacked the worthiness of Jili 季歷, and yet Jizi practiced the yielding of Taibo 太伯—how could this be supreme virtue? That disasters of contention and regicide arose, armies were overthrown, and the state was ruined—who laid the steps for this? Can it not be said that the worthy and wise erred by going too far and failing to attain the mean! Demoting him and recording him by his personal name was the way to expect much of him and hold him to the standard of perfection. In general, the sage's treatment of men is like Creative Nature's treatment of things: the great are brought to completion as great, the small are brought to completion as small; each thing is simply dealt with according to what it is—how could any personal bias be admitted therein? Even in the case of [Gongzi (?)] Xishi 公子喜時, the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) still praised his posterity for his worthiness; how could there be the lofty character of Jizi in the world without the Spring and Autumn Annals holding him to the full standard of a worthy man? Alas! Only one who shares the same virtue as Heaven and Earth and comprehends the timely mean is able to participate in this. Truly, none but a sage could have compiled it!

"The Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, an officer of Jiang, and an officer of Huang met at Yanggu" [Second year of Duke Xi]; "The Duke met the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Earl of Cao to make an incursion into Cai; they thereupon attacked Chu and halted at Xing, and covenanted at Shaoling; the people of Qi seized Yuan Taotu of Chen; together with forces of Jiang and Huang, we attacked Chen" [Fourth year of Duke Xi].

Shu Hong 舒洪

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
可用江黄以伐楚不當用之以伐陳者每以服楚之後執陳仍以□
伯心驕者間得奇正之說又分截不明者殊失本旨惟此作得傳
意者闡錄有斷制非蘊經中之作者乎故表而出之
考試官學正汪　批此題胡氏專辨陽穀一會之謀作者往往
昧旨惟此篇體傳立意而文足以發之故錄出以範學者
考試官教授林　批得屬詞比事之旨
即伯好而知其攘夷之謀究伯事以驗其用人之實
于以見齊桓陽穀之會結江黄以謀伐楚而其行師
之奇正處事之方略春秋詳書始末以善之也嘅念
===
周道既微楚氛寖惡陵我中華已非一日幸而齊桓
者出盡安攘之遠謀啓陽穀之大會彼諸侯之崇莫
尊乎宋宋公既至中華之友邦協矣要荒之君莫遠
乎江黄江黄既來外夷之右臂失矣吾想其會聚之
時意豈不曰荆尸甚堅乘廣甚銳今欲制之計將安
在必也孰當其前俾之進焉不能敵孰掇其後俾之
退焉無所憑謀既定乎十全師遂合于八國侵蔡而
南及陘而次諸侯大衆厚集其陣聲罪致討則楚人
理屈而吾之內勢既震所謂聚而為正也江人黄人
punctuated:
可用江、黄以伐楚，不當用之以伐陳者，每以服楚之後執陳仍以□伯心驕者，間得奇正之說又分截不明者，殊失本旨。惟此作得傳意者，闡錄有斷制，非蘊經中之作者乎？故表而出之。
考試官學正汪批：此題胡氏專辨陽穀一會之謀，作者往往昧旨。惟此篇體傳立意，而文足以發之，故錄出以範學者。
考試官教授林批：得屬詞比事之旨。
即伯好而知其攘夷之謀，究伯事以驗其用人之實，于以見齊桓陽穀之會，結江、黄以謀伐楚，而其行師之奇正、處事之方略，《春秋》詳書始末以善之也。嘅念周道既微，楚氛寖惡，陵我中華，已非一日。幸而齊桓者出，盡安攘之遠謀，啓陽穀之大會。彼諸侯之崇，莫尊乎宋；宋公既至，中華之友邦協矣。要荒之君，莫遠乎江、黄；江、黄既來，外夷之右臂失矣。吾想其會聚之時，意豈不曰：「荆尸甚堅，乘廣甚銳，今欲制之，計將安在？必也孰當其前，俾之進焉不能敵；孰掇其後，俾之退焉無所憑。」謀既定乎十全，師遂合于八國。侵蔡而南，及陘而次。諸侯大衆，厚集其陣，聲罪致討，則楚人理屈而吾之內勢既震，所謂聚而為正也；江人、黄人
translation_en:
…[arguing that] one could use Jiang and Huang to attack Chu, yet should not have used them to attack Chen, or frequently [attributing] the seizure of [Yuan Taotu of] Chen after the submission of Chu to [?] the hegemon's heart growing arrogant, while those who occasionally grasp the theory of the unorthodox and orthodox [maneuvers] fail to divide the sections clearly—all of which utterly miss the fundamental purport. Only this composition grasps the meaning of the Commentary, expounding and recording it with decisive judgment; is its author not one deeply steeped in the Classic? Therefore we single it out for publication.

Examiner Wang, Subprefectural Instructor, comments: On this topic, Master Hu [An'guo] specifically analyzes the strategy behind the single meeting at Yanggu, yet writers frequently obscure the main point. Only this essay embodies the Commentary in establishing its theme, and its prose suffices to bring it forth; therefore it is recorded and published as a model for scholars.

Examiner Lin, Prefectural Instructor, comments: It grasps the principle of connecting words and comparing events.

By examining the hegemon's amicable meetings, one knows his strategy for repelling the barbarians; by investigating the hegemon's deeds, one verifies the reality of how he employed men. From this we see how in Duke Huan of Qi's meeting at Yanggu, he allied with Jiang and Huang in order to plan the campaign against Chu, and how the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) recorded the beginning and end in detail in order to commend the unorthodox and orthodox deployments of his military marches and the strategic planning of his handling of affairs. Looking back with a sigh, once the Way of Zhou had declined, the miasma of Chu grew increasingly noxious, encroaching upon our Central States for more than a single day. Fortunately, Duke Huan of Qi emerged, exhausting far-reaching plans to pacify [the interior] and repel [the barbarians], and convened the great assembly at Yanggu. Among the exalted feudal lords, none was more venerable than Song; once the Duke of Song arrived, the friendly states of the Central States were brought into harmony. Among the rulers of the remote and wild domains, none were more distant than Jiang and Huang; once Jiang and Huang came, the right arm of the outer barbarians was lost. When I imagine the moment of their gathering, did their thoughts not run thus: "The Chu battle array (jingshi) is exceedingly solid, and their war chariots (shengguang) are exceedingly sharp; if we now wish to subdue them, where shall our plan lie? Assuredly, who will confront their front so that when they advance they cannot withstand us, and who will press upon their rear so that when they retreat they have nothing to rely upon?" Once the strategy was settled with complete perfection, the armies were thereupon united from eight states. Invading Cai and moving south, they reached Xing and halted. The great multitude of the feudal lords massed their formations thickly, proclaiming [Chu's] crimes and executing punitive expedition; thus the men of Chu were put in the wrong while our internal might already reverberated—this is what is called gathering together to form the orthodox [force]. The men of Jiang and the men of Huang…

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
各守其境按兵不動則楚人勢孤而吾之外援已成
所謂分而為奇也偉哉堯敵制勝之謀允矣戰勝攻
取之策及夫屈完如師桓則退于召陵而盟禮定陳
人悞軍桓則循海以歸而濤塗執文告昭宣于一時
武略震驚于四裔功既成矣志既遂矣然後披及江
黃之師以為伐陳之舉則知侵蔡次陘而二國不與
自為犄角之勢明矣故春秋於陽穀之役只會而未
言者蓋是謀也非所謂即伯好而知其攘夷之謀究
伯事以驗其用人之實者乎吁齊桓一匡天下免民
左衽其功正在于此春秋備書之也宜哉大抵慮勝
而動好謀而成自入春秋以來未有及於□□桓治楚
之事者也獨惜乎蔡仁既盟楚人滅黃而□
卒使小國賢君坐困於蠻夷之手可覩□
桓而桓有負於江黃矣孟子曰五伯桓公□
五伯假之也觀此益信
禮記
禮樂交錯於中發形於外是故其成也懌恭敬
而温文立太傅少傅以養之欲其知父子君
punctuated:
各守其境，按兵不動，則楚人勢孤，而吾之外援已成，所謂分而為奇也。偉哉，料敵制勝之謀；允矣，戰勝攻取之策！及夫屈完如師，桓則退于召陵而盟禮定；陳人悞軍，桓則循海以歸而濤塗執。文告昭宣于一時，武略震驚于四裔。功既成矣，志既遂矣，然後披及江、黃之師，以為伐陳之舉，則知侵蔡、次陘而二國不與，自為犄角之勢明矣。故《春秋》於陽穀之役，只會而未言者，蓋是謀也。非所謂即伯好而知其攘夷之謀，究伯事以驗其用人之實者乎？吁！齊桓一匡天下，免民左衽，其功正在于此，《春秋》備書之也，宜哉！大抵慮勝而動，好謀而成，自入《春秋》以來，未有及於□□桓治楚之事者也。獨惜乎蔡仁既盟，楚人滅黃，而□卒使小國賢君坐困於蠻夷之手，可覩□桓，而桓有負於江、黃矣。孟子曰：「五伯，桓公□。」五伯，假之也，觀此益信。

《禮記》
「禮樂交錯於中，發形於外，是故其成也懌，恭敬而温文。立太傅、少傅以養之，欲其知父子君
translation_en:
… each guard their own borders and hold their troops in position without moving, then the men of Chu are isolated in strength and our external assistance is already established—this is what is called dividing forces to act as the unorthodox flank. How grand was this plan for assessing the enemy and securing victory [reading 料 for 堯]! How fitting was this strategy for winning battles and taking by storm! When Qu Wan came to the army, Duke Huan retreated to Shaoling and the covenant rites were settled; when the men of Chen misled the army, Duke Huan returned along the coast and Yuan Taotu was seized. Civil proclamations were brilliantly announced at the time, and military strategy awed the four borderlands. Once the merit was achieved and the ambition fulfilled, only then did he draw upon the armies of Jiang and Huang to undertake the campaign against Chen. Thus we know that when he invaded Cai and halted at Xing, the fact that those two states did not participate shows clearly that they formed a pincer formation on their own. Therefore, in the campaign of Yanggu, that the Spring and Autumn Annals merely recorded the meeting without stating more was doubtless because of this plan. Is this not what is meant by examining the hegemon's amity to know his plan for repelling the barbarians, and investigating the hegemon's deeds to verify the reality of how he employed men? Alas! Duke Huan of Qi brought order to the entire realm and saved the people from buttoning their garments on the left; his merit lies precisely in this, and it is fitting indeed that the Spring and Autumn Annals recorded it in full! On the whole, in calculating victory before moving and delighting in planning to achieve success, ever since the beginning of the Spring and Autumn period there had been nothing to equal Duke Huan's [□□] management of the affair of Chu. It is only a pity that after the covenant at Caiqiu [蔡仁(?)] had been sworn, the men of Chu destroyed Huang, and [□] in the end allowed the worthy rulers of small states to sit trapped at the hands of the southern barbarians. One can see that [Jiang and Huang did not fail(?)] Duke Huan, yet Duke Huan failed Jiang and Huang! Mencius said: "Of the Five Hegemons, Duke Huan [was the most盛 (flourishing)]." And: "The Five Hegemons borrowed it [benevolence]." Viewing this, it is all the more credible.

Record of Rites (Liji)
"Rites and music interweave within, and manifest in form without; therefore, when his character is completed, he is joyful, respectful, reverent, gentle, and refined. The Grand Mentor and Junior Mentor are established to nurture him, desiring that he know the way of father and son, ruler and …"

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
臣之道也
葉元
同考試官學正陳　批〔題本正大作者多分截不明晚得此卷　理明詞達讀之令人躍然〕
考試官學正汪　批〔先王所以教養者欲其明人倫也此作良是〕
考試官教授林　批〔得三王教養世子之道〕
觀先王於世子教有成功養有常職者無非欲其審
夫人倫之理焉盖父子君臣人之大倫也然所以教
而養之者豈非欲世子知乎此哉且夫三王之教世
===
子有禮以脩外而禮之脩則達於中有樂以脩內而
樂之脩則達於外然既有諸中必發形於外是以其
成也懽忻之情油然而生悅懌之意藹然而出有以
見其內之和恭見乎外敬主乎中温而不暴文而不
野有以見其外之和如此則教之之道可謂大矣苟
非其人道不虛行於是設太傅之官以身爲教乎以
長而成之使禮樂之道無不行立少傅之職以言爲
教乎以造而就之俾禮樂之教無敢廢如此則養之
之道可謂至矣夫所以教養之者豈有他哉誠以內
punctuated:
臣之道也。」

葉元

同考試官學正陳　批〔題本正大，作者多分截不明，晚得此卷，理明詞達，讀之令人躍然。〕
考試官學正汪　批〔先王所以教養者，欲其明人倫也，此作良是。〕
考試官教授林　批〔得三王教養世子之道。〕

觀先王於世子，教有成功，養有常職者，無非欲其審夫人倫之理焉。盖父子、君臣，人之大倫也，然所以教而養之者，豈非欲世子知乎此哉？且夫三王之教世子，有禮以脩外，而禮之脩則達於中；有樂以脩內，而樂之脩則達於外。然既有諸中，必發形於外，是以其成也，懽忻之情油然而生，悅懌之意藹然而出，有以見其內之和；恭見乎外，敬主乎中，温而不暴，文而不野，有以見其外之和。如此，則教之之道可謂大矣。苟非其人，道不虛行。於是設太傅之官，以身爲教乎，以長而成之，使禮樂之道無不行；立少傅之職，以言爲教乎，以造而就之，俾禮樂之教無敢廢。如此，則養之之道可謂至矣。夫所以教養之者，豈有他哉？誠以內
translation_en:
… and ruler and minister."

Ye Yuan 葉元

Associate Examiner and Subprefectural Instructor (Xuezheng) Chen 陳 comments: [The quotation is inherently upright and grand, yet most writers failed to divide its sections clearly. Late in the reading I obtained this paper: its reasoning is clear and its phrasing lucid; reading it makes one leap with delight.]
Examiner and Subprefectural Instructor (Xuezheng) Wang 汪 comments: [The reason the former kings instructed and nurtured the Heir Apparent was that they wished him to understand human moral relationships; this composition gets it quite right.]
Examiner and Prefectural Instructor (Jiaoshou) Lin 林 comments: [It grasps the Way by which the Three Kings instructed and nurtured the Heir Apparent.]

When we observe that in dealing with the Heir Apparent, the former kings achieved success in his instruction and established regular offices for his nurturing, all of this was solely because they wished him to thoroughly understand the principles of human moral relationships. For father and son, and ruler and minister, are the great moral relationships of mankind; how could the reason for instructing and nurturing him be anything other than wishing the Heir Apparent to know these?

Now, when the Three Kings instructed the Heir Apparent, there was ritual to cultivate the exterior, and the cultivation of ritual reached into the interior; there was music to cultivate the interior, and the cultivation of music reached out to the exterior. Once these were possessed within, they necessarily manifested in form without. Therefore, upon his completion, feelings of joy arose spontaneously and an air of gladness came forth abundantly, whereby one could see the harmony of his interior; respectfulness appeared on the outside while reverence presided within, gentle and not violent, refined and not rustic, whereby one could see the harmony of his exterior. Being thus, the Way of instructing him may truly be called great.

Yet if there are not the right men, the Way does not operate in a vacuum. Thereupon they established the office of Grand Mentor (Taifu), teaching through personal example to foster and bring him to completion, so that the Way of ritual and music would never fail to be practiced; and they instituted the post of Junior Mentor (Shaofu), teaching through words to mold and bring him to accomplishment, so that the instruction of ritual and music would never dare be neglected. Being thus, the Way of nurturing him may truly be called utmost.

Why did they so instruct and nurture him—could there have been any other reason? Truly it was because within…

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
則父子人之大倫也今所以教養世子者正欲其知
乎父子之親焉外則君臣亦人之大倫也今所以教
養世子者正欲其知乎君臣之義焉吁教養之道既
無不盡世子之德又豈有不成者哉大抵世子者天
下之大本也處夫儲貳之位將有承天踐阼之任君
國子民之責爲君父者苟教之無方養之無法何以
成君人之德而勝負荷之重哉故曰有父之親有君
之尊然後兼天下而有之然則先王之教養世子豈
事虛文也哉
===
五行以爲質故事可復也
趙玉
同考試官學正陳　批〔場中作者多於五行爲質處安頓不切惟此能覆說前章之事深合本旨宜錄以冠本房〕
考試官學正汪　批〔發明五行爲質處可觀〕
考試官教授林　批〔允如初考〕
惟歲事取正於五行故歲事旣周而可舉蓋五行之
氣周而復始也國家歲事之常苟能取正於五行之
時令則其事又豈不可周而復始哉記禮者謂文聖
punctuated:
則父子，人之大倫也；今所以教養世子者，正欲其知乎父子之親焉。外則君臣，亦人之大倫也；今所以教養世子者，正欲其知乎君臣之義焉。吁！教養之道既無不盡，世子之德又豈有不成者哉？大抵世子者，天下之大本也。處夫儲貳之位，將有承天踐阼之任、君國子民之責。爲君父者，苟教之無方，養之無法，何以成君人之德而勝負荷之重哉？故曰：「有父之親，有君之尊，然後兼天下而有之。」然則先王之教養世子，豈事虛文也哉？

五行以爲質，故事可復也。
趙玉
同考試官學正陳　批〔場中作者多於「五行爲質」處安頓不切，惟此能覆說前章之事，深合本旨，宜錄以冠本房。〕
考試官學正汪　批〔發明「五行爲質」處可觀。〕
考試官教授林　批〔允如初考。〕

惟歲事取正於五行，故歲事旣周而可舉。蓋五行之氣，周而復始也；國家歲事之常，苟能取正於五行之時令，則其事又豈不可周而復始哉？記禮者謂文：聖
translation_en:
… within the family, the relation of father and son is a great human bond; the reason for educating and nurturing the heir apparent now is precisely to make him understand the affection between father and son. Outside the family, the relation of ruler and subject is also a great human bond; the reason for educating and nurturing the heir apparent now is precisely to make him understand the duty between ruler and subject. Ah! Once the way of educating and nurturing has been exhausted in every respect, how could the virtue of the heir apparent fail to be brought to completion? In general, the heir apparent is the great foundation of the realm. Occupying the position of heir and second in command, he will bear the task of succeeding to Heaven's mandate and ascending the throne, and the responsibility of ruling the state and treating the people as his children. If he who is ruler and father educates him without proper method and nurtures him without proper model, how could the heir complete the virtue of one who rules over men and bear the weight of his burden? Therefore it is said: "Only when one has the affection due a father and the reverence due a ruler can one embrace and possess all under Heaven." This being so, in educating and nurturing the heir apparent, how could the former kings have been engaging in empty formalities?

"Having the Five Phases as their substance, affairs can therefore be repeated."
Zhao Yu 趙玉
Associate Examiner, Subprefectural Instructor (xuezheng) Chen 陳 comments: [Most writers in the examination hall did not place "having the Five Phases as substance" aptly; only this essay was able to recapitulate the affairs of the preceding passage, deeply matching the original purport. It should be selected to head this examination ward.]
Examiner, Subprefectural Instructor (xuezheng) Wang 汪 comments: [Its elucidation of "having the Five Phases as substance" is well worth reading.]
Examiner, Prefectural Instructor (jiaoshou) Lin 林 comments: [I concur with the initial assessment.]

Because the yearly affairs take the Five Phases as their standard, once the yearly affairs have completed a cycle they can be carried out again. For the vital energy (qi) of the Five Phases completes a cycle and begins anew; if the regular yearly affairs of the state can take the seasonal ordinances of the Five Phases as their standard, then how could those affairs not also complete a cycle and begin anew?
