title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
人作則必本造化彼春木夏火秋金冬水而土旺四
季位居中央此五行之運於四時而有十二月也聖
人作為五聲六律十二管而取正於五行之時令則
春角夏徵秋商冬羽宮配乎中央而更迭為主每月
各有其律焉造為五味六和十二食而取正於五行
之時令則春酸夏苦秋辛冬鹹滑甘寓乎四時而更
相為質每月各有其食焉以至施為五色六章十二
衣而又取正於五行之時令則春青夏朱秋白冬黑
黃合乎中央而更相為主每月豈不各有其衣乎惟
===
其取正於五行之時令如此則其事有可復者焉如
聲律用於今歲既一周矣來歲由春徂冬皆可依昔
而舉用非若他事之宜於已然而不宜於將然也色
味用於今歲既一終矣來歲自春至冬悉可循序而
興行非如他事之宜於已往而不宜於將來也愚故
曰惟歲事取正於五行故歲事既周而可舉者以此
抑考是章之旨自天地以為本至人情以為田皆是
覆說前章諸事無非聖人仰觀於天俯察於地近取
諸人作為典則以示教於天下也然為法甚備為治
punctuated: 人作則，必本造化。彼春木、夏火、秋金、冬水，而土旺四季、位居中央，此五行之運於四時而有十二月也。聖人作為五聲、六律、十二管，而取正於五行之時令，則春角、夏徵、秋商、冬羽，宮配乎中央，而更迭為主，每月各有其律焉；造為五味、六和、十二食，而取正於五行之時令，則春酸、夏苦、秋辛、冬鹹，滑甘寓乎四時，而更相為質，每月各有其食焉；以至施為五色、六章、十二衣，而又取正於五行之時令，則春青、夏朱、秋白、冬黑，黃合乎中央，而更相為主，每月豈不各有其衣乎？惟其取正於五行之時令如此，則其事有可復者焉。如聲律用於今歲，既一周矣，來歲由春徂冬，皆可依昔而舉用，非若他事之宜於已然而不宜於將然也；色味用於今歲，既一終矣，來歲自春至冬，悉可循序而興行，非如他事之宜於已往而不宜於將來也。愚故曰：「惟歲事取正於五行，故歲事既周而可舉」者，以此。抑考是章之旨，自「天地以為本」至「人情以為田」，皆是覆說前章諸事，無非聖人仰觀於天、俯察於地、近取諸人，作為典則，以示教於天下也。然為法甚備，為治
translation_en:
… the sages, in establishing standards, necessarily grounded them in the workings of nature. Thus, wood in spring, fire in summer, metal in autumn, and water in winter, while earth flourishes across the four seasons and occupies the central position—this is how the Five Phases circulate through the four seasons to form the twelve months. When the sages instituted the five notes, six yang pitch-pipes, and twelve pitch-tubes, taking their standard from the seasonal ordinances of the Five Phases, then jiao corresponded to spring, zhi to summer, shang to autumn, and yu to winter, with gong matched to the center; alternating as the dominant tone, each month had its proper pitch-pipe. When they created the five flavors, six harmonizations, and twelve seasonal foods, taking their standard from the seasonal ordinances of the Five Phases, then sour corresponded to spring, bitter to summer, acrid to autumn, and salty to winter, with slippery and sweet lodged throughout the four seasons; alternating as the substance, each month had its proper food. And when they went on to display the five colors, six emblems, and twelve seasonal garments, again taking their standard from the seasonal ordinances of the Five Phases, then blue-green corresponded to spring, vermilion to summer, white to autumn, and black to winter, with yellow matched to the center; alternating as the dominant hue, did not each month likewise have its proper garment?

Precisely because these take their standard from the seasonal ordinances of the Five Phases in this way, the practices can be repeated. For instance, once the notes and pitch-pipes used in the present year have completed their cycle, in the coming year from spring through winter they can all be put into effect just as before—unlike other affairs that suit what has already been done but not what is yet to come. Once the colors and flavors used in the present year have come to an end, in the coming year from spring through winter they can all be carried out in due sequence—unlike other affairs that suit the past but not the future. This is why I say: "Because the yearly affairs take their standard from the Five Phases, once the yearly affairs have completed their cycle they can be carried out again."

Moreover, if we examine the import of this passage, from "taking Heaven and Earth as the root" down to "taking human feelings as the field," it all recapitulates the various matters of the preceding passage: none of it is anything other than the sages looking up to contemplate Heaven, looking down to examine Earth, and drawing near at hand from humanity to establish canons and standards so as to set forth instruction for all under Heaven. Yet when the regulations are so complete and the governance …

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
甚詳宜有休徵以應之矣故下文又以四靈以為畜
言之於此可見聖人體信達順之道也歟
論
王者以仁義為麗
四　羅奎
同考試官教諭沈　批〔議論曲折且善斷制非有筆底波瀾者不能也多士之冠舍子其誰〕
考試官學正汪　批〔議論醇正筆意老健讀之令人起敬宜置之魁選與論俱然〕
考試官教授林　批〔筆力老蒼文勢雄偉真百鳥中之孤鳳也〕
天子所以光天下者不以人麗為麗而以天麗
為麗焉天麗之麗乃麗天下之麗也豈以宮室
為哉麗天下莫切於仁義莫大於仁義仁義乃
天麗之麗耳不必雕飾而自輝煌於天下不必
聳瞻而自壯觀於天下宮室云乎哉宮室乃人
麗之麗耳人麗之麗不過麗人之目不能麗人
之心不過麗人之欲不能麗人之天仁義乃麗
人之心麗人之天王者以仁義為麗是乃為真
punctuated:
甚詳，宜有休徵以應之矣。故下文又以「四靈以為畜」言之。於此可見聖人體信達順之道也歟！

論

王者以仁義為麗

四　羅奎

同考試官教諭沈　批〔議論曲折，且善斷制，非有筆底波瀾者不能也。多士之冠，舍子其誰？〕
考試官學正汪　批〔議論醇正，筆意老健，讀之令人起敬。宜置之魁選，與論俱然。〕
考試官教授林　批〔筆力老蒼，文勢雄偉，真百鳥中之孤鳳也。〕

天子所以光天下者，不以人麗為麗，而以天麗為麗焉。天麗之麗，乃麗天下之麗也，豈以宮室為哉？麗天下莫切於仁義，莫大於仁義，仁義乃天麗之麗耳。不必雕飾，而自輝煌於天下；不必聳瞻，而自壯觀於天下，宮室云乎哉？宮室乃人麗之麗耳。人麗之麗，不過麗人之目，不能麗人之心；不過麗人之欲，不能麗人之天。仁義乃麗人之心、麗人之天。王者以仁義為麗，是乃為真
translation_en:
… is extremely detailed, so there ought to be auspicious signs in response to it. Therefore, the text below goes on to speak of "taking the four灵 (numinous creatures) as domestic animals." From this, can one not see the sage's Way of embodying trustworthiness and achieving compliance!

Discourse

"A true king takes benevolence and righteousness as his magnificence."

[No. 4?] Luo Kui 羅奎

Associate Examiner, County Director of Studies Shen 沈, comments: [The argument winds through intricate turns and excels at decisive judgment; none without surging waves beneath his brush could achieve this. Who if not you should be the crown of the many scholars?]
Examiner, Subprefectural Director of Studies Wang 汪, comments: [The argument is pure and orthodox, the brushwork mature and vigorous; reading it inspires respect. He ought to be placed among the top selections—both the person and his discourse are worthy of it (or: public opinion agrees).]
Examiner, Prefectural Director of Studies Lin 林, comments: [The force of the brush is seasoned and venerable, the momentum of the prose grand and imposing; truly a lone phoenix among a hundred birds!]

That by which the Son of Heaven illuminates all under Heaven is not taking human magnificence as magnificence, but taking heavenly magnificence as magnificence. The magnificence of heavenly magnificence is the magnificence that adorns all under Heaven; how could it consist of palaces and chambers? For adorning all under Heaven, nothing is more essential than benevolence and righteousness, and nothing is greater than benevolence and righteousness; benevolence and righteousness are simply the magnificence of heavenly magnificence. Without needing carved ornaments, they naturally shine brightly throughout the realm; without needing to tower aloft for men to gaze upon, they naturally present a grand spectacle throughout the realm—what do palaces and chambers have to do with it? Palaces and chambers are merely the magnificence of human magnificence. The magnificence of human magnificence merely dazzles people's eyes, yet cannot adorn people's minds; it merely gratifies people's desires, yet cannot adorn people's heavenly nature. Benevolence and righteousness are what adorn people's minds and adorn people's heavenly nature. When a true king takes benevolence and righteousness as his magnificence, this is true…

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
麗矣蕭何以宮室爲麗曷能麗天下哉原何之
心正以天下甫定人心初服非極壯觀無以聳
天下之觀瞻一天下之心志貽範後世使無以
加故於未央之作極大其規模殊不知王者之
麗天下不在於宮室而在於仁義仁即天下之
廣居也義即天下之大道也能大脩其仁大脩
其義則仁也義也即嚴人心之殿陛即凜人心
之門墻即固人心之郛郭豈在於壯宮室始足
以誇麗於天下哉天下之心同此仁也同此義
===
也以仁義爲麗豈不麗其所麗哉大脩於一身
麗於一家矣大脩於一家麗於一國矣大脩於
一國麗于天下矣大脩於天下麗于四夷矣贊
化育者在是參天地者在是宮室之麗寧有此
哉若宮室有以麗天下堯何土階其級也禹何
宮室其卑也惟其所以麗者不在乎此此古先
聖王皆不以此爲麗而以仁義爲麗焉堯之都
平陽光被四表堯以仁義爲麗也舜之都蒲坂
光宅天下舜以仁義爲麗也禹之都安邑文
punctuated: 麗矣。蕭何以宮室爲麗，曷能麗天下哉？原何之心，正以天下甫定，人心初服，非極壯觀，無以聳天下之觀瞻，一天下之心志，貽範後世，使無以加；故於未央之作，極大其規模。殊不知王者之麗天下，不在於宮室，而在於仁義。仁即天下之廣居也，義即天下之大道也。能大脩其仁，大脩其義，則仁也、義也，即嚴人心之殿陛，即凜人心之門墻，即固人心之郛郭，豈在於壯宮室，始足以誇麗於天下哉？天下之心，同此仁也，同此義也；以仁義爲麗，豈不麗其所麗哉？大脩於一身，麗於一家矣；大脩於一家，麗於一國矣；大脩於一國，麗于天下矣；大脩於天下，麗于四夷矣。贊化育者在是，參天地者在是，宮室之麗寧有此哉？若宮室有以麗天下，堯何土階其級也？禹何宮室其卑也？惟其所以麗者不在乎此，此古先聖王皆不以此爲麗，而以仁義爲麗焉。堯之都平陽，光被四表，堯以仁義爲麗也；舜之都蒲坂，光宅天下，舜以仁義爲麗也；禹之都安邑，文
translation_en: …splendor! Xiao He 蕭何 took palaces and halls as splendor—how could that bring splendor to the realm? Tracing Xiao He's intention, it was precisely because the realm had just been pacified and people's hearts had only newly submitted; without extreme magnificence, there would be no way to awe the gaze of the world, unify the minds and wills of the realm, and leave a standard for later generations so that nothing more could be added to it. Therefore, in constructing the Weiyang Palace 未央宮, he maximized its scale. Yet he failed to realize that a true king's bringing splendor to the realm lies not in palaces and halls, but in benevolence and righteousness. Benevolence is none other than the spacious dwelling of the world; righteousness is none other than the great highway of the world. If one can greatly cultivate his benevolence and greatly cultivate his righteousness, then benevolence and righteousness themselves will dignify the palace steps within people's hearts, make awesome the gates and walls within people's hearts, and fortify the outer city walls within people's hearts. How could it depend on making palaces and halls magnificent before one is able to boast of splendor to the world? The hearts of the world share this same benevolence and share this same righteousness. Taking benevolence and righteousness as splendor—does this not make splendid that which truly ought to be splendid? When greatly cultivated in one's own person, it shines in one's family; when greatly cultivated in one's family, it shines in one's state; when greatly cultivated in one's state, it shines throughout the realm; when greatly cultivated throughout the realm, it shines among the four barbarian tribes. That which assists the transforming and nourishing powers of nature lies in this; that which forms a triad with Heaven and Earth lies in this. How could the splendor of palaces and halls ever possess such power? If palaces and halls were enough to bring splendor to the realm, why did Yao 堯 have earthen steps for his stairs? Why did Yu 禹 make his palaces and halls so humble? It was solely because that by which they brought splendor did not lie therein; thus the ancient sage-kings never took these as splendor, but instead took benevolence and righteousness as splendor. When Yao made his capital at Pingyang 平陽, his radiance reached the four extremities—this was Yao taking benevolence and righteousness as splendor. When Shun 舜 made his capital at Puban 蒲坂, he gloriously dwelt over the realm—this was Shun taking benevolence and righteousness as splendor. When Yu made his capital at Anyi 安邑, his civilizing influence…

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
敷于四海禹以仁義爲麗也懋昭大德兆民允
殖非湯之都于亳以仁義爲麗乎光于四方顯
于西土非文王之都于岐以仁義爲麗乎丕單
稱德海隅率俾抑非武王都于鎬以仁義爲麗
乎王者既皆以仁義爲麗矣何也何獨以宮室
爲麗哉以宮室爲麗必不能麗天下矣彼其飛
宮傾室非不麗也適足以來胥讒麗何在焉瑤
臺瓊室非不麗也適足以致怨讟麗何有焉作
阿房走咸陽跨渭川非不欲麗天下也然未免
===
於焦土又何麗之有哉是則麗天下誠不在宮
室而在於仁義也脩之以仁義不必麗宮室而
自麗於天下矣蕭何以宮室爲麗非矣雖曰天
子當以四海爲家惟極壯麗方能鎮服其心然
亦末上論事耳豈知所本也歟雖然何固不知
所本然漢高亦豈知所本者耶未央之成初見
其壯麗之極固未嘗不怒及聆四海爲家之語
又未嘗不悅此其心非以宮室爲麗乎噫漢之
君相舉不知所麗矣然自漢而下能知仁義者
punctuated: 敷于四海，禹以仁義爲麗也。懋昭大德，兆民允殖，非湯之都于亳，以仁義爲麗乎？光于四方，顯于西土，非文王之都于岐，以仁義爲麗乎？丕單稱德，海隅率俾，抑非武王都于鎬，以仁義爲麗乎？王者既皆以仁義爲麗矣，何也，何獨以宮室爲麗哉？以宮室爲麗，必不能麗天下矣。彼其飛宮傾室，非不麗也，適足以來胥讒，麗何在焉？瑤臺瓊室，非不麗也，適足以致怨讟，麗何有焉？作阿房，走咸陽，跨渭川，非不欲麗天下也，然未免於焦土，又何麗之有哉？是則麗天下誠不在宮室而在於仁義也。脩之以仁義，不必麗宮室而自麗於天下矣。蕭何以宮室爲麗，非矣。雖曰天子當以四海爲家，惟極壯麗方能鎮服其心，然亦末上論事耳，豈知所本也歟？雖然，何固不知所本，然漢高亦豈知所本者耶？未央之成，初見其壯麗之極，固未嘗不怒；及聆「四海爲家」之語，又未嘗不悅，此其心非以宮室爲麗乎？噫！漢之君相，舉不知所麗矣。然自漢而下，能知仁義者，
translation_en: …spread across the four seas; thus Yu took benevolence and righteousness as his magnificence. "He exerted himself to make his great virtue illustrious, and the millions of the people were truly cherished"—was this not Tang establishing his capital at Bo and taking benevolence and righteousness as his magnificence? "His brightness extended to the four quarters, and was gloriously manifest in the western territory"—was this not King Wen establishing his capital at Qi and taking benevolence and righteousness as his magnificence? "Greatly exhausting his praiseworthy virtue, so that the corners of the seas all submitted"—was this not furthermore King Wu establishing his capital at Hao and taking benevolence and righteousness as his magnificence? Since true kings all took benevolence and righteousness as their magnificence, why did Xiao He alone take palaces and halls as magnificence? If one takes palaces and halls as magnificence, one certainly cannot bring magnificence to the world. Those "soaring palaces andleaning halls" [of Jie of Xia] were not unmagnificent, yet they served only to invite mutual slander—where was the magnificence in that? The "jade terraces and gemmed chambers" [of Zhou of Yin] were not unmagnificent, yet they served only to incur resentment and sedition—what magnificence was there in that? Building the Epang Palace, running from Xianyang and spanning the Wei River—it was not that [Qin] did not wish to display magnificence to the world, yet it could not escape becoming scorched earth; what magnificence was left of it? Thus, bringing magnificence to the world truly lies not in palaces and halls, but in benevolence and righteousness. If one cultivates it with benevolence and righteousness, one need not make palaces and halls magnificent, and yet one will naturally be magnificent throughout the world. For Xiao He to take palaces and halls as magnificence was wrong. Although he said that the Son of Heaven takes the four seas as his home and that only extreme grandeur and magnificence could overawe and subdue people's minds, this was merely discussing affairs on the level of secondary branches; how could he know what is fundamental? Even so, while He certainly did not know what is fundamental, did Emperor Gao of Han know what is fundamental either? When the Weiyang Palace was completed and he first saw its extreme grandeur and magnificence, he was indeed angry at first; yet upon hearing the words about "taking the four seas as his home," he could not help being pleased. In his heart, did he not also take palaces and halls as magnificence? Alas! Neither the ruler nor the chancellor of Han knew wherein true magnificence lay. Yet from the Han dynasty onward, among those capable of understanding benevolence and righteousness…

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
— "非窒欲陋漢武無怠無荒偃武則坐收藩鎮之".雖有唐之太宗近似矣未免雜霸宋之太祖
庶幾矣未能醇於王是以終不如唐虞三代之
以仁義麗天下麗萬世也求其以仁義麗天下
者幸惟我
聖天子在
表
擬宋進士安守亮等召試講武殿謝表
葉元
同考試官學正陳 批有事實且忠誠溢於言表可嘉
===
考試官學正汪 批表佳
考試官教授林 批〔駢儷得體〕
伏以
六龍御極開景運於萬年四海歸心建弘基於一統
自愧巖棲之士獲叨
廷對之榮儒道生輝士林增重茲盖伏遇
文武聖神謙恭仁孝應天生聖人之祝際
奎聚五星之期正心脩德如唐堯惟精惟一防
非窒欲陋漢武無怠無荒偃武則坐收藩鎮之
punctuated:
雖有唐之太宗近似矣，未免雜霸；宋之太祖庶幾矣，未能醇於王。是以終不如唐虞、三代之以仁義麗天下、麗萬世也。求其以仁義麗天下者，幸惟我聖天子在。

表

擬宋進士安守亮等召試講武殿謝表

葉元
同考試官學正陳批：有事實，且忠誠溢於言表，可嘉。
考試官學正汪批：表佳。
考試官教授林批：〔駢儷得體。〕

伏以六龍御極，開景運於萬年；四海歸心，建弘基於一統。自愧巖棲之士，獲叨廷對之榮。儒道生輝，士林增重。茲盖伏遇文武聖神、謙恭仁孝，應天生聖人之祝，際奎聚五星之期。正心脩德，如唐堯惟精惟一；防非窒欲，陋漢武無怠無荒。偃武則坐收藩鎮之
translation_en:
… Although Emperor Taizong of the Tang 唐太宗 came close, he could not avoid mixing in the ways of a hegemon; Emperor Taizu of the Song 宋太祖 nearly attained it, yet he was unable to be purely a true king. Therefore, in the end they did not match how in the eras of Tang 唐 [Yao], Yu 虞 [Shun], and the Three Dynasties, benevolence and righteousness brought splendor to all under heaven and to ten thousand generations. If we seek one who brings splendor to all under heaven through benevolence and righteousness, fortunately we have our Sacred Son of Heaven!

Memorial (表)

In Imitation of the Song Metropolitan Graduates (jinshi) An Shouliang 安守亮 and Others: A Memorial of Thanks upon Being Summoned for Examination at the Hall for Lecturing on Martial Affairs (講武殿)

Ye Yuan 葉元
Associate Examiner and Subprefectural Instructor Chen 陳 comments: It is grounded in historical fact, and loyalty and sincerity overflow beyond the words; commendable.
Examiner and Subprefectural Instructor Wang 汪 comments: A fine memorial.
Examiner and Prefectural Instructor Lin 林 comments: [The parallel prose is fitting and proper.]

Humbly we consider: As the six dragons ascend the supreme throne, a luminous destiny is opened for ten thousand years; as the four seas turn their hearts in allegiance, a grand foundation is established in unified rule. Ashamed as we are to be mere scholars dwelling among crags and cliffs, we have been favored with the glory of answering in the Palace Examination. The Confucian Way shines forth in splendor, and the forest of literati gains in esteem. This is because we humbly encounter Your Majesty—civil and martial, sacred and divine, modest and reverent, benevolent and filial—answering the prayer that Heaven give birth to a sage, and meeting the auspicious juncture of the five planets gathering in the Kui 奎 constellation. Rectifying the mind and cultivating virtue, you are like Yao of Tang 唐堯 in being refined and single-minded; guarding against wrong and restraining desires, you look down upon Emperor Wu of the Han 漢武 by being neither negligent norremiss. In laying down arms, you effortlessly reclaimed the power of the regional military commands…

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
權崇文則載封聖賢之僭嚴覆試之法匪樹私
恩復拔萃之科大明公道特
賜臨軒之問用資訪道之勤臣等章句腐儒縉紳
末品正誼明道愧董仲舒之賢良博學宏詞慚
張九齡之蹇諤濫膺鶚薦幸覩
龍飛新進十一人舉登名於
天府諸科十七士咸通籍於金閨此誠千載之奇
逢一朝之新制也臣等敢用有階報恩無地敢
不益精舊學求無忝於甲科永竭愚衷冀有裨
===
於
盛治伏願人文宣朗如雲漢之昭回
聖學緝熙同日星之炳煥固臣民於有極綿
宗社於無疆臣等無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
表稱
謝以
聞
punctuated: 權，崇文則載封聖賢之僭〔後〕。嚴覆試之法，匪樹私恩；復拔萃之科，大明公道。特賜臨軒之問，用資訪道之勤。臣等章句腐儒，縉紳末品。正誼明道，愧董仲舒之賢良；博學宏詞，慚張九齡之蹇諤。濫膺鶚薦，幸覩龍飛。新進十一人，舉登名於天府；諸科十七士，咸通籍於金閨。此誠千載之奇逢，一朝之新制也。臣等敢〔進〕用有階，報恩無地。敢不益精舊學，求無忝於甲科；永竭愚衷，冀有裨於盛治。伏願人文宣朗，如雲漢之昭回；聖學緝熙，同日星之炳煥。固臣民於有極，綿宗社於無疆。臣等無任瞻天仰聖，激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。
translation_en:
…power [of the regional military governors]; in exalting civil culture, You have again enfeoffed the descendants [transcribed as "usurpers" 僭 for 後?] of the sages and worthies. By strictly enforcing the law of re-examination, You refrain from establishing private favors; by restoring the special selection category for the preeminent (bacui), You greatly illuminate the public way. You have specially bestowed questions from the palace veranda, thereby aiding Your diligence in inquiring into the Way.

Your servants are pedantic Confucians of chapter and phrase, the lowest rank among the gentry. In rectifying righteousness and clarifying the Way, we fall short of the "worthy and good" (xianliang) exemplar Dong Zhongshu; in broad learning and magnificent literary composition (boxue hongci), we are ashamed before the outspoken candor of Zhang Jiuling. Having unworthily received recommendation, we are fortunate to behold the flight of the imperial dragon. The eleven newly advanced graduates have all had their names entered in the imperial roster; the seventeen scholars of the various categories have all been registered at the Golden Gate. This is truly a rare encounter of a thousand years, and a new institution of the dynasty.

Though Your servants have a step by which to advance in employment [reading 進用 for 敢用?], we have no ground from which to repay Your grace. How dare we not further refine our former learning, seeking not to disgrace the highest examination category, and forever exhaust our humble loyalty, hoping to be of some aid to Your flourishing governance? We humbly pray that human culture may shine forth brightly, like the radiant revolution of the Milky Way; and that Your Sacred Learning may continue in bright illumination, as resplendent as the sun and stars—securing subjects and people in the standard of ultimate perfection, and extending the ancestral altars and altars of soil and grain without bound.

Your servants, overwhelmed with emotion and reverent trepidation as we gaze up at Heaven and look up to Your Sacred Majesty,谨 respectfully present this memorial of gratitude for Your Majesty's hearing.

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
第一問
同考試官學正陳　批〔問聖正大場中多不知古今身教言教之實惟此能以古人嘉言善行反我〕
趙玉
考試官學正汪　批〔條答詳明可取〕
考試官教授林　批〔叙古頗〕
〔朝廷乾坤正直條答兼遺信策手也〕
〔今最為切當非留心於治道者不能敘羨欽羨〕
===
行而世為天下法言而世為天下則此聖人所
以為天地立心為生民立命為萬世開太平者
也前乎二帝三王所以繼天立極者此也後乎我
朝
列聖所以繼往開來者庸非此乎且聖人者出中天
地而立身綱常之寄其道豈有他哉亦惟身教
言教二者相須而並行焉稽之於古堯明峻德
而慎徽五典允迪厥德而克諧以孝堯舜之身
教也祇台德先而懋昭大德緝熙敬止而細行
punctuated:
第一問

同考試官學正陳　批〔問聖正大，場中多不知古今身教言教之實，惟此能以古人嘉言善行，反我朝廷乾坤正直，條答兼遺，信策手也。〕
趙玉
考試官學正汪　批〔條答詳明，可取。〕
考試官教授林　批〔叙古頗今，最為切當，非留心於治道者不能，敘羨欽羨。〕

行而世為天下法，言而世為天下則，此聖人所以為天地立心，為生民立命，為萬世開太平者也。前乎二帝三王，所以繼天立極者，此也；後乎我朝列聖，所以繼往開來者，庸非此乎？且聖人者出，中天地而立，身綱常之寄，其道豈有他哉？亦惟身教、言教二者，相須而並行焉。稽之於古，堯明峻德而慎徽五典，允迪厥德而克諧以孝，堯、舜之身教也；祇台德先而懋昭大德，緝熙敬止而細行
translation_en:
First Policy Question

Associate Examiner and Subprefectural Instructor (Xuezheng) Chen comments: [The question concerning the sages is grand and upright [?], yet most candidates in the examination hall did not grasp the realities of teaching by personal example and teaching by precept in ancient and modern times. Only this essay is able to take the admirable words and good deeds of the ancients and reflect upon the cosmic uprightness [?] of our Dynastic Court, answering each point without omission. Truly the hand of a master of policy essays!]
Zhao Yu 趙玉
Examiner and Subprefectural Instructor (Xuezheng) Wang comments: [The point-by-point responses are detailed and clear; worthy of selection.]
Examiner and Prefectural Instructor (Jiaoshou) Lin comments: [Its account of antiquity and comparison [?] with the present are most apt. None but one who pays close attention to the Way of governance could achieve this; truly admirable!]

To act so that for generations one's actions are a model for All under Heaven, and to speak so that for generations one's words are a standard for All under Heaven—this is whereby the sages establish a heart for Heaven and Earth, establish a destiny for the living people, and inaugurate great peace for ten thousand generations. In earlier times, this was how the Two Emperors and Three Kings succeeded Heaven and established the supreme standard; in later times, how could this not be how the Successive Sages of our Dynasty carry on the past and open the way for the future? Moreover, when a sage emerges, standing at the center of Heaven and Earth and bearing in his person the charge of the Three Bonds and Five Constant Virtues, how could his Way be anything else? It is simply that teaching by personal example and teaching by precept are mutually dependent and practiced together. Examining antiquity: Yao made bright his lofty virtue, and Shun cautiously beautified the Five Teachings; they sincerely pursued their virtue and were able to live in harmony through filial piety—such was the teaching by personal example of Yao and Shun. Reverently taking his own virtue first, and striving to make bright his great virtue; continuing and making bright his reverent resting, while even in minor conduct…

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
亦矜禹湯文武之身教也咨舜以允執厥中命
契以勞來匡直與夫危微精一之訓欽其克艱工
之語非堯舜之言教乎垂訓言以貽孫子而色
荒禽荒之戒具制官刑以儆有位而三風十愆
之訓明與夫毖酒之教皇極之訓非禹湯文武
之言教乎是以萬邦協和四方風動文命四敷
而兆民允懷西土怙冒而丕單稱德民之從教
治之隆盛無以加矣洪惟我
朝
===
太祖高皇帝備至聖之資創一統之業褒崇
先帝隆武王尊親之孝分封諸王敦帝堯睦族之仁
祖訓一篇允矣家國之元龜
大誥三編貽乎臣民之至寶身教言教揆之二帝
三王符節相合也
太宗文皇帝懋德建中端一身以出治慮人心善孝
有未協也輯
為善陰隲
孝順事實二書以勸俗炳乎
punctuated: 亦矜，禹、湯、文、武之身教也。咨舜以「允執厥中」，命契以「勞來匡直」，與夫「危微精一」之訓、「欽哉克艱」[工]之語，非堯、舜之言教乎？垂訓言以貽孫子，而「色荒禽荒」之戒具；制官刑以儆有位，而「三風十愆」之訓明；與夫「毖酒」之教、「皇極」之訓，非禹、湯、文、武之言教乎？是以萬邦協和，四方風動，文命四敷而兆民允懷，西土怙冒而丕單稱德。民之從教、治之隆盛，無以加矣。洪惟我朝太祖高皇帝，備至聖之資，創一統之業，褒崇先帝，隆武王尊親之孝；分封諸王，敦帝堯睦族之仁。《祖訓》一篇，允矣家國之元龜；《大誥》三編，貽乎臣民之至寶。身教、言教，揆之二帝、三王，符節相合也。太宗文皇帝，懋德建中，端一身以出治；慮人心善孝有未協也，輯《為善陰隲》、《孝順事實》二書以勸俗，炳乎
translation_en:
…also scrupulous in minor conduct—such was the teaching by personal example of Yu, Tang, King Wen, and King Wu. Charging Shun to "sincerely hold fast the Mean," commanding Xie to "encourage the来 [coming], straighten the crooked," together with the instruction on the "precariousness of the human mind, the subtlety of the moral mind, refinement, and single-mindedness" and the words on "reverence and being able to recognize the difficulty of one's office" [?]—were these not the teaching by words of Yao and Shun? Handing down words of instruction to bequeath to grandsons and sons, in which the warnings against "wildness in lust and wildness in hunting" were set forth in full; instituting penal regulations for officials to admonish those in office, whereby the instruction on the "three evil customs and ten offenses" was made clear; together with the teaching on "caution regarding wine" and the instruction on the "Supreme Standard"—were these not the teaching by words of Yu, Tang, King Wen, and King Wu? Therefore the myriad states were brought into harmony and the four quarters were moved as by the wind; cultural teachings spread in all four directions and the millions of the common people truly cherished them; the western lands relied upon and were sheltered by them, and universally proclaimed their virtue. The people's compliance with teaching and the flourishing abundance of good governance could not be surpassed.

Reverently contemplating our dynasty: Emperor Gao, the Grand Progenitor (Taizu), endowed with the qualities of supreme sageliness, founded the enterprise of great unification. In honoring and exalting his imperial ancestors, he exalted the filial piety of King Wu in honoring his parents; in enfeoffing the various princes, he deepened the benevolence of Emperor Yao in harmonizing the imperial clan. The single work Ancestral Injunctions (Zuxun) is truly the great divination tortoise for family and state; the three compilations of the Grand Pronouncements (Dagao) are a supreme treasure bequeathed to officials and subjects. Measured against the Two Emperors and Three Kings, his teaching by personal example and teaching by words tally like the two halves of a credential.

Emperor Wen, the Grand Ancestor (Taizong), cultivated virtue and established the Mean, rectifying his own person in order to bring forth good governance. Concerned that human minds might not yet be fully aligned in goodness and filiality, he compiled the two books Hidden Rewards for Doing Good (Weishan yinzhi) and True Records of Filial Piety (Xiaoshun shishi) to encourage popular customs—resplendent…

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
綸音之渙發
宣宗章皇帝法
祖敬
天備一德以守文憲天下綱常有未正也釐
五倫一書以導民彝乎
睿藻之輝煌身教言教實之二帝三王軌轍相同
也方今
聖皇在上克篤前烈益弘文教崇大孝於
慈闈溥至恩於同姓纘熙
===
聖學臨幸辟雍頒
明詔懇懇乎求賢養老之言發
德音切切乎制治保邦之訓是以綱舉目張而政
治爲之脩明禮備樂和而教化爲之洋溢人稷
契户程朱大回渟古之風家詩書俗仁讓丕變
雍熙之治駕唐虞而越三代矣夫豈漢唐宋之
可擬哉愚何幸躬逢其盛
第二問
punctuated:
綸音之渙發。宣宗章皇帝法祖敬天，備一德以守文，憲天下綱常有未正也，釐《五倫》一書以導民，彝乎睿藻之輝煌。身教言教，實之二帝、三王，軌轍相同也。
方今聖皇在上，克篤前烈，益弘文教，崇大孝於慈闈，溥至恩於同姓，纘熙聖學，臨幸辟雍，頒明詔懇懇乎求賢養老之言，發德音切切乎制治保邦之訓。是以綱舉目張而政治爲之脩明，禮備樂和而教化爲之洋溢。人稷、契，户程、朱，大回渟古之風；家《詩》、《書》，俗仁讓，丕變雍熙之治。駕唐、虞而越三代矣，夫豈漢、唐、宋之可擬哉？愚何幸躬逢其盛！

第二問
translation_en:
…the proclamation of His imperial words. Emperor Xuanzong Zhang modeled himself on the Ancestors and revered Heaven, possessing pure virtue to uphold civil governance. Concerned [?] that the cardinal principles and constant virtues throughout the realm were not yet rectified, he compiled the single work Book of the Five Human Relationships (Wulun shu) to guide the people—how magnificent the brilliance of His imperial compositions! Teaching by personal example and teaching by words, when verified against those of the Two Emperors and Three Kings, followed the exact same tracks.

At present, the Sage Emperor reigns above, steadfastly carrying forward the meritorious achievements of His predecessors and further expanding civil education. He exalts great filial piety toward the Empress Dowager's palace, extends the utmost grace to imperial clansmen, continues and brightens sacred learning, and visits the Imperial University in person. He issues luminous edicts, earnest in their words on seeking out the worthy and nourishing the aged; He proclaims virtuous pronouncements, ardent in their instructions on ordering governance and preserving the state. Therefore, when the main cord is lifted, all the meshes open, and governance thereby becomes well-ordered and clear; rites are complete and music is harmonious, and moral transformation thereby brims over. Every person is a Ji or a Xie, and every household a Cheng or a Zhu, greatly restoring the ethos of pure antiquity; every family studies the Odes and the Documents, and customs are marked by benevolence and deference, grandly transforming the realm into a governance of harmony and splendor. This surpasses Tang and Yu and transcends the Three Dynasties—how could Han, Tang, or Song possibly be compared to it? How fortunate am I, in my humble person, to witness such a flourishing age!

Second Question

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭張　批〔策場正欲觀士子學識此卷斟酌廟廷〕
〔議禮尤爲允當他日〕
〔臨軒有問必不遺子矣〕
同考試官教諭陳　批〔此策善答所問較之前二場允稱其士〕
〔林之翹楚者〕
同考試官教諭鄭　批〔場中能條答六藝者衆然於議祀禮處〕
〔多無的見此策斟酌得宜必有識之士也〕
考試官學正汪　批〔六藝一策隨問隨答足見博古通今之學〕
考試官教授林　批〔條答詳明確有的見〕
===
對六藝之用於古者當考其詳祀禮之行於今
者當揆以義六藝之所先者禮而禮之所重者
祭此皆吾儒之所當講所以不能不厪執事之
問也粤稽諸古周禮大司徒所以教萬民而賓
興之者六藝其一也禮所以教之中有五禮焉
吉禮十有二所謂禋祀實柴槱燎血祭之類是
也凶禮五所謂喪荒弔襘恤之屬是也賓禮八
非朝宗覲遇會同問視之謂乎軍禮五非師均
田役封之謂乎飲食冠昏賓射饗燕脤膰賀慶
punctuated:
同考試官教諭張批：〔策場正欲觀士子學識，此卷斟酌廟廷議禮，尤爲允當。他日臨軒有問，必不遺子矣。〕
同考試官教諭陳批：〔此策善答所問，較之前二場允稱，其士林之翹楚者。〕
同考試官教諭鄭批：〔場中能條答六藝者衆，然於議祀禮處多無的見。此策斟酌得宜，必有識之士也。〕
考試官學正汪批：〔六藝一策，隨問隨答，足見博古通今之學。〕
考試官教授林批：〔條答詳明，確有的見。〕

對：六藝之用於古者，當考其詳；祀禮之行於今者，當揆以義。六藝之所先者禮，而禮之所重者祭，此皆吾儒之所當講，所以不能不厪執事之問也。粤稽諸古，《周禮》大司徒所以教萬民而賓興之者，六藝其一也。禮所以教之中，有五禮焉：吉禮十有二，所謂禋祀、實柴、槱燎、血祭之類是也；凶禮五，所謂喪、荒、弔、襘、恤之屬是也；賓禮八，非朝、宗、覲、遇、會、同、問、視之謂乎？軍禮五，非師、均、田、役、封之謂乎？飲食、冠昏、賓射、饗燕、脤膰、賀慶，
translation_en:
Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies Zhang comments: [The policy essay session is precisely intended to observe the learning and insight of the candidates. This paper weighs the court discussions on ritual with particular appropriateness. When the Emperor someday questions candidates in person at the Palace Examination, you will surely not be overlooked.]
Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies Chen comments: [This policy essay answers the question well and matches the quality of the candidate's first two sessions; he is truly an outstanding figure among the literati.]
Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies Zheng comments: [In the examination compound, many were able to respond point by point regarding the Six Arts, yet when it came to discussing sacrificial rituals, most lacked definite insight. This policy essay deliberates appropriately; its author must be a scholar of discernment.]
Examiner and Subprefectural Director of Studies Wang comments: [In this policy essay on the Six Arts, each question is answered in turn, amply demonstrating learning that is both conversant with antiquity and informed about the present.]
Examiner and Prefectural Director of Studies Lin comments: [The point-by-point responses are detailed and clear, possessing genuinely definite insight.]

Response: As for how the Six Arts (liuyi) were employed in antiquity, one ought to examine their particulars; as for how sacrificial rituals are practiced today, one ought to measure them by right principle. First among the Six Arts is ritual, and foremost within ritual is sacrifice. All of these are matters that we Confucian scholars ought to study and discuss, which is why they could not but engage the concern of Your Honor's question. Examining antiquity, in the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli), among the means by which the Minister of Education (Dasitu) instructed the myriad people and presented them as honored guests for appointment, the Six Arts were one. Ritual, by which he taught them centrality, comprises the Five Rites (wuli): the Auspicious Rites (jili) are twelve in number, namely such sacrifices as the pure sacrifice (yinsi), the sacrifice on stacked firewood (shichai), the blazing woodpile sacrifice (youliao), and the blood sacrifice (xueji); the Inauspicious Rites (xiongli) are five, namely those pertaining to bereavement (sang), famine (huang), condolence (diao), aid after disaster (gui), and relief from incursion (xu); the Guest Rites (binli) are eight—do they not refer to spring court (chao), summer court (zong), autumn audience (jin), winter encounter (yu), occasional assembly (hui), general assembly (tong), missions of inquiry (wen), and missions of inspection (shi)? The Military Rites (junli) are five—do they not refer to campaigning (shi), equalizing taxation and labor (jun), hunting (tian), construction labor (yi), and defining boundaries (feng)? Ceremonies of food and drink, capping and marriage, guest archery, banqueting and feasting, sharing sacrificial meat, and offering felicitations…

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
又嘉禮之有六也此五禮節目之詳可知矣樂
所以教之和有六樂焉黃帝之樂曰雲門周人
冬至舞之以祀天神帝堯之樂曰咸池周人夏
至舞之以祀地祇大韶舜樂也周人祭四望則
舞之大夏禹樂也周人祭大川則舞之湯有大
濩之樂周人舞之以祭姜嫄武王作大武之樂
周人舞之以祭宗廟此周人用樂之不同可知
矣射所以觀德行御所以正驅馳射有五曰白
矢參連剡注襄尺井儀焉御有五曰鳴和鸞逐
===
水曲過君表舞交衢逐禽左焉此射御之節目
也書以見心畫數以盡事變書有六曰象形會
意轉注處事假借諧聲而已數有九曰方田粟
布衰分少廣商功均輸盈朒方程勾股而已此
書數之名義也六藝之中禮樂為先禮莫重於
祭而祭必有義若顏曾思身任道統之傳其配
享於孔子也固宜然顏路曾晳孔鯉父也顏回
曾參孔伋子也以道統之傳論之則父固不及
於子然而古者立廟專以明人倫烏有子南面
punctuated:
又嘉禮之有六也。此五禮節目之詳可知矣。樂所以教之和，有六樂焉：黃帝之樂曰《雲門》，周人冬至舞之，以祀天神；帝堯之樂曰《咸池》，周人夏至舞之，以祀地祇；《大韶》，舜樂也，周人祭四望則舞之；《大夏》，禹樂也，周人祭大川則舞之；湯有《大濩》之樂，周人舞之，以祭姜嫄；武王作《大武》之樂，周人舞之，以祭宗廟。此周人用樂之不同可知矣。射所以觀德行，御所以正驅馳。射有五：曰白矢、參連、剡注、襄尺、井儀焉。御有五：曰鳴和鸞、逐水曲、過君表、舞交衢、逐禽左焉。此射御之節目也。書以見心畫，數以盡事變。書有六：曰象形、會意、轉注、處事、假借、諧聲而已。數有九：曰方田、粟布、衰分、少廣、商功、均輸、盈朒、方程、勾股而已。此書數之名義也。

六藝之中，禮樂為先，禮莫重於祭，而祭必有義。若顏、曾、思身任道統之傳，其配享於孔子也固宜。然顏路、曾晳、孔鯉，父也；顏回、曾參、孔伋，子也。以道統之傳論之，則父固不及於子；然而古者立廟專以明人倫，烏有子南面…
translation_en:
…are furthermore the six categories of felicitous rites. From this, the detailed particulars of the five rites can be known. Music is the means to teach people harmony, and there are six kinds of music: the music of the Yellow Emperor is called Yunmen ("Cloud Gate"), which the people of Zhou performed with dance at the winter solstice to sacrifice to the heavenly spirits; the music of Emperor Yao is called Xianchi ("All-Embracing Pond"), which the people of Zhou performed with dance at the summer solstice to sacrifice to the earthly deities; Dashao ("Great Shao") is the music of Shun, which the people of Zhou performed with dance when sacrificing to the Four Vistas; Daxia ("Great Xia") is the music of Yu, which the people of Zhou performed with dance when sacrificing to the great rivers; Tang had the music of Dahuo ("Great Protection"), which the people of Zhou performed with dance to sacrifice to Jiang Yuan; King Wu created the music of Dawu ("Great Martiality"), which the people of Zhou performed with dance to sacrifice in the ancestral temple. From this, the different applications of music by the people of Zhou can be known. Archery is the means to observe virtuous conduct, and charioteering is the means to regulate driving and galloping. There are five techniques of archery: namely, "white arrowhead" (baishi, shooting clean through the target), "three in a row" (sanlian, rapid successive shots), "slanted flight" (yanzhu, the arrow flying level with feather high and point low), "yielding a foot" (xiangchi, standing a foot behind the lord when shooting with him), and "well-grid deportment" (jingyi, four arrows hitting the target like the character for a well). There are five techniques of charioteering: namely, "sounding the He and Luan bells in harmony" (ming heluan), "following the bends of a stream" (zhu shuiqu), "passing the ruler's marker" (guo junbiao), "circling at the crossroads" (wu jiaoqu), and "driving game to the left" (zhu qinzuo, for the ruler to shoot). These are the particulars of archery and charioteering. Calligraphy is for displaying the delineations of the mind, and mathematics is for exhausting the variations of affairs. There are six principles of calligraphy: namely, pictographs (xiangxing), compound ideographs (huiyi), derivative cognates (zhuanzhu), simple indicatives (chushi), phonetic loans (jiajie), and phono-semantic compounds (xiesheng), and nothing more. There are nine categories of mathematics: namely, rectangular fields (fangtian, land measurement), millet and cloth (subu, proportions and exchange), proportional distribution (cuifen), diminishing breadth (shaoguang, root extraction), consultations on engineering works (shanggong, solid geometry), equitable taxation and transport (junshu), excess and deficit (yingnu), rectangular arrays (fangcheng, linear equations), and base and altitude (gougu, right triangles), and nothing more. These are the names and meanings of calligraphy and mathematics.

Among the Six Arts, rites and music come first; of the rites, none is more important than sacrifice, and sacrifice must have its proper principle. Figures such as Yan [Hui], Zeng [Shen], and Zisi personally bore the transmission of the Orthodox Way (daotong), so their being enshrined as correlates in sacrifices to Confucius is certainly fitting. Yet Yan Lu, Zeng Xi, and Kong Li were the fathers; Yan Hui, Zeng Shen, and Kong Ji [Zisi] were the sons. Discussing it in terms of the transmission of the Orthodox Way, the fathers indeed did not equal their sons. However, in antiquity the establishment of temples was exclusively for clarifying human moral relations—how could there be sons facing south…

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
以先父乎子雖齊聖不先父食故禹不先鯀湯
不先契文武不先不窋其理章章乎明矣子配
享堂上父從祀廡間雖道統攸繫顏曾思之心
其安乎哉然禮因人情莫若別立後寢主之以
孔叔梁紇配之以顏路曾晳孔鯉則彝倫以明
道統益尊而父子之間兩無憾矣若夫周子以
自得之學而著太極易通之旨兩程以誠敬之
學而接孔孟道學之傳張子訂頑砭愚而西銘
有作朱子開來繼往而孔道大明此五子所以
===
有功於前聖有功於後學而朱子則集諸儒之
大成其功尤多也以五子從祀兩廡而不獲乎
配享亦以世之先後而為之耳以德行論則五
子固不下於子貢以下之諸賢而功則倍之以
著述論則五子又多於鄭康成以下之諸儒而
理則過之然禮以義起以周程張朱配享廟廷
而儕於顏曾思孟之列則道學益顯祀典大明
而天下之公議未必不以為當也至於古樂之
亡久矣秦漢去周未遠其器與聲猶有存者逮
punctuated: 以先父乎？子雖齊聖，不先父食。故禹不先鯀，湯不先契，文、武不先不窋，其理章章乎明矣。子配享堂上，父從祀廡間，雖道統攸繫，顏、曾、思之心其安乎哉？然禮因人情，莫若別立後寢，主之以孔叔梁紇，配之以顏路、曾晳、孔鯉，則彝倫以明，道統益尊，而父子之間兩無憾矣。若夫周子以自得之學，而著《太極》、《易通》之旨；兩程以誠敬之學，而接孔、孟道學之傳；張子訂頑砭愚，而《西銘》有作；朱子開來繼往，而孔道大明。此五子所以有功於前聖，有功於後學，而朱子則集諸儒之大成，其功尤多也。以五子從祀兩廡，而不獲乎配享，亦以世之先後而為之耳。以德行論，則五子固不下於子貢以下之諸賢，而功則倍之；以著述論，則五子又多於鄭康成以下之諸儒，而理則過之。然禮以義起，以周、程、張、朱配享廟廷，而儕於顏、曾、思、孟之列，則道學益顯，祀典大明，而天下之公議未必不以為當也。至於古樂之亡久矣，秦、漢去周未遠，其器與聲猶有存者，逮
translation_en: …and take precedence over the father? Even if a son is wise and sage, he does not partake of sacrificial offerings before his father. Therefore, Yu 禹 did not precede Gun 鯀, Tang 湯 did not precede Xie 契, and Kings Wen 文 and Wu 武 did not precede Buzhu 不窋; the principle in this is abundantly clear. When the sons are correlated in sacrifice up in the main hall while their fathers are enshrined as secondary figures in the side galleries, even though this is tied to the transmission of the Way, how could the minds of Yan 回, Zeng 參, and Zisi 子思 be at peace? Yet ritual accords with human feelings. Nothing would be better than to separately establish a rear shrine, with Kong Shuliang He 孔叔梁紇 as its principal spirit, and Yan Lu 顏路, Zeng Xi 曾晳, and Kong Li 孔鯉 correlated with him in sacrifice. Then the constant human relationships would be made clear, the transmission of the Way would be all the more revered, and between fathers and sons neither side would have cause for regret. As for Master Zhou 周子 [Zhou Dunyi 周敦頤], through his self-attained learning he set forth the purport of the Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate (Taiji tushuo 太極圖說) and Penetrating the Book of Changes (Yitong 易通); the two Masters Cheng 程 [Cheng Hao 程顥 and Cheng Yi 程頤], through their learning of sincerity and reverence, continued the transmission of the Learning of the Way from Confucius and Mencius; Master Zhang 張子 [Zhang Zai 張載] corrected the obstinate and remedied the foolish, and thus composed the Western Inscription (Ximing 西銘); and Master Zhu 朱子 [Zhu Xi 朱熹] opened the way for the future and continued the past, making the Way of Confucius brilliantly clear. This is how these Five Masters rendered meritorious service to the former sages and to later scholars, while Master Zhu synthesized the great achievements of the various Confucians, his merit being especially great. That the Five Masters are enshrined as secondary figures in the two side galleries and have not been granted correlated sacrifices in the main hall was done merely on the basis of chronological sequence. Judged in terms of moral conduct, the Five Masters are certainly not inferior to the worthies from Zigong 子貢 on down, while their merit is double theirs; judged in terms of writings, the Five Masters are more prolific than the Confucian scholars from Zheng Kangcheng 鄭康成 [Zheng Xuan 鄭玄] on down, while their grasp of principle surpasses theirs. Yet ritual arises from righteousness: if Zhou, the two Chengs, Zhang, and Zhu were accorded correlated sacrifices in the temple court and ranked alongside Yan, Zeng, Zisi, and Mencius, then the Learning of the Way would become even more manifest, the sacrificial canon would be made brilliantly clear, and impartial opinion throughout the realm would not necessarily fail to deem it appropriate. As for ancient music, it has long been lost. Qin and Han were not far removed from Zhou, and some of its instruments and sounds still survived; when it came down to…

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
乎後世有祖孝孫之所奏和峴之所制王朴李□
論徒徇其末而不知其本是以愈多而愈不□
也迨蔡季通之作律呂新書此朱子之所以深
取焉雖然稽古禮文固學者急務然而廟庭禮
議愚已略陳於前矣若夫律呂本原蔡氏新書
詳悉無遺至於先求聲氣之元則有乎其人焉
愚生學識膚淺斟酌未得其宜也推詳未得其
要也姑撮其大畧為執事言倘以為可與而進
之則挾此而往以俟
===
聖天子臨軒之問
羅奎
第三問
同考試官教諭沈　批〔士生百世下而欲辯論古人於百世之上使是非□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□〕
〔似錙銖不爽者自觀其時而身處其事者亦難矣此卷□□□□□□□□〕
〔當乎人心非博學洽聞胸中有素蘊者不能與於此〕
考試官學正汪　批〔援据而□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□〕
〔繁考多聚博者子豈多與此〕
考試官教授林　批〔有考据有□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□〕
punctuated:
乎後世，有祖孝孫之所奏、和峴之所制、王朴李□論，徒徇其末而不知其本，是以愈多而愈不□也。迨蔡季通之作《律呂新書》，此朱子之所以深取焉。雖然，稽古禮文，固學者急務；然而廟庭禮議，愚已略陳於前矣。若夫律呂本原，蔡氏《新書》詳悉無遺；至於先求聲氣之元，則有乎其人焉。愚生學識膚淺，斟酌未得其宜也，推詳未得其要也，姑撮其大畧為執事言。倘以為可與而進之，則挾此而往，以俟聖天子臨軒之問。
羅奎
第三問
同考試官教諭沈　批：〔士生百世下，而欲辯論古人於百世之上，使是非□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□，似錙銖不爽者，自觀其時而身處其事者亦難矣。此卷□□□□□□□□，當乎人心，非博學洽聞、胸中有素蘊者，不能與於此。〕
考試官學正汪　批：〔援据而□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□，繁考多聚博者，子豈多與此？〕
考試官教授林　批：〔有考据，有□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□□。〕
translation_en:
…later ages, there were what Zu Xiaosun 祖孝孫 presented, what He Xian 和峴 devised, and the discussions of Wang Pu 王朴 and Li [□] 李□ [Li Zhao 李照]; they merely pursued the branches without knowing the root, and therefore the more numerous they became, the more they failed to […]. Coming down to Cai Jitong’s 蔡季通 [Cai Yuanding 蔡元定] composition of the New Treatise on the Pitch-Pipes (Lülü xinshu 律呂新書), this was what Master Zhu [Zhu Xi 朱熹] deeply approved of. Even so, investigating ancient ritual texts is indeed an urgent task for scholars; yet concerning the ritual deliberations of the temple court, I have already briefly set them forth above. As for the fundamental origins of the pitch-pipes, Mr. Cai’s New Treatise is thorough and leaves nothing out; as for first seeking the primal source of sound and qi, that depends on having the right person for it. A foolish student of shallow learning and knowledge, in weighing matters I have not attained what is fitting, and in investigating details I have not grasped the essentials; I provisionally gather the general outline to speak of it before Your Reverences. Should you deem me worthy of endorsement and advance me, I shall carry this forth and go to await the Sacred Son of Heaven’s questioning at the palace balustrade.

Luo Kui 羅奎

Question Three

Comment (批) by Associate Examiner, Instructor (教諭) Shen: [For a scholar born a hundred generations later to wish to debate and judge the ancients of a hundred generations earlier, causing right and wrong to […] as though not off by the slightest fraction—even for those who witnessed the times themselves and personally handled the affairs, this would be difficult! This paper […] accords with human hearts; no one who is not of broad learning and wide knowledge, with long-cultivated stores in his breast, could have a part in this.]

Comment by Examiner, Director of Studies (學正) Wang: [Citing evidence and […], among those of extensive investigation and broad accumulation [?], how could there be many who share in this with you?]

Comment by Examiner, Instructor (教授) Lin: [It has evidential grounding, and it has […].]

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
權然後知輕重度然後知長短故君子於事變
之来度以本然之權度則天下無難處之事矣
夫事莫不有是非亦莫不有利害是非利害混
於一途則當酌其輕重以制事焉法重於恩割
恩以伸法可也恩重於法屈法以伸恩可也法
恩俱重則又當委曲而兩全之焉古之人有處
之者矣事重于身於是乎舍生取義事重于親
於是乎不告而娶事重于天下於是乎竊負而
逃訢然樂而忘天下如此則天下無難處之事
===
矣愚嘗讀史而觀古人之遇事變如執事所舉
者未嘗不歎其不幸而際此兩難也然豈無道
以處之乎夫父既犯法曲護而保全之必不得
已復命于輔行而竊負以逃亦不為過石奢之
死陋矣如父何著石昔人大義滅親君子是之
蓋國為重家為輕也毋若賊李家告而求生之
必不得已委城于將佐而輕身赴母亦未為失
趙苞之事忠矣如母何故徐庶請辭先主程子
是之蓋母為重功為輕也懷光之逆李璀逃以
punctuated:
權，然後知輕重；度，然後知長短。故君子於事變之来，度以本然之權度，則天下無難處之事矣。夫事莫不有是非，亦莫不有利害。是非利害混於一途，則當酌其輕重以制事焉。法重於恩，割恩以伸法可也；恩重於法，屈法以伸恩可也；法恩俱重，則又當委曲而兩全之焉。古之人有處之者矣：事重于身，於是乎舍生取義；事重于親，於是乎不告而娶；事重于天下，於是乎竊負而逃，訢然樂而忘天下。如此，則天下無難處之事矣。
愚嘗讀史，而觀古人之遇事變如執事所舉者，未嘗不歎其不幸而際此兩難也。然豈無道以處之乎？夫父既犯法，曲護而保全之；必不得已，復命于輔行，而竊負以逃，亦不為過。石奢之死，陋矣，如父何？著石昔人「大義滅親」，君子是之，蓋國為重、家為輕也。毋若賊李家，告而求生之；必不得已，委城于將佐，而輕身赴母，亦未為失。趙苞之事，忠矣，如母何？故徐庶請辭先主，程子是之，蓋母為重、功為輕也。懷光之逆，李璀逃以
translation_en:
Only after weighing on a scale does one know what is light and what is heavy; only after measuring with a rule does one know what is long and what is short. Therefore, when the gentleman encounters sudden turns of events, if he measures them by the inherent scale and rule of his mind, there will be no affair in the world that is difficult to handle. Now, every affair has its right and wrong, as well as its benefit and harm. When right and wrong, benefit and harm, are mingled together along a single course, one ought to weigh their relative gravity in order to regulate the affair. When the law outweighs personal grace, it is permissible to sever grace in order to uphold the law; when personal grace outweighs the law, it is permissible to bend the law in order to extend grace; and when both law and grace are weighty, one ought to find an accommodating way to preserve them both. There were men of antiquity who handled such situations: when the matter outweighed one's own life, they gave up life to choose righteousness; when the matter outweighed informing one's parents, he married without telling them; when the matter outweighed the Empire, he would have secretly carried his father on his back and fled, joyfully forgetting the Empire. Acting in this way, there is no affair in the world that is difficult to handle.

I have read the histories and observed how the ancients met with sudden turns of events such as those Your Excellency has cited, and I have never failed to sigh over their misfortune in encountering such dilemmas. Yet how could there be no proper way to handle them? Once one's father has violated the law, one should go to every length to shield and preserve him; if there is truly no alternative, to report back to one's deputy and then secretly carry one's father on one's back and flee would not be going too far. The death of Shi She 石奢 was narrow-minded indeed—what good did it do his father? As for Shi Que 石碏 [?] of old, who "out of supreme righteousness destroyed his own kin," the gentleman approved of him, because the state was weighty and the family light. When one's mother falls into the hands of bandits [?], one should plead to save her life; if there is truly no alternative, to entrust the city to one's subordinate commanders and go alone to join one's mother would not be a failing. The conduct of Zhao Bao 趙苞 was loyal indeed, yet what of his mother? Thus when Xu Shu 徐庶 asked leave to depart from the Former Lord (Liu Bei 劉備), Master Cheng (Cheng Yi 程頤) approved of him, because his mother was weighty and merit was light. In the rebellion of Li Huaiguang 李懷光, Li Cui 李璀 [?]…

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
諫其父進以告□君死可哀矣子南之誅棄□
既不諫其君又不告其父死何益邪父與夫孰
重而可逆其父然順父以害夫亦非也雍姬於
是乎失君與友孰重而敢逆其君然順君以誅
友亦非也左儒於是乎得王道雖弟王臣也王
敦雖兄國賊也當是之時知有天下不知有其
兄自附周公殆非過矣建成無功太子也秦王
有功藩王也當是之際但知有兄不知有天下
自附子臧豈至此乎無忌之命縮高是以父攻
===
子也在子不可拒在父不可往高之辭適宜矣
武后之討敬業是以逆攻順也僞周不可附敬
業不可討孝逸之功爲罪矣武宗君也宣宗嘗
北面而事之可以叔而加其君乎是未知春秋
之議逆祀也守禮父也世宗不由空桑而生可
以天子而臣其父乎是未知孟子之論北山也
薄昭之罪赦之固不可誅之亦未當先正謂當
上慰母心斯可也濮園之議稱親固不可稱伯
亦未安先儒謂當增一父字庶幾也維州之取
punctuated: 諫其父，進以告□君，死可哀矣。子南之誅，棄□既不諫其君，又不告其父，死何益邪？父與夫孰重？而可逆其父？然順父以害夫亦非也，雍姬於是乎失。君與友孰重？而敢逆其君？然順君以誅友亦非也，左儒於是乎得。王道雖弟，王臣也；王敦雖兄，國賊也。當是之時，知有天下，不知有其兄，自附周公，殆非過矣。建成無功，太子也；秦王有功，藩王也。當是之際，但知有兄，不知有天下，自附子臧，豈至此乎？無忌之命縮高，是以父攻子也，在子不可拒，在父不可往，高之辭適宜矣。武后之討敬業，是以逆攻順也，僞周不可附，敬業不可討，孝逸之功爲罪矣。武宗，君也，宣宗嘗北面而事之，可以叔而加其君乎？是未知《春秋》之議逆祀也。守禮，父也，世宗不由空桑而生，可以天子而臣其父乎？是未知《孟子》之論《北山》也。薄昭之罪，赦之固不可，誅之亦未當，先正謂當上慰母心，斯可也。濮園之議，稱親固不可，稱伯亦未安，先儒謂當增一「父」字，庶幾也。維州之取
translation_en: …remonstrate with his father, and go forward to inform [his] sovereign; his death was lamentable indeed. In the execution of Zinan 子南, Qi[ji] 棄[疾] neither remonstrated with his ruler nor informed his father—what good did his death do? Between father and husband, who is more important that one could defy one's father? Yet to obey one's father so as to harm one's husband is also wrong; in this, Yong Ji 雍姬 erred. Between ruler and friend, who is more important that one would dare defy one's ruler? Yet to obey one's ruler so as to execute one's friend is also wrong; in this, Zuo Ru 左儒 acted rightly. Although Wang Dao 王導 [transcribed 王道] was the younger brother, he was the king's minister; although Wang Dun 王敦 was the elder brother, he was a traitor to the state. At that time, to recognize only the empire and not one's elder brother, comparing oneself to the Duke of Zhou 周公, was scarcely excessive. Although Jiancheng 建成 had no merit, he was the Heir Apparent; although the Prince of Qin 秦王 had merit, he was a feudatory prince. At that juncture, had he recognized only his elder brother and not the empire, comparing himself to Zizang 子臧, how would things have come to such a pass? When Wuji 無忌 commanded Su Gao 縮高, it was using a father to attack a son; on the son's part he could not resist, and on the father's part he could not go—Gao's refusal was quite fitting. When Empress Wu 武后 sent a punitive expedition against Jingye 敬業, it was the rebellious attacking the rightful; the usurping Zhou 周 could not be adhered to, and Jingye could not be attacked—Xiaoyi's 孝逸 merit was in fact a crime. Emperor Wuzong 武宗 was the ruler, and Emperor Xuanzong 宣宗 had once faced north to serve him as a subject; could he then place himself above his ruler because he was an uncle? This was failing to understand the critique of reversing the sacrificial order in the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu). Shouli 守禮 was the father, and Emperor Shizong 世宗 was not born out of a hollow mulberry tree; could he then treat his father as a subject because he was the Son of Heaven? This was failing to understand the Mencius's (Mengzi) discussion of the ode "Northern Mountain" (Beishan). As for the crime of Bo Zhao 薄昭, to pardon him was certainly impossible, yet to execute him was also inappropriate; former worthies said that if only he had comforted his mother's heart above, that would have sufficed. In the debate over the Prince of Pu 濮園, to call him "parent" (qin 親) was certainly impossible, yet to call him "uncle" (bo 伯) was also unsettling; former Confucians said that one should add the character "father" (fu 父), which would be nearly right. As for the taking or…

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
舍當以李德裕之言為是蓋維州本唐故地所
當得也豈可以小信而妨大計靈州之棄守當
以輔臣之言為是蓋靈州乃必爭之地不可棄
也豈可以險要移于夷狄傳曰大夫無遂事又
曰大夫出境有利於社稷者專之可也以是而
酌陳湯之矯制興師不罪可矣又何功乎是難
免乎匡衡之議傳曰殺人而義令勿讎又曰父
不受誅子復讎可也以是而論徐元慶之手刃
父讎赦之可矣又何誅乎宜有取乎柳宗元之
===
駮嗟夫天下之事幸而處其常則易不幸而遇
其變則難使不度於本然之權度其不至背倫
逆理傷恩害義者幾希愚生僭議及此惟執事
有以折衷之
第四問　　　　　　　　　　　　吳秀
同考試官教諭謝　批〔格物一策正欲覘士子學識此作有考據有歸宿非體認親切者不能宜置前列〕
考試官學正汪　批〔此條答天地萬物之理皆鑿鑿有據必窮物之〕
punctuated:
舍，當以李德裕之言為是。蓋維州本唐故地，所當得也，豈可以小信而妨大計？靈州之棄守，當以輔臣之言為是。蓋靈州乃必爭之地，不可棄也，豈可以險要移于夷狄？《傳》曰：「大夫無遂事。」又曰：「大夫出境，有利於社稷者，專之可也。」以是而酌陳湯之矯制興師，不罪可矣，又何功乎？是難免乎匡衡之議。《傳》曰：「殺人而義，令勿讎。」又曰：「父不受誅，子復讎可也。」以是而論徐元慶之手刃父讎，赦之可矣，又何誅乎？宜有取乎柳宗元之駮。嗟夫！天下之事，幸而處其常則易，不幸而遇其變則難。使不度於本然之權度，其不至背倫逆理、傷恩害義者幾希。愚生僭議及此，惟執事有以折衷之。

第四問　吳秀
同考試官教諭謝批：〔格物一策，正欲覘士子學識。此作有考據，有歸宿，非體認親切者不能，宜置前列。〕
考試官學正汪批：〔此條答天地萬物之理，皆鑿鑿有據。必窮物之〕
translation_en:
…or abandoning [of Weizhou], one should take the words of Li Deyu 李德裕 as right. For Weizhou 維州 was originally former Tang territory that ought to be recovered; how could one allow minor good faith to obstruct a grand strategy? Regarding the abandonment or defense of Lingzhou 靈州, one should take the words of the輔臣 (chief councilor, Li Hang 李沆) as right. For Lingzhou was a strategic point that had to be contested and could not be abandoned; how could one hand over a strategic stronghold to the barbarians? The Commentary (Gongyang Commentary) says: "A grand master has no authority to act on his own initiative." Yet it also says: "Once a grand master has crossed the border, if an action is beneficial to the altars of soil and grain, he may act on his own authority." Weighing Chen Tang's 陳湯 forging of an imperial edict to mobilize troops by this standard, it was enough not to punish him—what merit could he claim? Thus he could hardly escape the criticism of Kuang Heng 匡衡. The tradition (Rites of Zhou / Gongyang Commentary) says: "If a killing is righteous, command that there be no vengeance." And it also says: "When a father suffers an unjust execution, it is permissible for the son to avenge him." Judging Xu Yuanqing's 徐元慶 slaying of his father's enemy with his own hands by this standard, it was enough to pardon him—why execute him? Thus there is good reason to adopt the refutation by Liu Zongyuan 柳宗元. Alas! In the affairs of the world, when one is fortunate enough to deal with normal circumstances, it is easy; when one is unfortunate enough to encounter extraordinary contingencies, it is difficult. If one does not measure them against the inherent standard of weighing and discretion, rare indeed are those who do not end up violating human relationships, defying principle, harming affection, and injuring righteousness! As a foolish student, I have presumptuously discussed matters to this extent; I pray only that Your Excellency will judge and decide upon them.

Fourth Question — Wu Xiu 吳秀
Associate Examiner Instructor Xie 謝 comments: [This policy question on the investigation of things was intended precisely to observe the scholars' learning and insight. This essay is well-grounded in evidence and reaches a sound conclusion; none but one with intimate personal comprehension could have written it. It ought to be placed in the front ranks.]
Examiner Director of Studies Wang 汪 comments: [This point-by-point response concerning the principles of Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things is in every respect solidly substantiated. That one must exhaust the… of things…]

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
理會于一心尤見學識
考試官教授林　批〔批窮理誠身之學此作見之〕
窮天下之理於萬物會萬物之理於一心天地
萬物本吾一體苟於天下之物無一而不格萬
物之理無一而不窮則天地雖大萬物雖多皆
吾度內豈有性外之物哉請因明問以復其萬
一夫盈天地間者惟萬物天地亦物耳天地非
陰陽不能成天地萬物非陰陽不能成萬物天
地萬物一陰陽也陰陽一太極也天之體圓以
===
氣而依乎地地之體方以形而附乎天天地之
所以自相依附者一太極也天之行健其旋轉
也當晝則自左旋而向右向夕則自前降而歸
後當夜則右轉而復左將旦則自後升而趨前
然其所以旋轉無窮者亦一太極也以在天成
象者言之風則火氣之化雨則水氣之化金氣
之肅而為霜土氣之升而為露其所以成者陰
陽之氣聚而有跡耳日曰太陽月曰太陰星則
少陽而辰則少陰也其所以運者陰陽之氣升
punctuated:
〔理會于一心，尤見學識。〕
考試官教授林　批〔批窮理誠身之學，此作見之。〕
窮天下之理於萬物，會萬物之理於一心。天地萬物，本吾一體。苟於天下之物無一而不格，萬物之理無一而不窮，則天地雖大，萬物雖多，皆吾度內，豈有性外之物哉？請因明問以復其萬一。夫盈天地間者惟萬物，天地亦物耳。天地非陰陽不能成天地，萬物非陰陽不能成萬物。天地萬物，一陰陽也；陰陽，一太極也。天之體圓，以氣而依乎地；地之體方，以形而附乎天。天地之所以自相依附者，一太極也。天之行健，其旋轉也，當晝則自左旋而向右，向夕則自前降而歸後，當夜則右轉而復左，將旦則自後升而趨前；然其所以旋轉無窮者，亦一太極也。以在天成象者言之：風則火氣之化，雨則水氣之化，金氣之肅而為霜，土氣之升而為露，其所以成者，陰陽之氣聚而有跡耳；日曰太陽，月曰太陰，星則少陽，而辰則少陰也，其所以運者，陰陽之氣升
translation_en:
… [exhaustive investigation of the] principles [of things] and synthesizing them within a single mind especially demonstrates learning and insight.]
Examiner and Confucian School Director Lin comments: [Comment [?]: The learning of exhaustively investigating principle and making the person sincere is seen in this composition.]

To exhaustively investigate all the principles under heaven in the myriad things is to synthesize the principles of the myriad things within a single mind. Heaven, earth, and the myriad things are fundamentally one body with myself. If there is not a single thing under heaven that is not investigated, and not a single principle of the myriad things that is not exhaustively fathomed, then even though heaven and earth are vast and the myriad things are numerous, all are within the scope of my measure—how could there be anything external to human nature? Allow me to follow your enlightened question in order to reply with one ten-thousandth of the whole.

Now, what fills the space between heaven and earth is simply the myriad things, and heaven and earth are themselves also things. Without yin and yang, heaven and earth cannot form heaven and earth; without yin and yang, the myriad things cannot form the myriad things. Heaven, earth, and the myriad things are one yin and yang; yin and yang are one Supreme Ultimate (Taiji). The substance of heaven is round, relying on vital energy (qi) to lean upon the earth; the substance of earth is square, relying on physical form to adhere to heaven. That by which heaven and earth mutually depend on and adhere to each other is the one Supreme Ultimate. The movement of heaven is vigorous; in its rotation, during the day it revolves from the left toward the right, toward evening it descends from the front and returns to the rear, during the night it turns from the right and returns to the left, and as dawn approaches it ascends from the rear and advances to the front. Yet that by which it rotates without end is also the one Supreme Ultimate.

Speaking in terms of what forms visible phenomena in the heavens: wind is the transformation of the qi of fire, rain is the transformation of the qi of water, the austerity of the qi of metal becomes frost, and the rising of the qi of earth becomes dew; that by which they are formed is simply the qi of yin and yang gathering and leaving traces. The sun is called Greater Yang (taiyang), the moon is called Greater Yin (taiyin), the stars are Lesser Yang (shaoyang), and the zodiacal markers (chen) are Lesser Yin (shaoyin); that by which they revolve is simply the qi of yin and yang ascending…

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
而復降耳至於星隕而爲石雷化而爲斧非怪
誕也在天本氣隕地則成形矣月星無光受日
之光其明一也但月光生於日所照魄生於日
所蔽當日則光滿就日則明盡此弦望晦朔所
由分也月質常圓受日之光猶粉塗其半月中
黑處山河之影猶鏡照物顧兎在腹世俗惑也
何莫而非太極爲之根柢乎以在地成形者言
之人得氣之正氣正而理亦通鳥獸得氣之偏
氣偏而理亦塞然皆有知覺也若夫草木澆灌
===
之則敷榮摧折之則枯落謂其無知覺則不可
鳥獸胎而生卵而化五穀草木種而生根而長
謂其無種亦不可至於麒麟之生鍾天地之和
應文明之瑞世不常有豈有種耶魚龍皆鱗族
然魚得陰數故其鱗三十有六積老陰之數也
龍得陽數故其鱗八十有一積老陽之數也草
木皆植物草得陰氣故其質弱木得陽氣故其
質堅草木之分本乎陰陽也海則水流東極氣
盡而散如沃焦釜無有遺餘是以江漢朝宗而
punctuated: 而復降耳。至於星隕而爲石，雷化而爲斧，非怪誕也，在天本氣，隕地則成形矣。月、星無光，受日之光，其明一也。但月光生於日所照，魄生於日所蔽，當日則光滿，就日則明盡，此弦、望、晦、朔所由分也。月質常圓，受日之光，猶粉塗其半；月中黑處，山河之影，猶鏡照物；「顧兎在腹」，世俗惑也。何莫而非太極爲之根柢乎？以在地成形者言之：人得氣之正，氣正而理亦通；鳥獸得氣之偏，氣偏而理亦塞，然皆有知覺也。若夫草木，澆灌之則敷榮，摧折之則枯落，謂其無知覺則不可。鳥獸胎而生、卵而化，五穀、草木種而生、根而長，謂其無種亦不可。至於麒麟之生，鍾天地之和，應文明之瑞，世不常有，豈有種耶？魚、龍皆鱗族，然魚得陰數，故其鱗三十有六，積老陰之數也；龍得陽數，故其鱗八十有一，積老陽之數也。草、木皆植物，草得陰氣，故其質弱；木得陽氣，故其質堅，草木之分本乎陰陽也。海則水流東極，氣盡而散，如沃焦釜，無有遺餘，是以江漢朝宗而
translation_en: …and then descending again. As for stars falling and becoming stones, or thunder transforming into axes, this is not bizarre or absurd: in heaven they are originally vital force (qi), and when they fall to earth they take on physical form. The moon and stars have no light of their own, but receive the light of the sun; their brightness is one and the same. However, the moon's light arises where the sun shines upon it, and its dark disk (po) arises where the sun is blocked. When facing the sun directly, its light is full; when approaching the sun, its brightness is exhausted. This is how the quarter moons (xian), the full moon (wang), the last day of the lunar month (hui), and the new moon (shuo) are differentiated. The substance of the moon is always round, and its receiving the light of the sun is like powder smeared over half of it. The dark places within the moon are the reflections of mountains and rivers, just like a mirror reflecting things; the notion that "a gazing hare is in its belly" is a vulgar delusion. What among these does not have the Supreme Ultimate (Taiji) as its root and foundation? Speaking in terms of things that take form on earth: humans receive the uprightness of vital force, and because their vital force is upright, their principle (li) is also penetrative; birds and beasts receive the partiality of vital force, and because their vital force is partial, their principle is also obstructed—yet all of them possess perception and awareness. As for grasses and trees, when watered they blossom and flourish, and when broken they wither and fall, so one cannot say they have no perception. Birds and beasts are born from wombs or hatch from eggs; the five grains, grasses, and trees sprout from seeds and grow from roots, so one cannot say they have no seed. Yet as for the birth of the unicorn (qilin), it concentrates the harmony of heaven and earth and responds as an auspicious omen of civilonius culture; it does not always appear in the world, so how could it have a seed? Fish and dragons are both scaly creatures, yet fish obtain the yin number, so their scales number thirty-six, the product of the number of Old Yin; dragons obtain the yang number, so their scales number eighty-one, the product of the number of Old Yang. Grasses and trees are both plants: grasses obtain yin vital force, so their substance is weak; trees obtain yang vital force, so their substance is firm. The distinction between grasses and trees is rooted in yin and yang. As for the sea, waters flow to the eastern extreme, where their vital force is exhausted and disperses, like water poured into a scorching cauldron, leaving no remainder. Therefore, the Yangtze and Han rivers pay court to the sea, and…

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
日夜而不見其泄百川歸海亘古今而不見其
溢矣何莫而非太極為之樞紐乎然天地之間
何往而非物何物而非理無一不具於吾之心
學者苟能格物以窮其理窮理以至於誠身則
無適而非仁矣殆見天高地下心之一濂也日照
月臨心之明也雲行雨施心之游也山川流峙
心之動靜也飛潛動植心之形見也何者而非
吾性分內乎故曰仁者以天地萬物為一體管
見如斯惟執事進退
===
第五問
同考試官教諭馮　批〔以仁義為闢異端之本足見所學之正其亦聖人之徒歟〕
黃表
同考試官教諭余　批〔闢異端吾儒分內事也觀子所學所趨之正不能此策立議嚴整條荅詳明他日為政必有補風教〕
置前列
考試官學正汪　批〔異端一策重在扶正氣使異端之徒聞之亦將進而歸吾儒矣〕
punctuated:
日夜而不見其泄，百川歸海，亘古今而不見其溢矣。何莫而非太極為之樞紐乎？然天地之間，何往而非物，何物而非理，無一不具於吾之心。學者苟能格物以窮其理，窮理以至於誠身，則無適而非仁矣。殆見天高地下，心之一濂也；日照月臨，心之明也；雲行雨施，心之游也；山川流峙，心之動靜也；飛潛動植，心之形見也。何者而非吾性分內乎？故曰：「仁者以天地萬物為一體。」管見如斯，惟執事進退。

第五問
同考試官教諭馮　批〔以仁義為闢異端之本，足見所學之正，其亦聖人之徒歟！〕
黃表
同考試官教諭余　批〔闢異端，吾儒分內事也。觀子所學所趨之正，不能此策立議嚴整，條荅詳明，他日為政，必有補風教。〕
置前列
考試官學正汪　批〔異端一策，重在扶正氣，使異端之徒聞之，亦將進而歸吾儒矣。〕
translation_en:
…day and night without appearing to drain away; the hundred rivers return to the sea throughout antiquity and the present without appearing to overflow. What among these does not have the Supreme Ultimate (Taiji) as its pivot? Yet between heaven and earth, wherever one goes there are things, and whatever thing there is has its principle—not a single one fails to be complete within my own mind. If a scholar can investigate things to exhaust their principles, and exhaust principles so as to arrive at making the person sincere, then nowhere he goes will not be humaneness (ren). One will then nearly see that the height of heaven and the lowliness of earth are the unity [?] of the mind; the shining of the sun and the approach of the moon are the brightness of the mind; the movement of clouds and the bestowal of rain are the roaming of the mind; the flowing of rivers and the standing of mountains are the activity and tranquility of the mind; the flying, submerging, moving, and rooted beings are the manifestations of the mind. Which of these is not within the allotment of my own nature? Therefore it is said: "The humane person forms one body with heaven, earth, and the myriad things." Such is my narrow view; I await only Your Excellency's judgment to advance or reject it.

Fifth Question
Associate Examiner Feng, Instructor (jiaoyu), comments: [Taking humaneness and righteousness as the foundation for refuting heterodoxy suffices to show the correctness of his learning; is he not also a disciple of the sages!]
Huang Biao 黃表
Associate Examiner Yu, Instructor, comments: [Refuting heterodoxy is the proper duty of us Confucians. Observing the correctness of your learning and orientation [?]... this policy essay establishes its arguments with rigor and order, and answers point by point with detail and clarity. When you govern in the future, you will surely be of benefit to moral customs and education.]
Placed in the front ranks.
Examiner Wang, Director of Studies (xuezheng), comments: [This policy essay on heterodoxy places its emphasis on upholding upright qi; if followers of heterodoxy were to hear it, they too would come forward and return to our Confucianism.]

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教授林　批〔邪正之辯與夫闢之之術詞嚴義正足見學識之高〕
甚矣異端之蠹人心也不啻洚水之墊溺猛獸
之逼人夷狄之為我中華病也治之不可不急
驅之不可不力攘斥之不可不嚴且遠也夫然
後人心之蠹銷而仁義之大道廓如也治之驅
之攘斥之其術安在不過脩其本以勝之而巳
夫豈可以口舌諍勢力加哉彼老子為周柱下
史退而隱去嘗著道德五千言而漢明帝時又
===
有西方所謂佛者入焉老氏以虛無為宗而易
大象曰君子以虛受人似也殊不知易之謂虛
虛而有有焉無所不具也佛氏以寂滅為教而
易大傳曰寂然不動似也殊不知易之謂寂寂
而感感焉無所不通也且老子之學虛靜無為
冲退自守其自言曰將欲取之必固與之竊弄
闔闢其體其用視之孟子存心養性擴充其四
端者氷炭相反邵子以為老子得易之體孟子
得易之用不其謬歟佛書之初僅有二十四篇
punctuated:
考試官教授林　批：〔邪正之辯，與夫闢之之術，詞嚴義正，足見學識之高。〕

甚矣，異端之蠹人心也！不啻洚水之墊溺、猛獸之逼人、夷狄之為我中華病也。治之不可不急，驅之不可不力，攘斥之不可不嚴且遠也。夫然後人心之蠹銷，而仁義之大道廓如也。治之、驅之、攘斥之，其術安在？不過脩其本以勝之而巳，夫豈可以口舌諍、勢力加哉！彼老子為周柱下史，退而隱去，嘗著《道德》五千言；而漢明帝時，又有西方所謂佛者入焉。老氏以虛無為宗，而《易·大象》曰：「君子以虛受人」，似也；殊不知《易》之謂虛，虛而有有焉，無所不具也。佛氏以寂滅為教，而《易·大傳》曰：「寂然不動」，似也；殊不知《易》之謂寂，寂而感感焉，無所不通也。且老子之學，虛靜無為，冲退自守，其自言曰：「將欲取之，必固與之」，竊弄闔闢。其體其用，視之孟子存心養性、擴充其四端者，氷炭相反。邵子以為老子得《易》之體，孟子得《易》之用，不其謬歟？佛書之初，僅有二十四篇，
translation_en:
Examiner and Prefectural Director of Studies Lin comments: 〔The distinction between heterodoxy and orthodoxy, together with the methods for refuting heterodoxy, are presented with stern words and upright principles, which suffices to show the loftiness of the candidate's learning and insight.〕

Extreme indeed is the way heterodox teachings eat away at the human mind! It is no less than the drowning caused by floodwaters, the menacing of people by fierce beasts, or the affliction brought upon our Central Lands by barbarians. Bringing them under control cannot but be urgent, driving them away cannot but be forceful, and rejecting and expelling them cannot but be strict and keep them far off. Only then will the rot in the human mind be dissolved, and the Great Way of benevolence and righteousness be opened wide. Wherein lies the method for bringing them under control, driving them away, and rejecting and expelling them? It is nothing more than cultivating the fundamental so as to overcome them—how could it be done by arguing with tongue and lips or by applying coercion and force! That Laozi 老子 served as an Archivist of the Zhou dynasty, and upon retiring into seclusion composed the five thousand words on the Way and its Virtue (Daodejing 道德經); then in the time of Emperor Ming of the Han dynasty (Han Mingdi 漢明帝), there also entered from the West what is called the Buddha. Master Lao takes emptiness and non-being as his core tenet, and the "Great Images" (Daxiang 大象) commentary on the Book of Changes (Yi 易) says, "The superior man receives others with emptiness [humility]," which seems similar; yet one fails to realize that what the Book of Changes calls emptiness is an emptiness that possesses real being within it, lacking nothing at all. The Buddha takes quiescent extinction (nirvana) as his teaching, and the "Great Treatise" (Dazhuan 大傳) commentary on the Book of Changes says, "Quiescent and unmoving," which seems similar; yet one fails to realize that what the Book of Changes calls quiescence is a quiescence that responds when stimulated, penetrating everywhere. Moreover, the learning of Laozi emphasizes empty stillness and non-action,谦退 (modest withdrawal) and self-preservation, yet in his own words he says, "If you would take from it, you must first give to it," stealthily manipulating the opening and closing of things. When its substance and its function are compared with Mencius's (Mengzi 孟子) preserving the mind, nourishing one's nature, and expanding and fulfilling the Four Beginnings, they are as opposite as ice and glowing charcoal. When Master Shao (Shao Yong 邵雍) held that Laozi attained the substance of the Changes while Mencius attained the function of the Changes, was that not erroneous? At the beginning of Buddhist scriptures, there were only twenty-four sections [standardly forty-two sections], …

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
言甚鄙俚其後竊引莊列之語恣爲妄誕之書
及梁而有達磨者出一切掃蕩遂有心靜見理
之論當時既無真儒而老莊亦皆淺近朱子謂
老氏亦難抗衡程子謂攻之者執說反出其下
不其然歟自是而下浸失本真竟爲滅罪資福
生死輪廻之說以營居室衣食之計雖使老佛
復生亦必厭惡而況不爲老佛者乎柰何智者
溺于茫昧愚者誘于禍福或割田園以擴其居
或竭粟帛以給其用而名山勝境宮殿巍峩有
===
所惑也有所利也創建不爲之制也繪飾不爲
之度也僭擬不問糜費不惜也反有過於吾夫
子廟庭之開于禮制者不亦宜乎他如誦法孔
子而徼福文昌斯蓋士之下者嗚呼異端之說
盤據轇轕信之者深奉之者至人其人火其書
廬其居恐未易及但當脩吾仁義之道使天下
之人曉然皆知仁義吾心之固有如水火如穀
粟如布帛雖欲一日離之而不可得則仁之於
父子也義之於君臣也推之夫婦長幼朋友無
punctuated: 言甚鄙俚。其後竊引莊、列之語，恣爲妄誕之書。及梁而有達磨者出，一切掃蕩，遂有心靜見理之論。當時既無真儒，而老、莊亦皆淺近，朱子謂「老氏亦難抗衡」，程子謂「攻之者執說反出其下」，不其然歟？自是而下，浸失本真，竟爲滅罪資福、生死輪廻之說，以營居室衣食之計。雖使老、佛復生，亦必厭惡，而況不爲老、佛者乎？柰何智者溺于茫昧，愚者誘于禍福，或割田園以擴其居，或竭粟帛以給其用，而名山勝境，宮殿巍峩，有所惑也，有所利也。創建不爲之制也，繪飾不爲之度也，僭擬不問，糜費不惜也，反有過於吾夫子廟庭之開于禮制者，不亦宜乎？他如誦法孔子而徼福文昌，斯蓋士之下者。嗚呼！異端之說，盤據轇轕，信之者深，奉之者至。「人其人，火其書，廬其居」，恐未易及。但當脩吾仁義之道，使天下之人曉然皆知仁義吾心之固有，如水火，如穀粟，如布帛，雖欲一日離之而不可得；則仁之於父子也，義之於君臣也，推之夫婦、長幼、朋友，無…
translation_en: …whose language was exceedingly crude and vulgar. Later on, they stealthily borrowed expressions from Zhuangzi 莊子 and Liezi 列子 to indulgedly compose preposterous and fantastical books. By the Liang dynasty (502–557), someone named Bodhidharma (Damo 達磨) appeared, sweeping away everything that had come before and advancing the doctrine of calming the mind to perceive principle. At that time there were no true Confucians, and the followers of Laozi 老子 and Zhuangzi were all shallow as well. Master Zhu (Zhu Xi 朱熹) said that "even the Daoists could hardly contend with them," and Master Cheng (Cheng Hao 程顥 / Cheng Yi 程頤) said that "those who attack them hold to arguments that actually fall beneath theirs"—is this not indeed so? From that point onward, they gradually lost their original truth, ultimately fabricating doctrines of absolving sins, accumulating blessings, and the cycle of life, death, and rebirth as a scheme to secure dwellings, food, and clothing. Even if Laozi and the Buddha were to come back to life, they would surely detest this—how much more so those who are not followers of Laozi and the Buddha! Why is it, then, that the wise drown in their obscure subtleties while the foolish are enticed by their talk of misfortune and blessing? Some carve up their fields and gardens to expand their monasteries; others exhaust their grain and silk to supply their needs. Thus, among famous mountains and scenic sites, their palatial halls rise towering and majestic—because people are deluded by them, and because people seek profit from them. Their construction is not subject to regulations; their painted ornamentation is not bound by limits; their僭越 (usurpatory imitation of imperial styles) goes unquestioned, and their extravagant waste is ungrudged. Is it any wonder that they end up surpassing the temples and courtyards of our Master Confucius, which are established in accordance with ritual regulations? As for other cases, such as reciting and modeling oneself on Confucius while begging for good fortune from Wenchang 文昌, these are truly the lowest sort of scholars. Alas! Heterodox doctrines are deeply entrenched and intricately entangled; those who believe in them do so deeply, and those who revere them do so to the utmost. To "turn their people back into ordinary subjects, burn their books, and convert their monasteries into common dwellings" is, I fear, not easily achieved right away. We ought simply to cultivate our Way of humanity and righteousness, causing all people in the world to clearly understand that humanity and righteousness are inherent in our own minds—like water and fire, like grain and millet, like cloth and silk, which one could not part from for even a single day even if one wished to. Then, from humanity between father and son and righteousness between ruler and minister, extended to husband and wife, elder and younger, and friend and friend, there will be nowhere one goes…

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
適而不盡其道也彼佛老之棄親戚去人倫毀
身滅性而淪于夷狄之歸者自將日銷月鑠而
不得為吾道蠹也孟子曰君子反經而已矣經
正則庶民興庶民興斯無邪慝矣愚敢以是復
明問未知執事以為何如
punctuated: 適而不盡其道也。彼佛、老之棄親戚、去人倫、毀身滅性，而淪于夷狄之歸者，自將日銷月鑠，而不得為吾道蠹也。孟子曰：「君子反經而已矣。經正則庶民興，庶民興斯無邪慝矣。」愚敢以是復明問，未知執事以為何如？
translation_en: …every situation without fully realizing their proper Way. Those followers of Buddha and Laozi, who abandon their relatives, cast aside human relationships, destroy their bodies and extinguish their innate nature, sinking into the ways of barbarians, will naturally waste away day by day and month by month, unable to act as pests upon our Way. Mencius said: "The superior man simply returns to the standard norm. When the standard norm is rectified, the common people are roused to virtue; when the common people are roused to virtue, there will be no perverse wickedness." I venture in my foolishness to offer this in reply to your enlightened question, though I do not know what you, the Examiner, may think of it.

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
江西鄉試錄後序
迺成化十年甲午大比之秋戶部
左侍郎原傑適將
上命巡視江西以科舉登賢重典有司
者不可以非人處其經費必周而
當監察御史程宏楊守隨復議以
貢院湫隘不足以容衆蒹夏潦之
===
後堂屋皆倚側欝蒸之氣拂人不
可以居乃與藩臬二司執事者謀
所以更新加廣焉於堂後別建屋
十二楝令高大敗弊者悉易之拓
地於右方從衡若干尺於是場屋
侈然以改觀有容矣旣走書幣四
方延聘雲等至則禮遇加隆而防
punctuated:
江西鄉試錄後序

迺成化十年甲午大比之秋，戶部左侍郎原傑適將上命巡視江西，以科舉登賢重典，有司者不可以非人，處其經費必周而當。監察御史程宏、楊守隨復議以貢院湫隘，不足以容衆，蒹夏潦之後，堂屋皆倚側，欝蒸之氣拂人，不可以居，乃與藩、臬二司執事者謀所以更新加廣焉。於堂後別建屋十二楝，令高大，敗弊者悉易之，拓地於右方，從衡若干尺，於是場屋侈然以改觀，有容矣。旣走書幣四方，延聘雲等至，則禮遇加隆，而防
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Jiangxi Provincial Examination

Now in the autumn of the triennial examination in the jiawu year, the tenth year of the Chenghua reign (1474), Vice Minister of Revenue of the Left Yuan Jie 原傑 happened to carry the Emperor's command to inspect Jiangxi. Considering that selecting worthies through the civil-service examinations is a weighty institution, he held that the local officials in charge must not be unsuitable men, and that the management of the expenses must be thorough and proper. Investigating Censors Cheng Hong 程宏 and Yang Shousui 楊守隨 further deliberated that because the examination compound was low-lying and cramped, it was insufficient to accommodate the multitude; moreover [?], after the summer floods, the halls and buildings were all leaning and tilted, and the sultry, steaming vapors assailed people so that the place could not be inhabited. Thereupon they consulted with the administrators of the Provincial Administration Commission and Surveillance Commission on how to renovate and expand it. Behind the main hall they separately constructed a building of twelve ridges [?], making it tall and spacious; whatever was dilapidated and ruined was entirely replaced, and the grounds were expanded on the right side by a certain number of feet in length and breadth. Thus the examination compound took on a grand new appearance and had ample room. After they had sent letters and gifts in all directions to invite me, [Liu] Yun 雲, and others, upon our arrival we were treated with heightened courtesy, while the precautions…

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
慎益寀凡入院諸執事皆精一時
之選而諸士子就試者二千七百
餘人仲秋八日庚寅張宴於南昌
道宴畢以樂導送入院辛卯四鼓
入諸生其命題則揭五經四書而
剌之付之至公而任之無情若化
工之誕物吾何得輕重之偏私之
===
倒置之豈惟禁之即使肆之勢能
為乎至公無情之主之也是日也
輕雲開霽北風微涼甲午再試丁
酉三試風日益清朗無煩暑流汗
之苦諸士子人人自奮有李白揚
眉吐氣激昂青雲之志且終塲以
疾故不入者不百人雲等夜以繼
punctuated: 慎益寀。凡入院諸執事，皆精一時之選，而諸士子就試者二千七百餘人。仲秋八日庚寅，張宴於南昌道，宴畢，以樂導送入院。辛卯四鼓，入諸生。其命題，則揭《五經》、《四書》而剌之，付之至公而任之無情，若化工之誕物，吾何得輕重之、偏私之、倒置之？豈惟禁之，即使肆之，勢能為乎？至公無情之主之也。是日也，輕雲開霽，北風微涼；甲午再試，丁酉三試，風日益清朗，無煩暑流汗之苦。諸士子人人自奮，有李白「揚眉吐氣，激昂青雲」之志。且終塲以疾故不入者，不百人。雲等夜以繼
translation_en: … precautions grew ever more thorough [?]. All the functionaries entering the examination compound were the finest selections of the time, and the scholars presenting themselves for the examination numbered over two thousand seven hundred. On the eighth day, gengyin, of the eighth lunar month, a banquet was held at the Nanchang Circuit; when the banquet ended, we were escorted with music into the examination compound. At the fourth watch on the xinmao day, the candidates were admitted. As for setting the examination topics, we opened the Five Classics and Four Books and selected passages by probing [?], committing the process to the utmost impartiality and entrusting it to dispassionate objectivity, just like the Creator bringing forth all things—how could we possibly weigh them unequally, show partiality toward them, or invert their proper order? Not only is such manipulation forbidden, even if one wished to indulge in it, would the circumstances allow it? Utmost impartiality and dispassionate objectivity govern the process. On that day, light clouds parted to reveal clear skies, and the north wind was gently cool. On the jiawu day the second session was held, and on the dingyou day the third session; the breeze and sunshine grew ever clearer and brighter, without the misery of oppressive heat and running sweat. Every one of the candidates exerted himself eagerly, possessing the ambition described by Li Bai (李白) of "raising the eyebrows and exhaling in triumph, roused toward the lofty clouds." Moreover, by the end of the sessions, fewer than a hundred had failed to enter on account of illness. I, Yun, and my colleagues worked night after…

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
日收其文之粹者九十五人自錄
限以定額喟焉惜之而已既小錄
成謂雲宜序後惟人以眇眇之軀
而虛靈應物之地不滿方寸然理
而正之安而和之推而廣之則與
天地可以同太可以相終始者蓋
吾之心天地之心吾之氣天地之
===
氣正則俱正順則俱順正順之感
休祥以集人心與天地相流通豈
容毫毛間哉先是靈芝產於豐城
甘露降於吉水道路籍籍傳以為
異識者知其為人文兆矣而未察
其端以予觀於諸執事之秉心晝
謀一付之至公無情則人心和矣
punctuated:
日，收其文之粹者九十五人。自錄限以定額，喟焉惜之而已。既小錄成，謂雲宜序後。

惟人以眇眇之軀，而虛靈應物之地，不滿方寸。然理而正之，安而和之，推而廣之，則與天地可以同太，可以相終始者，蓋吾之心、天地之心，吾之氣、天地之氣，正則俱正，順則俱順。正順之感，休祥以集。人心與天地相流通，豈容毫毛間哉？

先是，靈芝產於豐城，甘露降於吉水，道路籍籍，傳以為異。識者知其為人文兆矣，而未察其端。以予觀於諸執事之秉心畫謀，一付之至公無情，則人心和矣。
translation_en:
…day, selecting ninety-five men whose essays were the finest. Since the roster was restricted by the fixed quota, we could only sigh with regret over the rest. Once the examination record was completed, it was said that I, Yun, ought to write the postface.

I reflect that although man has a minute body, and the seat of his clear spiritual awareness that responds to things is less than a square inch in size, yet if one orders and rectifies it, settles and harmonizes it, and extends and broadens it, then one can equal the vastness of Heaven and Earth and endure alongside them from beginning to end. This is because our mind is the mind of Heaven and Earth, and our vital energy (qi) is the vital energy of Heaven and Earth: when one is upright, both are upright; when one is harmonious, both are harmonious. Through the resonance of uprightness and harmony, auspicious omens gather. The human mind and Heaven and Earth flow into one another—how could there be the slightest hair's breadth of separation between them?

Prior to this,numinous mushrooms (lingzhi) grew in Fengcheng, and sweet dew fell in Jishui. Along the roads people talked excitedly, passing the word around as a marvel. Those with insight knew that these were omens of cultural and human flourishing, yet they had not discerned their cause. As I observe how all the officiating functionaries held fast to their minds and laid their plans, committing everything entirely to supreme impartiality without personal feeling, human minds were brought into harmony.…

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
心和則氣和氣和則天地之和應
宜其徵兆爲之先見而人才于是
挺出吾国知九十五人中必多名
德忠孝之士起而增
國華安
社稷福元元開太平殄道統以收
國家百年養士之功豈不偉然大丈
===
夫哉於乎西江一省也科舉一事
也有諸執事之謀爲感召且爾使
居宰物之地而一付之至公無情
其和順感通又當何如謂世不底
平俗不還厚禮樂刑政教化之具
不脩舉雨暘不時若四夷不賓服
草木鳥獸不咸遂休徵嘉兆不至
punctuated: 心和則氣和，氣和則天地之和應。宜其徵兆爲之先見，而人才于是挺出。吾固知九十五人中，必多名德忠孝之士，起而增國華，安社稷，福元元，開太平，殄道統，以收國家百年養士之功，豈不偉然大丈夫哉！於乎！西江一省也，科舉一事也，有諸執事之謀爲，感召且爾；使居宰物之地，而一付之至公無情，其和順感通又當何如？謂世不底平，俗不還厚，禮樂刑政教化之具不脩舉，雨暘不時若，四夷不賓服，草木鳥獸不咸遂，休徵嘉兆不至，
translation_en:
When minds are harmonious, vital qi is harmonious; when vital qi is harmonious, the harmony of Heaven and Earth responds in kind. It is fitting, then, that auspicious signs appeared beforehand, and that men of talent have now stood forth. I therefore know that [? "国" for 固] among these ninety-five men there will surely be many gentlemen of renowned virtue, loyalty, and filial piety who will rise to add luster to the state, bring peace to the altars of soil and grain, bless the common people, inaugurate an era of great peace, and carry on [? "殄" for 續/繼] the transmission of the Way, thereby reaping the fruits of the dynasty's century-long cultivation of scholars. Would they not truly be great men!

Alas! Jiangxi is but a single province, and the civil service examination is but a single affair, yet through the planning and conduct of the various administrating officials, the cosmic response summoned forth was already like this. Suppose one were to occupy the position of governing all things and likewise commit everything to the utmost impartiality without personal bias—what then would the harmonious resonance and cosmic response be like? To say that the world would not be brought to peace, that customs would not return to thickness and generosity, that the instruments of rites, music, punishments, governance, and moral transformation would not be put in order and promoted, that rain and sunshine would not be seasonably favorable, that the four surrounding peoples would not submit in allegiance, that plants, trees, birds, and beasts would not all flourish according to their natures, and that auspicious signs and favorable omens would not arrive—…

title: 成化十年江西鄉試錄
text:
吾不信也今而後盖望之諸士子
矣
山西澤州儒學學正汪雲蘿序
punctuated:
吾不信也。今而後，盖望之諸士子矣。
山西澤州儒學學正汪雲蘿序。
translation_en:
…I do not believe it. From now on, indeed, our hopes rest upon all of you scholars.
Postface by Wang Yunluo 汪雲蘿, Director of Studies (xuezheng) of the Confucian School of Zezhou 澤州 in Shanxi 山西.
